中文原文

吴云（1811—1883）是清代书画家、藏书家，清咸丰年间曾任苏州知府，清同治三年（1864年）筑此宅居住。1910年文学家、书画家朱祖谋在此租住，著有《听枫园春集》。

这座宅园包括东、西两路，西路为住宅，尚存门厅、轿厅、大厅和花厅等。东路北部为听枫园，是一座书斋园林，以听枫仙馆为中心，东对平斋，西邻味道居、待霜亭和两罍轩，馆前出游廊，折而向南通往适然亭。仙馆南北各有一座小院。南为旱院，叠湖石假山，下有洞穴，上有蹬道通墨香阁上层。北为水院，开凿小池，绕池堆土山、植花木，饶有自然之趣。

· · · · ·
English

Wu Yun (1811-1883) was a Qing-dynasty calligrapher, painter, and book collector, who served as Suzhou prefect during the Xianfeng reign and built this residence in the 3rd year of Tongzhi (1864).

In 1910, writer, calligrapher, and painter Zhu Zumou rented here and wrote the "Tingfeng Garden Spring Collection.

" This residence-garden includes east and west roads; the west road is the residence, still retaining the gate hall, sedan hall, main hall, and flower hall.

The northern part of the east road is Tingfeng Garden (Listening to Maple Garden), a study garden centered on the Tingfeng Xianguan (Listening to Maple Immortal Hall), facing Pingzhai to the east and adjacent to Weidaoju, Daishuang Ting, and Lianglei Xuan to the west.

A corridor extends from in front of the hall, turning south to the Shiran Pavilion.North and south of the immortal hall are each a small courtyard.

The south is a dry courtyard with a Taihu rockery, with caves below and climbing paths to the upper floor of the Moxiang Pavilion.

The north is a water courtyard with a small pond dug, earth hills piled around the pond, and flowers and trees planted—quite natural charm.

14 怡园
Yiyuan Garden
清
级别 Level
第三批江苏省保（1982年）
地址 Address
姑苏区人民路1256号
类型 Type
古典园林
门票 Ticket
15元
开放时间 Hours
7:30-17:00（16:30停止售票）
中文原文

怡园据传原为明代吴宽（1435—1504）的宅园，吴宽号匏庵，苏州人，中成化八年（1472年）状元，官至礼部尚书，极负声望，清乾隆年间"吴人数吴中往哲文章笔翰，必首推匏庵"（乾隆《长洲县志》）。

吴家在苏州城东有一处别业，称东庄，为明中期名园，现为苏州大学本部，今有沈周所绘《东庄图册》传世。近年有学者考证，认为怡园建于吴宽宅园旧址讹传，文章考述严谨，其说可信（郭明友《苏州怡园建于吴宽"复园"旧址说考证》）。

清同治十三年（1874年）浙江宁绍道台顾文彬（1811—1889）购得此地，先后建造住宅、祠堂和园林，总体格局与留园和狮子林相近。

构园事宜由顾文彬、顾承父子共同主持，身为画家的顾承又邀请任阜长、顾法等画家商讨斟酌，吸取苏州各园的长处，如网师园之水池、环秀山庄之假山、狮子林之洞壑、沧浪亭之复廊……园成之后，广邀名士雅集，颇享盛名。顾文彬给顾承的信中曾说，此园"在我则可自怡，在汝则为怡亲"，因而题名怡园。抗日战争时期怡园遭到轰炸，毁坏较大，新中国成立后重修。

今园林入口位于东侧，入门穿过天井进入前院，南有玉延亭，西有四时潇洒亭，通过游廊相连，构成一处前导庭园。西部园林由复廊隔为内、外两园，廊壁上开漏窗，使两园风景可相互渗透。外园北为坡仙琴馆，收藏宋代苏轼的古琴，敞向北侧，与游廊、玉虹亭构成一处抚琴、听琴的场所，为当年"怡园琴会"的雅集胜地。

园南为拜石轩，是一座四面厅，南北皆栽植花木、点置峰石，供人在轩内欣赏。由坡仙琴馆向北经石舫和锁绿轩，或由拜石轩向西经南雪亭，皆可进入内园，为怡园主景区。内园模仿拙政园远香堂一带。南侧为主堂，是一座鸳鸯厅：南为锄月轩，可欣赏轩南的湖石花台；北为藕香榭，前出平台，朝向北部的山池主景。

池北堆土叠山，大致分为三片：东部较为平坦，建四角金粟亭；中部为平缓土丘，建六角小沧浪亭；西部为湖石假山，立峰构洞，山顶建螺髻亭。池水在西山南端收紧变为溪流，折向西北后又汇成一处小池，池西建画舫斋。南侧以游廊连接面壁亭、碧梧栖凤轩，与藕香榭相通，此处空间曲折宛转，亭内悬一大镜，愈显扑朔迷离，同时又可向北欣赏石壁桥亭、对岸溪山，俨如画屏。

在苏州园林中怡园建造时间较晚，因而得以广泛借鉴他园手法，但这种集锦式的造园手法也使园林主题不够突出，人在园中但觉此处肖沧浪亭，彼处似狮子林，而每每忘其为怡园。

· · · · ·
English

Yiyuan Garden is said to have originally been the residence garden of Wu Kuan (1435-1504) of the Ming.

Wu Kuan, hao Pao'an, was a native of Suzhou who won the zhuangyuan (top scholar) in the 8th year of Chenghua (1472) and rose to Minister of Rites, enjoying great prestige; during the Qianlong reign of the Qing, "when Suzhou people discussed the writings and calligraphy of former worthies in Wu, they always first named Pao'an" (Qianlong "Changzhou County Gazetteer").

The Wu family had a villa east of Suzhou called Dongzhuang, a famous mid-Ming garden, now the main campus of Suzhou University, with Shen Zhou's "Dongzhuang Album" surviving.

In recent years, scholars have argued that the claim that Yiyuan was built on the site of Wu Kuan's residence garden is a misattribution, with rigorous textual research supporting this view (Guo Mingyou, "Textual Research on the Claim that Suzhou Yiyuan Was Built on the Site of Wu Kuan's 'Fuyuan'").

In the 13th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1874), Gu Wenbin (1811-1889), Circuit Intendant of Ning-Shao in Zhejiang, purchased this site and successively built a residence, ancestral hall, and garden, with an overall layout similar to the Lingering Garden and Lion Grove.

The garden design was jointly directed by Gu Wenbin and his son Gu Cheng; Gu Cheng, himself a painter, invited painters Ren Fuchang and Gu Fa to discuss and deliberate, absorbing the strengths of various Suzhou gardens—such as the pond of the Master of Nets Garden, the rockery of Huanxiu Manor, the caves of the Lion Grove, and the double corridor of the Surging Wave Pavilion.

After completion, famous scholars were widely invited for elegant gatherings, earning considerable renown.

In a letter to Gu Cheng, Gu Wenbin wrote that this garden "for me is for self-delight, for you it is for delighting kin"—hence the name Yiyuan (Delight Garden).

During the War of Resistance against Japan, Yiyuan was bombed and heavily damaged; restored after the founding of New China.

Today the garden entrance is on the east side; entering through a courtyard leads to the front yard, with the Yuyan Pavilion to the south and the Sishi Xiaosa Pavilion to the west, connected by a corridor, forming a introductory courtyard.

The western garden is divided by a double corridor into inner and outer gardens; lattice windows in the corridor wall allow the scenery of both gardens to interpenetrate.

North of the outer garden is the Poxian Qin Guan (Su Shi Qin Pavilion), housing a Song-dynasty guqin (zither) of Su Shi, open to the north, forming a place for playing and listening to the qin with the corridor and Yuhong Pavilion—the venue for the famous "Yiyuan Qin Gatherings.

" South of the garden is the Baishi Xuan (Worshipping Stones Studio), a four-sided hall with flowers, trees, and peak rocks planted both north and south for appreciation from inside the hall.

From the Poxian Qin Guan northward via the Stone Boat and Suolu Xuan, or from the Baishi Xuan westward via the Nanxue Pavilion, one can enter the inner garden—the main scenic area of Yiyuan.

The inner garden imitates the area around Yuanxiang Tang of the Humble Administrator's Garden.

The south side is the main hall, a mandarin-duck hall: the south is Chuyue Xuan (Hoeing Moon Studio), for admiring the Taihu rock flower terrace south of the studio; the north is Ouxiang Xie (Lotus Fragrance Pavilion), with a platform extending forward facing the northern mountain-pond main scenery.

North of the pond, earth is piled and rocks stacked, roughly divided into three sections: the east is relatively flat, with the four-corner Jinsu Pavilion; the middle is a gentle earth mound, with the hexagonal Xiaocanglang Pavilion; the west is a Taihu rockery with standing peaks and caves, topped by the Luoji Pavilion.

The pond water narrows at the south end of the west hill into a stream, turning northwest and forming another small pond, with the Huafang Zhai (Painted Boat Studio) west of the pond.

On the south side, a corridor connects the Mianbi Pavilion and Biwu Qifeng Xuan, communicating with the Ouxiang Xie; here the space twists and turns, with a large mirror hanging in the pavilion enhancing the labyrinthine feeling, while also offering northward views of stone walls, bridges, and pavilions and the stream-mountain opposite—like a painted screen.

Among Suzhou gardens, Yiyuan was built relatively late, allowing it to widely borrow techniques from other gardens; however, this anthology-style garden method also makes the garden's theme less prominent—visitors feel this place resembles the Surging Wave Pavilion and that place resembles the Lion Grove, often forgetting they are in Yiyuan.

15 玄妙观
Xuanmiao Taoist Temple
宋
级别 Level
第二批全国重点文物保护单位（1982年）
地址 Address
姑苏区观前街94号
类型 Type
道观
门票 Ticket
参观10元，表演35元
开放时间 Hours
7:30-17:15（16:45停止售票）
中文原文

苏州玄妙观始建于西晋咸宁二年（276年），初名真庆道院，唐代改称开元宫，宋称天庆观，元代始称玄妙观。

玄妙观位于苏州最核心的位置，为苏州道观之首，最兴盛时有殿宇30余座，如今仅存中路的山门、三清殿和殿前的朝北玄帝铜殿、五代古井，东路的文昌殿、斗姆阁和寿星殿，以及西路的雷尊殿和火神殿等。此外附近还有五鹤街、六合亭和四海亭等古迹。

玄妙观主殿三清殿建于南宋淳熙六年（1179年），是苏州仅存的南宋木构殿宇，也是江南现存最大的木构古建筑。

三清殿为九开间，殿柱采用"满堂柱"式，南北共七列，每列十根，外部檐柱为八角形青石柱，其中上檐内槽中央四缝的"六铺作重抄上昂"与《营造法式》记载相合，是中国现存之孤例。

殿内供奉上清、玉清、太清三清塑像，俗称太上老君、元始天尊、通天教主。三尊塑像高达17米，造型逼真，姿态协调，表情自然，为宋代雕塑佳作。

殿后西北角有老子像碑，为唐吴道子绘像，唐玄宗题赞，颜真卿书写和南宋宝庆元年（1225年）刻石高手张允迪摹刻，被誉为"四绝"碑，是镇殿之宝，目前国内仅存两块（另一块在武当山南寿宫）。

大殿台基南侧青石栏板上浮雕神仙、鱼龙、鸟兽和山水亭台，刻画细致。

· · · · ·
English

Suzhou's Xuanmiao Temple was founded in the 2nd year of Xianning of the Western Jin (276), originally called Zhenqing Daoist Abbey, renamed Kaiyuan Palace in the Tang, Tianqing Temple in the Song, and Xuanmiao Temple from the Yuan.

Located at the very heart of Suzhou, it is the foremost Taoist temple in Suzhou.

At its peak it had over 30 halls; today only the central road's gate hall, Sanqing Hall (Three Purities Hall), the north-facing Xuandi Bronze Hall in front of the hall, and the Five Dynasties ancient well survive; the east road's Wenchang Hall, Doumu Pavilion, and Shouxing Hall; and the west road's Leizun Hall and Huoshen Hall.

Nearby are also ancient sites such as Wuhe Street, Liuhe Pavilion, and Sihai Pavilion.

The main hall Sanqing Hall was built in the 6th year of Chunxi of the Southern Song (1179), the only surviving Southern Song wooden hall in Suzhou and the largest surviving wooden ancient building in Jiangnan.

Sanqing Hall is nine bays wide, with columns in a "full-hall column" arrangement—seven rows north-south, ten columns per row; the external eave columns are octagonal bluestone columns.

Among them, the "six-bracket-set double-copy upper-ang" of the central four seams in the upper eave's inner trough matches the records in the "Yingzao Fashi" (Treatise on Architectural Methods), a unique surviving example in China.

Inside the hall are enshrined the Three Purities statues—Shangqing, Yuqing, and Taiqing—commonly called the Supreme Lord, Primordial Heavenly Venerable, and Tongtian Sect Leader.

The three statues stand 17 meters high, with realistic modeling, coordinated postures, and natural expressions—excellent Song-dynasty sculptures.

At the northwest corner behind the hall is the Laozi Portrait Stele, with the portrait painted by Wu Daozi of the Tang, eulogy inscribed by Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, calligraphy by Yan Zhenqing, and carved in the 1st year of Baoqing of the Southern Song (1225) by master carver Zhang Yundi—hailed as the "Four Wonders" stele, a treasure of the hall, with only two surviving in China (the other at Nanshou Palace, Wudang Mountain).

The bluestone railing on the south side of the hall's platform has relief carvings of immortals, fish and dragons, birds and beasts, and landscapes with pavilions, finely detailed.

建筑要点 / Key Features
西晋咸宁二年建；苏州最核心道观；三清殿南宋淳熙六年建；江南现存最大木构古建筑；六铺作重抄上昂孤例；老子像碑四绝
16 文起堂（张献翼故居）
Wenqi Hall Garden (Former Residence of Zhang Xianyi)
明
级别 Level
第六批江苏省保（2006年）
地址 Address
干将东路712号
类型 Type
故居
开放时间 Hours
暂未开放
中文原文

文起堂是明代文学家张献翼（1534—1601）的故居，他与其兄凤翼（戏曲作家）、其弟燕翼（画家）以才学著称，被誉为"吴中三张"。张献翼生平举止怪诞，被今人戏称为"万历第一行为艺术家"，这与他早年的应试经历有关。

明嘉靖四十三年（1564年）张氏三兄弟一起中举，但主考官"以三人同列稍引嫌，为裁其一，则幼于（献翼）也。归家愤愤，因而好怪诞以消不平"。文起堂之名乃张献翼好友皇甫汸所题，喻指张家"文脉从此起矣"，可惜因中举不成，张献翼一生潦倒，行止癫狂。他曾在堂庑间挂十余张牌子，上题"张幼予卖诗""卖文"，甚至"卖浆""卖痴""卖呆"等。

其兄张凤翼对好友沈德符调侃："吾更虞其再出一牌，云'幼子卖兄'，则吾危矣。"沈德符回答："果尔再出一牌，云'卖友'，则吾辈将奈何？"张献翼晚年好穿奇装异服，并改名为"敉"。沈德符担忧地对张凤翼说，献翼所戴"红帽乃俘囚所顶，一献阙下，即就市曹，大非吉征，奈何？"凤翼回答："奚止是，其新改之名亦似杀字，吾方深虑之。

"但亲人、朋友虽然忧心，却对他的怪诞行为无可奈何，最终张献翼"以妓致殒"，凤翼、德符唯有相对挥泪（沈德符《万历野获编》卷23）。文起堂坐北朝南，现存两进，包括轿厅、大厅和东西两侧的厢房。入门为天井，北侧是三间轿厅，采用木柱础，梁架为圆作扁做，是苏州市区仅存的孤例。

厅北有一座苏州罕见的双面砖雕门楼，雕刻精美，两翼出贴砖照壁。门楼北侧为正厅文起堂，也是三开间，采用扁作抬梁式，梁柱用料粗壮，虽经过清代大修，仍保持了明代风格。

入清后文起堂归大兴县知县汤彦祥，重修了正厅，轿厅和门楼仍为明代旧物，是研究明代民居的重要实例。

· · · · ·
English

Wenqi Hall is the former residence of Ming-dynasty writer Zhang Xianyi (1534-1601).

He and his brother Fengyi (a playwright) and younger brother Yanyi (a painter) were renowned for their talent, hailed as the "Three Zhangs of Wu.

" Zhang Xianyi's eccentric behavior throughout his life earned him the modern nickname "the first performance artist of the Wanli era," related to his early examination experience.

In the 43rd year of Jiajing of the Ming (1564), the three Zhang brothers all passed the provincial examination, but the chief examiner "slightly suspected impropriety with all three listed together, so cut one—that was the youngest, Youyu (Xianyi).

Returning home resentful, he thus became fond of eccentricity to dissipate his indignation.

" The name Wenqi Hall was inscribed by Zhang Xianyi's friend Huang Fang, metaphorically meaning the Zhang family's "cultural lineage begins here.

" Unfortunately, due to failing the examination, Zhang Xianyi lived in poverty all his life with deranged behavior.

He once hung over ten signs in his hall and corridors, inscribed with "Zhang Youyu sells poetry," "sells writing," even "sells porridge," "sells madness," "sells stupidity," etc.

His brother Zhang Fengyi joked to their friend Shen Defu: "I'm even more afraid he'll put out another sign saying 'younger brother sells older brother'—then I'm in danger.

" Shen Defu replied: "If he really puts out another sign saying 'sells friends,' what will we do?" In his later years Zhang Xianyi loved wearing bizarre clothing and changed his name to "Mi.

" Shen Defu worriedly said to Zhang Fengyi that the red hat Xianyi wore was "what prisoners wear, and once presented at court, he'd go to the execution ground—very inauspicious, what can be done?

" Fengyi replied: "Not only that, his newly changed name also resembles the character for 'kill'—I'm deeply worried.

" But though family and friends were concerned, they could do nothing about his eccentric behavior; ultimately Zhang Xianyi "died because of a prostitute," and Fengyi and Defu could only weep at each other (Shen Defu, "Wanli Yehuo Bian" vol.

23).Wenqi Hall faces south, with two surviving bays including the sedan hall, main hall, and east-west side rooms.

Entering is a courtyard; the north side is a three-bay sedan hall with wooden column bases and round-timber flattened beam framing—the only surviving example in urban Suzhou.

North of the hall is a rare double-sided brick-carved gate tower in Suzhou, exquisitely carved, with brick screen walls extending from both wings.

North of the gate tower is the main hall Wenqi Tang, also three bays, using flattened beam-and-column construction with stout timber; though heavily repaired in the Qing, it retains Ming style.

After the Qing, Wenqi Hall passed to Tang Yanxiang, magistrate of Daxing County, who rebuilt the main hall; the sedan hall and gate tower remain Ming originals—an important example for studying Ming-dynasty residences.

17 惠荫园
Huiyin Garden
明—清
级别 Level
第六批江苏省保（2006年）
地址 Address
姑苏区临顿路南显子巷13号
类型 Type
古典园林
开放时间 Hours
参观需经批准
中文原文

明代嘉靖年间太学生归湛初聘请叠山名手周丹泉在此造园，模仿太湖洞庭西山的林屋洞叠筑"小林屋"水假山，清初归复社成员韩馨。

韩馨曾为虎丘五人墓书丹，得罪阉党，后又拒绝与阮大铖合作，晚明之际便隐居避祸，清顺治六年（1649年）购得归氏园，改筑后更名洽隐园。

清康熙四十六年（1707年）园中建筑、花木毁于火灾，仅存水假山，清乾隆十六年（1751年）修复（韩是升《小林屋记》）。此园后归布政使倪莲舫，太平天国时期略有毁伤。

清光绪年间李鸿章奏请朝廷在园内建忠烈程公祠和安徽会馆，更名惠荫园，并构筑惠荫园八景。20世纪30年代园林学家童寯前往考察时尚保存完整，"文革"期间大部分建筑被毁，今仅存水假山与山顶四面厅。

周丹泉技艺高超，此山为其得意之作，属晚明叠山的上乘作品，受到历代有识之士的赞赏。韩是升提到小林屋山到清乾隆年间："历二百年，苔藓若封，烟云自吐。碧梧银杏，紫荆翠柏，春夏之交，浓荫蔽日。时雨初霁，岩乳欲滴。有水一泓，清可鉴物。嵌空架楼，吟眺自适。游其中者，几莫辨为匠心之运。

"陈从周称誉此山"层叠巧石如洞曲，引水灌之，点以步石。人行其间，如入洞壑"。至今仍可从中体会明人叠山理水的精雅奇巧。

· · · · ·
English

During the Jiajing reign of the Ming, imperial student Gui Zhanchu hired the renowned rockery master Zhou Danquan to build a garden here, imitating the Linwu Cave of West Dongting Mountain in Lake Tai to pile the "Xiaolinwu" (Small Forest House) water rockery.

In the early Qing it passed to Han Xin, a member of the Restoration Society (Fushe).

Han Xin had written the epitaph for the Five Men's Tomb at Huqiu, offending the eunuch faction, and later refused to cooperate with Ruan Dacheng; in the late Ming he went into seclusion to avoid disaster, purchasing the Gui family garden in the 6th year of Shunzhi of the Qing (1649), rebuilding and renaming it Qiyin Garden.

In the 46th year of Kangxi (1707), the garden's buildings and flowers/trees were destroyed by fire, leaving only the water rockery; restored in the 16th year of Qianlong (1751) (Han Shisheng, "Record of Xiaolinwu").

The garden later passed to Ni Lianfang, administrative commissioner; it suffered slight damage during the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom period.

During the Guangxu reign, Li Hongzhang petitioned the court to build the Zhonglie Chenggong Shrine and Anhui Guildhall in the garden, renaming it Huiyin Garden, and constructing the Eight Scenes of Huiyin Garden.

In the 1930s, garden scholar Tong Jun visited and found it well preserved; during the Cultural Revolution most buildings were destroyed; today only the water rockery and the four-sided hall on the mountaintop survive.

Zhou Danquan was highly skilled, and this mountain was his masterpiece—a superior late-Ming rockery work, appreciated by discerning people throughout history.

Han Shisheng noted of the Xiaolinwu mountain by the Qianlong period: "After two hundred years, moss seals it, clouds and mist emanate from it.

Green parasol trees and ginkgoes, redbud and emerald cypress—between spring and summer, dense shade blocks the sun.After fresh rain, rock drips seem about to fall.

There is a pool of water, clear enough to reflect objects.Buildings are framed in the void, for chanting and gazing at leisure.Those wandering within can hardly distinguish the workings of craft.

" Chen Congzhou praised this mountain: "Layered and ingenious stones like winding caves, with water channeled through, stepping stones placed.Walking among them is like entering a ravine.

" Today one can still appreciate the refined ingenuity of Ming-dynasty rockery piling and water management.

18 卫道观前潘宅（礼耕堂）
Pan's Family Residence before Weidao Temple (Ligeng Hall)
清
级别 Level
第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
地址 Address
姑苏区临顿路钮家巷1、3、7、9号
类型 Type
民居
门票 Ticket
参观要许可
中文原文

卫道观前潘宅原为清康熙年间河南巡抚顾汧的"凤池园"，清乾隆五十八年（1793年）吴县人潘世恩（1769—1854）高中状元，于清嘉庆十四年（1809年）购得凤池园西部作为父亲潘奕基的养老之所，仍称"凤池园"，大厅题额"留余堂"。

潘世恩为官五十余年，官至武英殿大学士、太傅，为乾隆、嘉庆、道光、咸丰"四朝元老"。他晚年居家尽孝13年，在留余堂博览群书，完成《读史镜古编》《正学编》《有真意斋文集》《思补斋诗集》和《思补老人自订年谱》等著述，堪称学术有成的状元宰相。

陈康祺《郎潜纪闻》将潘世恩誉为清朝第一有福之人："本朝耆臣，生加太傅者五人，重宴琼林者八人，状元作宰相者八人，唯潘文恭公兼之。又大拜不阶协办，枢廷不始学习，皆异数也。富贵寿考，子孙继武，公之福祉，三百年一人而已。"宅第今存东、中、西三路，西路与中路之间有备弄。

中路自南向北共四进，依次为门厅、轿厅、正厅和上房，正厅礼耕堂宽三间，前后皆有船篷轩，木雕精美。西路前部有鸳鸯厅，厅后小院点缀山石花木。东侧的备弄墙上开图案各异的八扇漏窗，构思细巧。厅北为三间纱帽厅，前出抱厦，内部的壁橱、梁枋和绰木雕镂精细。厅北又有一座小庭园，环境幽雅。

除了卫道观前，在姑苏区南石子街10号还有一处潘祖荫（1830—1890）故居，是他的伯父、潘世恩的次子潘曾莹（1808—1878）改建，内有清池曲桥、湖石亭榭，景致清丽，现为花间堂高档旅舍。

· · · · ·
English

The Pan Family Residence before Weidao Temple was originally the "Fengchi Garden" of Gu Qian, Henan Governor during the Kangxi reign of the Qing.

In the 58th year of Qianlong (1793), Pan Shien (1769-1854), a native of Wu County, won the zhuangyuan (top scholar); in the 14th year of Jiaqing (1809) he purchased the western part of Fengchi Garden as a retirement home for his father Pan Yiji, still calling it "Fengchi Garden," with the main hall inscribed "Liuyu Tang" (Preserving Surplus Hall).

Pan Shien served as an official for over fifty years, rising to Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall and Grand Tutor—a "veteran of four reigns" (Qianlong, Jiaqing, Daoguang, Xianfeng).

In his later years he lived at home fulfilling filial piety for 13 years, reading extensively in Liuyu Tang and completing works such as "Reading History as a Mirror of the Ancient," "Correct Learning Compilation," "Collected Writings of Youzhenyi Studio," "Poetry Collection of Sibu Studio," and "Self-Compiled Chronicle of the Sibu Elder"—a scholar-accomplished zhuangyuan prime minister.

Chen Kangqi's "Langqian Jiwen" hailed Pan Shien as the most blessed person of the Qing Dynasty: "Among veteran ministers of this dynasty, five were given the title Grand Tutor while alive, eight reattended the Qionglin Banquet, eight zhuangyuan became prime ministers—only Pan Wengong (Pan Shien) combined all.

Moreover, he became grand secretary without first serving as associate administrator, and entered the Grand Council without first serving as apprentice—both exceptional.

Wealth, honor, longevity, and descendants succeeding him—his blessings were unique in three hundred years.

" The residence today retains east, middle, and west roads, with a service alley between the west and middle roads.

The middle road has four bays from south to north: gate hall, sedan hall, main hall, and inner quarters.

The main hall Ligeng Tang (Ritual Plowing Hall) is three bays wide, with boat-canopy porches front and rear, with exquisite wood carvings.

The front of the west road has a mandarin-duck hall, with a small courtyard behind decorated with rocks, flowers, and trees.

The service alley wall on the east side has eight lattice windows with different patterns, ingeniously conceived.

North of the hall is a three-bay Shamao (Official Hat) Hall, with a front portico and finely carved interior closets, beams, and lintels.

North of the hall is another small garden with elegant surroundings.Besides Weidaoqian, at No.

10 South Shizi Street in Gusu District there is another former residence of Pan Zuyin (1830-1890), rebuilt by his uncle Pan Zengying (1808-1878), Pan Shien's second son, with clear ponds, winding bridges, Taihu rocks, and pavilions—beautiful scenery, now a high-end Blossom Hill Inn.

19 耦园
The Couple's Retreat Garden
清
级别 Level
世界文化遗产，第五批全国重点文物保护单位（2001年）
地址 Address
姑苏区仓街小新桥巷6号
类型 Type
古典园林
门票 Ticket
旺季20元，淡季15元
开放时间 Hours
7:30-17:15（16:45停止售票）
中文原文

耦园位于苏州古城东隅小新桥巷6号，北、东、南三面临水，西面临街。前身为清雍正年间四川保宁知府陆锦（1681—？）致仕回乡修筑的涉园，程章华曾作《涉园记》，李果作《涉园杂咏》八首，徐瑶圃绘《涉园消夏图》，今图已佚失，仅存杨绳武《涉园消夏图记》。后来园归书法家郭凤梁，又归崇明祝氏，太平天国时期被毁。

清同治十三年（1874年）沈秉成（1822—1895）购得园址，聘请画家顾沄重新经营，在园址中央插入住宅部分，取宋诗"东园载酒西园醉"之意，改为东、西两园。

清光绪二年（1876年）落成，沈秉成与夫人严永华偕隐园中，唱和相随，取名耦园。后来园林散为民居、校舍、工厂，"文革"结束后修复开放，2000年作为苏州古典园林扩展项目列入《世界遗产名录》，2001年定为全国重点文物保护单位。

耦园主入口在中路住宅部分，沿中轴线自南向北依次布置门厅、轿厅、正厅载酒堂和后楼，共四进。西园以织帘老屋为主堂，分为南北两院。南院较大，堆湖石假山，靠近主堂处较低，以湖石围出花台，向后逐渐高起。

山上云墙是20世纪50年代居民为防相互干扰而建，阻断了假山浑然一体的气势，却又营造出"奇峰绝巘，累累乎墙外"的气氛。山上有山洞石道可穿可登，西、北有折廊、半亭和鹤寿亭，围成一处步移景异的曲折庭院。北院相对较小也较方整，用湖石堆筑三处花台，略肖"一池三山"之意，院北建二层藏书楼。东园是耦园的精华所在，主体为一池一山。

从东墙下引内城河水入园，向南形成南北狭长的受月池，水池中部架三折宛虹桥，池南建"山水间"四面厅。假山位于水池西北，分为东、西两山。东为留云岫主山，西北、东北、东南三面可登，内藏石室，开口在东南。其东下临水池，陡峭如绝壁，设蹬道可降到池边，是全山最精妙处。西为桃屿辅山，与主山气脉相连，向西渐趋平缓，其间断为邃谷，可通游人。

整座假山用大小相同的黄石叠成，突出横向纹理，颇得山水画之斧披皴画意，叠山技艺之高超，在苏州黄石假山中堪称第一。山间植山茶、黄杨和桧柏等古木，增添山林气息。山池北部是东园主厅城曲草堂，东西两侧都有亭、廊，可从不同角度欣赏山容水态。园林最南部还有听橹楼和魁星阁，可眺望园林内外景色。

耦园主要建于清末，建筑密度较大，反映了时代特点。园林以夫妇偕隐为主题，形成罕见的东、西园格局。两园一大一小，一为旱院为一水院，一用黄石一用湖石，处处形成呼应和对仗，园景命名如双照楼和枕波双隐等，共同突出了耦园主题。

· · · · ·
English

The Couple's Retreat Garden (Ouyuan) is located at No.

6 Xiaoxinqiao Lane, Cang Street, in the eastern corner of Suzhou's old city, facing water on the north, east, and south sides and a street on the west.

Its predecessor was the She Garden (Wading Garden) built by Lu Jin (1681-?), former prefect of Baoning in Sichuan, after retiring during the Yongzheng reign of the Qing.

Cheng Zhanghua wrote the "Record of She Garden," Li Guo wrote eight poems "Miscellaneous Chants of She Garden," and Xu Yaopu painted the "Summer Retreat at She Garden"—the painting is now lost, only Yang Shengwu's "Record of the Summer Retreat at She Garden" survives.

Later the garden passed to calligrapher Guo Fengliang, then to the Zhu family of Chongming, and was destroyed during the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom period.

In the 13th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1874), Shen Bingcheng (1822-1895) purchased the site and hired painter Gu Yun to redesign it, inserting a residential section in the center.

Taking the meaning of the Song poem "carrying wine in the east garden, getting drunk in the west garden," he divided it into east and west gardens.

Completed in the 2nd year of Guangxu (1876), Shen Bingcheng and his wife Yan Yonghua lived in seclusion together in the garden, composing poetry in response to each other, hence the name Ouyuan (Couple's Garden).

Later the garden was divided into residences, schools, and factories; restored and opened after the Cultural Revolution; in 2000, as an extension of Suzhou Classical Gardens, it was inscribed on the World Heritage List; in 2001 designated a National Key Cultural Heritage Site.

The main entrance is in the central residential section, with four bays along the central axis from south to north: gate hall, sedan hall, main hall Zaijiu Tang (Carrying Wine Hall), and rear building.

The west garden centers on the Zhulian Laowu (Weaving Curtain Old House) as the main hall, divided into north and south courtyards.

The south courtyard is larger, with a Taihu rockery—lower near the main hall, with Taihu rocks enclosing flower terraces, gradually rising toward the back.

The cloud wall on the mountain was built by residents in the 1950s to prevent mutual interference, blocking the rockery's unified momentum but creating an atmosphere of "strange peaks and precipices, piling up outside the wall.

" The mountain has caves and stone paths to pass through and climb; on the west and north are winding corridors, half-pavilions, and the Heshou Pavilion (Crane Longevity Pavilion), forming a courtyard where scenery changes with each step.

The north courtyard is relatively smaller and more regular, with three Taihu rock flower terraces, slightly resembling the "one pond, three mountains" motif; north of the courtyard is a two-story library building.

The east garden is the essence of Ouyuan, with one pond and one mountain as the main body.

Water from the inner city moat is channeled in from under the east wall, forming the north-south elongated Shouyue Pond (Receiving Moon Pond); a three-bend Wanhong Bridge spans the middle of the pond, and south of the pond is the "Shanshui Jian" (Between Mountains and Water) four-sided hall.

The rockery is northwest of the pond, divided into east and west hills.

The east is the main hill Liuyun Xiu (Cloud-Retaining Peak), climbable from northwest, northeast, and southeast, with a stone chamber inside opening to the southeast.

Its east side drops steeply to the pond like a cliff, with climbing paths down to the pond edge—the most exquisite part of the whole mountain.

The west is the secondary hill Taoyu (Peach Islet), connected to the main hill by qi and pulse, gradually flattening westward, with a deep ravine in between for visitors to pass through.

The entire rockery is piled with yellow stones of similar size, emphasizing horizontal texture, capturing the axe-cut texture of landscape painting—its rockery technique is arguably the finest among Suzhou's yellow-stone rockeries.

Ancient camellias, boxwoods, and cypresses are planted among the mountains, adding mountain-forest atmosphere.

North of the mountain-pond is the east garden's main hall Chengqu Caotang (City-Curve Thatched Hall), with pavilions and corridors on both east and west sides for admiring mountain and water from different angles.

At the southernmost part of the garden are the Tinglu Tower (Listening to Sculls Tower) and Kuixing Pavilion, offering views of scenery inside and outside the garden.

Ouyuan was mainly built in the late Qing, with high building density reflecting the era's characteristics.

The garden takes couple's seclusion as its theme, forming a rare east-west garden layout.

The two gardens are one large and one small, one dry courtyard and one water courtyard, one using yellow stone and one using Taihu stone—everywhere forming echoes and antitheses.

Garden scene names such as Shuangzhao Tower (Double Illumination Tower) and Zhenbo Shuangyin (Pillow-Wave Double Seclusion) jointly emphasize the Ouyuan theme.

20 全晋会馆（中国昆曲博物馆）
Quanjin Guild Hall (Kunqu Opera Museum)
清
级别 Level
第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
地址 Address
姑苏区平江路中张家巷14号
类型 Type
会馆/博物馆
门票 Ticket
免费开放
开放时间 Hours
8:30-16:30，周日14:00-15:30表演昆曲
中文原文

苏州全晋会馆始创于清光绪五年（1879年），由山西商人集资兴建，又称山西会馆，在江苏会馆中最为精雅。会馆原有东、中、西三路，现存中、西两路。中路自南而北布置头门、戏楼和正殿。

戏楼坐南朝北，面向正殿，底层为仪门和两廊，二层为开敞的戏台，南有五间横列的后台。北部正殿南侧设平台，与戏楼两侧向北伸出的五间厢楼共同构成一处完整的观戏空间。戏台采用歇山顶，檐角高翘，额枋、垂柱雕刻精美。

台内的穹窿藻井直径3米，高2米，由632个木雕构件采用榫卯方式组成旋形纹饰，既富丽堂皇，又能聚声扩音，被誉为江苏现存最精美的古戏台。西路布置庭池花木，精雅可观。

北部的昆曲文物史料展和西侧曲尺形房屋中的昆曲戏台模型展较为精彩，展出江苏各地的戏台模型，值得一看。

· · · · ·
English

Suzhou's Quanjin Guild Hall was founded in the 5th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1879), built with funds raised by Shanxi merchants, also called the Shanxi Guild Hall—the most elegant among Jiangsu's guild halls.

The guild hall originally had east, middle, and west roads; today the middle and west roads survive.The middle road has the gate hall, theater building, and main hall arranged from south to north.

The theater building faces south toward north, facing the main hall; the ground floor is the ceremonial gate and two corridors, the second floor is an open stage, with five bays of backstage arranged horizontally to the south.

On the south side of the northern main hall is a platform, which together with the five-bay wing buildings extending northward from both sides of the theater building forms a complete performance-viewing space.

The stage uses a hip-and-gable roof with high upturned eaves, with exquisite carvings on the architraves and hanging columns.

The domed caisson ceiling inside the stage is 3 meters in diameter and 2 meters high, composed of 632 wooden carved components joined by mortise and tenon to form spiral patterns—both magnificent and capable of concentrating and amplifying sound—hailed as the most exquisite surviving ancient stage in Jiangsu.

The west road has courtyards, ponds, flowers, and trees, elegant and worthy of viewing.

The Kunqu cultural relics exhibition in the north and the Kunqu stage model exhibition in the L-shaped west-side buildings are particularly精彩, displaying stage models from various places in Jiangsu—worth seeing.

21 甲辰巷塔
Jiachenxiang Brick Pagoda
宋
级别 Level
第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
地址 Address
姑苏区相门内干将东路甲辰巷
类型 Type
古塔
中文原文

甲辰巷塔位于苏州古城东北角，古时候这一带为手工纺织业集中地，现为普通民居和苏州大学校园。苏州旧有"七塔八幢九馒头"的俗谚，"七塔"指建在街头巷尾的七座小佛塔（顾震涛《吴门表隐》卷一"城中七塔"），如今仅有甲辰巷塔尚存。这座古塔造型优美，结构合理，构件精巧，具有很高的科学价值和艺术价值。

其始建年代未见记载，因在宋《平江图碑》中已有标示，故被认作宋塔；但从材料、结构和造型看，有学者倾向认为其建于唐末宋初，是研究唐宋间造塔风格和工艺演变的重要实例。

民国时期塔被围入民房中，塔刹和第五层有所损毁。1993年拆除部分民房辟出一处塔院，对各层进行修复加固，并重建了第五层和塔顶，制作安装了塔刹。

这是一座五层八角仿木楼阁式塔，通高6.82米，全用清水砖砌筑，不施粉彩。各层皆以菱角牙子和板檐砖相间叠涩挑出腰檐，上架平座，隐出斗栱、壶门和直棂窗。

各层相间开设四门四窗，上下层的门窗错开，结构合理。门、窗洞口上方用砖叠涩出阑额，角部各设一朵斗栱，上托由菱角牙子和板檐砖相间挑出的屋檐。顶部镇着塔刹和宝珠。

· · · · ·
English

The Jiachen Lane Pagoda is located at the northeast corner of Suzhou's old city.

In ancient times this area was a center of the hand-weaving industry; today it is ordinary residences and the Suzhou University campus.

Suzhou had the old saying "seven pagodas, eight pillars, nine steamed buns"—the "seven pagodas" referring to seven small Buddhist pagodas built at street corners and lane ends (Gu Zhentao, "Wumen Biaoyin" vol.

1, "Seven Pagodas in the City").Today only the Jiachen Lane Pagoda survives.

This ancient pagoda has an elegant form, reasonable structure, and exquisite components, with high scientific and artistic value.

Its founding date is unrecorded; because it is already marked on the Song-dynasty "Pingjiang Map Stele," it is regarded as a Song pagoda.

However, from its materials, structure, and form, some scholars lean toward believing it was built in the late Tang to early Song period—an important example for studying the evolution of pagoda style and craftsmanship between Tang and Song.

During the Republic period the pagoda was enclosed within private houses, with the finial and fifth story damaged.

In 1993, part of the houses were demolished to create a pagoda courtyard; each story was repaired and reinforced, the fifth story and top were rebuilt, and a finial was made and installed.

This is a five-story octagonal wooden-imitating pavilion-style pagoda, 6.82 meters high overall, built entirely with plain brick without painted decoration.

Each story uses alternating water-chestnut-tooth bricks and flat eave bricks in corbelled courses to project the waist eave, with a flat balcony above, showing brackets, pot-door openings, and lattice windows.

Each story alternately opens four doors and four windows, with doors and windows of adjacent stories staggered—structurally sound.

Above door and window openings, brick corbelling forms the architrave; at each corner is one bracket set, supporting the eave formed by alternating water-chestnut-tooth and flat eave bricks.

The top is crowned with a finial and precious pearl.

22 罗汉院双塔及正殿遗址
Double Pagodas and Site of Main Hall in Arhat Courtyard
北宋
级别 Level
第四批全国重点文物保护单位（1996年）
地址 Address
姑苏区定慧寺巷吴作人艺术馆附近
类型 Type
古塔/遗址
中文原文

苏州罗汉院始建于唐咸通年间，初名般若院，到五代吴越时改称罗汉院，后又改称万寿禅院。寺院西部不远处有一座子院，独立成一寺，现为"定慧寺"。北宋太平兴国七年（982年）王文罕兄弟捐建双塔，东西对立，一为舍利塔，一为功德舍利塔，形式、尺度基本相同，其后多次重修。

清咸丰十年（1860年）寺庙被毁，仅余双塔和正殿的石柱。1935年建筑学家刘敦桢与梁思成等一同考察，撰成《江苏吴县罗汉院双塔》一文，对其做了详细的研究和介绍。刘敦桢追溯了双塔的制度渊源。

《南齐书》提到明帝曾想建造一座十层塔，由于太高，"不可立，分为两刹，各五层"，这是最早提到双塔的文献。

唐代也有双塔的零星记载，日本奈良时代的药师寺、东大寺都有东、西两塔，可知从唐至五代、北宋期间有相当数量的双塔。罗汉院双塔建在正殿南侧，都是八角七层砖塔。

一层塔身四面皆有入口，其上各层洞口相互错开，既使各处塔身重量保持平衡，又能避免应力集中在洞口处造成破坏。塔身外部的出檐、平座以及隐出的柱、额、斗栱和直棂窗等，都模仿木塔；但塔身直径较小，从而形成瘦削玲珑的外观，与木塔大不相同。

罗汉院双塔是从唐塔向宋塔转型的典型例证，外观虽模仿木塔，但平座和檐端等局部作法、塔内方室与走道的分配方式等，仍遵循唐塔作法。

· · · · ·
English

Suzhou's Arhat Courtyard was founded during the Xiantong reign of the Tang, originally called Prajna Courtyard; in the Five Dynasties Wuyue period it was renamed Arhat Courtyard, later renamed Wanshou Chan Monastery.

Not far west of the temple is a sub-temple, independent as a separate temple, now "Dinghui Temple.

" In the 7th year of Taiping Xingguo of the Northern Song (982), the Wang Wenhan brothers donated to build the twin pagodas, standing east and west—one a relic pagoda, one a merit relic pagoda—with basically identical form and scale, subsequently repaired multiple times.

In the 10th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1860), the temple was destroyed, leaving only the twin pagodas and the stone columns of the main hall.

In 1935, architectural historians Liu Dunzhen and Liang Sicheng visited together and wrote the article "The Twin Pagodas of Arhat Courtyard in Wuxian, Jiangsu," providing detailed research and introduction.

Liu Dunzhen traced the institutional origins of twin pagodas.

The "Book of Southern Qi" mentions that Emperor Mingdi once wanted to build a ten-story pagoda, but because it was too tall, "it could not be erected, so it was divided into two pagodas, each five stories"—the earliest document mentioning twin pagodas.

There are also scattered records of twin pagodas in the Tang; the Yakushiji and Todaiji temples of Japan's Nara period both have east and west pagodas, indicating a considerable number of twin pagodas existed from Tang through Five Dynasties and Northern Song.

The Arhat Courtyard twin pagodas are built south of the main hall, both octagonal seven-story brick pagodas.

The first story has entrances on all four sides; the openings of upper stories are staggered, both balancing the weight of each part of the pagoda body and preventing stress concentration at openings from causing damage.

The external eaves, flat balconies, and recessed columns, architraves, brackets, and lattice windows all imitate wooden pagodas; but the pagoda body diameter is small, creating a slender and exquisite appearance quite different from wooden pagodas.

The Arhat Courtyard twin pagodas are a typical example of the transition from Tang to Song pagodas—though the exterior imitates wooden pagodas, local techniques such as flat balconies and eave ends, and the allocation of square chambers and corridors inside, still follow Tang pagoda methods.

建筑要点 / Key Features
唐咸通年间般若院；北宋太平兴国七年王文罕兄弟建；东西对立舍利塔功德塔；八角七层砖塔；刘敦桢梁思成考察；唐塔向宋塔转型典型例证
23 东吴大学旧址（苏州大学本部）
Site of Former Soochow University (Main Campus of Soochow University)
清—民国
级别 Level
第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
地址 Address
姑苏区干将东路333号
类型 Type
近代建筑/校园
中文原文

清同治十年（1871年）基督徒曹子实在苏州十全街筹办存养书院，清光绪五年（1879年）迁至古城东南角的天赐庄，改名博习书院，清光绪二十七年（1901年）美国基督教监理公会在此基础上筹建东吴大学堂，林乐知（1836—1907，Young J. Allen）任董事长、传教士孙乐文（1850—1911，David L. Anderson）任校长。

1952年东吴大学被合并为江苏师范学院，1982年更名苏州大学。

· · · · ·
English

In the 10th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1871), Christian Cao Zishi founded the Cunyang Academy at Shiquan Street in Suzhou.

In the 5th year of Guangxu (1879) it moved to Tiancizhuang at the southeast corner of the old city, renamed Boxi Academy.

In the 27th year of Guangxu (1901), the American Methodist Episcopal Church South established Soochow University Hall on this basis, with Young J.Allen (1836-1907) as chairman and missionary David L.

Anderson (1850-1911) as president.In 1952, Soochow University was merged into Jiangsu Normal College; in 1982 renamed Soochow University.

建筑要点 / Key Features
清同治十年存养书院；清光绪二十七年东吴大学堂；美国基督教监理公会；林乐知任董事长；孙乐文任校长；1952年合并为江苏师范学院
24 苏州织造署旧址（含瑞云峰）
Site of Suzhou Weaving Department (including Ruiyunfeng Stone)
清
级别 Level
第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
地址 Address
姑苏区带城桥下塘18号，苏州第十中学内
类型 Type
官署/园林
开放时间 Hours
参观要许可
中文原文

苏州丝织业发达，从元代起就设立制造局，供应宫廷所需。明代由太监兼理织造。

清顺治三年（1646年）在明末贵戚周奎故宅的基础上建织造局，清康熙十三年（1674年）改为织造衙门，也称织造署。《红楼梦》作者曹雪芹的先辈曹寅和李煦曾先后担任苏州织造。

清康熙二十三年（1684年）在署西辟建皇帝南巡驻跸的行宫。清咸丰十年（1860年）衙门与行宫全部毁于兵火，清同治十年（1871年）重建。

苏州织造署现存头门、仪门、西侧多祉轩、龙井、行宫遗址和清代历次修建碑等，是"江南三织造"（江宁、杭州、苏州）中保存遗迹最多的一处。

行宫遗址的主要遗存是"瑞云峰"，这尊太湖石是北宋"花石纲"遗物，明嘉靖年间归徐泰时，布置在东园（今留园），清乾隆四十五年（1780年）为迎乾隆南巡，官员将其移至织造署旁的行宫内。

如今石峰位于第十中学校园北侧的水池中央，周围配置峰石花木。石高约5米，以"透"为主，体态秀巧、宛转多姿，被誉为"妍巧甲于江南"，与豫园玉玲珑、杭州绉云峰并称为"江南三大奇石"。

· · · · ·
English

Suzhou's silk weaving industry was developed, and from the Yuan Dynasty a manufacturing bureau was established to supply the court.

In the Ming, eunuchs concurrently managed weaving.

In the 3rd year of Shunzhi of the Qing (1646), a weaving bureau was built on the former residence of late-Ming noble Zhou Kui; in the 13th year of Kangxi (1674) it was changed to a weaving yamen, also called the weaving department.

Cao Yin and Li Xu, ancestors of "Dream of the Red Chamber" author Cao Xueqin, successively served as Suzhou weaving commissioner.

In the 23rd year of Kangxi (1684), an imperial palace for the emperor's southern tours was built west of the department.

In the 10th year of Xianfeng (1860), both the yamen and palace were destroyed by war; rebuilt in the 10th year of Tongzhi (1871).

The Suzhou Weaving Department site today retains the gate hall, ceremonial gate, west-side Duozhi Xuan, Dragon Well, palace ruins, and steles from Qing-dynasty reconstructions—the most well-preserved among the "Three Jiangnan Weaving Departments" (Jiangning, Hangzhou, Suzhou).

The main relic of the palace site is "Ruiyunfeng" (Auspicious Cloud Peak), a Taihu rock that is a relic of the Northern Song "Flower and Stone Convoy.

" In the Jiajing reign of the Ming it passed to Xu Taishi, placed in the East Garden (today's Lingering Garden); in the 45th year of Qianlong (1780), to welcome the Qianlong Emperor's southern tour, officials moved it to the palace beside the weaving department.

Today the stone peak stands in the center of a pond north of the No.10 Middle School campus, surrounded by peak rocks, flowers, and trees.

About 5 meters high, it emphasizes "perforation," with an elegant and graceful form, hailed as "the most exquisite in Jiangnan," and together with Yulinglong in Yu Garden and Zhouyunfeng in Hangzhou is called one of the "Three Great Strange Stones of Jiangnan.

"

建筑要点 / Key Features
元代起设立制造局；曹雪芹祖父曹寅曾任苏州织造；清康熙二十三年建行宫；瑞云峰花石纲遗物；江南三大奇石；江南三织造
25 网师园
Wangshi Garden (Master of Nets Garden)
清
级别 Level
世界文化遗产，第二批全国重点文物保护单位（1982年）
地址 Address
姑苏区带城桥路阔家头巷11号
类型 Type
古典园林
门票 Ticket
30元
开放时间 Hours
旺季（4.16-10.30）7:30-17:30，淡季（10.31-4.15）7:30-17:00
中文原文

网师园在南宋时为史正志"万卷堂"藏书楼及花园，称"渔隐"，今看松读画轩前的古柏和池南"槃涧"石刻皆为当时遗物。

清乾隆年间光禄少卿宋宗元在此造园，因园北有"王思巷"，兼取"渔隐"古意，题名网师园，又称网师小筑，构濯缨水阁、小山丛桂轩等12景，今东南轿厅西首门洞上仍保留"网师小筑"门额。

乾隆末年园归富商瞿兆骥（号远村，1741—1808），重加改建，有月到风来亭、竹外一枝轩等8景。瞿氏父子慷慨好客，常在园中举行诗酒游宴，改筑后的网师园结构极佳，时人称誉"东南此绝胜，足冠阖闾城"，是网师园最兴盛的一段时期。同治年间清军从太平军手中收复苏州，因长洲县署已毁，便将县署设在网师园内。

清光绪二年（1876年）园归江苏按察使李鸿裔，填平园东部分水面，插入今东路的住宅，对园林格局造成较大破坏；同时又改园名为"苏邻园"，以邻近苏舜钦沧浪亭为豪，自降身价。此后网师园多次易主，但主景基本未变。1932年画家张善孖、张大千兄弟寓居园内，在殿春簃养乳虎作画，传为佳话。

1980年美国纽约大都会博物馆在馆内仿园中殿春簃建"明轩"庭园，使网师园名扬海外。1982年此园被定为全国重点文物保护单位，1997年列入世界文化遗产名录。

今园林入口位于东南，入门依次有轿厅、万卷堂和撷秀楼三进建筑，皆为清光绪年间李鸿裔所添。由轿厅西北的角门可进入小山丛桂轩前院，院西为蹈和馆，由于东路住宅的插入，这部分格局凌乱，较为尴尬。小山丛桂轩为鸳鸯厅，轩前置石栽树，略成小筑；轩后堆筑黄石假山，掩映北部主景。

绕过黄石假山为网师园的精华部分，被陈从周誉为"静观型"园林的典范。

网师园主景建于清乾隆年间，不及沧浪亭、狮子林、拙政园古老；面积只有10亩，也比拙政园、留园小，但却凭其精雅的池园布置跻身名园之列，予人独特的艺术享受。

园林学家陈从周将"静观为主之网师园，动观为主之拙政园，苍古之沧浪亭，华瞻之留园"，合称为"苏州四大名园"。居中是一座半亩左右的水池，略呈方形，东南、西北两角伸出水湾，上架小桥，使水面有聚有分。沿池一周，景致皆精雅可爱。池东以粉墙为底，前叠假山、建方亭、植花木，疏朗入画。

池东亭北经射鸭廊通向北岸的竹外一枝轩，临池处设美人靠，可供游人静坐观鱼；轩内圆洞门透出北侧庭院深深。轩东看松读画轩稍稍退后，前部掩以山石、古柏、小桥，使池面不显逼仄。池西爬山廊起伏有致，偏北点缀月到风来亭，最适合秋夜凭栏赏月。南岸濯缨水阁悬挑水上，为夏日纳凉佳处，向北可赏三面风景。阁东的黄石假山增添了池周的自然风味，山间蹬道盘旋，又可涉步成趣。

由于水池不大，四周景致较为密集，可以互赏互借，形成各种观赏角度，令人应接不暇。池西爬山廊北侧有门通向西侧庭院，北部为书房殿春簃，其南庭院以山为主，三面叠石，在西南角凿涵碧泉，旁建冷泉亭；与中部开阔的池景形成对比。园林东北有五峰书屋和梯云室等，自成一区，幽静闲适。

· · · · ·
English

The Wangshi Garden (Master of Nets Garden) was, in the Southern Song, the "Wanjuan Tang" (Ten Thousand Volumes Hall) library and garden of Shi Zhengzhi, called "Yuyin" (Fishing Hermitage).

Today the ancient cypress in front of the Kansong Duhua Xuan and the "Panjian" rock carving south of the pond are relics from that time.

During the Qianlong reign of the Qing, Guanglu Junior Vice Minister Song Zongyuan built a garden here; because north of the garden was "Wangsi Lane," and taking the ancient meaning of "fishing hermitage," he named it Wangshi Yuan (Master of Nets Garden), also called Wangshi Xiaozhu, constructing 12 scenes including the Zhuoying Water Pavilion and Xiaoshan Conggui Xuan.

Today the gate lintel "Wangshi Xiaozhu" is still preserved above the doorway at the west end of the southeast sedan hall.

In the late Qianlong period the garden passed to wealthy merchant Qu Zhaoji (hao Yuancun, 1741-1808), who heavily rebuilt it, adding 8 scenes including the Yuedao Fenglai Pavilion and Zhuyi Yizhi Xuan.

The Qu father and son were generous and hospitable, often holding poetry and wine gatherings in the garden.

After reconstruction, the Wangshi Garden had an excellent structure, praised by contemporaries as "the most exquisite in the southeast, crowning Helü City"—the most prosperous period of the Wangshi Garden.

During the Tongzhi period, after Qing forces recaptured Suzhou from the Taiping, because the Changzhou County yamen had been destroyed, the county yamen was set up in the Wangshi Garden.

In the 2nd year of Guangxu (1876), the garden passed to Li Hongyi, Jiangsu Surveillance Commissioner, who filled in part of the water surface east of the garden and inserted today's east-road residence, causing considerable damage to the garden's layout; he also renamed it "Sulin Garden," taking pride in its proximity to Su Shunqin's Surging Wave Pavilion, thus devaluing itself.

Thereafter the Wangshi Garden changed hands many times, but the main scenery remained basically unchanged.

In 1932, painter brothers Zhang Shanzi and Zhang Daqian lived in the garden, raising tiger cubs in the Dianchun Yi for painting—a celebrated story.

In 1980, the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York built the "Ming Xuan" courtyard modeled on the Dianchun Yi inside the museum, making the Wangshi Garden famous overseas.

In 1982 the garden was designated a National Key Cultural Heritage Site; in 1997 inscribed on the World Cultural Heritage List.

Today the garden entrance is at the southeast; entering, there are three bays of buildings: sedan hall, Wanjuan Tang, and Xiexiu Lou—all added by Li Hongyi during the Guangxu period.

From the corner gate northwest of the sedan hall, one can enter the front courtyard of Xiaoshan Conggui Xuan; west of the courtyard is the Daohe Guan.

Due to the insertion of the east-road residence, this part's layout is messy and awkward.

Xiaoshan Conggui Xuan is a mandarin-duck hall, with rocks piled and trees planted in front, forming a small composition; behind the hall a yellow-stone rockery is piled, screening the northern main scenery.

Passing around the yellow-stone rockery is the essence of the Wangshi Garden, hailed by Chen Congzhou as a model of the "contemplative" garden type.

The main scenery of the Wangshi Garden was built during the Qianlong reign, not as old as the Surging Wave Pavilion, Lion Grove, or Humble Administrator's Garden; with an area of only 10 mu, smaller than the Humble Administrator's Garden and Lingering Garden, yet it ranks among famous gardens by virtue of its exquisite pond-garden arrangement, offering a unique artistic experience.

Garden scholar Chen Congzhou combined "the contemplative Wangshi Garden, the dynamic Humble Administrator's Garden, the ancient Surging Wave Pavilion, and the magnificent Lingering Garden" as the "Four Great Gardens of Suzhou.

" In the center is a pond of about half a mu, roughly square, with water inlets extending from the southeast and northwest corners, spanned by small bridges, giving the water surface both gathering and division.

Around the pond, the scenery is all exquisite and lovely.East of the pond, with a white wall as backdrop, rockeries are piled, square pavilions built, and flowers/trees planted—sparse and picturesque.

North of the east pavilion, via the Sheya Corridor, leads to the Zhuyi Yizhi Xuan on the north bank; a beauty's rest (bench with backrest) is set by the pond for visitors to sit quietly and watch fish; the round-arched door inside the studio reveals the deep courtyard to the north.

East of the studio, the Kansong Duhua Xuan is slightly set back, with rocks, ancient cypresses, and small bridges in front, preventing the pond from feeling cramped.

West of the pond, the climbing corridor rises and falls gracefully, with the Yuedao Fenglai Pavilion slightly north—ideal for leaning on the railing and admiring the moon on autumn nights.

On the south bank, the Zhuoying Water Pavilion cantilevers over the water, an excellent place for summer cooling, offering views of scenery on three sides to the north.

The yellow-stone rockery east of the pavilion adds natural flavor around the pond, with winding mountain paths and stepping stones for amusement.

Because the pond is small and the surrounding scenery is dense, they can be mutually admired and borrowed, forming various viewing angles that keep visitors engaged.

North of the west climbing corridor, a door leads to the west courtyard; the north part is the study Dianchun Yi, with its south courtyard dominated by mountains, rocks piled on three sides, the Hanbi Spring dug at the southwest corner with the Lengquan Pavilion beside it—contrasting with the open pond scenery of the center.

Northeast of the garden are the Wufeng Book Room and Tiyun Room, forming their own quiet and leisurely zone.

26 天香小筑
Tianxiang Xiaozhu Garden Villa
1935年
级别 Level
第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
地址 Address
姑苏区人民路80号，苏州图书馆内
类型 Type
近代园林/别墅
中文原文

天香小筑是吴县洞庭东山人席启荪所筑。席启荪在东山建有启园，1935年他在上海任钱庄经理时到苏州建造了这座花园别墅。今为苏州图书馆古文献阅览室附属花园，免费开放。天香小筑包括西部住宅和东部园林两部分。住宅南部的鸳鸯厅和东西厢楼构成品字形，然后一起与北部的主楼构成"回"字形。建筑皆为二层，采用硬山绿琉璃顶，为中西合璧风格。

东部园林呈横长方形，北部开凿水池，南岸堆筑假山，以土为主，山上设六角亭，周围点缀湖石，因形似各种动物而被称作"百兽园"。池北贯以长廊，设有亭榭，可供临池赏景。此园的赏石品位不高，但山水格局精雅，花木扶疏，不失为近代园林的佳作。

· · · · ·
English

Tianxiang Xiaozhu was built by Xi Qisun, a native of Dongting Dongshan in Wu County.

Xi Qisun built the Qi Garden in Dongshan; in 1935, while working as a bank manager in Shanghai, he came to Suzhou and built this garden villa.

Today it is the附属 garden of the ancient literature reading room of Suzhou Library, open free of charge.Tianxiang Xiaozhu includes two parts: a western residence and an eastern garden.

The mandarin-duck hall south of the residence and the east-west wing buildings form a pin (品) shape, then together with the northern main building form a hui (回) shape.

All buildings are two stories, with hard-gable green glazed tile roofs—a Chinese-Western fusion style.

The eastern garden is horizontally rectangular, with a pond dug in the north and a rockery piled on the south bank, mainly earth, with a hexagonal pavilion on the hill and Taihu rocks dotted around—called the "Hundred Beasts Garden" because they resemble various animals.

A long corridor runs north of the pond, with pavilions for admiring scenery by the water.

The garden's rock-appreciation taste is not high, but its mountain-water layout is refined, with lush flowers and trees—a fine example of a modern garden.

27 畅园
Smooth Garden (Chang Garden)
清
级别 Level
第七批江苏省保（2011年）
地址 Address
庙堂巷22号
类型 Type
古典园林
开放时间 Hours
参观需经过批准
中文原文

畅园是清末潘氏的宅第附园，位于住宅东侧，约1亩。入园门为桂花厅，因后院曾植桂树、梧桐而得名。院北为桐华书屋，宽三间，中为书房，梢间做成周围廊，与两侧游廊相接。书屋北面即为园林主景。畅园以水池为中心，北侧池岸方整，与建筑结合紧密；南侧曲折自由，饶自然之趣。

主厅留云山房位于池北，前方有宽敞的平台，向南对着悠长的水面，远处截以折桥增添层次，对岸堆叠湖石假山，点缀六角亭，视野开阔、景致丰富，在狭小庭园中营造出"舒畅"之意，与园名呼应。平台东侧是一座较大的四角亭，向南经傍水长廊通向憩间亭，继而通向南侧的延辉成趣六角亭；池西则有涤我尘襟船厅和四角亭，或紧贴或悬挑水面，与东岸的廊、亭俯仰相得。

池南假山体量不大，内构石洞，上建待月亭，可从洞中登到亭内，或由爬山廊逐级攀登，廊、亭增大了山的体量，成为留云山房的主要对景。沿池岸栽有白皮松、紫藤、石榴和木樨等花木。园池虽小却布置合宜，要素紧凑而有疏朗之致。

2013年在北京建成的中国园林博物馆特意对苏州畅园进行全盘复制，作为江南园林的代表作向观众展示。

· · · · ·
English

Chang Garden (Smooth Garden) was the attached garden of the Pan family residence in the late Qing, located east of the residence, about 1 mu.

Entering the garden gate is the Guihua Hall (Osmanthus Hall), named for the osmanthus and paulownia trees once planted in the rear courtyard.

North of the courtyard is the Tonghua Book Room, three bays wide, with the center as the study and the end bays made into surrounding corridors connecting to the side corridors.

North of the book room is the garden's main scenery.

Chang Garden centers on a pond, with the north bank square and tightly integrated with buildings; the south bank is winding and free, full of natural charm.

The main hall Liuyun Shanfang (Remaining Cloud Mountain Room) is north of the pond, with a spacious platform in front facing the long water surface to the south; a zigzag bridge in the distance adds layers, and Taihu rockeries are piled on the opposite bank with a hexagonal pavilion—open views and rich scenery, creating a sense of "smoothness" in the small courtyard, echoing the garden's name.

East of the platform is a larger four-corner pavilion, leading south via a waterside long corridor to the Qijian Pavilion, then to the Yanhui Chengqu hexagonal pavilion on the south side; west of the pond are the Diwo Chenjin boat hall and four-corner pavilion, either close to or cantilevering over the water, complementing the east bank's corridors and pavilions.

The rockery south of the pond is not large, with a stone cave inside and the Daiyue (Waiting for Moon) Pavilion on top—one can climb from the cave into the pavilion, or ascend step by step via the climbing corridor; the corridor and pavilion increase the mountain's volume, becoming the main opposite scene for Liuyun Shanfang.

Along the pond bank are planted lacebark pine, wisteria, pomegranate, and osmanthus.Though the pond is small, the arrangement is appropriate, with elements compact yet spacious.

In 2013, the Chinese Garden Museum built in Beijing specifically made a full replica of Suzhou's Chang Garden, displaying it as a representative work of Jiangnan gardens.

28 沧浪亭
Canglang Pavilion (Surging Wave Pavilion)
元—清
级别 Level
世界文化遗产，第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
地址 Address
姑苏区人民路沧浪亭街3号
类型 Type
古典园林
门票 Ticket
淡季15元，旺季20元
开放时间 Hours
7:30-17:30
中文原文

沧浪亭在苏州现存园林中始建时间最早。五代时曾为吴越王近戚孙承祐的池馆，北宋庆历五年（1045年）政治家、文学家苏舜卿（字子美，1008—1048）因支持范仲淹的庆历革新，被守旧派借故弹劾，削籍为民。

他流落到苏州后，用四万钱买下孙氏旧园，在水边筑亭，取《楚辞·渔夫》"沧浪之水清兮，可以濯吾缨；沧浪之水浊兮，可以濯吾足"，题名沧浪亭，寄托不平之意。此地山环水绕、颇有野趣，苏舜钦作《沧浪亭记》寄给欧阳修求副对联，欧阳修打趣曰："清风明月本无价，可惜只卖四万钱。

"苏舜卿收下上句，取自己《过苏州》诗"绿杨白鹭俱自得，近水远山皆有情"的下句，合成"清风明月本无价，近水远山皆有情"，此联今题在园内山顶沧浪亭的石柱上。苏舜卿卒后园归他姓，南宋时属抗金名将韩世忠，元代废为僧舍，从此不再属于私家。

清康熙三十五年（1696年）江苏巡抚宋荦重修沧浪亭，画家王翚为绘《沧浪亭图》，从中可知宋荦将原来临水的沧浪亭移至山顶，在园北建造折桥，桥东临水有两座轩屋，即今面水轩与观鱼处的前身。作为一座公共园林，此园以水为界，不设围墙，任人隔水纵赏。

康熙、乾隆南巡时皆到园中游览题诗，今园北假山西侧为康熙御碑亭，东侧为乾隆御碑亭。清道光七年（1827年）官方在园内建五百名贤祠，刻石供奉吴中名士画像500幅，沧浪亭成为一座祠庙园林。

太平天国时期园中建筑全部被毁，清同治十二年（1873年）重修，并在山南建明道堂，形成今日格局。2000年沧浪亭被列入世界文化遗产名录。沧浪亭入口位于北侧，有长桥凌跨水上，入门东西横亘一座大型土山，中有山路分为东、西两段。

东段修筑较早，驳砌黄石，自然古朴；西段后期叠置湖石，略嫌芜杂。向东有多条路径可登至山顶沧浪亭，眺览四周景致；西侧湖山下砌石洞，上有蹬道，体现了清中期喜好登山入穴的趣味，山南有座小池，是园内仅有的水景，成为点睛之笔。

围绕大假山四周有一整圈游廊，串起大门、西御碑亭、清香馆、明道堂、东御碑亭、观鱼处和面水轩，廊壁漏窗造型各异，上百处无一复廊，成为此园一大特色。

游廊最精彩的是山北复廊，廊子中央立有一道墙壁，随廊蜿蜒转折，壁上开各色漏窗，廊内为假山，廊外为池水，山水若隐若现，相映相借，无论走在园内、园外都别具风味。园林南部为祠堂建筑区，有五百名贤祠和明道堂两路庭院，主要用于讲学观戏、仰止先贤，与北部山林关系较弱。最南端为看山楼，下砌印心石屋，为别出心裁之作。

· · · · ·
English

The Canglang Pavilion (Surging Wave Pavilion) has the earliest founding date among Suzhou's surviving gardens.

In the Five Dynasties it was the pond villa of Sun Chengyou, a close relative of the Wuyue king.

In the 5th year of Qingli of the Northern Song (1045), statesman and writer Su Shunqin (style name Zimei, 1008-1048), because he supported Fan Zhongyan's Qingli reforms, was impeached on pretext by conservatives and dismissed from office.

After drifting to Suzhou, he bought the old Sun family garden for 40,000 coins and built a pavilion by the water, taking from the "Chu Ci·Fisherman": "When the Canglang waters are clear, I can wash my hatstrings; when the Canglang waters are muddy, I can wash my feet"—naming it Canglang Pavilion, expressing his indignation.

This place, surrounded by mountains and water with much wild charm, inspired Su Shunqin to write the "Record of Canglang Pavilion" and send it to Ouyang Xiu requesting a couplet.

Ouyang Xiu joked: "Clear wind and bright moon are originally priceless, pity they were sold for only 40,000 coins.

" Su Shunqin accepted the first line and took the second line from his own poem "Passing Suzhou": "Green willows and white egrets are both content, nearby water and distant mountains are both affectionate"—forming the couplet "Clear wind and bright moon are originally priceless; nearby water and distant mountains are both affectionate," today inscribed on the stone pillars of the Canglang Pavilion at the mountaintop.

After Su Shunqin's death the garden passed to other families; in the Southern Song it belonged to anti-Jin general Han Shizhong; in the Yuan it was abandoned and became a monk's quarters, henceforth no longer private.

In the 35th year of Kangxi of the Qing (1696), Jiangsu Governor Song Luo rebuilt the Canglang Pavilion; painter Wang Hui painted the "Canglang Pavilion Map," from which we know Song Luo moved the originally waterside Canglang Pavilion to the mountaintop, built a zigzag bridge north of the garden, and two waterside studios east of the bridge—the predecessors of today's Mianshui Xuan and Guanyu Chu.

As a public garden, this garden uses water as its boundary, with no enclosing wall, allowing anyone to admire it across the water.

During the Kangxi and Qianlong southern tours, both emperors visited and inscribed poems in the garden; today west of the north rockery is the Kangxi Imperial Stele Pavilion, and east is the Qianlong Imperial Stele Pavilion.

In the 7th year of Daoguang (1827), the authorities built the Five Hundred Worthies Shrine in the garden, carving 500 portraits of famous Wu scholars on stone for worship—the Canglang Pavilion became a shrine garden.

During the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom period all garden buildings were destroyed; rebuilt in the 12th year of Tongzhi (1873), with the Mingdao Hall built south of the mountain, forming today's layout.

In 2000 the Canglang Pavilion was inscribed on the World Cultural Heritage List.The Canglang Pavilion entrance is on the north side, with a long bridge spanning the water.

Entering, a large earth mountain runs east-west, with a mountain path divided into east and west sections.

The east section was built earlier, faced with yellow stone, natural and simple; the west section was later piled with Taihu rocks, slightly cluttered.

Eastward, multiple paths lead to the Canglang Pavilion at the mountaintop for viewing surrounding scenery; west of the Taihu mountain, a stone cave is built below with climbing paths above—reflecting the mid-Qing taste for climbing mountains and entering caves.

South of the mountain is a small pond, the only water scenery in the garden, a finishing touch.

Around the large rockery runs a complete circle of corridors, connecting the gate, west imperial stele pavilion, Qingxiang Guan, Mingdao Hall, east imperial stele pavilion, Guanyu Chu, and Mianshui Xuan.

The lattice windows on the corridor walls have varied designs, over a hundred with no duplicates—a major feature of this garden.

The most精彩 part of the corridor is the double corridor north of the mountain: a wall stands in the center of the corridor, winding along with it, with various lattice windows opened on the wall; inside the corridor is the rockery, outside is the pond water—mountains and water half-hidden, mutually complementing and borrowed, offering unique flavor whether walking inside or outside the garden.

The southern part of the garden is the shrine building area, with the Five Hundred Worthies Shrine and Mingdao Hall forming two courtyard routes, mainly used for lectures, opera viewing, and venerating former worthies, with weaker connection to the northern mountain forest.

At the southernmost end is the Kanshan Lou (Viewing Mountain Tower), with the Yinxin Stone House built below—a creative work.

建筑要点 / Key Features
五代吴越孙承祐池馆；北宋庆历五年苏舜钦；苏州现存园林中始建最早；苏舜钦《沧浪亭记》；清风明月本无价近水远山皆有情；复廊
29 苏州文庙及宋代石刻
Temple of Confucius in Suzhou and Stone Sculptures of Song Dynasty
南宋、明
级别 Level
第一批全国重点文物保护单位（1961年）
地址 Address
姑苏区人民路613号
类型 Type
文庙/石刻
门票 Ticket
8:30-16:00（周一闭馆），免费
中文原文

北宋景祐二年（1035年）范仲淹在吴越钱氏南园旧址上建造庙学，首创"左庙右学"的格局，将祭孔的文庙和授业的学宫合为一体，并作为定制推向全国，因此有"天下有学自吴郡始"之说。

苏州文庙在后世多次重建，清咸丰十年（1860年）遭遇战火，同治年间修复。现存建筑主要为明代所建，清代重修。

东庙有戟门、棂星门、大成殿和崇圣祠等，西学有泮池、七星池和明伦堂等。今为苏州碑刻博物馆，藏有各类碑石1000多块，较重要的有平江图碑、天文图碑、地理图碑和帝王绍运图碑等宋代石刻。

庙内主体建筑是大成殿，重建于明成化十年（1474年），以后虽经重修，仍保持明代风格。殿宽七间，坐落在台基上，采用重檐庑殿顶，上覆黄色琉璃瓦，古朴庄重。殿内展出苏州碑刻拓片，分为人物、历史、古迹和书法4类。

人物碑有孔子及七十二弟子像、白居易像、苏东坡像、海瑞像、文徵明像、顾炎武像和章太炎像等名士像，古迹碑有《沧浪亭图》和《瑞光塔图》等名胜，书法则有晋陆机《平复帖》、三苏手迹、祝允明草书和文徵明行草等珍品。

· · · · ·
English

In the 2nd year of Jingyou of the Northern Song (1035), Fan Zhongyan built a temple-school on the former site of the Wuyue Qian family's South Garden, pioneering the "temple on the left, school on the right" layout, integrating the Confucian Temple for sacrificing to Confucius and the school palace for teaching, and promoting it as a standard nationwide—hence the saying "the world's schools began in Wu Commandery.

" Suzhou's Confucian Temple was rebuilt many times in later generations; in the 10th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1860) it suffered war damage and was repaired during the Tongzhi period.

The surviving buildings are mainly Ming-dynasty constructions, repaired in the Qing.

The east temple has the Halberd Gate, Lingxing Gate, Dacheng Hall, and Chongsheng Shrine; the west school has the Pan Pond, Seven-Star Pond, and Minglun Hall.

Today it is the Suzhou Stele Carving Museum, housing over 1,000 various steles, with important Song-dynasty stone carvings including the Pingjiang Map Stele, Astronomical Map Stele, Geographical Map Stele, and Emperor's Succession Map Stele.

The main building in the temple is the Dacheng Hall, rebuilt in the 10th year of Chenghua of the Ming (1474); although later repaired, it retains Ming style.

The hall is seven bays wide, sitting on a platform, with a double-eave hip roof covered in yellow glazed tiles—simple and solemn.

Inside the hall, Suzhou stele rubbings are exhibited in four categories: figures, history, ancient sites, and calligraphy.

Figure steles include portraits of Confucius and his seventy-two disciples, Bai Juyi, Su Dongpo, Hai Rui, Wen Zhengming, Gu Yanwu, and Zhang Taiyan; ancient-site steles include famous places such as the "Canglang Pavilion Map" and "Ruiguang Pagoda Map"; calligraphy includes treasures such as Jin-dynasty Lu Ji's "Pingfu Letter," the Three Sus' handwriting, Zhu Yunming's cursive script, and Wen Zhengming's running-cursive script.

建筑要点 / Key Features
北宋景祐二年范仲淹建；首创左庙右学格局；天下有学自吴郡始；大成殿明成化十年重建；苏州碑刻博物馆；平江图碑天文图碑地理图碑帝王绍运图碑
30 开元寺无梁殿
Beamless Hall of Kaiyuan Temple
明
级别 Level
第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
地址 Address
姑苏区盘门内东大街11号万丽花园小区内
类型 Type
佛寺/无梁殿
中文原文

开元寺初名通玄寺，三国东吴时孙权为乳母陈氏所建，唐开元二十六年（738年）改称开元寺，唐大顺二年（891年）毁于战火。

五代后唐同光三年（925年），吴越钱氏将寺庙迁至盘门内现址重建。清咸丰十年（1860年）又毁于兵火，现仅存明代无梁殿一座。

无梁殿建于明万历四十六年（1618年），坐北朝南，高两层，采用砖券技术建造。原为开元寺藏经阁，楼上藏经，楼下供无量寿佛，也称无量殿，民间则因其不用木构梁柱，俗称无梁殿。

大殿宽七间，坐落在石雕须弥座上，南北立面相同，上下各辟五座拱门，门旁砌半圆形倚柱。柱端装饰小垂莲柱，两侧辅以砖雕额枋、斗栱和雀替等仿木构件。其上有砖斗栱，一层较密，柱间用两攒平身科；二层较疏，柱间仅一攒。

一层腰檐和二层殿顶覆盖黄、绿相间的琉璃瓦，与清水砖墙相映成趣。南面二层明间拱门上方嵌汉白玉横额，题"敕赐藏经阁"，北面二层题"显密法藏"；南面底层中央三间皆有横额，分别题"修多罗""毗奈耶"和"阿比昙"，对应佛典三藏总目"经""律"和"论"梵文的音译。

大殿内部二层明间顶部有八角形砖藻井，四角以斗栱承托，采用叠涩手法收敛至中央，为明代砖构精品。

明代有多座无梁殿存世，开元寺无梁殿规模不算大，但以结构和细部取胜。底层的砖雕须弥座，檐下的垂莲柱、雀替、额枋和斗栱，以及殿顶的琉璃游龙脊饰和戗角四天王立像等，皆工巧细致。

整座殿阁宏伟高大而有玲珑之致，反映了明代苏州高超的建筑技艺。

· · · · ·
English

Kaiyuan Temple was originally called Tongxuan Temple, built by Sun Quan of the Three Kingdoms Eastern Wu for his wet nurse Lady Chen.

In the 26th year of Kaiyuan of the Tang (738) it was renamed Kaiyuan Temple; in the 2nd year of Dashun (891) it was destroyed by war.

In the 3rd year of Tongguang of the Later Tang (925), the Wuyue Qian family moved and rebuilt the temple at the present site inside Panmen.

In the 10th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1860) it was again destroyed by war; today only the Ming-dynasty Beamless Hall survives.

The Beamless Hall was built in the 46th year of Wanli of the Ming (1618), facing south, two stories high, built using brick arch technology.

Originally the scripture depository of Kaiyuan Temple—scriptures stored upstairs, the Buddha of Infinite Life enshrined downstairs—also called the Wuliang (Infinite Life) Hall; commonly called the Beamless Hall by the people because it uses no wooden beams or columns.

The main hall is seven bays wide, sitting on a carved stone Sumeru pedestal, with identical north and south facades, each having five arched doorways on both upper and lower levels, with semicircular engaged pillars beside the doors.

The pillar ends are decorated with small hanging lotus columns, flanked by brick-carved architraves, brackets, and spandrels imitating wooden components.

Above are brick brackets: the first story is denser, with two sets of intermediate brackets between columns; the second story is sparser, with only one set between columns.

The first-story waist eave and second-story hall roof are covered with alternating yellow and green glazed tiles, contrasting delightfully with the plain brick walls.

Above the central bay archway on the second story south face is a white marble horizontal plaque inscribed "Imperially Bestowed Scripture Depository"; the north second story is inscribed "Exoteric and Esoteric Dharma Storehouse.

" The central three bays of the south ground floor each have horizontal plaques inscribed "Xiuduoluo," "Pinalaiye," and "Abitan"—the Sanskrit transliterations corresponding to the three baskets of Buddhist scriptures: sutra, vinaya, and abhidharma.

Inside the hall, the top of the central bay on the second story has an octagonal brick caisson ceiling, supported at the four corners by brackets, using corbelling to converge to the center—a Ming-dynasty brick-construction masterpiece.

Several beamless halls survive from the Ming Dynasty; the Kaiyuan Temple Beamless Hall is not large in scale but excels in structure and detail.

The brick-carved Sumeru pedestal at the base, the hanging lotus columns, spandrels, architraves, and brackets under the eaves, and the glazed dragon ridge ornaments and the four heavenly kings standing at the upturned corners of the roof are all exquisitely crafted.

The entire hall is grand and tall yet delicate, reflecting the superb architectural craftsmanship of Ming-dynasty Suzhou.

建筑要点 / Key Features
三国东吴孙权为乳母陈氏建通玄寺；唐开元二十六年改称开元寺；明万历四十六年建无梁殿；砖券技术；原藏经阁；八角形砖藻井
31 盘门景区
Panmen Scenic Area
北宋—清
级别 Level
瑞光寺塔为第三批国保（1988年），盘门为第六批国保（2006年），吴门桥为省保（2002年）
地址 Address
姑苏区东大街49号
类型 Type
古城门/古塔/古桥
门票 Ticket
40元
开放时间 Hours
7:30-17:30
中文原文

景区包括水陆城门、瑞光寺塔和吴门桥等遗迹，合称"盘门三景"，曾经登上中国与新加坡联合发行的邮票。1. 瑞光寺塔：在盘门景区东门外可望见瑞光寺塔。瑞光寺旧称普济禅院，始建于三国东吴赤乌四年（241年），赤乌十年（247年）孙权为报答母恩建造13层舍利塔。

北宋年间寺改称瑞光禅院，北宋景德元年至天圣八年（1004—1030）重建寺、塔。清咸丰十年（1860年）寺庙毁于战火，仅存此塔。

瑞光寺塔是一座八角七层塔，内部为砖砌塔身，由外壁、回廊和塔心组成；外壁用砖木斗栱挑出木构的腰檐和平座，形成楼阁式。塔总高53.6米，自下而上逐层收缩，轮廓微成曲线，挺拔古朴。

塔身五层以下为宋代原构，其上为后代重建，其中第三层为全塔中心，1978年曾在该层顶部发现一批五代和北宋初期的珍贵文物，从而推断出建塔年代。

2. 盘门：公元前514年伍子胥奉吴王之命建造阖闾大城，奠定苏州古城的基本格局。两千多年来苏州虽历尽沧桑，但城址、范围、格局甚至城门名称都变化不大，足见当时选址、建城之成功。如今苏州仍保存下胥门、阊门及部分城墙，以位于西南角的盘门水陆两门最为完整，为国内仅存。盘门是伍子胥当年所辟大城门之一，古称蟠门。

现存城门修筑于元至正十一年（1351年），元末张士诚增建瓮城。水门位于内城河通向城外运河的交接点上，由内、外两重城门组成。外门砌石拱券，前后分置闸门、木门各两道。闸门可以上下升降，水下则有木栅，防止敌人潜水进入。内门由三道石拱券并列而成，形成三组门洞。

在前组和中组之间有水闸，其左壁开便门，内有石阶直通城门顶部。陆门在水门北侧，也有两重，内外城墙之间是接近方形的瓮城。外城门位于瓮城东北，由三道石拱券并列而成，曾置闸门和木门各一道。内城门位于西南，外面砖砌门额上刻"盘门"二字，门洞内也由三道拱券构成，门前拱顶上方开"品"字孔，可向内注水抵御火攻。

水门、陆门顶部城墙相通，置女儿墙、雉堞、射孔，外部砌马面。水、陆两门布置周密，防卫森严，体现了古代高超的筑城技术和防御系统。

3. 吴门桥：出盘门水门或在城门上可望见吴门桥，横跨在古运河（护城河）上，始建于北宋元丰七年（1084年），清同治十一年（1872年）重建，是江苏现存最高的单孔石拱桥，2002年列为省保单位。

此桥也是在景区外欣赏盘门水门的最佳位置。

· · · · ·
English

The scenic area includes the water-land city gate, Ruiguang Temple Pagoda, and Wumen Bridge—collectively called the "Three Scenes of Panmen," which once appeared on a joint stamp issued by China and Singapore.

1.Ruiguang Temple Pagoda: Visible outside the east gate of the Panmen Scenic Area.

Ruiguang Temple was formerly called Puji Chan Monastery, founded in the 4th year of Chiwu of the Three Kingdoms Eastern Wu (241); in the 10th year of Chiwu (247), Sun Quan built a 13-story relic pagoda to repay his mother's kindness.

During the Northern Song, the temple was renamed Ruiguang Chan Monastery; from the 1st year of Jingde to the 8th year of Tiansheng (1004-1030), the temple and pagoda were rebuilt.

In the 10th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1860), the temple was destroyed by war, leaving only this pagoda.

The Ruiguang Temple Pagoda is an octagonal seven-story pagoda, with a brick body internally composed of outer wall, corridor, and central pillar; the outer wall uses brick-wood brackets to project wooden waist eaves and flat balconies, forming a pavilion style.

The pagoda is 53.6 meters high overall, tapering story by story from bottom to top, with a slightly curved silhouette—tall, straight, and simple.

The body below the fifth story is original Song construction; above was rebuilt by later generations.

The third story is the center of the whole pagoda; in 1978, a batch of precious cultural relics from the Five Dynasties and early Northern Song was discovered at the top of this story, from which the construction date was inferred.

2.Panmen Gate: In 514 BC, Wu Zixu, by order of the King of Wu, built the Great City of Helü, establishing the basic layout of Suzhou's old city.

Over two thousand years, though Suzhou has experienced many vicissitudes, the city site, scope, layout, and even gate names have changed little—testifying to the success of the original site selection and city construction.

Today Suzhou still preserves the Xumen Gate, Changmen Gate, and parts of the city wall; the Panmen water and land gates at the southwest corner are the most complete, the only surviving example in China.

Panmen was one of the eight great gates opened by Wu Zixu, anciently called Panmen (Coiled Gate).

The existing gate was built in the 11th year of Zhizheng of the Yuan (1351); at the end of the Yuan, Zhang Shicheng added the barbican.

The water gate is at the junction where the inner city moat leads to the canal outside the city, composed of inner and outer double gates.

The outer gate is a stone arch, with two sets each of sluice gates and wooden gates front and back.

The sluice gates can be raised and lowered; underwater there are wooden gratings to prevent enemies from diving in.

The inner gate consists of three parallel stone arches, forming three groups of doorways.

Between the front and middle groups is a water sluice, with a side door on its left wall and stone steps leading directly to the top of the gate.

The land gate is north of the water gate, also double, with a nearly square barbican between the inner and outer walls.

The outer gate is at the northeast of the barbican, composed of three parallel stone arches, once fitted with one sluice gate and one wooden gate.

The inner gate is at the southwest, with a brick plaque outside inscribed "Panmen"; the doorway is also composed of three arches, with a "pin" (品)-shaped hole above the front arch top for pouring water inside to resist fire attacks.

The top walls of the water and land gates are connected, with parapets, battlements, and arrow slits, and buttresses (mamian) built outside.

The water and land gates are meticulously arranged with strict defense, reflecting ancient superb city-building technology and defense systems.3.

Wumen Bridge: Exiting the Panmen water gate or viewing from atop the gate, one can see Wumen Bridge spanning the ancient canal (moat).

First built in the 7th year of Yuanfeng of the Northern Song (1084), rebuilt in the 11th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1872), it is the highest surviving single-arch stone bridge in Jiangsu, designated a provincial protected site in 2002.

This bridge is also the best place outside the scenic area to admire the Panmen water gate.

建筑要点 / Key Features
盘门三景；水陆城门国内仅存；瑞光寺塔八角七层；盘门元至正十一年建；吴门桥江苏现存最高单孔石拱桥；伍子胥阖闾大城
32 留园
Liuyuan Garden (Lingering Garden)
清
级别 Level
世界文化遗产，第一批全国重点文物保护单位（1961年）
地址 Address
阊门外留园路302号
类型 Type
古典园林
门票 Ticket
旺季40元；淡季30元
开放时间 Hours
7:30-18:00；7:30-17:30
中文原文

明万历二十一年（1593年）太仆寺少卿徐泰时罢官回乡，在苏州城外一处旧园基址上建造"东园"，是为留园的前身；今留园西侧的戒幢律寺又称西园寺，当时是徐泰时的西园。徐氏为苏州大族，在苏州还拥有紫芝园、拙政园、徐参议园和徐子本园等名园。

徐泰时聘请造园名手周丹泉叠筑园中假山，"高三丈，阔可二十丈，玲珑峭削，如一幅山水横披画，了无断续痕迹"（袁宏道《园亭纪略》），受到时人赞赏。此山今已不存，但在城内惠荫园仍可看到周丹泉的叠山作品。当时园中另一处名胜是奇石"瑞云峰"，号称江南名石之首。清乾隆年间为迎接皇帝南巡，此石被移至织造府西行宫内，即今苏州第十中学内。

清乾隆五十九年（1794年）园归藏书家刘恕，他曾在柳州、庆远任官，因水土不服告病还乡，改筑东园更名寒碧山庄，俗称刘园，大致奠定今日格局。园中最著名的是12尊太湖石奇峰，刘恕特邀王学浩为绘《寒碧庄十二峰图》。

清同治十二年（1873年）园归布政使盛康，大加修葺，因太平天国时期城西唯此园未毁，并取"刘园"谐音，更名留园。

当时只包括今濠濮池和五峰山房一带，清光绪十四年（1888年）辟建西路"别有洞天"，清光绪十七年（1891年）又建东路冠云峰庭园，构成东、中、西三区。

1961年留园被定为第一批全国重点文物保护单位，1997年列入世界文化遗产名录。

留园南侧旧为盛氏宅第和祠堂，园林入口夹在二者之间，需经过两重曲廊小院，行进时忽明忽暗、时宽时狭，形成令人称道的曲折悠长的前导空间。行至尽头"古木交柯"，墙壁上设漏窗隐现出园内风景，向西来到绿荫轩则豁然开朗，满池风景尽收眼中。

这一带围绕中央的水池布局，西、北以山林为主，东、南以建筑为主，自然与人工隔池相赏，池中又堆小蓬莱岛，架设曲桥、藤架，增添了景致层次。绿荫轩西侧是明瑟楼和主厅涵碧山房，一高一低，远望有如画舫。厅北出平台面向水池主景，南侧另筑庭山小景；明瑟楼南部也有假山，可循山登至二楼，眺览园景。

池东为二层的曲溪楼和西楼，造型多样，同时又稍稍后退，前部掩以枫杨等花木，使建筑不显突兀。中央水池被岛、桥隔为一大一小两处，东北小池宛如大池的具体而微；南为濠濮亭、东为清风池馆等建筑，皆贴近水面，可赏鱼吹风；北为山石、西为桥岛等自然景致，有天然风味。大池北岸假山以黄石为主，其上罗列湖石，稍嫌琐碎。

山顶点缀六角可亭，东北角有两层的远翠阁，皆可驻足临眺。由水池向东为庭院建筑区。五峰仙馆是座五开间楠木大厅，宏敞精丽，号称"江南第一厅堂"。大厅南北皆有假山，以南部为主，山上峰石穷形极态，模仿十二生肖。

堂东的鹤所、揖峰轩、还我读书处由折廊相连，构成一系列天井小院，花木扶疏，亭榭宛转，令游者如入幻境，堪称江南园林小庭之极致。这组庭园既与五峰仙馆形成对照，也是向东路林泉耆硕之馆的过渡。林泉耆硕之馆是座五开间鸳鸯厅，厅内陈设华丽，北面面对冠云峰池主景。

这处庭园围绕太湖名石"冠云峰"布置，瑞云、岫云两峰分列两侧作为陪衬，南为浣云沼，西为冠云台，东为冠云亭，北为冠云楼，有如众星捧月。古人喜好把石比作云，此石号称"冠云"，可见园主对其之自负；而此石雄奇挺拔，宛转隽秀，既具丈夫气，又有巾帼风，各个角度皆尽善尽美，可谓实至名归。由冠云峰庭园向西，经快雪时晴之亭，穿过北部山林为西路别有洞天景区。此区以山林野趣为主，土山上叠砌黄石，建筑较少，景致相对平淡。

留园林木幽曲、馆阁壮丽、花石秀美，其繁复华赡的建筑空间代表了晚清苏州园林的突出成就，堪与拙政园代表的明代山林之疏朗、狮子林代表的清中期峰石之奇幻并列，三座园林分别在建筑、山林、峰石三方面各臻其至，体现了苏州园林的最高成就。

· · · · ·
English

In the 21st year of Wanli of the Ming (1593), Xu Taishi, Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, returned home after dismissal from office and built the "East Garden" on an old garden site outside Suzhou—the predecessor of the Lingering Garden.

Today's Jiechuanglü Temple west of the Lingering Garden, also called Xiyuan Temple, was then Xu Taishi's West Garden.

The Xu family was a great clan in Suzhou, also owning famous gardens such as Zizhi Garden, Humble Administrator's Garden, Xu Canyi Garden, and Xu Ziben Garden.

Xu Taishi hired the renowned garden master Zhou Danquan to pile the garden's rockery, "three zhang high, about twenty zhang wide, exquisite and precipitous, like a horizontal landscape painting, with no trace of discontinuity" (Yuan Hongdao, "Record of Gardens and Pavilions"), admired by contemporaries.

This mountain no longer survives, but Zhou Danquan's rockery work can still be seen in the Huiyin Garden in the city.

At that time another famous scenic spot in the garden was the strange stone "Ruiyunfeng" (Auspicious Cloud Peak), known as the foremost famous stone in Jiangnan.

During the Qianlong reign of the Qing, to welcome the emperor's southern tour, this stone was moved to the west palace of the Weaving Department, today inside Suzhou No.

10 Middle School.

In the 59th year of Qianlong (1794), the garden passed to book collector Liu Shu, who had served in Liuzhou and Qingyuan but returned home due to illness from the local climate; he rebuilt the East Garden and renamed it Hanbi Mountain Villa, commonly called Liu Garden, roughly establishing today's layout.

The most famous feature of the garden was 12 extraordinary Taihu rock peaks; Liu Shu specially invited Wang Xuehao to paint the "Twelve Peaks of Hanbi Villa.

" In the 12th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1873), the garden passed to Administrative Commissioner Sheng Kang, who extensively renovated it.

Because it was the only garden west of the city not destroyed during the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom period, and taking the homophone of "Liu Garden," he renamed it Liuyuan (Lingering Garden).

At that time it only included today's Haopu Pond and Wufeng Shanfang area; in the 14th year of Guangxu (1888) the west road "Another World" was opened; in the 17th year of Guangxu (1891) the east road Guanyun Peak courtyard was built, forming east, middle, and west sections.

In 1961 the Lingering Garden was designated one of the first batch of National Key Cultural Heritage Sites; in 1997 inscribed on the World Cultural Heritage List.

South of the Lingering Garden was formerly the Sheng family residence and ancestral hall; the garden entrance is sandwiched between them, requiring passage through two winding corridor courtyards—alternating bright and dark, wide and narrow—forming a praised winding and lengthy introductory space.

At the end is "Ancient Trees Intertwining," with lattice windows on the wall revealing glimpses of the garden scenery; turning west to the Lvyin Xuan (Green Shade Studio) suddenly opens up, with the full pond scenery in view.

This area is laid out around the central pond, with mountains and forests dominating the west and north, buildings the east and south—nature and artifice admired across the pond.

In the pond, the small Penglai Island is piled, with zigzag bridges and vine trellises adding scenic layers.

West of Lvyin Xuan are the Mingse Lou and the main hall Hanbi Shanfang, one high and one low, resembling a painted boat from afar.

North of the hall, a platform faces the pond's main scenery; to the south, a small courtyard mountain scene is built.

South of Mingse Lou there is also a rockery, with a path up to the second floor for viewing the garden.

East of the pond are the two-story Quxi Lou and West Tower, varied in form, slightly set back with maple and poplar trees in front, preventing the buildings from appearing obtrusive.

The central pond is divided by islands and bridges into a large and a small section; the northeast small pond is like a miniature of the large one.

To the south is the Haopu Pavilion, to the east the Qingfeng Chiguan building—both close to the water for admiring fish and enjoying breezes.

To the north are rocks, to the west bridges and islands—natural scenery with a rustic flavor.

The rockery on the north bank of the large pond is mainly yellow stone, with Taihu rocks arranged on top, slightly cluttered.

The hexagonal Ke Pavilion sits on the mountaintop, and the two-story Yuancui Pavilion is at the northeast corner—both places for stopping and gazing.

East of the pond is the courtyard building area.The Wufeng Xian'guan (Five Peaks Immortal Hall) is a five-bay nanmu wood main hall, grand and exquisite, known as "the foremost hall in Jiangnan.

" North and south of the hall are rockeries, with the south as the main one; the peak rocks on the mountain take myriad forms, imitating the twelve zodiac animals.

East of the hall, the He Suo (Crane Place), Yifeng Xuan (Greeting Peak Studio), and Huanwo Dushu Chu (Return-Me Reading Place) are connected by winding corridors, forming a series of courtyard small yards with lush flowers and trees and graceful pavilions—making visitors feel as if entering a fantasy realm, arguably the ultimate of small courtyards in Jiangnan gardens.

This group of courtyards both contrasts with Wufeng Xian'guan and serves as a transition to the east road Linquan Qishuo Guan.

The Linquan Qishuo Guan (Forest and Spring Elders' Hall) is a five-bay mandarin-duck hall with luxurious furnishings, facing the Guanyun Peak pond main scenery to the north.

This courtyard is arranged around the famous Taihu stone "Guanyun Peak" (Cloud-Crowning Peak), with Ruiyun and Xiuyun peaks on both sides as foils; to the south is Huanyun Pond, west Guanyun Platform, east Guanyun Pavilion, north Guanyun Tower—like stars surrounding the moon.

The ancients liked to compare stones to clouds; this stone is called "Crowning Cloud," showing the owner's pride in it.

And this stone is majestic and tall, graceful and delicate, possessing both masculine and feminine qualities, perfect from every angle—truly living up to its name.

From the Guanyun Peak courtyard westward, via the Kuai Xue Shi Qing (Quick Snow and Clear Sky) Pavilion, through the northern mountain forest is the west road "Another World" scenic area.

This area focuses on mountain-forest rustic charm, with yellow stones piled on earth hills and few buildings—the scenery is relatively plain.

The Lingering Garden has winding trees, magnificent halls, and beautiful flowers and stones.

Its complex and gorgeous architectural space represents the outstanding achievement of late-Qing Suzhou gardens, comparable to the open Ming-dynasty mountain-forest style represented by the Humble Administrator's Garden and the fantastical mid-Qing peak-rock style represented by the Lion Grove.

The three gardens each excel in architecture, mountain forest, and peak rocks respectively, embodying the highest achievement of Suzhou gardens.

建筑要点 / Key Features

33 西园寺（戒幢律寺）
Xiyuan Temple (Jiezhuanglv Temple)
元—清
级别 Level
第三批江苏省保（1982年）
地址 Address
枫桥路北的西园弄18号
类型 Type
佛寺

中文原文

元至元年间在此建归元寺，晚明为徐泰时西园，他卒后其子徐溶舍园为寺，复称归元寺。明崇祯八年（1635年）此寺提倡律宗，更名戒幢律寺，俗称西园寺。

太平天国时期寺、园皆毁，清末民初逐渐修复。西园寺位于上塘河北，前有福德、智慧二桥，过桥自南而北为牌坊、天王殿、香花桥、大雄宝殿和藏经楼等，大雄宝殿东为观音殿，西为罗汉堂。

其中以建于清光绪二十六年（1900年）的罗汉堂最著名，呈田字形布局，内塑五百罗汉，是江南仅存的五百罗汉堂。堂内鲍子云塑的疯僧、吴晓芳塑的济公，以及用整根香樟木雕成的千手观音，惟妙惟肖，为雕塑杰作。由罗汉堂向西为西园。

入园有曲廊、天井、假山，较为清幽；向西进入主院，居中是一座大型放生池，中央建八角湖心亭，两侧以九曲桥与岸相连，景致优美，与上海豫园前的湖心亭相似。池东建苏满春台厅，为园中主堂，向西正对湖心亭。

池西月台上有铜鼋雕塑，池中自明代开始养鼋，体现了寺庙园林的特色。

· · · · ·
English

During the Zhiyuan reign of the Yuan, Guiyuan Temple was built here; in the late Ming it was Xu Taishi's West Garden.

After his death, his son Xu Rong donated the garden as a temple, again called Guiyuan Temple.

In the 8th year of Chongzhen of the Ming (1635), this temple promoted the Vinaya school and was renamed Jiezhuanglü Temple, commonly called Xiyuan Temple (West Garden Temple).

During the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom period both temple and garden were destroyed; gradually restored in the late Qing and early Republic.

Xiyuan Temple is located north of Shangtang River, with the Ford and Wisdom bridges in front.

Crossing the bridge, from south to north are the memorial archway, Heavenly King Hall, Xianghua Bridge, Mahavira Hall, and Scripture Depository.

East of the Mahavira Hall is the Guanyin Hall, west is the Arhat Hall.

The most famous is the Arhat Hall built in the 26th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1900), with a tian (田)-shaped layout, housing 500 arhat statues—the only surviving 500-Arhat Hall in Jiangnan.

Inside, the Mad Monk statue by Bao Ziyun, the Jigong statue by Wu Xiaofang, and the Thousand-Armed Guanyin carved from a whole camphor wood are lifelike—masterpieces of sculpture.

West of the Arhat Hall is the West Garden.

Entering the garden, there are winding corridors, courtyards, and rockeries, quite secluded; westward into the main courtyard, a large free-life pond occupies the center, with an octagonal lake-center pavilion in the middle, connected to the banks by nine-bend bridges on both sides—beautiful scenery, similar to the lake-center pavilion in front of Shanghai's Yu Garden.

East of the pond is the Suman Chuntai Hall, the main hall of the garden, facing west toward the lake-center pavilion.

On the west platform of the pond is a bronze soft-shelled turtle sculpture; soft-shelled turtles have been raised in the pond since the Ming, reflecting the character of temple gardens.

34 山塘街
Shantang Street
明—清
