中文原文

山塘街区免费，景点联票，含玉涵堂、泉州会馆、绍兴会馆、古戏台、山塘阁、安泰救火会和江南成衣馆。山塘街东起苏州古城阊门外，向西北直到虎丘山，长约七里，俗语称"七里山塘到虎丘"，有"姑苏第一名街"之誉。据说此塘为唐宝历年间，白居易担任苏州刺史时所开。

山塘街可分为东、西两段。东段从阊门渡僧桥起至半塘桥，多为商铺和住家，繁华热闹。今颐和园后山的苏州街，模仿的便是山塘街这一段。西段从半塘桥至虎丘山，河面变宽，远离城市，较有野趣。沿山塘街散布着大量古寺、祠堂和会馆，并有玉涵堂、五人墓和葛成墓三处省保单位。

1. 玉涵堂：玉涵堂是明代尚书吴一鹏（1460—1542）的故居，俗称阁老厅，共分三路，其中多建楼房。中路共五进，第三进正房为玉涵堂，建于明代，面阔三间，梁架采用扁作形式，青石柱础形制古朴。其他房屋多建于清代和民国时期。

2. 五人墓：明天启五年（1625年）魏忠贤发布《东林党人榜》，通缉东林人士，次年三月派缇骑到苏州逮捕周顺昌，在开读假诏时激起数万民众抗击，史称"开读之变"。这年闰六月，为首的五位义士颜佩韦、杨念如、沈扬、马杰和周文元被阉党处死。

崇祯皇帝即位后为之平反，并将虎丘附近的魏忠贤"普惠生祠"拆建为"五人之祠"，复社首领张溥为撰《五人墓碑记》。五人墓旁有葛成墓，葛成是明万历二十九年（1601年）苏州丝织工人抗税领袖，明崇祯三年（1630年）葬。

· · · · ·
English

The Shantang Street area is free; a combined ticket for attractions includes Yuhan Hall, Quanzhou Guildhall, Shaoxing Guildhall, ancient stage, Shantang Pavilion, Antai Fire Brigade, and Jiangnan Ready-Made Clothing Hall.

Shantang Street starts east outside the Changmen Gate of Suzhou's old city, extending northwest to Tiger Hill, about seven li long—hence the saying "seven li of Shantang to Tiger Hill," hailed as "the foremost street of Gusu.

" It is said this canal was dug by Bai Juyi when he served as prefect of Suzhou during the Baoli reign of the Tang.Shantang Street can be divided into east and west sections.

The east section, from the Duseng Bridge at Changmen to Bantang Bridge, is mostly shops and residences, bustling and lively.

Today's Suzhou Street at the back of Beijing's Summer Palace imitates this section of Shantang Street.

The west section, from Bantang Bridge to Tiger Hill, has a wider river, farther from the city, with more rustic charm.

Along Shantang Street are scattered numerous ancient temples, ancestral halls, and guildhalls, with three provincial protected sites: Yuhan Hall, Five Men's Tomb, and Ge Cheng's Tomb.1.

Yuhan Hall: Yuhan Hall is the former residence of Ming-dynasty Minister Wu Yipeng (1460-1542), commonly called the Elder Pavilion Hall, divided into three roads, with many multi-story buildings.

The middle road has five bays; the third bay's main hall is Yuhan Hall, built in the Ming, three bays wide, with flattened beam framing and simple bluestone column bases.

Other buildings were mostly built in the Qing and Republic periods.2.

Five Men's Tomb: In the 5th year of Tianqi of the Ming (1625), Wei Zhongxian issued the "Donglin Party List,"通缉 Donglin figures; the following March, imperial guards were sent to Suzhou to arrest Zhou Shunchang.

When the false edict was publicly read, tens of thousands of people rose up in resistance—historically called the "Kaidu Incident.

" In the leap sixth month of that year, the five leading righteous men—Yan Peiwei, Yang Nianru, Shen Yang, Ma Jie, and Zhou Wenyuan—were executed by the eunuch faction.

After Emperor Chongzhen ascended the throne, they were rehabilitated, and Wei Zhongxian's "Puhui Living Shrine" near Tiger Hill was demolished and rebuilt as the "Shrine of the Five Men," with the Restoration Society leader Zhang Pu writing the "Epitaph of the Five Men.

" Beside the Five Men's Tomb is Ge Cheng's Tomb; Ge Cheng was the leader of the Suzhou silk weavers' tax resistance in the 29th year of Wanli (1601), buried in the 3rd year of Chongzhen (1630).

中文原文

虎丘原名海涌山，据传远古时期为湖中小岛。吴王阖闾卒后葬此，征发十万人从湖中取土筑坟，形成山丘，"葬经三日，白虎踞其上，故名虎丘山"。这段文字见于唐代陆广微《吴地记》引用的《史记》，书中又引《吴越春秋》称，蹲伏在阖闾坟上的白虎乃是阖闾的金精所化，这位王侯的精魂盘踞于此，护佑着整座城市，虎丘因此被誉为"吴中第一山"。

晋代王珣兄弟在虎丘建造别业，后来舍宅为寺，称虎丘山寺。唐代称报恩寺，宋代称云岩寺，清代复称虎丘禅寺。虎丘并不大，却是吴中最著名的游览胜地，如诗所称"虎丘吴小山，东南称奇观"，宋代苏轼称："到苏州不游虎丘，乃憾事也！"山中景致可分为前山、千人石和山顶三处游赏区。

1. 前山：前山包括头山门、海涌桥、断梁殿、憨憨泉、试剑石、石桃、枕石、真娘墓和拥翠山庄等。头山门位于山塘街，对面隔着山塘河立有照壁。进门穿过海涌桥（1956年）是二山门，又称断梁殿。

此殿始建于唐，元至正四年（1338年）重建，特别之处在于大殿正梁由两根对接的木头组成，中央有明显的拼缝。这种有违力学常规的做法，体现了古代工匠的技艺和智慧。在苏州东山轩辕宫，还有一座规模更大的断梁殿。

过断梁殿沿山路拾级而上，左侧有憨憨泉，曾出现在沈周的《虎丘十二景图》册中，古朴可爱。泉周围还有试剑石、枕石和真娘墓等。憨憨泉西侧高台上是环翠山庄，可在下山时游赏。清光绪十年（1884年）状元洪钧与友人朱修庭、彭南屏和文小坡等游虎丘，发现荒废的憨憨泉，遂决定集资在泉西建环翠山庄。

山庄坐北朝南，依山而建，逐层升高。园门外两侧墙上题"龙虎豹熊"四字，笔力遒劲威猛，是清咸丰八年（1858年）桂林总兵陶茂森游虎丘时即兴挥就。入门第一层为抱瓮轩庭院，透过院东墙上的花窗可望见憨憨泉。向上第二层东侧平台上建问泉亭，内设石桌石凳，可供小憩临视憨憨泉。

第三层为园中主厅灵澜精舍，舍东筑平台，突出于园外不设围墙，使内外景致可以互借。最后一层是后堂送青移，在堂前可欣赏远山送来的一片青翠。环翠山庄布局紧凑，近可借周围各景，远可借虎丘塔、狮子山，是虎丘名胜中一座别致的园中园。2. 千人石：千人石一带是虎丘的精华所在，包括千人石、剑池题刻、石经幢、莲花池、点头石和二仙亭等。

沿山路行至尽头，豁然开朗，出现一片平坦如砥、自南向北微微倾斜的盘陀巨石，即为千人石。周围景点错落布置，互成对景。东南山坡上是孙武练兵场。东北低凹处是白莲池，池中有点头石，池南立石经幢。

北侧石壁上题李阳冰篆书"生公讲台"、胡缵宗篆书"千人坐"，据说南朝宋高僧生公在此对石讲经，石皆点头，听众越聚越多，座无虚席，千人石由此得名。

"千人坐"题刻向西，紧贴北壁为二仙亭，传为陈抟老祖与吕洞宾下棋处，始建于宋，清嘉庆三年（1798年）重建。

亭西石壁嵌两块青石，左侧"剑池"为唐代书法家颜真卿真迹，他所题的右侧"虎丘"到明代已漫漶不清，明万历四十二年（1614年）石刻名家章仲玉勾摹补刻，从而留下"假虎丘，真剑池"的俗谚。石刻西侧有座圆洞门，入门即为剑池。

剑池东、西两侧石壁拔地而起，耸然相对，顶部跨石拱桥。两壁之间是一道水池，南北狭长，有如宝剑。池水幽深甘冽，仿佛透出寒气，森森逼人。西侧石壁上有元代书法家周伯琦所书"剑池"篆书，雄浑古朴；东侧石壁是宋代书法家米芾题写的"风壑云泉"行楷，圆润苍劲。据传吴王阖闾的墓就深藏在剑池之下。沿剑池东侧石级登山，转至池顶拱桥上，可从高处俯瞰剑池。

桥中央有两处像井口的圆洞，称双井桥。古代僧人住在山顶，日常用水皆需下到剑池打水，据说宋代在桥上凿出双洞，设置辘轳从池中汲水。3. 山顶：山顶包括"五十三参"石阶、云岩寺大殿和云岩寺塔。由千人石东侧向北，依顺山势有一道石阶通向云岩禅寺，共有53级，俗称"五十三参"，取佛教"五十三参，参参见佛"之意。

石级尽头为大雄宝殿，内供释迦牟尼像。

此处原为虎丘寺的天王殿，清咸丰十年（1860年）寺庙毁于战火，清同治十年（1871年）在天王殿遗址上建造大雄宝殿。由殿北庭院向西，便可望见云岩寺塔。

4. 云岩寺塔：云岩寺塔是虎丘的标志建筑。早在南朝陈时就曾在山顶建塔，今塔建于五代后周显德六年（959年），历代多次重修，俗称虎丘塔。这是一座八角七层仿木楼阁式砖塔。内部为砖砌塔身，下部六层是五代原构，第七层为明崇祯年间重建。

塔的平面自外向内依次为外壁、回廊、内部和塔心室，各层回廊顶部通过叠涩砖构的楼面联系起内外塔壁，形成套筒式结构。塔身外部曾附建木构平座、楼阁，后来毁于火，仅存塔心。如今塔身倾斜接近4度，有"东方斜塔"之称。

· · · · ·
English

Tiger Hill was originally called Haiyong Mountain (Sea-Surge Mountain), legendarily a small island in a lake in ancient times.

After King Helü of Wu died and was buried here, 100,000 people were conscripted to take soil from the lake to build the tomb, forming the hill.

"Three days after burial, a white tiger squatted on it, hence the name Tiger Hill Mountain.

" This passage appears in the "Records of Wu" quoted by Tang-dynasty Lu Guangwei, which also cites the "Spring and Autumn of Wu and Yue" saying the white tiger crouching on Helü's tomb was the transformation of Helü's golden essence—the prince's spirit coiling here to protect the entire city—hence Tiger Hill is hailed as "the foremost mountain in Wu.

" In the Jin Dynasty, brothers Wang Xun and Wang Min built villas at Tiger Hill, later donating their residences as a temple called Tiger Hill Mountain Temple.

In the Tang it was called Bao'en Temple, in the Song Yunyan Temple, and in the Qing restored as Tiger Hill Chan Temple.

Tiger Hill is not large, but it is the most famous scenic spot in Wu, as the poem says "Tiger Hill, a small mountain of Wu, a wonder of the southeast"; Song-dynasty Su Shi said: "To visit Suzhou without touring Tiger Hill is a regret!

" The mountain's scenery can be divided into three touring areas: front mountain, Thousand Men Rock, and mountaintop.1.

Front Mountain: Includes the main gate, Haiyong Bridge, Broken Beam Hall, Hanhan Spring, Sword-Testing Rock, Stone Peach, Pillow Rock, Zhenniang's Tomb, and Yongcui Mountain Villa.

The main gate is on Shantang Street, with a screen wall across the Shantang River.Entering and crossing Haiyong Bridge (1956) is the second gate, also called the Broken Beam Hall.

This hall was first built in the Tang and rebuilt in the 4th year of Zhizheng of the Yuan (1338).

Its special feature is that the main beam consists of two joined pieces of wood, with a visible joint in the center.

This unconventional structural approach reflects the skill and wisdom of ancient craftsmen.At Xuanyuan Palace in Dongshan, Suzhou, there is an even larger Broken Beam Hall.

Passing the Broken Beam Hall and climbing the mountain path, on the left is Hanhan Spring, which appeared in Shen Zhou's "Twelve Scenes of Tiger Hill" album—simple and lovely.

Around the spring are Sword-Testing Rock, Pillow Rock, and Zhenniang's Tomb.On the high platform west of Hanhan Spring is Yongcui Mountain Villa, visitable when descending.

In the 10th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1884), zhuangyuan Hong Jun and friends Zhu Xiuting, Peng Nanping, and Wen Xiaopo visited Tiger Hill, discovered the abandoned Hanhan Spring, and decided to raise funds to build Yongcui Mountain Villa west of the spring.

The villa faces south, built against the mountain, rising level by level.

Outside the garden gate, the walls on both sides are inscribed with the four characters "Dragon, Tiger, Leopard, Bear" in powerful, fierce calligraphy, improvised by Tao Maosen, commander-in-chief of Guilin, when visiting Tiger Hill in the 8th year of Xianfeng (1858).

The first level inside is the Baoweng Xuan courtyard; through the lattice window on the east wall, Hanhan Spring can be seen.

On the east platform of the second level is the Wenquan Pavilion, with stone table and stools for resting and viewing Hanhan Spring.

The third level is the main hall Linglan Jingshe; east of the hall a platform extends beyond the garden without a wall, allowing interior and exterior scenery to borrow from each other.

The last level is the rear hall Songqing Yi, where the greenery of distant mountains can be appreciated.

Yongcui Mountain Villa has a compact layout, borrowing nearby scenery and distant views of Tiger Hill Pagoda and Lion Mountain—a distinctive garden-within-a-garden among Tiger Hill's sights.2.

Thousand Men Rock: The area around Thousand Men Rock is the essence of Tiger Hill, including Thousand Men Rock, Sword Pool inscriptions, stone pillar, Lotus Pond, Nodding Rock, and Two Immortals Pavilion.

Following the mountain path to the end, the view suddenly opens to a flat, smooth, gently north-sloping huge rock—Thousand Men Rock.Surrounding scenic spots are arranged in错落, forming opposite views.

On the southeast slope is Sun Wu's training ground.In the northeast depression is the White Lotus Pond, with Nodding Rock in the pond and a stone pillar south of the pond.

On the north cliff are Li Yangbing's seal script "Shengong Lecture Platform" and Hu Zuanzong's seal script "Thousand Men Seated.

" It is said that the Liu-Song dynasty eminent monk Shengong lectured on sutras to the rocks here, and the rocks all nodded; the audience grew larger and larger with no empty seats—hence the name Thousand Men Rock.

West of the "Thousand Men Seated" inscription, against the north wall, is the Two Immortals Pavilion, said to be where Ancestor Chen Tuan and Lü Dongbin played chess, first built in the Song and rebuilt in the 3rd year of Jiaqing of the Qing (1798).

On the west wall of the pavilion are two bluestones: the left "Sword Pool" is the genuine calligraphy of Tang calligrapher Yan Zhenqing; the right "Tiger Hill" he inscribed had become illegible by the Ming, and in the 42nd year of Wanli (1614) stone-carving master Zhang Zhongyu traced and recarved it—hence the saying "fake Tiger Hill, real Sword Pool.

" West of the carvings is a round-arched gate; entering is the Sword Pool.The east and west cliffs of the Sword Pool rise sharply, facing each other, with a stone arch bridge spanning the top.

Between the two cliffs is a long, narrow north-south pool, like a precious sword.The pool water is deep, sweet, and cold, seeming to emit chill—imposing and awe-inspiring.

On the west cliff is Yuan-dynasty calligrapher Zhou Boqi's seal script "Sword Pool," powerful and simple; on the east cliff is Song-dynasty calligrapher Mi Fu's running-regular script "Wind Valley Cloud Spring," rounded and vigorous.

It is said that King Helü of Wu's tomb lies deep beneath the Sword Pool.Climbing stone steps east of the Sword Pool to the arch bridge at the top, one can overlook the Sword Pool from above.

In the center of the bridge are two well-like round holes, called the Double-Well Bridge.

Ancient monks living on the mountaintop needed to fetch water from the Sword Pool; it is said that in the Song, double holes were chiseled on the bridge with windlasses to draw water from the pool.

3.Mountaintop: Includes the "Fifty-Three Steps" stone stairs, Yunyan Temple main hall, and Yunyan Temple Pagoda.

North from the east side of Thousand Men Rock, following the mountain slope, a stone staircase of 53 steps leads to Yunyan Chan Temple, commonly called "Fifty-Three Steps," taking the Buddhist meaning "fifty-three steps, each step sees the Buddha.

" At the end of the steps is the Mahavira Hall, enshrining Sakyamuni.

This was originally the Heavenly King Hall of Tiger Hill Temple; in the 10th year of Xianfeng (1860) the temple was destroyed by war, and in the 10th year of Tongzhi (1871) the Mahavira Hall was built on the Heavenly King Hall site.

From the north courtyard of the hall westward, the Yunyan Temple Pagoda comes into view.4.Yunyan Temple Pagoda: The Yunyan Temple Pagoda is the landmark of Tiger Hill.

As early as the Southern Chen dynasty, a pagoda was built on the mountaintop; today's pagoda was built in the 6th year of Xiande of the Later Zhou (959), repaired many times over the dynasties, commonly called Tiger Hill Pagoda.

This is an octagonal seven-story brick pagoda imitating a wooden pavilion style.

The interior is a brick body; the lower six stories are original Five Dynasties construction, the seventh story rebuilt in the Chongzhen reign of the Ming.

The pagoda's plan from outside inward consists of outer wall, corridor, interior, and central chamber; the top of each story's corridor connects the inner and outer pagoda walls through corbelled brick floors, forming a sleeve-tube structure.

The exterior of the pagoda body once had attached wooden flat balconies and pavilions, later destroyed by fire, leaving only the pagoda core.

Today the pagoda body tilts nearly 4 degrees, known as the "Leaning Tower of the East."

建筑要点 / Key Features
吴王阖闾葬此；吴中第一山；苏东坡到苏州不游虎丘乃憾事；前山千人石山顶云岩寺塔；断梁殿元至正四年重建；东方斜塔倾斜近4度
36 寒山寺
Hanshan Temple
清
级别 Level
第三批江苏省保（1982年）
地址 Address
枫桥路寒山寺弄24号
类型 Type
佛寺
门票 Ticket
20元
中文原文

寒山寺得名自唐代僧人寒山，安史之乱期间诗人张继漂泊吴中，作《枫桥夜泊》诗："月落乌啼霜满天，江枫渔火对愁眠。姑苏城外寒山寺，夜半钟声到客船。"饱含流离之苦、家国之忧，寒山寺由此闻名天下，历代不断重修，今为寒山寺景区，以"古寺、古桥、古关、古镇、古运河"著称。

"古寺"为寒山寺，因唐代高僧寒山、拾得在此住持而得名，现存建筑多建于晚清。寺门朝西，自西向东沿中轴线有山门、大雄宝殿、寒拾殿和普明宝塔（1995年）。

寺中保存着大量碑刻，以俞樾所书张继《枫桥夜泊》诗碑最著名，1982年列为省保单位。"古桥"枫桥旧名封桥，唐代已有记载，清乾隆三十五年（1770年）重建，清同治十年（1871年）重修。

这是一座单孔拱桥，桥拱由九排券石并列砌成。"古关"铁铃关位于枫桥东南，又名枫桥敌楼，1982年列为省保单位。明嘉靖三十六年（1557年）为抵御倭寇侵扰，吴县知县督造铁铃关，扼守水陆要冲，与古运河、枫桥共同构成一套完整的防御体系。关下有大路纵穿而过，关门两侧墙内建有驻军洞窟和登关石阶。

清道光九年（1829年）在关上建文星阁，后来毁坏，1986年重建关楼，恢复古貌。

· · · · ·
English

Hanshan Temple takes its name from the Tang-dynasty monk Hanshan.

During the An Lushan Rebellion, poet Zhang Ji drifted in the Wu region and wrote the poem "Night Mooring at Maple Bridge": "The moon sets, crows cry, frost fills the sky; river maples and fishing fires face my sorrowful sleep.

Outside Gusu city, Hanshan Temple; the midnight bell reaches my guest boat.

" Full of the bitterness of displacement and worry for country and home, Hanshan Temple became world-famous from this poem, repaired repeatedly over the dynasties.

Today it is the Hanshan Temple scenic area, known for "ancient temple, ancient bridge, ancient pass, ancient town, ancient canal.

" The "ancient temple" is Hanshan Temple, named because Tang eminent monks Hanshan and Shide served as abbots here; surviving buildings were mostly built in the late Qing.

The temple gate faces west; from west to east along the central axis are the gate, Mahavira Hall, Hanshi Hall, and Puming Pagoda (1995).

The temple preserves numerous stele carvings, the most famous being the stele of Zhang Ji's "Night Mooring at Maple Bridge" in Yu Yue's calligraphy, designated a provincial protected site in 1982.

The "ancient bridge" Maple Bridge was formerly called Feng Bridge (Seal Bridge), recorded as early as the Tang, rebuilt in the 35th year of Qianlong (1770) and repaired in the 10th year of Tongzhi (1871).

It is a single-arch bridge, with the arch built of nine rows of voussoir stones laid side by side.

The "ancient pass" Tieling Pass (Iron Bell Pass) is southeast of Maple Bridge, also called the Maple Bridge Watchtower, designated a provincial protected site in 1982.

In the 36th year of Jiajing of the Ming (1557), to resist Japanese pirate raids, the magistrate of Wu County supervised the construction of Tieling Pass, guarding the strategic land-water junction, together with the ancient canal and Maple Bridge forming a complete defense system.

A main road passes through under the pass; inside the walls on both sides of the gate are troop caves and stone steps to climb the pass.

In the 9th year of Daoguang of the Qing (1829), the Wenxing Pavilion was built on the pass, later destroyed; in 1986 the pass tower was rebuilt, restoring the ancient appearance.

37 宝带桥
Precious Belt Bridge
明
级别 Level
第五批全国重点文物保护单位（2001年）
地址 Address
吴中区澹台湖东
类型 Type
古桥
中文原文

宝带桥始建于唐元和十一年（816年），据传御史王仲舒曾捐玉带筹资建桥，因此得名，南宋绍定五年（1232年）重建，明正统十年（1445年）大修。

桥南北跨在澹台河上，全长317米，共有53孔连缀而成，桥身之长、孔数之多，世所罕见。中间的三孔位于主航道上，为方便行船向上抬高，中跨7.45米，两侧边跨各6.5米，其余50孔跨度皆在4.6米左右，保证了桥面的平坦。

桥宽4.1米，除用于交通，还作为纤道使用，因此两侧不设栏板。桥拱券由一段纵向并列条石与一段横向石条相间砌成，是南宋江浙一带常见的砌法。桥墩较为单薄，属于柔性桥墩，既节省了石料，又能减少阻水面积。

· · · · ·
English

The Precious Belt Bridge was first built in the 11th year of Yuanhe of the Tang (816).

Legend says Censor Wang Zhongshu donated his jade belt to raise funds for building the bridge, hence the name.

Rebuilt in the 5th year of Shaoding of the Southern Song (1232), and majorly repaired in the 10th year of Zhengtong of the Ming (1445).

The bridge spans north-south across the Dantai River, with a total length of 317 meters and 53 connected arches—its length and number of arches are rare in the world.

The middle three arches are over the main navigation channel, raised upward for convenient boat passage; the central span is 7.45 meters, the side spans 6.

5 meters each, and the remaining 50 arches have spans of about 4.6 meters, ensuring a flat bridge deck.The bridge is 4.

1 meters wide, used not only for transportation but also as a towpath, hence no railings on both sides.

The arch voussoirs are built by alternating sections of longitudinally laid stone bars and transversely laid stone bars—a common construction method in the Jiangsu-Zhejiang region during the Southern Song.

The bridge piers are relatively slender, belonging to flexible piers, both saving stone and reducing water-blocking area.

建筑要点 / Key Features
唐元和十一年王仲舒捐玉带筹资建桥；全长317米53孔连缀；桥身之长孔数之多世所罕见；柔性桥墩；南宋江浙常见砌法
38 楞伽寺塔
Lengjia Temple Pagoda
北宋
级别 Level
第二批江苏省保（1982年）
地址 Address
吴中区石湖上方山顶
类型 Type
古塔
中文原文

楞伽寺塔始建于隋大业四年（608年），北宋太平兴国三年（978年）重建，明崇祯九年（1636年）重修，主体为宋塔。这是一座七层八角仿木楼阁式砖塔，高约23米，向上逐层收缩。

塔底层四面开门，原有副阶，上覆重檐；其上各层皆有屋檐，今仅存内部塔身。各层交错开门，两侧设佛龛，使上下洞口不在同一直线上，以增强稳固性。

· · · · ·
English

The Lengjia Temple Pagoda was first built in the 4th year of Daye of the Sui (608), rebuilt in the 3rd year of Taiping Xingguo of the Northern Song (978), and repaired in the 9th year of Chongzhen of the Ming (1636), with the main body being a Song pagoda.

This is a seven-story octagonal brick pagoda imitating a wooden pavilion style, about 23 meters high, tapering story by story upward.

The bottom story has doors on four sides, originally with a surrounding corridor covered by double eaves; each upper story has eaves, today only the internal pagoda body survives.

Each story has staggered doors with Buddhist niches on both sides, so that upper and lower openings are not in a straight line, enhancing stability.

中文原文

寂鉴寺位于吴中区藏书镇天池山坞，内有3座元代石殿。该寺前身先后为南朝刘宋会稽太守张裕私第、南宋秘书监张廷杰别业，有天池十八景。

元至正十七年（1357年）创建寂鉴禅庵，明弘治年间天目禅师普惠重修，更名华山天池院。寺庙平面呈椭圆形。最南侧为山门，1980年重建，只有抱鼓石是原物。门外两侧各有一座石屋，皆为坐南朝北的巨型佛龛。

东为兜率宫，南侧巨石上雕2.55米高弥勒像，北侧覆一间单檐歇山顶石屋。

西为极乐园，内供2.6米高阿弥陀佛立像，下有须弥座，上立石柱、石墙、石门窗隔扇及重檐歇山顶，屋脊有吻兽，平远较兜率宫精细。

山门内是三开间的西天寺石殿，平面呈凸字形，南为单檐歇山顶，后出抱厦与北部山岩相接，有工字殿的意味。殿内分成前后两进，前部为祭祀活动场所，后部为佛龛和供案。

室内顶部有六处藻井，以明间佛龛上部的最为华美，自下而上由方形、斗八和圆形藻井层层构成。寂鉴寺三座石殿是全国仅存的元代仿木石构建筑，内部石刻佛像精美，具有重要的建筑和雕塑价值。

· · · · ·
English

Jijian Temple is located in the Tianchi Mountain valley of Cangshu Town, Wuzhong District, containing three Yuan-dynasty stone halls.

The temple's predecessors were successively the private residence of Zhang Yu, Governor of Kuaiji in the Liu Song of the Southern Dynasties, and the villa of Zhang Tingjie, Secretary of the Southern Song, with the Eighteen Scenes of Tianchi.

In the 17th year of Zhizheng of the Yuan (1357), the Jijian Chan Nunnery was founded; during the Hongzhi reign of the Ming, Master Tianmu Puhui repaired it and renamed it Huashan Tianchi Courtyard.

The temple has an oval plan.At the southernmost is the gate, rebuilt in 1980, with only the drum-shaped bearing stones being original.

Outside the gate on both sides are stone houses, both giant Buddhist niches facing south toward north.The east is the Tusita Palace, with a 2.

55-meter Maitreya statue carved on the huge stone to the south, and a single-eave hip-and-gable roof stone house covering the north.The west is the Bliss Garden, enshrining a 2.

6-meter standing Amitabha statue, with a Sumeru pedestal below and stone columns, walls, door-window lattice, and double-eave hip-and-gable roof above, with roof ornaments on the ridge—more refined than the Tusita Palace.

Inside the gate is the three-bay Western Heaven Temple stone hall, with a convex (凸) plan; the south has a single-eave hip-and-gable roof, with a rear portico connecting to the northern mountain rock, resembling an I-shaped hall.

The interior is divided into front and rear sections: the front is for sacrificial activities, the rear for Buddhist niches and offering tables.

There are six caisson ceilings inside, the most magnificent above the central bay's Buddhist niche, composed layer by layer from below upward of square, douba (eight-sided), and circular caissons.

The three stone halls of Jijian Temple are the only surviving Yuan-dynasty wooden-imitating stone buildings in China, with exquisitely carved stone Buddha statues inside, having important architectural and sculptural value.

建筑要点 / Key Features
3座元代石殿；元至正十七年创建寂鉴禅庵；明弘治年间天目禅师普惠重修；全国仅存元代仿木石构建筑；西天寺兜率宫极乐园；六处藻井
40 万佛石塔
Ten Thousand-Buddha Stone Pagoda
元
级别 Level
第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
地址 Address
吴县镇湖乡西泾村
类型 Type
古塔
中文原文

万佛石塔始建于南宋绍兴年间，元大德十年（1306年）重建，原名禅师塔，因塔内须弥座上刻有万余尊小佛像，得名万佛石塔。

此塔由台基、塔身和塔刹组成，总高10.8米，是一座仿印度窣堵坡的单层方塔，形制罕见。台基为长方形，南侧设宽约1米的如意踏跺。塔身位于台北侧，形如覆斗，底边宽3.3米，顶边宽2.8米，角部有四根方石柱向内倾斜支撑横梁，其上叠砌平台。

平台上立塔刹，由石刻宝瓶、覆钵和相轮组成，正方形的塔檐微微上翘，覆盖着其下石座四面的佛像。

塔身南侧辟火焰状的喇嘛塔式眼光门，内部为穹窿式洞窟，上小下大，底部有1.7米高的须弥座，座上环砌十层武康石，刻60排小型坐佛像，每排180余尊，共计10000余尊，每尊高约5厘米，宽约3厘米，小巧精美。北壁正对塔门是一尊高30厘米、宽20厘米的主像。

· · · · ·
English

The Ten Thousand-Buddha Stone Pagoda was first built during the Shaoxing reign of the Southern Song, rebuilt in the 10th year of Dade of the Yuan (1306), originally named the Chan Master Pagoda.

Because over ten thousand small Buddha statues are carved on the Sumeru pedestal inside, it is named the Ten Thousand-Buddha Stone Pagoda.

This pagoda consists of a platform base, pagoda body, and finial, with a total height of 10.8 meters.

It is a single-story square pagoda imitating the Indian stupa, with a rare form.The platform base is rectangular, with a 1-meter-wide ruyi-shaped step on the south side.

The pagoda body is on the north side of the platform, shaped like an inverted funnel (fudu), with a bottom width of 3.3 meters and top width of 2.8 meters.

At the corners, four square stone pillars tilt inward to support the beams, above which a platform is laid.

On the platform stands the finial, composed of a stone vase, inverted bowl, and chatra (umbrella); the square pagoda eave turns slightly upward, covering the Buddha statues on the four sides of the stone base below.

On the south side of the pagoda body, a flame-shaped Tibetan-style light gate is opened; the interior is a domed cave, smaller at top and larger at bottom, with a 1.

7-meter-high Sumeru pedestal at the base.

Around the pedestal, ten layers of Wukang stone are laid, carved with 60 rows of small seated Buddha statues, over 180 per row, totaling over 10,000 statues, each about 5 cm high and 3 cm wide—small and exquisite.

On the north wall facing the pagoda gate is a main statue 30 cm high and 20 cm wide.

建筑要点 / Key Features
南宋绍兴年间始建；元大德十年重建；原名禅师塔；塔内须弥座上万余尊小佛像；仿印度窣堵坡单层方塔；总高10.8米
41 天平山
Tianping Mountain
明—清
级别 Level
第四批江苏省保（1982年）

苏州城西15公里
类型 Type

门票 Ticket

7:30-17:00
中文原文

天平山与以范仲淹（989—1052）为代表的范氏家族关系密切。范仲淹是苏州吴县人，先祖葬在天平山下，北宋景祐年间宋仁宗将此山赐给他作为家山。南宋绍兴年间苏州士绅在天平山西麓为范仲淹建忠烈庙，此后多次重修。

从东南侧大门进入，沿中轴线依次有"先忧后乐"牌坊（1989年新建）、仪门、石桥、享堂和三太师祠。庙南为近年新建的范仲淹纪念馆。庙北有大片枫林，是明万历年间范仲淹的后人范允临（1558—1641）从福建移植而来，迄今已有400多年，每到仲秋，枫红如火，成为天平山的一大胜景。

枫林东南立乾隆御碑亭，题有乾隆四次游览天平山的诗文。枫林西侧是白云庵，始建于唐宝历二年（826年），北宋庆历四年（1044年）范仲淹奏请改名"功德香院"，成为范氏家庵。

明万历年间范允临重建，今为清同治年间范学炳重建，内有三间主殿。从白云庵向上可登天平山顶，沿路有更衣亭、鹦鹉石和一线天等景点。其中白云泉水味甘洌，得到白居易、范仲淹等人品题，为镇山名泉；"万笏朝天"奇石林立，有如朝臣所用的笏板，极为罕见，二者与山下的古枫并称为"天平三绝"。

白云庵北侧为高义园，明万历年间范允临建，原名天平山庄。建成后范允临携妻子徐媛宴请四方宾客，遨游山水胜景，名扬吴中。晚明名士张岱曾被邀请游园，在《陶庵梦忆》里描述园景："进门则长廊复道，直达山麓……山之左为桃源，峭壁回湍，桃花片片流出。右孤山，种梅千树。渡涧为小兰亭，茂林修竹，曲水流觞，件件有之。

"明清之际山庄废圮，清康熙、乾隆年间范氏后人两次重修，乾隆十六年（1751年）乾隆驾临山庄，赐名高义园。此园依山而筑，背倚"万笏朝天"，层层抬升。

最前方为清乾隆十六年（1751年）所立四柱三间冲天式汉白玉牌坊，向西为接驾亭。穿过长堤是主体庭院，有轿厅、乐天楼、逍遥亭和正殿共四进，正殿内悬御匾"高义园"。园内建筑白墙黛瓦，与其北咒钵庵的黄墙黛瓦倒映在前方的十景塘中，景色秀美。

此外周围还有来燕榭、桃花涧和范坟群等景点。

· · · · ·
English

Tianping Mountain is closely related to the Fan family, represented by Fan Zhongyan (989-1052).

Fan Zhongyan was a native of Wu County, Suzhou; his ancestors were buried at the foot of Tianping Mountain.

During the Jingyou reign of the Northern Song, Emperor Renzong bestowed this mountain on him as a family mountain.

During the Shaoxing reign of the Southern Song, Suzhou gentry built the Zhonglie (Loyal Martyr) Temple for Fan Zhongyan at the western foot of Tianping Mountain, subsequently repaired multiple times.

Entering from the southeast gate, along the central axis are successively the "First Worry, Later Joy" memorial archway (newly built in 1989), ceremonial gate, stone bridge, offering hall, and Three Grand Tutor Shrine.

South of the temple is the Fan Zhongyan Memorial Hall built in recent years.

North of the temple is a large maple forest, transplanted from Fujian by Fan Zhongyan's descendant Fan Yunlin (1558-1641) during the Wanli reign of the Ming—now over 400 years old.

Every mid-autumn, the maples turn red like fire, becoming a major scenic spot of Tianping Mountain.

Southeast of the maple forest stands the Qianlong Imperial Stele Pavilion, inscribed with poems and prose from Qianlong's four visits to Tianping Mountain.

West of the maple forest is the Baiyun Nunnery, first built in the 2nd year of Baoli of the Tang (826); in the 4th year of Qingli of the Northern Song (1044), Fan Zhongyan petitioned to rename it "Merit and Virtue Fragrant Courtyard," becoming the Fan family nunnery.

Rebuilt by Fan Yunlin during the Wanli reign of the Ming; today it was rebuilt by Fan Xuebing during the Tongzhi reign of the Qing, with three main bays inside.

From Baiyun Nunnery upward, one can climb to the top of Tianping Mountain, with scenic spots along the way such as the Changing Clothes Pavilion, Parrot Rock, and Thread of Sky.

Among them, Baiyun Spring has sweet, clear water, praised by Bai Juyi, Fan Zhongyan, and others—a famous spring guarding the mountain; the "Wanhu Chaotian" (Ten Thousand Tablets Facing Heaven) strange rocks stand in clusters, like the hu tablets used by court officials—extremely rare.

These two, together with the ancient maples at the foot of the mountain, are called the "Three Wonders of Tianping.

" North of Baiyun Nunnery is Gaoyi Garden (High Righteousness Garden), built by Fan Yunlin during the Wanli reign of the Ming, originally named Tianping Mountain Villa.

After completion, Fan Yunlin and his wife Xu Yuan entertained guests from all directions, roaming the scenic mountains and waters, becoming famous in Wu.

Late-Ming scholar Zhang Dai was once invited to visit the garden and described its scenery in "Tao'an Dream Memories": "Entering the gate, long corridors and repeated paths lead directly to the mountain foot.

..left of the mountain is the Peach Blossom Spring, with sheer cliffs and rushing currents, peach blossom petals flowing out.Right is the Solitary Mountain, planted with a thousand plum trees.

Crossing the stream is the Small Orchid Pavilion, with lush forests and tall bamboos, winding water for floating wine cups—everything is there.

" At the Ming-Qing transition the villa fell into ruin; during the Kangxi and Qianlong reigns of the Qing, Fan descendants rebuilt it twice.

In the 16th year of Qianlong (1751), Qianlong visited the villa and bestowed the name Gaoyi Garden.

This garden is built against the mountain, backed by the "Ten Thousand Tablets Facing Heaven," rising level by level.

At the very front is a four-pillar, three-bay, sky-reaching white marble archway erected in the 16th year of Qianlong (1751); west is the Jieja Pavilion (Receiving the Emperor Pavilion).

Crossing the long embankment is the main courtyard, with four bays: sedan hall, Letian Tower, Xiaoyao Pavilion, and main hall; the main hall hangs the imperial plaque "Gaoyi Garden.

" The garden buildings have white walls and dark tiles, which, together with the yellow walls and dark tiles of the Zhoubo Nunnery to its north, are reflected in the Ten-Scenery Pond in front—beautiful scenery.

Additionally, there are scenic spots such as the Laiyan Pavilion, Peach Blossom Stream, and Fan family tombs.

建筑要点 / Key Features
范仲淹家族家山；北宋景祐年间宋仁宗赐山；万笏朝天奇石林立；白云泉镇山名泉；天平三绝；高义园乾隆十六年赐名
42 木渎镇
Mudu Town
明—清
级别 Level
中国历史文化名镇
地址 Address
吴中区木渎镇
类型 Type
历史文化名镇
中文原文

木渎镇是苏州著名的历史文化名镇，拥有多处古典园林和历史遗迹。1. 严家花园（羡园）：严家花园位于山塘街北，最初是清乾隆年间沈德潜（1673—1769）的寓所，清道光八年（1828年）归钱端溪，开池叠山改筑为端园。

后又售予严国馨（1826—1905），清光绪二十八年（1902年）严氏聘请香山帮名匠姚承祖修葺一新，改称羡园，俗称严家花园。1958年在园内大炼钢铁，后又建农机厂，羡园被拆成平地，1999年在原址重建。

此园坐北朝南，中部为住宅，包括门厅、怡宾厅、尚贤堂、明是楼和眺农楼；环宅三面为花园，采用春、夏、秋、冬主题，用青石和黄石叠筑四季假山。2. 虹饮山房：由羡园沿山塘街向东约300米为虹饮山房，清乾隆年间徐士元建。

乾隆南巡经木渎曾驻跸在虹饮山房，其南临河建有御码头和石构的怡泉亭（市保单位）。虹饮山房包括三路，中路为住宅，沿轴线依次布置门厅、舞彩堂和春晖楼戏台，东、西两路为花园。

东路花园原为明代李氏的小隐园，徐士元加以改筑，清末归陈氏，"绣圣"沈寿（1874—1921）是陈家的外孙女，幼年在此生活，今园中建有沈寿纪念馆。西路花园在明代是刑部侍郎王心一的秀野园。

王心一在苏州拙政园东建有归田园居，后来喜爱木渎的幽静，又在此建造别业。今园中有与皇家相关的圣旨馆、科举制度馆和宫廷用品馆等。3. 古松园：紧邻虹饮山房东侧为古松园，原为清末蔡少渔的住宅，1998年在宅后扩建园林。住宅中轴包括门厅、轿厅、古松堂和凤凰楼。

凤凰楼向东隔水有一株明代罗汉松，园林由此得名。水池贯穿全园，沿池布置建筑，堆叠假山，较为精雅。4. 榜眼府第：榜眼府第位于下塘街，是林则徐的弟子冯桂芬（1809—1874）故居，冯氏中清道光二十年（1840年）一甲二名，因而得名。府第采用前宅后园格局。

住宅现存门厅、大厅显志堂和后部芙蓉楼共三进，今为冯桂芬纪念馆和周士心美术馆。后部花园围绕荷花池布置亭廊桥榭，在园北假山顶部的含山亭可眺望灵岩山。5. 灵岩山：沿山塘街向西，灵岩山入口在灵天路与中山西路交叉口处，门票20元，开放时间8:30—16:30。

山内有吴王姑苏台、清代状元毕沅的灵岩山馆和清代诗人张永夫纪念馆等景点。山下有流水清池，沿路登山，则可寻访馆娃宫、西施洞和琴台等春秋时期的遗迹。

· · · · ·
English

Mudu Town is a famous historical and cultural town in Suzhou, with numerous classical gardens and historical relics.1.

Yan Family Garden (Xianyuan): Located north of Shantang Street, originally the residence of Shen Deqian (1673-1769) during the Qianlong reign of the Qing.

In the 8th year of Daoguang (1828), it passed to Qian Duanxi, who dug ponds and piled rockeries to rebuild it as Duanyuan (Duan Garden).

Later sold to Yan Guoxin (1826-1905); in the 28th year of Guangxu (1902), the Yan family hired Xiangshan master craftsman Yao Chengzu to renovate it completely, renaming it Xianyuan (Admiration Garden), commonly called Yan Family Garden.

In 1958, steel was smelted in the garden, and later an agricultural machinery factory was built, with Xianyuan demolished to flat ground; rebuilt on the original site in 1999.

This garden faces south, with the residence in the center including the gate hall, Yibin Hall, Shangxian Hall, Mingshi Tower, and Tiaonong Tower; the garden surrounds the residence on three sides, using spring, summer, autumn, and winter themes, with bluestone and yellow stone piled into four-season rockeries.

2.

Hongyin Shanfang (Rainbow Drinking Mountain Villa): About 300 meters east along Shantang Street from Xianyuan is Hongyin Shanfang, built by Xu Shiyuan during the Qianlong reign of the Qing.

When Qianlong's southern tour passed through Mudu, he stayed at Hongyin Shanfang; on its south side facing the river are an imperial dock and the stone-structured Yiquan Pavilion (municipal protected unit).

Hongyin Shanfang includes three roads; the middle road is the residence, with the gate hall, Wucai Hall, and Chunhui Tower stage arranged along the axis; the east and west roads are gardens.

The east garden was originally the Xiaoyin Garden of the Ming-dynasty Li family, modified by Xu Shiyuan; in the late Qing it passed to the Chen family.

The "Embroidery Sage" Shen Shou (1874-1921) was the Chen family's granddaughter, living here as a child; today the Shen Shou Memorial Hall is in the garden.

The west garden was the Xiuye Garden of Wang Xinyi, Vice Minister of Justice in the Ming.

Wang Xinyi built the Gui Tian Yuan Ju east of Suzhou's Humble Administrator's Garden, and later, loving the tranquility of Mudu, built another villa here.

Today the garden contains the Imperial Edict Hall, Imperial Examination System Hall, and Court Supplies Hall related to the imperial family.3.

Ancient Pine Garden: Immediately east of Hongyin Shanfang is the Ancient Pine Garden, originally the residence of Cai Shaoyu in the late Qing, with the garden expanded behind the residence in 1998.

The residential central axis includes the gate hall, sedan hall, Ancient Pine Hall, and Phoenix Tower.

East of the Phoenix Tower across water is a Ming-dynasty Buddhist pine (arhat pine), from which the garden takes its name.

A pond runs through the entire garden, with buildings arranged along the pond and rockeries piled—quite elegant.4.

Bangyan Fudi (Second-place Graduate Mansion): Located on Xiatang Street, this is the former residence of Feng Guifen (1809-1874), a disciple of Lin Zexu.

Feng won the second place (bangyan) in the 20th year of Daoguang of the Qing (1840), hence the name.The mansion adopts a front-residence, rear-garden layout.

The residence survives in three bays: gate hall, main hall Xianzhi Hall, and rear Hibiscus Tower—today the Feng Guifen Memorial Hall and Zhou Shixin Art Museum.

The rear garden arranges pavilions, corridors, bridges, and terraces around a lotus pond; the Hanshan Pavilion at the top of the north rockery offers views of Lingyan Mountain.5.

Lingyan Mountain: West along Shantang Street, the Lingyan Mountain entrance is at the intersection of Lingtian Road and West Zhongshan Road, admission 20 yuan, open 8:30-16:30.

Inside the mountain are scenic spots such as the King of Wu's Gusu Terrace, the Lingyan Mountain Villa of Qing-dynasty zhuangyuan Bi Yuan, and the Memorial Hall of Qing-dynasty poet Zhang Yongfu.

At the foot of the mountain are flowing water and clear ponds; climbing along the path, one can visit Spring and Autumn period relics such as the Guanwa Palace, Xishi Cave, and Qin (Zither) Terrace.

严家花园羡园；虹饮山房乾隆南巡驻跸；古松园明代罗汉松；榜眼府第冯桂芬故居；灵岩山吴王姑苏台；秀野园沈寿
