中文原文

东山又名东洞庭山，位于苏州西南，太湖东岸，最高峰为莫厘峰，与西洞庭山的缥缈峰东西相望。

东山拥有4处国保：以雕刻艺术著称的民国雕花楼（春在楼），供有南宋彩塑罗汉的紫金庵，建于元代的轩辕宫，以及位于杨湾古街的明代民居明善堂、凝德堂和怀荫堂；6处省保：瑞霭堂、念勤堂楠木厅、诸公井亭、务本堂、绍德堂和三山古文化遗址；11处市保及100余处明清古建筑。

与东山镇隔水相望的是西山镇。东山以名胜古迹居多，西山则以自然风光取胜，但也有栖贤巷门、锦绣堂、涵村店铺和仁本堂等省保建筑。1. 雕花楼（春在楼）：雕花楼主体建筑群坐西朝东，南北共三路。中路为雕花楼，自东向西依次为照壁、门楼、前厅、后厅和厨房餐厅；北路为花园，南路为状元府。

雕花楼建于民国年间，集砖雕、木雕、金雕、石雕、泥塑于一体，是苏州香山帮工匠的杰作，被誉为"江南第一楼"。雕花楼的雕饰和格局充分体现了富商的品位和需求。雕饰内容皆含吉祥寓意。门楼前地面用碎石铺砌"瓶生三戟"，即"平升三级"，祈求升官富贵。

门楼布满砖雕，以内侧为例：下枋刻"郭子仪上寿"，其上立福、禄、寿三星雕像；中枋镶蝠边砖额"聿修厥德"，左右兜肚分别为"尧舜禅让""文王访贤"圆雕，其上为横幅圆雕"福鹿十景"；上枋为"八仙庆寿"圆雕，其上垫拱板有五处透雕，正中为双喜，两侧为如意和绳带，比喻如意传代。屋顶垂脊塑天官赐福和鲤鱼跃龙门，正脊立植有万年青的青瓷聚宝盆。木雕主要集中在前厅和后厅。

前厅为五间两层硬山造，是举办婚丧大礼和接待贵客之所，雕刻最多，堪称"江南满堂木雕"的代表作。梁上有48则黄杨木雕《三国演义》；月梁两端雕凤凰，全厅共86对，取其谐音"百乐"；前檐长窗和半窗的裙板上刻"二十四孝"。后厅是女眷的活动中心，主要刻《西厢记》故事。

雕花楼的雕饰特点被总结为：出门有喜、进门有宝、抬头有寿、回头有官、伸手有钱和脚踏有福，充满了对福寿富贵的直白祈望。雕花楼的建筑布局主要依据现实需求。前厅一层为行礼和待客之所，后厅一层为内眷活动场所，两厅二层连通为走马楼，布置卧室和客房。前厅南侧藏有保险柜，后厅暗藏三层，储存奇珍异宝，以防强盗劫掠。一方面主人通过精美的雕饰炫耀富贵，一方面又绞尽脑汁保藏财富，求贵守富的复杂人性在雕花楼中展露无遗。

北路的花园有山有水，四组湖石假山多依墙叠筑，与曲池体现趣味。湖石重形象欣赏，模仿熊、象、鹰、鼠等，体现世俗趣味。西端尽处是一座二层佛楼，为家中女眷烧香念佛之所。南路状元府有宅有园，展览东山的科举文化。

2. 紫金庵罗汉塑像：紫金庵位于东洞庭山的西卯坞内，创建于唐初，盛唐和南宋两次大修，明初重建，清乾隆年间又有扩建。

今头山门位于西南角，入门一直前行，左侧可见二山门。庵内主体建筑群坐北朝南，依次为二山门、罗汉殿和净因堂。西侧附属有晴川轩、白云居和听松堂等。整组建筑面积不大，簇拥在苍松翠竹间，古朴典雅。

庵内最著名的是塑于南宋年间的十六罗汉（一堂），与济南长清灵岩寺的四十罗汉（一堂）、甪直保圣寺的九罗汉（半堂），合称"天下罗汉二堂半"。罗汉殿内面南正中为释迦三世佛，其间侍立迦叶、阿难二弟子；面北正中为望海观音金身像。十六罗汉分立在东、西两壁下，各有八尊。

他们出自南宋雕塑名家雷潮夫妇之手，是二人的巅峰之作，清康熙《苏州府志》称："（紫金庵）内大士及罗汉像，系雷潮装塑。潮夫妇俱称善手，一生止塑三处，本庵尤为称首。

"清人邱赓熙对紫金庵罗汉评价极高，他曾遍游苏杭的名山古寺，所见罗汉像往往高且大，而从未有"精神超乎、呼之欲活如金庵者"（《紫金庵净因堂记》）。这一评价点出了紫金庵罗汉的两大特点：一是与借助高大显示神威的惯用手法不同，紫金庵罗汉与真人大小相仿，坐像多在1.2米左右，头部、身体和手足的比例恰当协调。

二是这16尊罗汉将神像人性化，通过不同的容貌、迥异的神情，赋予他们丰富的情感和性格。如第一尊者长眉罗汉，手撩长眉（已失），含笑侧坐，体现了"慈"；第二尊者托塔罗汉，左手横胸，神态从容，体现了"稳"；其他评酒罗汉"醉"态朦胧，讲经罗汉侃侃而谈，听经罗汉俯首倾听，愁思罗汉眉头紧锁，骄傲罗汉唯我独尊……各具情态。

最具巧思的是东壁北侧的三尊罗汉：降龙罗汉袒胸露臂，怒目簇眉，顺着他的视线望去，柱头上盘着一条虬龙，完全被罗汉咄咄逼人的气势笼罩；旁边的钦佩罗汉全神贯注地观看，他右手摊开，嘴角抿起，似乎在连呼佩服；而他北边的藐视罗汉则架着右腿，摇晃两手，瞥视着虬龙，颇不以为然。

在罗汉殿北侧像龛中还有八尊塑像，是晚明塑工邱弥陀仿照宋代罗汉风格所塑，表情略显僵硬，衬托出宋塑的生动。在西壁第七尊者上方有诸天手持的经盖，自然下垂，褶皱柔畅，飘然如丝绸手卷；在面北的观音像头顶则有印着紫红缠枝牡丹花的绛红色华盖，宛如真丝织品，它们与十六罗汉并称为"金庵三绝"。

3. 轩辕宫正殿：轩辕宫是一处道教宫观，创建于唐贞观二年（628年），曾祭祀伍子胥，因称胥王庙。明代称显灵庙、灵顺宫，民国时期改供轩辕黄帝，始称轩辕宫。

整组建筑位于东山西麓，坐东朝西，原有山门、正殿、碧霞元君祠、城隍庙和火神殿等，现仅存轩辕宫正殿与北侧的城隍庙三进建筑。入口位于北路城隍庙前，今为碑刻陈列室，展出东山发现的明清石刻，其中以阴亭最为珍贵。

这是一座石构仿木六角亭，梁柱、门窗、斗栱和雕饰都刻画精细，亭子正面刻有"叶时敬妻周氏之墓"字样，内部储藏尸骨，是明代一种特殊的墓葬形式。轩辕宫正殿位于城隍庙后部偏南，建于元至正四年（1338年），以"断梁殿"著称。大殿坐东朝西，后依山峰，前有开阔的月台可向东欣赏湖景。

殿宇面阔三间，进深九檩，平面接近正方形，上为单檐歇山屋顶。室内明间金柱上方的檩木为二木对接，技艺巧妙。

殿内构件，如梭形金柱、檐柱，大部分梁架和斗栱都是元代遗构，构件粗壮，结构合理，是研究元代江南建筑的绝佳实例。4. 东山民居：东山民居是一组保存完好的明代民居建筑群，包括明善堂、怀荫堂和凝德堂等。

建筑用料粗大，明间用月梁，结点处设斗栱，并采用荷叶墩、圆栌斗和无斗蜀柱等作法，体现了典型的明代风格。怀荫堂采用前店后宅的格局，凝德堂有72幅精美彩绘，规模最大的是明善堂，南距轩辕宫仅300米。

明善堂坐北朝南，包括东、西两路。入口位于西南角，入门西路包括耳房、客堂和佛楼，楼后为花园；折向右为东部主路，东南角设花厅，正中为主厅。

各房屋之间通过天井、石库门和塞口墙分隔相连，16处天井中9处尚存假山花木。主厅为三开间，两侧带稍间，梁柱、轩架、彩画都很精彩。

厅前正对双面砖雕门楼，外侧相对简朴，内侧雕刻精细，有各种吉祥图案。

· · · · ·
English

Dongshan, also called East Dongting Mountain, is located southwest of Suzhou on the east bank of Lake Tai, with its highest peak Moli Peak facing the Piaomiao Peak of West Dongting Mountain across the lake.

Dongshan has 4 national protected sites: the Republic-era Carved Flower Tower (Chunzai Lou) famous for its carving art; Zijin (Purple Gold) Nunnery with Southern Song painted arhat statues; Xuanyuan Palace built in the Yuan Dynasty; and the Ming-dynasty residences Mingshan Tang, Ningde Tang, and Huaiyin Tang on Yangwan Old Street.

It also has 6 provincial protected sites: Rui'ai Tang, Nianqin Tang nanmu hall, Zhugong Well Pavilion, Wuben Tang, Shaode Tang, and the Sanshan ancient cultural site; 11 municipal protected sites and over 100 Ming-Qing ancient buildings.

Across the water from Dongshan is Xishan (West Mountain) Town.

Dongshan has more scenic spots and historical sites, while Xishan excels in natural scenery, though it also has provincial protected buildings such as Qixian Lane Gate, Jinxiu Tang, Hancun Shop, and Renben Tang.

1.Carved Flower Tower (Chunzai Lou): The main building complex faces east, with three roads north-south.

The middle road is the Carved Flower Tower, from east to west: screen wall, gate tower, front hall, rear hall, and kitchen-dining room; the north road is a garden, the south road is the Zhuangyuan (Top Scholar) Mansion.

Built in the Republic era, the Carved Flower Tower integrates brick carving, wood carving, gold carving, stone carving, and clay sculpture—a masterpiece of Suzhou Xiangshan craftsmen, hailed as "the foremost tower in Jiangnan.

" Its carvings and layout fully reflect a wealthy merchant's tastes and needs.The carvings all contain auspicious meanings.

The ground in front of the gate tower is paved with broken stones forming "a vase with three halberds," meaning "promotion to three ranks," praying for official success and wealth.

The gate tower is covered with brick carvings: on the inner side, the lower lintel carves "Guo Ziyi's Birthday Celebration," with statues of the Fu, Lu, Shou (Fortune, Prosperity, Longevity) Three Stars above; the middle lintel has a bat-bordered brick plaque "Cultivating Virtue," with round carvings "Yao and Shun's Abdication" and "King Wen's Visit to the Sage" on the left and right spandrels; above is a horizontal round carving "Ten Scenes of Fortune and Deer"; the upper lintel has the round carving "Eight Immortals Celebrating Longevity," with five openwork carvings on the arch-supporting plates above—double happiness in the center, ruyi and cords on both sides, symbolizing ruyi passed down through generations.

The roof's vertical ridges mold the Heavenly Official Bestowing Fortune and Carp Leaping Over the Dragon Gate; the main ridge holds a celadon treasure basin with evergreen plants.

Wood carvings are mainly concentrated in the front and rear halls.

The front hall is a five-bay two-story gable-roof building, used for weddings, funerals, and receiving distinguished guests, with the most carvings—arguably the representative work of "Jiangnan full-hall wood carving.

" On the beams are 48 boxwood carvings of "Romance of the Three Kingdoms"; both ends of the crescent beams carve phoenixes, 86 pairs in the whole hall, a homophone for "hundred joys"; the skirt boards of the front eave long windows and half-windows carve the "Twenty-Four Filial Exemplars.

" The rear hall is the activity center for female family members, mainly carving stories from "Romance of the Western Chamber.

" The carving characteristics of the Carved Flower Tower are summarized as: joy when leaving the door, treasure when entering, longevity when looking up, official rank when looking back, money when reaching out, and fortune underfoot—full of straightforward prayers for fortune, longevity, and wealth.

The building layout mainly follows practical needs: the first floor of the front hall is for ceremonies and receiving guests, the first floor of the rear hall is for female family members' activities; the second floors of both halls are connected as a "galloping horse corridor," with bedrooms and guest rooms.

A safe is hidden south of the front hall, and the rear hall has three hidden layers for storing treasures against robbery.

On one hand the owner shows off wealth through exquisite carvings, on the other he racks his brains to protect wealth—the complex human nature of seeking status and guarding wealth is fully revealed in the Carved Flower Tower.

The north garden has mountains and water, with four groups of Taihu rockeries mostly piled against walls, complementing the winding pond with趣味.

The Taihu rocks emphasize figurative appreciation, imitating bears, elephants, eagles, rats, etc., reflecting secular taste.

At the west end is a two-story Buddhist tower, where female family members burn incense and chant.

The south Zhuangyuan Mansion has both residence and garden, exhibiting Dongshan's imperial examination culture.2.

Zijin Nunnery Arhat Statues: Zijin Nunnery is located in the Ximao Valley of East Dongting Mountain, founded in the early Tang, majorly repaired in the High Tang and Southern Song, rebuilt in the early Ming, and expanded during the Qianlong reign of the Qing.

Today the main gate is at the southwest corner; entering straight ahead, the second gate is visible on the left.

The main building complex faces south, with the second gate, Arhat Hall, and Jingyin Hall in sequence.

On the west side are attached Qingchuan Xuan, Baiyun Ju, and Tingsong Tang.The whole complex is not large, nestled among pines and bamboos, simple and elegant.

The most famous in the nunnery are the sixteen arhats (one complete set) sculpted in the Southern Song, which, together with the forty arhats (one set) at Lingyan Temple in Changqing, Jinan, and the nine arhats (half a set) at Baosheng Temple in Luzhi, are called "two complete sets and one half set of arhats under heaven.

" In the center of the Arhat Hall facing south are the Sakyamuni Three Buddhas, with disciples Kashyapa and Ananda standing in between; facing north in the center is the golden statue of Guanyin Viewing the Sea.

The sixteen arhats stand under the east and west walls, eight on each side.

They were created by the Southern Song sculptor masters Lei Chao and his wife—their masterpiece.

The Kangxi-era "Suzhou Prefecture Gazetteer" states: "The Bodhisattva and arhat statues in (Zijin Nunnery) were sculpted by Lei Chao.

Both husband and wife were skilled hands, sculpting only three places in their lifetime, with this nunnery being the foremost.

" Qing scholar Qiu Gengxi highly praised the Zijin Nunnery arhats, having visited famous mountains and ancient temples throughout Suzhou and Hangzhou, finding arhat statues often tall and large, but never with "spirit transcending, seeming alive as at Zijin Nunnery" ("Record of Jingyin Hall of Zijin Nunnery").

This evaluation points out two major characteristics: first, unlike the common method of showing divine power through height, the Zijin Nunnery arhats are life-sized, with seated statues about 1.

2 meters, with well-proportioned heads, bodies, hands, and feet.

Second, these 16 arhats humanize the divine images, giving them rich emotions and personalities through different appearances and expressions.

For example, the first arhat Long-Browed Arhat, lifting his long eyebrows (now lost), sits smiling sideways, embodying "compassion"; the second arhat Pagoda-Holding Arhat, with left hand across his chest, composed in demeanor, embodying "stability"; others include the Wine-Tasting Arhat with hazy "drunken" expression, the Sutra-Preaching Arhat speaking eloquently, the Sutra-Listening Arhat bowing to listen, the Sorrow-Thinking Arhat with furrowed brows, the Proud Arhat with self-importance.

..each with distinct demeanor.

The most ingenious are the three arhats on the north side of the east wall: the Dragon-Subduing Arhat with bare chest and arms, angry eyes and knitted brows—following his gaze, a coiled dragon on the column capital is completely overshadowed by the arhat's imposing aura; beside him, the Admiring Arhat watches intently, right hand open, mouth corners pursed, as if repeatedly exclaiming admiration; while north of him, the Disdaining Arhat crosses his right leg, shakes both hands, and glances at the coiled dragon with considerable disapproval.

In the niche north of the Arhat Hall are eight more statues, sculpted by late-Ming craftsman Qiu Mituo imitating the Song arhat style, with slightly stiff expressions, setting off the vividness of the Song sculptures.

Above the seventh arhat on the west wall is a scripture canopy held by a deva, naturally drooping with soft, smooth folds like a silk handscroll; above the north-facing Guanyin statue's head is a crimson canopy printed with purple-red interlocking peony flowers, like real silk fabric—these, together with the sixteen arhats, are called the "Three Wonders of Zijin Nunnery.

" 3.

Xuanyuan Palace Main Hall: Xuanyuan Palace is a Taoist temple founded in the 2nd year of Zhenguan of the Tang (628), originally sacrificing to Wu Zixu, hence called the Xu King Temple.

In the Ming it was called Xianling Temple and Lingshun Palace; in the Republic era it was changed to enshrine the Yellow Emperor Xuanyuan, hence the name Xuanyuan Palace.

The whole complex is at the western foot of Dongshan, facing west, originally with a gate, main hall, Bixia Yuanjun Shrine, City God Temple, and Fire God Temple—today only the Xuanyuan Palace main hall and the three-bay City God Temple to the north survive.

The entrance is in front of the north City God Temple, now a stele exhibition room displaying Ming-Qing stone carvings found in Dongshan, with the Yin Pavilion being the most precious.

This is a stone structure imitating a wooden hexagonal pavilion, with beams, columns, doors, windows, brackets, and carvings all finely detailed; the front of the pavilion is inscribed "Tomb of Ye Shijing's Wife Zhou," with bones stored inside—a special Ming-dynasty burial form.

The Xuanyuan Palace main hall is south of the rear of the City God Temple, built in the 4th year of Zhizheng of the Yuan (1338), famous as a "Broken Beam Hall.

" The main hall faces west, backed by a mountain peak, with an open platform in front for viewing the lake to the east.

The hall is three bays wide, nine purlins deep, nearly square in plan, with a single-eave hip-and-gable roof.

Inside, the purlin above the central bay's golden columns is formed by two joined pieces of wood—a clever technique.

The hall's components, such as the spindle-shaped golden columns and eave columns, most of the beam frame and brackets, are Yuan-dynasty originals, with sturdy components and reasonable structure—an excellent example for studying Yuan-dynasty Jiangnan architecture.

4.

Dongshan Residences: Dongshan Residences are a well-preserved group of Ming-dynasty residential buildings, including Mingshan Tang, Huaiyin Tang, and Ningde Tang.

The buildings use thick materials, with crescent beams in the central bay, brackets at joints, and techniques such as lotus-leaf piers, round block brackets, and bracketless short columns—reflecting typical Ming style.

Huaiyin Tang adopts a front-shop, rear-residence layout; Ningde Tang has 72 exquisite painted decorations.

The largest is Mingshan Tang, only 300 meters south of Xuanyuan Palace.Mingshan Tang faces south, including east and west roads.

The entrance is at the southwest corner; entering, the west road includes an annex, guest hall, and Buddhist tower, with a garden behind the tower; turning right is the eastern main road, with a flower hall at the southeast corner and the main hall in the center.

The buildings are separated and connected through courtyards, stone-frame doors, and partition walls; among 16 courtyards, 9 still retain rockeries, flowers, and trees.

The main hall is three bays wide with side bays, with excellent beams, ceiling frames, and paintings.

In front of the hall is a double-sided brick-carved gate tower, relatively simple on the outside and exquisitely carved on the inside with various auspicious patterns.

44 甪直镇
Luzhi Town
南朝—清
级别 Level
中国历史文化名镇，保圣寺为第一批国保（1961年）
地址 Address
吴中区甪直镇
类型 Type
历史文化名镇
中文原文

甪直属吴中区，位于苏州东南，传说古代神兽"甪端"曾在此地流连栖居，角端形似麒麟，头仅一角，颇似角字，因而得名。镇内东市河与南市河形成L形，以保圣寺为起点向东北展开，河道西、北两侧为店铺，东、南两侧为住家，与两岸皆为店铺的周庄和两岸皆为住家的同里形成有趣对照。

甪直河多、桥多、古迹多，其中最著名的是保圣寺，由直便围绕此寺逐渐发展繁荣，此外还有唐人陆龟蒙的斗鸭池、叶圣陶《多收了三五斗》中的万盛米行、王韬故居，以及沈氏、萧氏的大宅等。甪直的"船鼻子"独具特色，是河岸上镶嵌的拴船石，大多一尺见方，中部双孔对穿，覆孔石雕刻成芭蕉、如意、寿桃、灵芝、仙鹤等各种花样，精巧雅致。

保圣寺：梁天监二年（503年）笃信佛教的梁武帝倡建保圣寺，唐会昌五年（845年）毁于武宗灭佛，北宋大中祥符六年（1013年）重建，最兴盛时有殿宇5000余间，僧侣上千人，占据了半座甪直镇。

今寺庙包括山门、二门、天王殿和古物馆等，庙西为叶圣陶纪念馆、陆龟蒙墓和斗鸭池。斗鸭池建于明代正德年间，方形水池，池中央立四角清风亭，东西各有石拱桥与岸相通。

寺门北侧为天王殿，明成化二十三年（1487年）在宋代殿址上重建，清同治年间大修，殿前的幡竿夹石和青石经幢为宋代遗物，上刻"宋皇五年（1053年）重立"，铁钟为明代遗物。

天王殿北原为大雄宝殿，内有18尊唐代"塑圣"杨惠之塑造的罗汉，民国初年殿顶倒塌，砸坏了西壁9尊。

蔡元培、马叙伦、顾颉刚等文化界名人为之奔走呼告，组成"唐塑罗汉保存会"，1932年由建筑师范文照设计，将大雄宝殿改为古物馆，保护尚存的9尊罗汉。

杨惠之早年与吴道子一同跟随张僧繇学画，吴道子成名，被唐玄宗召入宫中，尊为"画圣"。杨惠之耻居人后，弃画学塑，最终成为"塑圣"，时有"道子画，惠之塑，夺得僧繇神笔路"的美誉。唐代杨惠之的作品遍布各地，长安、洛阳、开封皆有佳作，可惜泥塑不易保存，甪直保圣寺的罗汉成为他硕果仅存的杰作。

与后世常见的各尊罗汉单独塑造不同，杨惠之的罗汉位于同一墙壁上，壁面塑有山云、石树、洞窟和海水等，营造出"崇卑之土坡，突兀之山崖，卷舒之云气"（大村西崖《吴郡奇迹塑壁残影》），其间上下各处配置罗汉。各尊罗汉与不同的自然环境结合，情态各异，这种巧妙的布置构图，在宋代以后已经失传。

元代赵孟頫为大殿题写的对联称赞"罗汉溯源惠之，为江南佛像无双"，《吴郡甫里志》也称这批罗汉"神光闪耀，形貌如生，真得塑中三昧者。江南北诸郡莫能及"。1926年日本学者大村西崖特来考察参观，称其为"吴郡奇迹"，使保圣寺罗汉名扬海外。

· · · · ·
English

Luzhi belongs to Wuzhong District, located southeast of Suzhou.

Legend says the ancient divine beast "Luduan" once lingered and dwelt here; Luduan resembles a qilin with only one horn on its head, quite like the character "lu" (角), hence the name.

In the town, the East Market River and South Market River form an L-shape, spreading northeast from Baosheng Temple as the starting point.

On the west and north sides of the river are shops, on the east and south sides are residences—forming an interesting contrast with Zhouzhuang (shops on both banks) and Tongli (residences on both banks).

Luzhi has many rivers, bridges, and historical sites, the most famous being Baosheng Temple, around which the town gradually developed and prospered.

Additionally, there are the Tang-dynasty Lu Guimeng's Duck-Fighting Pond, the Wansheng Rice Shop from Ye Shengtao's "A Few More Dou of Harvest," Wang Tao's former residence, and the large mansions of the Shen and Xiao families.

Luzhi's "boat nose" is distinctive—ship-tying stones inlaid on the riverbank, mostly about one chi square, with double holes through the center, and the stone covering the holes carved into various patterns such as banana, ruyi, longevity peach, lingzhi, and crane—exquisite and elegant.

Baosheng Temple: In the 2nd year of Tianjian of the Liang (503), the devout Buddhist Emperor Wu of Liang advocated building Baosheng Temple.

In the 5th year of Huichang of the Tang (845), it was destroyed during Emperor Wuzong's persecution of Buddhism; rebuilt in the 6th year of Dazhong Xiangfu of the Northern Song (1013).

At its peak it had over 5,000 halls and more than a thousand monks, occupying half of Luzhi Town.

Today the temple includes the gate, second gate, Heavenly King Hall, and Antiquities Hall; west of the temple are the Ye Shengtao Memorial Hall, Lu Guimeng's Tomb, and the Duck-Fighting Pond.

The Duck-Fighting Pond was built during the Zhengde reign of the Ming, a square pond with a four-corner Qingfeng (Clear Wind) Pavilion in the center, connected to the banks by stone arch bridges on east and west.

North of the temple gate is the Heavenly King Hall, rebuilt in the 23rd year of Chenghua of the Ming (1487) on a Song-dynasty hall site, majorly repaired during the Tongzhi reign of the Qing.

The banner-pole夹 stones and bluestone pillar in front of the hall are Song-dynasty relics, inscribed "re-erected in the 5th year of Huangyou (1053) of the Song," and the iron bell is a Ming-dynasty relic.

North of the Heavenly King Hall was originally the Mahavira Hall, containing 18 arhats sculpted by the Tang-dynasty "Sculpture Sage" Yang Huizhi.

In the early Republic, the hall roof collapsed, destroying 9 arhats on the west wall.

Cultural figures including Cai Yuanpei, Ma Xulun, and Gu Jiegang campaigned on their behalf, forming the "Tang Sculpture Arhat Preservation Society.

" In 1932, architect Fan Wenzhao designed the conversion of the Mahavira Hall into an Antiquities Hall to protect the 9 surviving arhats.

Yang Huizhi early studied painting with Wu Daozi under Zhang Sengyou; Wu Daozi became famous, was summoned to the palace by Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, and honored as the "Painting Sage.

" Ashamed to be behind, Yang Huizhi abandoned painting for sculpture, ultimately becoming the "Sculpture Sage," with the saying "Daozi's painting, Huizhi's sculpture—seizing the divine brush path of Sengyou.

" Yang Huizhi's works were spread across various places, with masterpieces in Chang'an, Luoyang, and Kaifeng; unfortunately clay sculptures do not survive easily, and the arhats of Luzhi's Baosheng Temple became his only surviving masterpiece.

Unlike later common practice of sculpting each arhat separately, Yang Huizhi's arhats are on the same wall, with the wall surface sculpted with mountain clouds, stone trees, caves, and seawater, creating "lofty and humble earth slopes, precipitous mountain cliffs, rolling and舒展 cloud vapors" (Omura Seigai, "Remnants of Sculpted Walls: Wonders of Wu Commandery"), with arhats arranged at various positions above and below.

Each arhat combines with a different natural environment with distinct expressions—this ingenious composition was lost after the Song Dynasty.

The couplet written by Zhao Mengfu of the Yuan for the main hall praises "Arhats tracing to Huizhi, unmatched among Buddhist statues in Jiangnan"; the "Wujun Fuli Gazetteer" also calls these arhats "divine light shining, lifelike in form and expression, truly attaining the essence of sculpture.

No place north or south of the Yangtze can match.

" In 1926, Japanese scholar Omura Seigai specially came to inspect and visit, calling it a "Wonder of Wu Commandery," making the Baosheng Temple arhats famous overseas.

45 同里镇
Tongli Town
宋—清
级别 Level
中国历史文化名镇，退思园为世界文化遗产、第五批国保（2001年）
地址 Address
吴江区同里镇
类型 Type
历史文化名镇
中文原文

同里镇位于吴江区东北，距苏州市区约20公里，在苏州汽车北站和南站都有汽车直达，流水发车。古镇通票100元，含退思园、嘉荫堂、崇本堂、珍珠塔、耕乐堂、陈去病故居和罗星洲等9处景点。

同里宋代建镇，被8座湖泊环绕，镇区又被15条河流分成7个岛圩，其间通过49座桥梁相连，镇内家家临水，户户通舟，成为古代士绅富豪退隐闲居的理想之地。

古镇今存耕乐堂、三谢堂、明优堂、承恩堂、侍御第和王鹤门楼等明代建筑；退思园、崇本堂、嘉荫堂、务本堂、慎修堂、庆善堂、任氏宗祠、庞氏宗祠和陈去病故居等清代建筑，在江南古镇中独具特色。

1. 退思园：清光绪十一年（1885年）时任安徽凤（阳）颍（州）六（合）泗（州）兵备道按察使（正三品）的任兰生（1837—1888）遭人弹劾罢官，他回乡后聘请同里画家袁龙构筑园林，取《左传》"进则尽忠，退思补过"之意，题名退思园。两年后园林落成，任兰生得到曾国荃等大员保奏，捐复原职，回安徽就任。

是年黄河大水，他刚到颍州便"冒雪奔驰，问民疾苦"，次年二月巡视水灾时，"马惊伤尾闾，病疽，竟以四月十九卒"，年仅51岁（曹允源《任阁学行状》，见《复盦类稿》卷4）。这座费心经营的园池，他未及享用便过世了。

清光绪三十二年（1906年），任兰生之子任传薪（味知）在园中创办丽则女学，开风气之先，直到1916年在退思园东侧建成三层新楼后才将女校迁出。任传薪掌管期间，退思园对外开放，惠及游人。他后来到上海圣约翰大学任教，结识陈从周，经陈氏介绍点评，退思园名声大噪。

2000年被列入世界文化遗产名录。袁龙（1820—1902）字怡孙，号东篱，与其族人袁景辂、袁栋、袁棠皆以诗画著称。袁龙幼承家学，潜心诗画、篆刻、考据之学，曾自建"复斋别墅"。陈去病《五石脂》称赞他："澹泊宁静，悠然物外，尤有遗民之风。所居复斋别墅，亭馆幽静，花木扶疏，闻皆先生躬操锸凿为之，故极得真趣。"由袁龙主持设计的退思园，简朴淡雅，深得画意幽趣。

退思园为宅第附园，处在住宅东侧，宅、园自西向东一路铺开，与传统宅园南北布置的惯例迥异。西路相当于外堂部分，自南向北有门厅、茶厅和正厅共三进，作会客之用。中路为内宅部分，是一圈两层走马楼，供主人和内眷居住。东侧为园林，又分为东、西两园。西园较小，是一座规整的庭院，为入园前导。院西小斋东西向，在东侧山面上开门，南北开和合窗，模仿画舫，宛如待航之舟，将人引向东部花园，东园门前障以湖石花台。

院北是五间坐春望月楼，楼东建有揽胜阁，伸入东园，当年女眷们可以坐在阁中欣赏园景。绕过院东湖石，经月洞门进入东园，为伸向池中的水芗榭。这座敞榭既是连接两园的节点，也是东向赏月的佳处。沿游廊向北，尽处为揽胜阁，折向东，经过一座小轩，到达主厅退思草堂。退思园被陈从周誉为"贴水园"的典范，"山、亭、馆、廊、轩、榭等皆紧贴水面，园如浮水上"（《说园·四》）。

草堂南部建有平台，前临水池，是畅览园景的最佳场所；西侧的水芗榭挑出水面，檐角高翘。绕到西南，"闹红一舸"画舫被湖石凌波托起，宛若扬波而行。这座画舫小巧玲珑、雕琢精细，成为全园的点睛之笔。水池南岸是两层的辛台和菰雨生凉轩，二者通过两层的复道长廊相连，宛转有致。廊北特置一尊高耸的"丈人峰"，作为北岸草堂的对景。

池西堆筑湖石假山，与其他三面的亭台廊榭相对照，饶有自然风味。山顶设眠云亭，可临眺园景。假山北部架有三曲桥，通向草堂东部的琴房，前对一湾静水，适合观鱼拍曲。

退思园宅园面积为九亩八分，园林仅约四亩，围绕中部的荷花池，通过建筑的布置联络、对照呼应，形成丰富的空间层次；山峰湖石、莲荷乔木的点缀穿插，则为人工的细致营造补入了天然气息，共同构成一座精雅别致的园林。2. 耕乐堂：耕乐堂位于古镇西侧陆家埭上，最初为明代处士朱祥（字廷瑞，号耕乐）所建。

据清嘉庆《同里志》卷15记载，明正统年间朱祥协助工部侍郎周忱修筑苏州宝带桥，因贡献巨大得以勒名于石，朝廷想授官给他，但朱祥"决志归隐，引疾家居，一时达官敬重之"。他退居同里后建造了耕乐堂，"日与邻翁、野叟徜徉山水间，于所居构燕翼楼，与宾客故旧觞咏其中"，《吴江志》的作者莫旦（1429—？）为撰堂记。

朱祥卒后，祝枝山为他撰写了墓志铭（《续同里先哲志·卷6》），耕乐堂则数易其主。现存建筑主要建于清乾隆、咸丰年间，清末归仲仰梁所有，新中国成立后曾作为育青中学校舍，后归地方福利院。1998年开始修缮，2002年竣工开放。耕乐堂坐西朝东，东面临河，采用前宅后园的布局。

前部住宅包括南、北两路，其间隔以狭窄的备弄。南为主路，自东向西依次为跨街廊、门厅、堂楼和绣楼。堂楼、绣楼都采用"三明两暗"的合院形制，虽为五间但院中只能看到三间。绣楼前加设一门，区隔内外。北为辅路，是后期并购的潘家房产，由门厅、正厅和花厅组成。后部花园以鸳鸯厅为区隔，南部为旱院，北部为水院。

鸳鸯厅是园中主厅，南北向，南面正对三友亭，亭旁植有松、竹、梅，与鸳鸯厅通过折廊相连。鸳鸯厅西是一处天井小院，采用《园冶·掇山》"以粉壁为纸，以石为绘"的手法，紧靠厅墙堆筑一座黄石假山，作为燕翼楼的对景。

燕翼楼高两层，上层四面开窗，登楼西望，可欣赏同里八景的"西津晚渡"；朝北的圆窗则可借景白皮松，构成一幅图画。这株白皮松植于明代，已有400余年，倚靠着湖石，俯临水池。其北是古松轩，可倚在轩内美人靠上赏鱼听松。

沿游廊到达北岸，与鸳鸯厅隔池相对的是二层环秀阁，建于清乾隆四十五年（1780年），阁跨在池上，有如浮水之舟，下层地板可自由开启，便于取水观鱼，手法独特。阁东以飞廊与墨香阁相连，后者建于清同治年间，原为潘宅藏书楼，风格较为朴实。耕乐堂花园的精华在北部水院。

围绕着中央水池，南岸鸳鸯厅贴水而筑，古朴典雅；其西燕翼楼轻盈飘逸，天井内的黄石假山，浑厚而空灵；池白皮松斜临水面，如龙戏珠；北岸环秀阁横跨水上，雕镂精致。水池四周的亭台楼阁布局紧凑，充溢着隐逸气息，与前部的住宅共同营造出一处理想的居所。

3. 嘉荫堂：嘉荫堂位于同里镇竹行街134号，2011年列为省保单位。1922年柳炳南建，共有四进32间，内有精美的木雕和石雕。穿过门厅，第二进正厅为明式建筑，因梁头棹木形似明代官员的帽翅，被称作纱帽厅。

厅内五架梁两侧中心刻《八骏图》、两端刻《凤穿牡丹图》，梁头棹木的纱帽翅上刻《三英战吕布》《三顾茅庐》《草船借箭》等八幅《三国演义》戏文透雕，生动逼真。正厅后的庭院中有湖石花台和曲廊半亭，院北为内宅堂楼衍庆楼。整组建筑的西北角还有一座水秀阁，在阁内可观望外面的河流游船，欣赏著名的"同里三桥"。4. 三桥：长庆桥、太平桥、吉利桥：三桥位于嘉荫堂西北，呈"品"字形跨在三河交汇处，成为古镇一道独特的风景。

同里人有"走三桥"的习俗，人们在绕行三桥时，口中念叨桥的名字"太平吉利长庆"，以此祈求幸福和好运。当地还流传着不同年龄人"走三桥"的谚语："小巴戏（孩童），走三桥，读书聪明，成绩年年好；小姑娘，走三桥，天生丽质，越长越苗条；小伙子，走三桥，平步青云，前程无限好；老年人，走三桥，鹤发童颜，寿比南山高；新郎新娘走三桥，心心相印，白首同偕老。

"5. 崇本堂：崇本堂位于同里镇富观街18号，与嘉荫堂隔河相望，2011年列为省保单位。1912年钱幼琴购得顾氏旧宅，翻建成崇本堂，有门厅、正厅、前楼、后楼和下房共五进，木雕100余幅。穿过门厅，背面有砖雕门楼，刻"崇德思本"四字。

正厅现为婚礼厅，展示当地传统的婚庆习俗，厅长窗的腰板上雕刻14幅《西厢记》故事，形象生动。前楼现为福寿堂，展示传统的拜寿习俗，长窗腰板上刻有《红楼梦》十二金钗图。

· · · · ·
English

Tongli Town is located northeast of Wujiang District, about 20 km from Suzhou city center, with direct buses from both Suzhou North and South Bus Stations running regularly.

The ancient town all-inclusive ticket is 100 yuan, including 9 attractions: Tuisi Garden, Jiayin Hall, Chongben Hall, Pearl Tower, Gengle Hall, Chen Qubing's Former Residence, and Luoxing Zhou.

Tongli was established as a town in the Song Dynasty, surrounded by 8 lakes, with the town area divided by 15 rivers into 7 island-weirs connected by 49 bridges.

Every family faces water and every household has boat access—an ideal place for ancient gentry and wealthy merchants to retire and live in seclusion.

The ancient town today preserves Ming-dynasty buildings such as Gengle Hall, Sanxie Hall, Mingyou Hall, Cheng'en Hall, Shiyu Di, and Wanghe Gate Tower; and Qing-dynasty buildings such as Tuisi Garden, Chongben Hall, Jiayin Hall, Wuben Hall, Shenxiu Hall, Qingshan Hall, Ren Family Ancestral Hall, Pang Family Ancestral Hall, and Chen Qubing's Former Residence—unique among Jiangnan ancient towns.

1.

Tuisi Garden (Retreat and Reflection Garden): In the 11th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1885), Ren Lansheng (1837-1888), then the (third rank) Administration Commissioner and Circuit Intendant of Fengyang, Yingzhou, Liuhe, and Sizhou in Anhui, was impeached and dismissed from office.

After returning home, he hired Tongli painter Yuan Long to construct a garden, taking the meaning from the "Zuo Zhuan": "When advancing, serve with complete loyalty; when retreating, reflect on and remedy faults"—naming it Tuisi Garden (Retreat and Reflection Garden).

Two years later the garden was completed; Ren Lansheng obtained recommendations from high officials such as Zeng Guoquan, donated to restore his original rank, and returned to office in Anhui.

That year the Yellow River flooded; upon arriving in Yingzhou he "raced through snow, inquiring into people's sufferings," and the following February while inspecting flood damage, "his horse startled, injuring his tailbone; he developed an abscess and died on April 19" at only 51 (Cao Yunyuan, "Biography of Ren Ge," in "Fuan Leigao" vol.

4).He did not live to enjoy this carefully crafted garden.

In the 32nd year of Guangxu (1906), Ren Lansheng's son Ren Chuanxin (Weizhi) founded the Lize Girls' School in the garden, a pioneering effort, until 1916 when a three-story new building was completed east of Tuisi Garden and the girls' school moved out.

During Ren Chuanxin's management, Tuisi Garden was open to the public, benefiting visitors.He later taught at St.

John's University in Shanghai, where he met Chen Congzhou; through Chen's introduction and commentary, Tuisi Garden became widely famous.In 2000 it was inscribed on the World Cultural Heritage List.

Yuan Long (1820-1902), style name Yisun, hao Dongli, and his clan members Yuan Jinglu, Yuan Dong, and Yuan Tang were all known for poetry and painting.

Yuan Long inherited family learning, devoting himself to poetry, painting, seal carving, and textual research, and once built the "Fuzhai Villa.

" Chen Qubing's "Wushizhi" praised him: "Detached and serene, beyond worldly concerns, especially with the spirit of a loyalist.

His Fuzhai Villa has quiet pavilions and halls with lush flowers and trees, all said to be personally planted and built by him, hence extremely authentic.

" The Tuisi Garden designed by Yuan Long is simple and elegant, deeply capturing the poetic charm of painting.

Tuisi Garden is an attached garden of a residence, located east of the residence, with residence and garden spreading from west to east—unlike the traditional north-south layout of residence-gardens.

The west road is equivalent to the outer hall section, with three bays from south to north: gate hall, tea hall, and main hall, for receiving guests.

The middle road is the inner residence section, a two-story "galloping horse corridor" building for the master and female family members.

The east side is the garden, divided into east and west gardens.The west garden is smaller, a regular courtyard serving as the introductory space before entering the garden.

The west small studio faces east-west, with doors on the east gable wall and he-he windows on north and south, imitating a painted boat—like a vessel about to sail, guiding visitors toward the eastern garden.

In front of the east garden gate, a Taihu rock flower terrace serves as a screen.

North of the courtyard is a five-bay Zuochun Wangyue Lou (Sitting in Spring, Gazing at Moon Tower), with the Lansheng Ge (Gathering Scenery Pavilion) extending east into the east garden, where female family members could sit and admire the garden scenery in olden days.

Passing around the east garden's Taihu rocks and through a moon gate, one enters the east garden to the Shuixiang Xie (Water Fragrance Pavilion) extending into the pond.

This open pavilion is both a node connecting the two gardens and an excellent place for moon-viewing facing east.

Following the corridor north, at the end is the Lansheng Ge; turning east, passing a small studio, one reaches the main hall Tuisi Caotang (Retreat and Reflection Thatched Hall).

Tuisi Garden is hailed by Chen Congzhou as a model of the "water-hugging garden": "mountains, pavilions, halls, corridors, studios, and pavilions all hug the water surface, the garden as if floating on water" ("On Gardens·Four").

South of the thatched hall is a platform facing the pond—the best place for unobstructed garden views; the west Shuixiang Xie cantilevers over the water with high upturned eaves.

Circling to the southwest, the "Naohong Yige" painted boat is lifted above the waves by Taihu rocks, as if sailing on the water.

This painted boat is small and exquisite with fine carvings, becoming the focal point of the whole garden.

South of the pond are the two-story Xintai and Guyu Shengliang Xuan, connected by a two-story double corridor, gracefully winding.

North of the corridor stands a tall "Zhangren Peak" (Elder Peak) as the opposite scene for the north bank's thatched hall.

West of the pond, a Taihu rockery is piled, contrasting with the pavilions, terraces, and corridors on the other three sides, rich in natural flavor.

At the top of the mountain is the Mianyun Pavilion (Sleeping Cloud Pavilion) for overlooking the garden.

North of the rockery, a three-bend bridge leads to the qin (zither) room east of the thatched hall, facing a quiet bay of water—suitable for watching fish and playing the qin.

Tuisi Garden's residence-garden area is nine mu and eight fen, with the garden only about four mu.

Around the central lotus pond, through the arrangement, connection, and contrast of buildings, rich spatial layers are formed; the interspersing of peak rocks, lotuses, and tall trees adds natural charm to the meticulous artificial construction—together forming an exquisite and refined garden.

2.Gengle Hall: Gengle Hall is located on Lujiadai in the west of the ancient town, originally built by Ming-dynasty scholar Zhu Xiang (style name Tingrui, hao Gengle).

According to the 15th volume of the Jiaqing-era "Tongli Gazetteer," during the Zhengtong reign of the Ming, Zhu Xiang assisted Zhou Chen, Vice Minister of Works, in building the Suzhou Baodai Bridge; for his great contribution his name was inscribed on stone, and the court wanted to appoint him official, but Zhu Xiang "resolved to retire, citing illness and staying at home, respected by high officials of the time.

" After retiring to Tongli he built Gengle Hall, "daily wandering among mountains and waters with neighboring elders and rustic scholars, constructing the Yanyi Tower in his residence, drinking and composing poetry with guests and old friends there.

" Mo Dan (1429-?), author of the "Wujiang Gazetteer," wrote a record for the hall.After Zhu Xiang's death, Zhu Zhishan wrote his epitaph ("Continued Records of Tongli's Former Sages·Vol.

6"), while Gengle Hall changed owners several times.

The surviving buildings were mainly constructed during the Qianlong and Xianfeng reigns of the Qing; in the late Qing it belonged to Zhong Yangliang; after the founding of New China it served as the Yuqing Middle School dormitory, later as a local welfare home.

Restoration began in 1998 and was completed and opened in 2002.Gengle Hall faces west with its east side by the river, adopting a front-residence, rear-garden layout.

The front residence includes south and north roads, separated by a narrow service alley.

The south is the main road, from east to west: cross-street corridor, gate hall, main hall tower, and embroidery tower.

Both the main hall tower and embroidery tower adopt the "three bright, two dark" courtyard form—though five bays, only three are visible from the courtyard.

A gate is added in front of the embroidery tower to separate inner and outer.The north is the secondary road, a Pan family property acquired later, consisting of gate hall, main hall, and flower hall.

The rear garden uses the Yuanyang (Mandarin Duck) Hall as a divider, with a dry courtyard to the south and a water courtyard to the north.

The Mandarin Duck Hall is the main hall of the garden, facing north-south, directly facing the Sanyou (Three Friends) Pavilion to the south, with pine, bamboo, and plum planted beside it, connected to the Mandarin Duck Hall by a winding corridor.

West of the Mandarin Duck Hall is a small courtyard, using the method from "Yuanye·Rockery Piling": "using the white wall as paper, rocks as painting," piling a yellow-stone rockery against the hall wall as the opposite scene for the Yanyi Tower.

The Yanyi Tower is two stories with windows on all four sides; climbing the tower and looking west, one can admire the "Xijin Evening Ferry" of Tongli's Eight Scenes; the north-facing round window borrows the view of a lacebark pine, forming a painting.

This lacebark pine was planted in the Ming, over 400 years old, leaning against Taihu rocks and overlooking the pond.

North of it is the Gusong Xuan (Ancient Pine Studio), where one can lean on the beauty's rest to watch fish and listen to pines.

Following the corridor to the north bank, facing the Mandarin Duck Hall across the pond, is the two-story Huanxiu Ge (Surrounding Beauty Pavilion), built in the 45th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1780), spanning across the pond like a floating boat; the lower floor can be freely opened for fetching water and watching fish—a unique technique.

East of the pavilion, a flying corridor connects to the Moxiang Ge (Ink Fragrance Pavilion), built during the Tongzhi reign of the Qing, originally the Pan family's library, with a relatively simple style.

The essence of Gengle Hall's garden is the northern water courtyard.

Around the central pond, the south bank Mandarin Duck Hall is built against the water, simple and elegant; its west Yanyi Tower is light and graceful, with the yellow-stone rockery in the courtyard solid yet airy; the pond lacebark pine leans over the water like a dragon playing with a pearl; the north bank Huanxiu Ge spans across the water, exquisitely carved.

The pavilions and towers around the pond are compactly arranged, full of a reclusive atmosphere, together with the front residence creating an ideal dwelling place.3.

Jiayin Hall: Jiayin Hall is located at No.134 Zhuhang Street, Tongli Town, designated a provincial protected site in 2011.

Built in 1922 by Liu Bingnan, it has four bays and 32 rooms, with exquisite wood and stone carvings inside.

Passing through the gate hall, the second bay main hall is a Ming-style building; because the beam-end bracket wood resembles the hat wings of Ming-dynasty officials, it is called the Shamao (Official Hat) Hall.

Inside the hall, the center of both sides of the five-purlin beam carves the "Eight Steeds"; both ends carve the "Phoenix Piercing Peony"; on the official-hat wings of the beam-end brackets are carved eight openwork scenes from "Romance of the Three Kingdoms" such as "Three Heroes Fight Lu Bu," "Three Visits to the Thatched Cottage," and "Borrowing Arrows with Thatched Boats"—vivid and lifelike.

In the courtyard behind the main hall are a Taihu rock flower terrace and a winding corridor half-pavilion; north of the courtyard is the inner residence tower Yanqing Lou.

At the northwest corner of the whole complex is a waterside pavilion, from which one can watch the river boats outside and admire the famous "Three Bridges of Tongli." 4.

Three Bridges: Changqing Bridge, Taiping Bridge, Jili Bridge: Located northwest of Jiayin Hall, the three bridges span the confluence of three rivers in a "pin" (品) shape, becoming a unique scenery of the ancient town.

Tongli people have the custom of "walking the three bridges"; while circling the three bridges, they recite the bridge names "Taiping (Peace), Jili (Auspicious), Changqing (Long Celebration)" to pray for happiness and good fortune.

There are also proverbs for people of different ages "walking the three bridges": "Little children, walk the three bridges—study smart, grades good year after year; young girls, walk the three bridges—natural beauty, growing ever more slender; young men, walk the three bridges—rapid advancement, boundless prospects; elderly people, walk the three bridges—white hair and youthful face, longevity higher than the southern mountains; bride and groom walk the three bridges—hearts united, growing old together.

" 5.Chongben Hall: Chongben Hall is located at No.18 Fuguan Street, Tongli Town, facing Jiayin Hall across the river, designated a provincial protected site in 2011.

In 1912, Qian Youqin purchased the old Gu family residence and rebuilt it as Chongben Hall, with five bays: gate hall, main hall, front tower, rear tower, and servants' quarters, with over 100 wood carvings.

Passing through the gate hall, on the back is a brick-carved gate tower inscribed with the four characters "Chongde Siben" (Honoring Virtue, Reflecting on Roots).

The main hall is now a Wedding Hall, displaying local traditional wedding customs; the waist panels of the hall's long windows carve 14 scenes from "Romance of the Western Chamber," vivid and lively.

The front tower is now the Fortune and Longevity Hall, displaying traditional birthday-worship customs; the waist panels of the long windows carve the Twelve Beauties of "Dream of the Red Chamber."

建筑要点 / Key Features
8座湖泊环绕15条河流7个岛圩49座桥梁；退思园任兰生袁龙；贴水园典范；耕乐堂明代处士朱祥；嘉荫堂纱帽厅三国演义木雕；三桥长庆太平吉利
46 思本桥
Siben Bridge
宋
级别 Level
第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
地址 Address
吴江区同里镇辽浜村
类型 Type
古桥
中文原文

据清嘉庆《同里志》记载，思本桥为南宋宝祐年间（1253—1258）诗人叶茵所建，又称思汾桥，是吴江现存最古老的石桥。这是一座单孔石拱桥，东西走向，跨在同里镇西南辽浜的水道上。桥身全用武康石（紫石），采用分节并列法砌筑，部分石阶后来改为花岗石。

桥全长22.5米，宽1.8米，跨度为9米，矢高4.5米，恰好构成半圆形桥洞，桥孔与水中倒影相接，形成一个完美的圆形。

· · · · ·
English

According to the Jiaqing-era "Tongli Gazetteer" of the Qing, Siben Bridge was built by poet Ye Yin during the Baoyou reign of the Southern Song (1253-1258), also called Sifen Bridge.

It is the oldest surviving stone bridge in Wujiang.This is a single-arch stone bridge, oriented east-west, spanning the waterway at Liaobang southwest of Tongli Town.

The bridge body is entirely made of Wukang stone (purple stone), built using the segmented parallel method, with some stone steps later changed to granite.The bridge has a total length of 22.

5 meters, width of 1.8 meters, span of 9 meters, and rise of 4.

5 meters—exactly forming a semicircular arch opening, with the arch opening and its reflection in the water joining to form a perfect circle.

47 黎里镇柳亚子旧居
Former Residence of Liu Yazi in Lili Town
1922—1937
级别 Level
第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
地址 Address
黎里镇浒泾街15号
类型 Type
名人故居
开放时间 Hours
8:30—11:30、13:00—16:30免费开放
中文原文

柳亚子故居原为清乾隆年间直隶总督、工部尚书周元理的府第"赐福堂"，始建于清康熙年间，现存六进，今为柳亚子纪念馆，是研究柳亚子和南社的重要基地。1899年柳亚子的母亲租得尚书第的第四、五进，柳亚子（1887—1958）从12岁到41岁的大部分时间都生活在这里。

前两进为门厅和茶厅，第三进大厅展出柳亚子创办的《新黎里报》，见证了他早年的民主革命活动。第四进为赐福堂，柳亚子领导南社20余年，这里是当时南社诗友集会的场所，目前展出与南社有关的照片、文稿和出版物，以及柳亚子的生平照片、往来书信和诗稿著作等。第五进是藏书楼，1927年国民党军警到黎里搜捕柳亚子，柳亚子便是躲在藏书楼二楼的厢橱间逃过一劫。

在黎里镇浒泾街4号和6号，还有周元理从兄周玉图的旧宅"鸿寿堂"，建于明代，原有七进，现存五进，2011年被列为省保单位。

· · · · ·
English

The former residence of Liu Yazi was originally the mansion "Cifu Tang" (Blessing Hall) of Zhou Yuanli, Viceroy of Zhili and Minister of Works during the Qianlong reign of the Qing, first built during the Kangxi reign of the Qing, with six bays surviving today.

It is now the Liu Yazi Memorial Hall, an important base for researching Liu Yazi and the Southern Society (Nanshe).

In 1899, Liu Yazi's mother rented the fourth and fifth bays of the Minister's Mansion; Liu Yazi (1887-1958) lived here for most of the time from age 12 to 41.

The first two bays are the gate hall and tea hall; the third bay main hall exhibits the "New Lili News" founded by Liu Yazi, witnessing his early democratic revolutionary activities.

The fourth bay is Cifu Tang; Liu Yazi led the Southern Society for over 20 years, and this was the gathering place for Southern Society poet friends at that time.

Currently it displays photos, manuscripts, and publications related to the Southern Society, as well as Liu Yazi's life photos, correspondence, and poetic manuscripts and works.

The fifth bay is the library tower; in 1927, when Nationalist military police came to Lili to arrest Liu Yazi, he hid in the side cabinet room on the second floor of the library tower and escaped.

At Nos.

4 and 6 Hujing Street, Lili Town, there is also the "Hongshou Tang" (Longevity Hall), the former residence of Zhou Yutu, Zhou Yuanli's cousin, built in the Ming Dynasty, originally with seven bays, five surviving today, designated a provincial protected site in 2011.

建筑要点 / Key Features
清乾隆年间直隶总督工部尚书周元理府第赐福堂；柳亚子12岁到41岁大部分时间生活；南社创始人；1927年国民党军警搜捕藏身藏书楼二楼厢橱间；鸿寿堂明代周元理从兄周玉图旧宅
48 盛泽镇先蚕祠
Silkworm God Temple in Shengze Town
清
级别 Level
第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
地址 Address
吴江区盛泽镇五龙路南口
类型 Type
祠庙
门票 Ticket
10元
开放时间 Hours
8:30—18:00
中文原文

先蚕祠俗称蚕花殿，清道光二十年（1840年）盛泽丝业公所建，祭祀蚕神嫘祖，同时作为公所议事之地。祠庙坐北朝南，今存门楼、正殿和偏殿等。门楼宽三间，上有精美的雕刻，正中开三座拱门，背后建戏台，向北面对高敞的正殿。正殿供奉嫘祖、黄帝和炎帝，殿前广场可容纳数千人。西侧近年新建了吴江丝绸陈列馆和后花园。

古代在江浙地区有多座祭祀蚕丝业祖师的公祠，如今仅剩盛泽先蚕祠，弥足珍贵。

· · · · ·
English

Xiancan Temple, commonly called Canhua Hall (Silkworm Flower Hall), was built in the 20th year of Daoguang of the Qing (1840) by the Shengze Silk Guild, sacrificing to the silkworm goddess Leizu, and also serving as a meeting place for the guild.

The temple faces south, with the gate tower, main hall, and side halls surviving today.

The gate tower is three bays wide with exquisite carvings, with three arch doors in the center and a stage built behind, facing the spacious main hall to the north.

The main hall enshrines Leizu, the Yellow Emperor, and the Yan Emperor; the square in front of the hall can accommodate thousands of people.

On the west side, the Wujiang Silk Exhibition Hall and rear garden were newly built in recent years.

In ancient times, there were many public temples in the Jiangsu-Zhejiang region sacrificing to the founder of the silk industry; today only the Shengze Xiancan Temple remains—extremely precious.

建筑要点 / Key Features
俗称蚕花殿；清道光二十年盛泽丝业公所建；祭祀蚕神嫘祖；门楼正中开三座拱门背后建戏台；正殿供奉嫘祖黄帝炎帝；江浙地区仅存祭祀蚕丝业祖师的公祠
49 震泽镇
Zhenze Town
宋—清
级别 Level
中国历史文化名镇，师俭堂为第六批国保（2006年），慈云寺塔为第七批国保（2013年）
地址 Address
吴江区震泽镇
类型 Type
历史文化名镇
门票 Ticket
古镇通票55元，含师俭堂、慈云寺塔和阊三处景点
开放时间 Hours
8:00—17:00
中文原文

震泽镇位于盛泽镇西南，可从吴江汽车站乘坐汽车到震泽，再转301、302公交车到师俭堂站，或自驾沿318国道到达。古镇通票55元，含师俭堂、慈云寺塔和阊三处景点。1. 师俭堂：师俭堂为清同治三年（1864年）徐氏先祖徐汝福建。

徐氏是震泽首富，号称"徐半镇"，世代经营米业、丝行及房地产等，此宅取《史记·萧相国世家》"后世贤，师吾俭；不贤，毋为势家所夺"之意，命名为"师俭堂"，实则极为豪华。宅第坐北朝南，前后共六进，以宝塔街为分隔，南侧两进，北侧四进，形成罕见的"宅内含街"格局。南侧原为高茂记米行，前部临河建码头，门屋高两层，两侧有飞翘的马头墙；第二进是米行商铺。

铺后是宝塔街，向东可望见慈云寺塔；第三进为住宅门厅，临街建有4米宽的木雕门楼，月梁上雕状元及第、刘备招亲等故事。门厅北部为第四进师俭堂，是一座宽五间的敞厅，厅内布满故事雕刻。堂北的砖雕门楼，采用透雕、高浮雕和线刻等多种手法雕刻。

门内第五、六进为二层走马楼，也有木雕和砖雕。主人的财力和工匠的技艺，主要便体现在这些精美的木雕和砖雕上。由第五进向东，是宅第内园锄经园，面积很小，被称作"江南最小的园林"，但园亭虽小，亭台楼阁，假山花木，一应俱全，饶有幽趣。

2. 慈云寺塔：慈云禅寺始建于南宋咸淳年间（1265—1274），当时便有慈云寺塔。明正统年间重建寺、塔，明万历五年（1577年）重修，后又重建大悲阁等建筑。

清乾隆五十三年（1788年）重修并增建钟楼，开凿洗钵池。清咸丰十年（1860年）寺庙毁于兵火，仅存佛塔。

1924年恢复寺院，重建山门、天王殿等。1926年塔的第五层被风吹坍，两年后修复。1937年遭到日军炮击，削去第四层的飞角廊柱。1982年、1998年两次重修。

2004年整治塔周边环境，挖掘出原大殿遗址和放生池，从池中发现了原大殿内的十八尊青石罗汉。慈云寺塔是一座六角五层木檐楼阁式砖塔，由回廊、塔壁和塔心室组成。从第二层起各层皆有平座腰檐，各层三面开壶门，上下层互相错开，避免形成通缝。第四、五层内有楠木刹柱直贯到顶端。

塔刹由铁质覆钵、仰莲、五重相轮、宝盖、宝珠、受花和铜质宝瓶等组成，仰莲中有明万历五年重修时的铸刻文字。该塔外观翼角轻举，玲珑挺秀，塔旁建有禹迹桥，拱桥塔影，共同构成水乡特有的恬静景色。

· · · · ·
English

Zhenze Town is located southwest of Shengze Town.One can take a bus from Wujiang Bus Station to Zhenze, then transfer to bus 301 or 302 to the Shijian Hall stop, or drive along National Highway 318.

The ancient town all-inclusive ticket is 55 yuan, including three attractions: Shijian Hall, Ciyun Temple Pagoda, and Chang.1.

Shijian Hall: Shijian Hall was built in the 3rd year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1864) by Xu Rufu, ancestor of the Xu family.

The Xu family was the wealthiest in Zhenze, known as "Xu Half-Town," generationally operating rice business, silk shops, and real estate.

This residence takes the meaning from "Records of the Grand Historian·Hereditary House of Chancellor Xiao": "If descendants are worthy, they will learn my frugality; if not worthy, they will not be seized by powerful families"—naming it "Shijian Hall" (Learning Frugality Hall), though in reality it is extremely luxurious.

The residence faces south, with six bays front to back, separated by Baota (Pagoda) Street: two bays on the south side, four on the north side—forming a rare "residence containing a street" layout.

The south side was originally the Gaomaoji Rice Shop, with a dock built by the river at the front; the gate house is two stories high, with upturned horse-head walls on both sides; the second bay is the rice shop.

Behind the shop is Baota Street, with Ciyun Temple Pagoda visible to the east; the third bay is the residential gate hall, with a 4-meter-wide wood-carved gate tower facing the street, with crescent beams carved with stories such as "Top Scholar Passing the Exam" and "Liu Bei's Marriage.

" North of the gate hall is the fourth bay Shijian Hall, a five-bay open hall filled with story carvings.

The brick-carved gate tower north of the hall uses multiple techniques such as openwork, high relief, and line carving.

Inside the gate, the fifth and sixth bays are two-story galloping horse corridor buildings, also with wood and brick carvings.

The owner's wealth and the craftsmen's skill are mainly reflected in these exquisite wood and brick carvings.

East from the fifth bay is the inner garden Chujing Yuan (Weeding Classics Garden), very small in area, called "the smallest garden in Jiangnan"; though small, it has pavilions, terraces, towers, rockeries, flowers, and trees—all complete, with secluded charm.

2.Ciyun Temple Pagoda: Ciyun Chan Temple was founded during the Xianchun reign of the Southern Song (1265-1274), when the Ciyun Temple Pagoda already existed.

The temple and pagoda were rebuilt during the Zhengtong reign of the Ming, repaired in the 5th year of Wanli of the Ming (1577), and later the Great Compassion Pavilion and other buildings were rebuilt.

In the 53rd year of Qianlong of the Qing (1788), it was repaired and a bell tower added, with the Alms-Bowl Washing Pond dug.

In the 10th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1860), the temple was destroyed by war, with only the Buddhist pagoda surviving.

In 1924 the temple was restored, with the gate and Heavenly King Hall rebuilt.In 1926 the fifth story of the pagoda collapsed in the wind, repaired two years later.

In 1937 it was shelled by Japanese forces, with the flying corner corridor columns of the fourth story削去.It was repaired twice in 1982 and 1998.

In 2004 the environment around the pagoda was renovated, excavating the original main hall site and the Free Life Pond, from which eighteen bluestone arhats from the original main hall were discovered.

Ciyun Temple Pagoda is a hexagonal five-story wooden-eave pavilion-style brick pagoda, composed of a surrounding corridor, pagoda wall, and central chamber.

From the second story upward, each story has a flat seat and waist eave; each story has pot-shaped doors on three sides, with upper and lower stories staggered to avoid continuous cracks.

Inside the fourth and fifth stories, a nanmu finial pillar runs straight through to the top.

The finial consists of an iron inverted bowl, upward lotus, five-layer chatra, treasure canopy, pearl, receiving flower, and copper treasure vase, with cast inscriptions from the 5th year of Wanli of the Ming repair on the upward lotus.

The pagoda's appearance has light upturned corners, exquisite and upright; beside the pagoda is the Yuji (Yu's Footprint) Bridge, with the arch bridge and pagoda reflection together forming the tranquil scenery characteristic of water towns.

建筑要点 / Key Features
师俭堂徐半镇宅内含街格局；江南最小的园林锄经园；慈云寺塔六角五层木檐楼阁式砖塔；南宋咸淳年间始建；禹迹桥拱桥塔影
50 七都镇东庙桥
Dongmiao Bridge in Qidu Town
宋
级别 Level
第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
地址 Address
吴江区七都镇东庙桥村横沽塘
类型 Type
古桥
中文原文

东庙桥中孔石梁上刻有"绍定"字样，推测建于南宋绍定年间（1228—1233）。

这是一座三跨石梁桥，东西走向，全长21.5米，中部宽2.1米，头尾宽2.75米，中孔跨度4.6米，高4.31米。桥身主体用武康石构筑，民国年间增置花岗岩栏杆和望柱。

桥面下设六根石梁，端头高31厘米，中部高51厘米，梁间铺石板，使桥面略呈拱形。桥底盘石和排柱浑厚稳重，排柱与横系石平接严密，受力匀称。梁下长石系石上有四个半月形孔，建桥时用来安置托木。桥石有精美的雕刻，如次孔梁端的如意云图案，为"八宝纹"之一，飘逸生动。

· · · · ·
English

The central opening's stone beam of Dongmiao Bridge is inscribed with the characters "Shaoding,"推测 built during the Shaoding reign of the Southern Song (1228-1233).

This is a three-span stone beam bridge, oriented east-west, with a total length of 21.5 meters, central width of 2.1 meters, end width of 2.75 meters, central span of 4.6 meters, and height of 4.

31 meters.The main body of the bridge is constructed of Wukang stone, with granite railings and baluster posts added during the Republic era.

Below the bridge deck are six stone beams, with ends 31 cm high and center 51 cm high; stone slabs are laid between the beams, making the bridge deck slightly arched.

The base stones and row columns at the bridge bottom are thick and steady, with row columns and transverse tie stones tightly joined, evenly bearing force.

On the long stone tie beams below are four half-moon-shaped holes, used to place support timbers during bridge construction.

The bridge stones have exquisite carvings, such as the ruyi cloud pattern at the ends of the secondary opening beams—one of the "Eight Treasures" patterns, elegant and vivid.

建筑要点 / Key Features
中孔石梁上刻有绍定字样；南宋绍定年间1228-1233；三跨石梁桥；武康石构筑；桥下六根石梁如意云图案八宝纹
51 彩衣堂
Caiyi Hall
明
级别 Level
第四批全国重点文物保护单位（1996年）
地址 Address
书院街翁家巷门2号
类型 Type
名人故居/宅第
门票 Ticket
20元
开放时间 Hours
8:30 — 16:30
中文原文

彩衣堂是清同治、光绪两代帝师翁同龢的故居。翁同龢（1830—1904）中清咸丰六年（1856年）状元，历任都察院左副都御使，刑、工、户部尚书，军机大臣等要职，出入朝廷40余年，对中国近代史产生了巨大影响。

他早年与李鸿章不合，牵制北洋水师，一定程度上影响到甲午海战；之后他接受康有为、梁启超的维新思想，积极支持光绪皇帝变法，被康有为誉为"中国维新第一导师"。变法失败后他被慈禧太后撤职，回到常熟度过晚年。这处宅第始建于明代隆庆、万历年间，清道光十三年（1833年）由翁同龢之父翁心存购得，更名彩衣堂。

宅第以东路为主，南北共七进，有门厅、轿厅、彩衣堂、后堂楼和双桂轩等；西路附建柏古轩庭园、知止斋书楼和思永堂等，共计90余间，体现了晚清官绅宅第的格局和风格。其中东路第三进主厅彩衣堂，梁、檩、枋上绘有116幅彩画，题材多样，制作精美，为江南"苏式彩画"的代表作。

宅第今为翁同龢纪念馆，设有"中国维新第一导师：翁同龢""翁氏一门书法"和"常熟状元历史陈列"等展览。

· · · · ·
English

Caiyi Hall is the former residence of Weng Tonghe (1830-1904), imperial tutor to both the Tongzhi and Guangxu emperors of the Qing.

Weng Tonghe won the top scholar (zhuangyuan) in the 6th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1856), and served in important positions including Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, Minister of Justice, Works, and Revenue, and Grand Councilor—serving at court for over 40 years, with enormous influence on modern Chinese history.

Early on he clashed with Li Hongzhang, restraining the Beiyang Fleet and affecting the First Sino-Japanese War to some extent; later he accepted the reformist ideas of Kang Youwei and Liang Qichao, actively supporting Emperor Guangxu's reform, and was praised by Kang Youwei as "China's foremost mentor of reform.

" After the reform failed, he was dismissed by Empress Dowager Cixi and returned to Changshu to spend his later years.

This mansion was first built during the Longqing and Wanli reigns of the Ming; in the 13th year of Daoguang of the Qing (1833), it was purchased by Weng Tonghe's father Weng Xincun and renamed Caiyi Hall.

The mansion centers on the east road, with seven bays north-south, including the gate hall, sedan hall, Caiyi Hall, rear hall tower, and Shuanggui Xuan; the west road has attached the Baigu Xuan garden, Zhizhai Library Tower, and Siyong Hall—totaling over 90 rooms, reflecting the layout and style of late-Qing official-gentry mansions.

Among them, the third bay main hall Caiyi Hall on the east road has 116 painted decorations on the beams, purlins, and tie beams, with diverse themes and exquisite craftsmanship—a representative work of Jiangnan "Suzhou-style painted decorations.

" The mansion is now the Weng Tonghe Memorial Hall, with exhibitions such as "China's Foremost Mentor of Reform: Weng Tonghe," "Calligraphy of the Weng Family," and "Historical Exhibition of Changshu Top Scholars.

"

建筑要点 / Key Features
清同治光绪两代帝师翁同龢故居；翁同龢中清咸丰六年状元；中国维新第一导师；始建于明隆庆万历年间；116幅苏式彩画江南苏式彩画代表作；东路第三进主厅彩衣堂
52 赵用贤宅
Residence of Zhao Yongxian
明
级别 Level
第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
地址 Address
书院街西南赵弄10号
类型 Type
名人故居/宅第
中文原文

在彩衣堂西侧，隔着书院街有一条南赵弄，内有晚明大臣赵用贤（1535—1596）故居。赵氏父子皆喜藏书，故居中的脉望馆当时与钱谦益绛云楼、毛晋汲古阁齐名，今为"虞山派古琴艺术馆"。

赵用贤中明隆庆五年（1571年）进士，明万历五年（1577年）弹劾张居正夺情，与武进吴中行同受杖刑罢归，闻名天下。张居正卒后他被重新起用，官至吏部左侍郎。

赵用贤性格刚直，《明史》认为东林党由赵用贤、吴中行开创于前，顾宪成、高攀龙继踵于后，从万历初年起，言事者皆訾议执政者，执政者压制言事者，"水火薄射，讫于明亡"。这处故居原有三路，现仅存中路的门房、正厅、后堂以及两侧配房等。正厅保闲堂宽三间，明间为抬梁式，山面用穿斗式。

正厅和后堂的梁枋上皆有精美的明代彩画，此外还保存下正厅雕花柱础、踢脚砖和丁字斗栱等明代原物。

· · · · ·
English

West of Caiyi Hall, across Shuyuan Street, is South Zhao Lane, containing the former residence of late-Ming minister Zhao Yongxian (1535-1596).

Both father and son of the Zhao family loved collecting books; the Maiwang (Bookworm) Library in the residence was then as famous as Qian Qianyi's Jiangyun Tower and Mao Jin's Jigu Pavilion.

Today it is the "Yushan School Guqin Art Museum.

" Zhao Yongxian passed the jinshi examination in the 5th year of Longqing of the Ming (1571); in the 5th year of Wanli (1577), he impeached Zhang Juzheng for seizing power during mourning, and together with Wu Zhongxing of Wujin was flogged and dismissed—becoming famous nationwide.

After Zhang Juzheng's death, he was reinstated, rising to Vice Minister of Personnel.

Zhao Yongxian had a forthright character; the "History of Ming" considers that the Donglin Party was pioneered by Zhao Yongxian and Wu Zhongxing, followed by Gu Xiancheng and Gao Panlong.

From the early Wanli reign, those who spoke out all criticized those in power, and those in power suppressed those who spoke out—"water and fire clashed, until the fall of the Ming.

" This residence originally had three roads; today only the middle road's gate house, main hall, rear hall, and side rooms survive.

The main hall Baoxian Hall is three bays wide, with the central bay using the column-and-tie beam (tailiang) system and the gable sides using the post-and-lintel (chuandou) system.

The beams and tie beams of both the main hall and rear hall have exquisite Ming-dynasty painted decorations; additionally, original Ming artifacts such as the carved column bases of the main hall, baseboard bricks, and T-shaped brackets are preserved.

建筑要点 / Key Features
晚明大臣赵用贤1535-1596故居；赵氏父子皆喜藏书脉望馆；与钱谦益绛云楼毛晋汲古阁齐名；今为虞山派古琴艺术馆；明隆庆五年进士；东林党赵用贤吴中行开创于前
53 赵园·曾园
Zhaoyuan Garden and Zengyuan Garden
明—清
级别 Level
第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
地址 Address
环城西路
类型 Type
古典园林
门票 Ticket
30元
开放时间 Hours
8:00 — 16:00
中文原文

此地原为明万历年间钱岱（1541—1620）别业。钱岱中明隆庆五年（1571年）进士，为张居正门生。他40多岁时上疏辞官，回乡辟建园林，屠隆《小辋川记略》称他"园居绝类王右丞蓝田辋川，而又雅慕右丞之为人，以故一切台阁亭榭，悉颜以辋川诸胜"，园名也题作"小辋川"。园林占地颇广，有"钱半城"之称。

今人李乃成、徐家骥《"小辋川"钩沉》对当时园景做了详细探讨。清同治年间园林西部归赵烈文（1832—1894），称赵湖园，后归盛宣怀，改为宁静莲社，俗称赵园。清光绪年间园林东部归曾之撰（1842—1897），叠山凿池大加改筑，更名虚廓居，俗称曾园。文学家曾朴幼时和晚年皆寓居园中，著有长篇小说《孽海花》。

曾园入口在南侧，前宅后园，南部为虚廓村居和归耕课读庐等，北部围绕水池布置小有天、啸台和不倚亭等。赵园与曾园相通，东部堆山，上建山满楼高阁；西部以水池为中心，西、南两面周以游廊，缀以水阁，池南设旱船，向北经九曲桥通向池中小岛。两园背靠虞山，多处皆可借景远山，饶古朴疏朗之趣。

· · · · ·
English

This place was originally the villa of Qian Dai (1541-1620) during the Wanli reign of the Ming.

Qian Dai passed the jinshi examination in the 5th year of Longqing of the Ming (1571), and was a student of Zhang Juzheng.

In his 40s he submitted a memorial resigning from office, returning home to build a garden.

Tu Long's "Brief Record of Small Wangchuan" says he "lived in a garden utterly resembling Wang Wei's Wangchuan in Lantian, and also admired Wang Wei's character, hence all pavilions and terraces were named after the scenic spots of Wangchuan," and the garden was also titled "Small Wangchuan.

" The garden occupied a large area, known as "Qian Half-City.

" Modern scholars Li Naicheng and Xu Jiaji's "Research on 'Small Wangchuan'" provides a detailed discussion of the garden scenery at that time.

During the Tongzhi reign of the Qing, the western part of the garden passed to Zhao Liewen (1832-1894), called Zhaohu Garden; later it passed to Sheng Xuanhuai, changed to the Tranquil Lotus Society, commonly called Zhaoyuan (Zhao Garden).

During the Guangxu reign of the Qing, the eastern part passed to Zeng Zhizhuan (1842-1897), who piled rockeries and dug ponds for major reconstruction, renaming it Xukuoju (Empty Expanse Residence), commonly called Zengyuan (Zeng Garden).

Writer Zeng Pu lived in the garden both as a child and in his later years, authoring the novel "A Flower in a Sea of Sin (Niehai Hua).

" The Zeng Garden entrance is on the south side, with front residence and rear garden; the south has Xukuocunju and Guigeng Kedu Lu, while the north arranges Xiaoyoutian, Xiaotai, and Buyi Pavilion around a pond.

Zhaoyuan and Zengyuan are connected; the east piles a mountain with the high Shanman Lou (Mountain-Full Tower) pavilion on top; the west centers on a pond, with corridors on the west and south sides, adorned with waterside pavilions; south of the pond is a land-boat, leading north via a nine-bend bridge to a small island in the pond.

Both gardens back onto Yushan (Yu Mountain), with many places borrowing the distant mountain scenery—rich in simple, sparse, and open charm.

建筑要点 / Key Features
明万历年间钱岱小辋川；清同治年间赵烈文赵园；清光绪年间曾之撰曾园虚廓居；文学家曾朴孽海花；赵园与曾园相通；借景虞山
54 崇教兴福寺塔
Chongjiao Xingfu Temple Pagoda
宋
级别 Level
第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
地址 Address
河东街塔弄方塔园内
类型 Type
古塔
中文原文

虞山位于常熟古城西侧，素有"十里青山半入城"之誉，到宋代风水家提出，古城"右高左下，失宾主之辨，宜于苍龙左角，作浮图以胜之"，认为虞山在右作为白虎，左侧缺少青龙呼应，因此决定建造一座高塔作为弥补，即今兴福寺塔。

1964年从塔下地宫发现石造像，其上铭文有"大宋端拱元年戊子岁五月五日题记……咸淳壬申再建宝塔"字样，可知此塔始建于北宋端拱元年（988年），咸淳八年（1272年）重建。

此后历经10余次大修，保留至今，一直是常熟的标志性建筑。这是一座九层方形木楼阁式砖塔，俗称方塔。各面皆宽三间，在明间开门。底层门洞呈拱券形，周围有一圈檐廊（副阶周匝），二层以上作壶门状。

内部自第七层起有塔心木直贯塔顶，上立塔刹，由覆钵、鼓形束腰、承露盘、七重相轮、宝盖、宝瓶和宝珠等构成。近年围绕方塔建成宋代风格的方塔园，其中的宋代古井和古银杏，与方塔合称园中三宝，此外还有常熟碑刻博物馆和常熟名人馆等。

· · · · ·
English

Yushan (Yu Mountain) is located west of the ancient city of Changshu, known for the reputation "ten li of green mountains half entering the city.

" By the Song Dynasty, fengshui masters proposed that the ancient city was "high on the right and low on the left, losing the distinction between host and guest; it is appropriate to build a stupa at the left horn of the Azure Dragon to overcome it"—believing Yushan on the right serves as the White Tiger, while the left side lacks the Azure Dragon's response, hence deciding to build a tall tower as compensation, today's Xingfu Temple Pagoda.

In 1964, stone statues were discovered from the underground palace beneath the pagoda, with inscriptions reading "Recorded on the 5th day of the 5th month, Wuwu year, the 1st year of Duangong of the Great Song.

..

the pagoda rebuilt in Renshen year of Xianchun"—indicating this pagoda was first built in the 1st year of Duangong of the Northern Song (988) and rebuilt in the 8th year of Xianchun (1272).

Since then it has undergone over 10 major repairs, surviving to today and always being the landmark building of Changshu.

This is a nine-story square wooden pavilion-style brick pagoda, commonly called the Square Pagoda.Each face is three bays wide, with doors in the central bay.

The bottom story's door opening is arch-shaped, surrounded by a一圈 eave corridor (fujie zhouza); from the second story upward, it is in the pot-door (humen) shape.

Inside, from the seventh story upward, a central pagoda timber runs straight through to the top, with a finial erected above, composed of an inverted bowl, drum-shaped waist, dew-receiving plate, seven-layer chatra, treasure canopy, treasure vase, and treasure pearl.

In recent years, a Song-style Square Pagoda Garden has been built around the pagoda; the Song-dynasty ancient well and ancient ginkgo, together with the Square Pagoda, are called the Three Treasures of the garden.

Additionally, there are the Changshu Stele Carving Museum and Changshu Famous People's Hall.

建筑要点 / Key Features
俗称方塔；九层方形木楼阁式砖塔；北宋端拱元年988年始建；南宋咸淳八年1272年重建；十里青山半入城；塔心木直贯塔顶

The Swallow Garden

中文原文

清乾隆四十三年（1778年）台湾知府蒋元枢（1738—1781）卸任回乡，在其叔蒋洞宅第东侧建造园林，是为燕园前身。蒋元枢卒后，其子好赌，将园林输掉。

清道光初年蒋元枢的侄子蒋因培（1768—1839）因狂放不羁被劾罢官（《啸亭杂录》卷5），回常热后购回蒋园，聘请造园名家戈裕良大加拓建，筑成一瓠阁、十愿楼、诗境、梅崖诸胜；戈裕良以虞山为蓝本，叠筑"燕谷"假山，取"燕子南归"之意，将园名改为燕园。

清道光六年（1826年）园林建成，蒋因培请画家钱杜（字叔美）绘《燕园图》册16幅，1912年上海神州国光社出版《钱叔美燕园八景册》刊印了其中8幅。蒋因培的拓建奠定了燕园的主要格局，此后燕园先后属归氏、蒋氏、张氏，但园貌基本未变。燕园包括东、西两路，东为主，西为辅。

入口在北侧，采用北宅南园的格局，分为前宅、中园和后园三部分。入门为主厅五芝堂庭院，是主人接待宾客、会见亲友之所；厅东的一瓠阁和十愿楼则是住宅和书

· · · · ·
English

In the 43rd year of Qianlong of the Qing (1778), Jiang Yuanshu (1738-1781), Prefect of Taiwan, returned home after leaving office and built a garden east of his uncle Jiang Dong's mansion—the predecessor of the Swallow Garden.

After Jiang Yuanshu's death, his son was fond of gambling and lost the garden.

In the early Daoguang reign of the Qing, Jiang Yuanshu's nephew Jiang Yinpei (1768-1839) was impeached and dismissed for being uninhibited and unconventional ("Xiaoting Zalu" vol.

5); after returning to Changshu, he bought back the Jiang Garden, hiring famous garden designer Ge Yuliang for major expansion, building the Yihu Pavilion, Shiyuan Tower, Shijing (Poetic Realm), and Meiya (Plum Cliff) scenic spots.

Ge Yuliang used Yushan as the blueprint, piling the "Swallow Valley" rockery, taking the meaning of "swallows returning south," and renaming the garden the Swallow Garden (Yan Yuan).

In the 6th year of Daoguang of the Qing (1826), the garden was completed; Jiang Yinpei asked painter Qian Du (style name Shumei) to paint an album of 16 "Swallow Garden Paintings"; in 1912, the Shanghai Shenzhou Guoguang She published the "Eight Scenes of Shumei's Swallow Garden Album," printing 8 of them.

Jiang Yinpei's expansion established the main layout of the Swallow Garden; thereafter the garden successively belonged to the Gui, Jiang, and Zhang families, but its appearance remained basically unchanged.

The Swallow Garden includes east and west roads, with the east as main and west as auxiliary.

The entrance is on the north side, adopting a north-residence, south-garden layout, divided into three parts: front residence, middle garden, and rear garden.

Entering the gate is the main hall Wuzhi Hall courtyard, where the master received guests and met relatives and friends; east of the hall, the Yihu Pavilion and Shiyuan Tower are the residence and study

建筑要点 / Key Features
清乾隆四十三年台湾知府蒋元枢；清道光六年蒋因培购回；造园名家戈裕良；燕谷假山以虞山为蓝本；钱叔美绘燕园图16幅；七十二石猴湖石假山
56 杨氏宅第
Residence of Yang's Family
清
级别 Level
第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
地址 Address
凤凰镇恬庄古街
类型 Type
宅第
中文原文

恬庄又称田庄，是明代奚浦富绅钱洪收田租的村庄，清中期在杨氏家族带动下，恬庄文风蔚起，人才济济，发展成地方大镇，当其全盛时被誉为"银恬庄"。

从清乾隆朝开始，杨氏家族名人辈出，如孝子杨岱、举人杨景仁、进士杨希铨、书法名家杨沂孙……其中最著名的是清咸丰二年（1852年）的榜眼杨泗孙（1823—1889）。杨氏宅第是恬庄的代表建筑，包括杨氏南宅、榜眼府和杨孝子祠。

清乾隆年间杨岱先建南宅，后建中宅，中宅后来成为榜眼府，清道光年间杨家后人又建孝子祠纪念杨岱及其夫人。这三座宅第反映了清代杨氏家族在当地的地位和影响，体现了中国"崇礼重教，忠孝传家"的传统，孝子祠、榜眼府都是典型的清官式建筑，杨氏南宅则属典型民房，较有特色。

杨氏南宅位于恬庄南街，坐西朝东。门厅在东北角，进门是一座园林式庭院，东、南设游廊，西北角有花坛，栽植孤松，点缀盆景，饶有幽趣。向西穿过庭院，再进一道门是一处方形天井，西侧的三间正房和两翼厢房皆为二层砖木结构，质量较高。榜眼府位于恬庄北街，也是坐西朝东，原有五进，现存四进。

第一进是五间门厅，采用金柱大门，入口空间敞亮，与高高的门槛一起，彰显出主人的地位。杨泗孙考中探花后，按清朝制度在门前立起4根旗杆，今尚存3只旗杆石柱础。第二进为轿厅，第三进为大厅，皆为三间，但大厅比轿厅宽，使平面呈现倒"凸"形，为风水说中的吉宅之相。

大厅后面有一座砖雕门楼，隔开内外，门楼东侧原有清乾隆四十五年（1780年）所刻"外言不入"，西侧刻"内言不出"。门内的五间楼房为内眷的起居之所，门窗隔扇雕刻精细。

清嘉庆十一年（1806年）朝廷敕建孝坊旌表杨岱，清道光年间在孝坊前建杨孝子祠，后来坊被毁，仅存祠堂。孝子祠坐西朝东，现存门厅、仪门、大厅和后厅四进，梁柱作法属于典型的清代官式风格。

· · · · ·
English

Tianzhuang, also called Tianzhuang (Field Village), was a village where Qian Hong, a wealthy gentryman of Xipu in the Ming Dynasty, collected field rents.

In the mid-Qing, driven by the Yang family, Tianzhuang saw a flourishing literary culture with abundant talents, developing into a major local town, known as "Silver Tianzhuang" at its peak.

From the Qianlong reign of the Qing, the Yang family produced many famous figures, such as the filial son Yang Dai, juren Yang Jingren, jinshi Yang Xiquan, and calligraphy master Yang Yisun.

..the most famous being Yang Sisun (1823-1889), the second-place graduate (bangyan) in the 2nd year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1852).

The Yang Family Residence is the representative building of Tianzhuang, including the Yang South Residence, the Bangyan (Second-Place Graduate) Mansion, and the Yang Filial Son Shrine.

During the Qianlong reign of the Qing, Yang Dai first built the south residence, then the middle residence, which later became the Bangyan Mansion; during the Daoguang reign, the Yang family descendants built the Filial Son Shrine to commemorate Yang Dai and his wife.

These three residences reflect the Yang family's status and influence in the local area during the Qing, embodying the Chinese tradition of "honoring propriety and valuing education, passing down loyalty and filial piety.

" The Filial Son Shrine and Bangyan Mansion are typical Qing official-style buildings, while the Yang South Residence is a typical folk house, quite distinctive.

The Yang South Residence is on Tianzhuang South Street, facing west with its back to east.

The gate hall is at the northeast corner; entering is a garden-style courtyard, with corridors on the east and south, a flower bed at the northwest corner planted with a solitary pine and dotted with bonsai—quite secluded and charming.

Passing west through the courtyard and another gate is a square courtyard; the three-bay main hall on the west and the two wing rooms are all two-story brick-wood structures, of high quality.

The Bangyan Mansion is on Tianzhuang North Street, also facing west, originally with five bays, four surviving today.

The first bay is a five-bay gate hall, using a golden-column gate with a spacious entrance, together with the high threshold,彰显 the owner's status.

After Yang Sisun passed the third-place exam (tanhua), according to Qing system, four flagpoles were erected in front of the gate; today three flagpole stone bases survive.

The second bay is the sedan hall, the third bay is the main hall, both three bays, but the main hall is wider than the sedan hall, making the plan an inverted "convex" shape—considered an auspicious house shape in fengshui.

Behind the main hall is a brick-carved gate tower separating inner and outer; the east side of the gate tower originally had the inscription "Outer words do not enter" carved in the 45th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1780), and the west side carved "Inner words do not exit.

" Inside the gate, the five-bay building is the living quarters for female family members, with finely carved doors, windows, and lattice.

In the 11th year of Jiaqing of the Qing (1806), the court ordered the construction of a filial piety archway to honor Yang Dai; during the Daoguang reign, the Yang Filial Son Shrine was built in front of the archway, later the archway was destroyed, leaving only the shrine.

The Filial Son Shrine faces west, with four surviving bays: gate hall, ceremonial gate, main hall, and rear hall; the beam-column construction belongs to the typical Qing official style.

建筑要点 / Key Features
恬庄又称田庄明代奚浦富绅钱洪收田租的村庄；清乾隆朝开始杨氏家族名人辈出；孝子杨岱举人杨景仁进士杨希铨书法名家杨沂孙；榜眼杨泗孙清咸丰二年1852年；杨氏南宅榜眼府杨孝子祠三座宅第；崇礼重教忠孝传家
57 周庄镇
Zhouzhuang Town
宋—清
级别 Level
中国历史文化名镇，玉燕堂（张厅）、敬业堂（沈厅）为第七批国保（2013年）
地址 Address
昆山市周庄镇
类型 Type
历史文化名镇
门票 Ticket
周庄通票100元，免费拍照后有效期为3天
中文原文

周庄古称摇城，是春秋时期吴国太子摇的封地；又名贞丰里，今古镇入口立有"贞丰泽国"牌坊。北宋元祐元年（1086年）迪功郎周氏在此设庄务农，周氏夫妇笃信佛教，后来捐庄建造全福寺，周庄由此得名。

元代中期沈万三的父亲从湖州南浔迁居周庄，沈万三善于经商，成为江南巨富，周庄也随之兴旺繁荣，到清康熙初年正式更名周庄镇。周庄四面环水，处在澄湖、白蚬湖、淀山湖和南湖之间，镇内南北市河通贯南北，与后港河、中市河构成井字形，商铺民居皆沿河依水而筑，至今保存良好的仍有近百余座，被誉为"中国第一水乡"。

周庄通票100元，免费拍照后有效期为3天，包含张厅（玉燕堂）、沈厅（敬业堂）、双桥、逸飞之家、迷楼、昆曲古戏台、全福讲寺、叶楚伧故居（2011年列为省保）和蚬江渔唱等景点。

1. 玉燕堂（张厅）：相传为明正统年间中山王徐达之弟徐逵的后代徐汝璞所建，原名怡顺堂，清初售给张氏，改名玉燕堂，俗称张厅，是周庄仅存的保留完整的明代民居。玉燕堂坐东朝西，采用前宅后园格局，共有大小房屋60余间。

前部住宅共六进，沿轴线为门厅、轿厅、主厅玉燕堂、堂楼、后河屋和水道阁。轿厅和玉燕堂建于明代，玉燕堂采用"明三暗二"的五开间形制，前后皆有轩廊。堂内4根楠木金柱和下部所用木鼓墩柱础，为明代所特有。

张厅的独特之处在于"轿从前门进，船自家中过"。紧贴住宅南侧有一条备弄，是家人日常进出之地。沿狭小幽暗的备弄向东走，行至尽头豁然开朗，眼前出现一座花园，脚下则有河水叮当流淌。这条小河叫"箬泾"，与南湖相通，在院中拓成大的方池，供船只停泊和调头。当时主人既可坐轿从正门进入，也可乘舟直达后园。

第六进水道阁东侧临河，靠窗设美人靠，供人隔水欣赏对面的花园。园中有花木廊榭，与河水相映，清新雅致；其中最吸引人的是一尊太湖石，上题"玉燕峰"，皱透宛转，似一只展翅欲翔的飞燕，与宅中主堂相呼应。

2. 敬业堂（沈厅）：敬业堂俗称沈厅，清乾隆七年（1742年）沈万三的后人沈本仁建。据清《周庄镇志》记载，沈本仁早年喜好结交游侠匪类，有人预言：不出三年，沈家必败。

沈本仁受此刺激，大设酒宴召集所交宾客，赠钱绝交，从此"闭门谢客经营家业，于所居大业堂侧拓创敬业堂宅，广厦百余，良田千亩，逐成一镇巨室"。沈厅坐东朝西，共七进，分为三部分，有房屋100余间，前后楼屋通过过街楼、阁连接，形成一组巨大的走马楼。西部只有一进，为河埠头和水墙门，供船只停靠和洗涤之用，与中部以街道相隔。

中部三进，包括轿厅、茶厅和正厅敬业堂，是迎接宾客、办理事务之所。敬业堂在晚清改名松茂堂，室内悬清末状元张謇所题匾额。东部有三进，包括大堂楼（两层）、小堂楼（两层）和后厅屋，是生活起居之处。其中后部的五座厅堂前方皆有门楼相对，以敬业堂前的最为精美。

敬业堂规模宏伟，西部河屋、东部前堂后寝的格局保存完整，木作、砖雕工艺精湛，为清代江南民居的上乘之作。3. 双桥及沿河建筑：双桥位于周庄古镇北市街，2002年被列为省保单位。双桥为世德桥和永安桥，始建于明万历年间。

世德桥是单孔拱桥，东西跨在北市河上；永安桥1957年由拱桥改为梁桥，南北跨在银子浜上，两桥垂直相交，被形象地称作"钥匙桥"。从双桥至富安桥之间，沿河两岸分布着多座明清建筑，如迮厅、张厅、贞固堂和太平桥等，堪称周庄最入画的一段景致。

1983年春，38岁的青年画家陈逸飞到周庄写生，以《故乡的回忆》为题创作了38幅油画，当年十月这组作品在纽约展出，引起轰动。1984年美国西方石油公司董事长阿曼德·哈默访华，送给邓小平的礼物就是《故乡的回忆》中的双桥。

1985年《双桥》油画又被用于联合国首日封上，使双桥所在的周庄声名鹊起，得到全世界的瞩目，也使双桥及其东侧的"逸飞之家"成为人们到周庄的必游之地。

· · · · ·
English

Zhouzhuang, anciently called Yaocheng (Shake City), was the fief of Prince Yao of Wu in the Spring and Autumn period; also called Zhenfengli, today the ancient town entrance has the "Zhenfeng Zeguo" (Zhenfeng Water Country) memorial archway.

In the 1st year of Yuanyou of the Northern Song (1086), Zhou Di, a low-ranking official, established a manor here for farming; the Zhou couple were devout Buddhists and later donated the manor to build Quanfu Temple, from which Zhouzhuang gets its name.

In the mid-Yuan, Shen Wansan's father moved from Nanxun in Huzhou to Zhouzhuang; Shen Wansan was skilled at business and became a great wealthy man of Jiangnan, and Zhouzhuang prospered accordingly, officially renamed Zhouzhuang Town in the early Kangxi reign of the Qing.

Zhouzhuang is surrounded by water, located between Cheng Lake, Baixian Lake, Dianshan Lake, and South Lake; the North-South Market River runs through the town north-south, forming a well shape with the Hougang River and Middle Market River.

Shops and residences are all built along the river by the water, with nearly a hundred well-preserved ones today—hailed as "China's Number One Water Town.

" The Zhouzhuang all-inclusive ticket is 100 yuan, valid for 3 days after free photo registration, including attractions such as Zhang Hall (Yuyan Hall), Shen Hall (Jingye Hall), Twin Bridges, Yifei's Home, Milou (Enchanting Tower), Kunqu Opera Ancient Stage, Quanfu Temple, Ye Chucang's Former Residence (provincial protected site in 2011), and Xianjiang Fishing Song.

1.

Yuyan Hall (Zhang Hall): Legend says it was built by Xu Rupu, a descendant of Xu Kui (younger brother of Zhongshan King Xu Da) during the Zhengtong reign of the Ming, originally named Yishun Hall; sold to the Zhang family in the early Qing, renamed Yuyan Hall, commonly called Zhang Hall.

It is the only completely preserved Ming-dynasty residence in Zhouzhuang.Yuyan Hall faces east, adopting a front-residence, rear-garden layout, with over 60 rooms of various sizes.

The front residence has six bays, along the axis: gate hall, sedan hall, main hall Yuyan Hall, hall tower, rear river house, and waterway pavilion.

The sedan hall and Yuyan Hall were built in the Ming; Yuyan Hall adopts the "three bright, two dark" five-bay form, with covered corridors front and back.

The four nanmu golden columns inside the hall and the wooden drum pier column bases below are unique to the Ming.

Zhang Hall's uniqueness lies in "sedan enters through the front gate, boats pass through the home.

" Close to the south side of the residence is a service alley, used by family members for daily entry and exit.

Walking east along the narrow, dark service alley, at the end it suddenly opens up to a garden, with river water tinkling beneath one's feet.

This small river is called "Ruo Jing," connected to South Lake, expanding into a large square pond in the courtyard for boats to dock and turn around.

At that time, the master could enter by sedan through the main gate or by boat directly to the rear garden.

The sixth bay waterway pavilion faces the river on its east side, with a beauty's rest by the window for people to admire the garden across the water.

The garden has flowers, trees, corridors, and pavilions, reflecting with the river water—fresh and elegant; the most attractive is a Taihu rock inscribed "Yuyan Peak," wrinkled and perforated, like a swallow about to spread its wings and fly, echoing the main hall of the residence.

2.Jingye Hall (Shen Hall): Jingye Hall, commonly called Shen Hall, was built in the 7th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1742) by Shen Benren, a descendant of Shen Wansan.

According to the Qing "Zhouzhuang Town Gazetteer," Shen Benren in his early years liked associating with wandering swordsmen and bandits; someone predicted that within three years, the Shen family would surely fail.

Stimulated by this, Shen Benren held a grand banquet summoning all his associates, gave them money and severed ties, and from then on "closed his door to guests and managed the family business, expanding and creating the Jingye Hall residence beside the Daye Hall where he lived, with over a hundred grand buildings and a thousand mu of fertile land, becoming a great family of the town.

" Shen Hall faces east, with seven bays divided into three parts, over 100 rooms; the front and rear buildings are connected through overhead corridors and pavilions, forming a huge galloping horse corridor building.

The west has only one bay, the river dock and water gate, for boats to dock and wash, separated from the middle by a street.

The middle has three bays, including the sedan hall, tea hall, and main hall Jingye Hall—for receiving guests and conducting business.

Jingye Hall was renamed Songmao Hall in the late Qing, with a plaque inscribed by the late-Qing top scholar Zhang Jian hanging inside.

The east has three bays, including the great hall tower (two stories), small hall tower (two stories), and rear hall—for daily living.

Among them, the five rear halls all have gate towers facing them in front, with the one in front of Jingye Hall being the most exquisite.

Jingye Hall is magnificent in scale, with the west river house and east front-hall, rear-bedroom layout completely preserved; the woodwork and brick-carving craftsmanship are exquisite—a superior example of Qing-dynasty Jiangnan residences.

3.Twin Bridges and Riverside Buildings: The Twin Bridges are on North Market Street of Zhouzhuang ancient town, designated a provincial protected site in 2002.

The Twin Bridges are the Shide Bridge and Yong'an Bridge, first built during the Wanli reign of the Ming.

Shide Bridge is a single-arch bridge spanning the North Market River east-west; Yong'an Bridge was changed from an arch bridge to a beam bridge in 1957, spanning Yinzi Bang north-south.

The two bridges intersect perpendicularly, vividly called the "Key Bridge.

" Between the Twin Bridges and Fu'an Bridge, along both river banks, are distributed many Ming-Qing buildings, such as Ze Hall, Zhang Hall, Zhengu Hall, and Taiping Bridge—arguably the most picturesque section of Zhouzhuang.

In the spring of 1983, 38-year-old young painter Chen Yifei came to Zhouzhuang to sketch, creating 38 oil paintings under the title "Memories of Hometown"; that October this group of works was exhibited in New York, causing a sensation.

In 1984, Armand Hammer, Chairman of the American Occidental Petroleum Corporation, visited China, and the gift given to Deng Xiaoping was the Twin Bridges from "Memories of Hometown.

" In 1985, the "Twin Bridges" oil painting was used on a United Nations first-day cover, making Zhouzhuang where the Twin Bridges are located famous worldwide, attracting global attention, and making the Twin Bridges and its east-side "Yifei's Home" a must-visit destination for people coming to Zhouzhuang.

建筑要点 / Key Features
春秋时期吴国太子摇的封地摇城；北宋元祐元年1086年迪功郎周迪；元代中期沈万三江南巨富；中国第一水乡；张厅轿从前门进船自家中过；沈厅七进走马楼；双桥陈逸飞故乡的回忆
58 千灯镇秦峰塔
Qinfeng Pagoda in Qiandeng Town
明
级别 Level
第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
地址 Address
千灯镇尚书路西岸1号
类型 Type
古塔
中文原文

千灯镇在苏州市区向东约35公里，是著名学者顾炎武的故乡，也是昆曲的发源地。主要景点有秦峰塔、顾炎武墓地、顾炎武故居（南墅街52号，2011年列为省保单位）和元代昆曲创始人顾坚纪念馆等。

秦峰塔原属波若寺，始建于南朝梁天监二年（503年），因在秦望山（今废）之南，得名秦峰塔。北宋大中祥符元年（1008年）朝廷改波若寺为延福禅寺，并重建佛塔，当时称释迦佛塔。元末寺毁，唯塔独存。

明洪武年间重修寺塔，清咸丰十年（1860年）大火烧毁塔上木构件，仅剩塔身。新中国成立后多次对塔进行重修、加固。秦峰塔是一座方形七层塔，各层逐级收分，轮廓优美，民间称作"美人塔"，是千灯古镇的地标建筑。内为砖砌塔身，内壁底层为八角形，二至七层为方形。

塔内设木梯，每层四面开壶门，可登临眺望。外壁附木檐楼阁，各层皆绕有腰檐、平座，塔身嵌44尊宋代砖刻佛像，较为珍贵。

顶部设塔刹，由覆钵、承露盘、相轮和宝瓶组成，用四根"浪风索"与塔的四角相连。

· · · · ·
English

Qiandeng Town is about 35 km east of Suzhou city, the hometown of famous scholar Gu Yanwu and the birthplace of Kunqu opera.

Main attractions include Qinfeng Pagoda, Gu Yanwu's Tomb, Gu Yanwu's Former Residence (No.

52 Nanshu Street, designated a provincial protected site in 2011), and the Memorial Hall of Gu Jian, founder of Kunqu opera in the Yuan Dynasty.

Qinfeng Pagoda originally belonged to Boruo Temple, first built in the 2nd year of Tianjian of the Liang in the Southern Dynasties (503), named Qinfeng Pagoda because it was south of Qinwang Mountain (now abandoned).

In the 1st year of Dazhong Xiangfu of the Northern Song (1008), the court changed Boruo Temple to Yanfu Chan Temple and rebuilt the Buddhist pagoda, then called the Sakyamuni Pagoda.

At the end of the Yuan, the temple was destroyed, with only the pagoda surviving.

The temple and pagoda were repaired during the Hongwu reign of the Ming; in the 10th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1860), a fire destroyed the wooden components on the pagoda, leaving only the pagoda body.

After the founding of New China, the pagoda was repaired and reinforced multiple times.

Qinfeng Pagoda is a square seven-story pagoda, with each story tapering gradually, with a graceful outline—folk-called the "Beauty Pagoda," a landmark of Qiandeng ancient town.

Inside is a brick pagoda body; the inner wall's bottom story is octagonal, while the second to seventh stories are square.

A wooden ladder is set inside the pagoda, with pot-shaped doors on four sides of each story, allowing climbing for distant views.

The outer wall has attached wooden-eave pavilions, with each story surrounded by waist eaves and flat seats; the pagoda body is inlaid with 44 Song-dynasty brick-carved Buddha statues—quite precious.

The top has a finial composed of an inverted bowl, dew-receiving plate, chatra, and treasure vase, connected to the four corners of the pagoda by four "wind ropes."

建筑要点 / Key Features
千灯镇著名学者顾炎武故乡昆曲发源地；秦峰塔原属波若寺始建于南朝梁天监二年503年；北宋大中祥符元年1008年朝廷改波若寺为延福禅寺；美人塔千灯古镇地标建筑；方形七层塔内壁底层八角形二至七层方形；44尊宋代砖刻佛像
