中文原文

锡惠公园位于北塘区惠山古镇，以锡山、惠山命名，包括锡山全部、惠山东麓及连接两山的映山湖，重要景点有惠山寺及其园林祠堂、寄畅园和锡山名胜等。1. 惠山寺：惠山有多个古称。

据唐代陆羽《游惠山寺记》载：老子《枕中记》称作吴西神山；南朝时多取北方山川郡邑之名，取舜耕于历山之意称作历山；顾欢《吴地记》作华山；因山有九峰，又称作九龙山或斗龙山；传说晋僧慧照曾在此弘法，还称作慧山。最后一种称呼流传最广，因慧、惠相通，最后定名惠山。

惠山寺前身是南朝宋长史湛挺的历山草堂，南朝宋景平元年（423年）舍宅为寺，称华山精舍。

南朝梁大同三年（537年）建大雄宝殿，寺名法云禅院，因山中出青莲花，又称慧山寺。唐会昌年间寺毁，大中元年（847年）重建。唐乾符三年（876年）建陀罗尼经幢。

北宋至道二年（996年）赐额"普利院"，北宋熙宁三年（1070年）建大白伞盖神咒幢。

北宋靖康元年（1126年）钦宗将普利禅院赐给李纲为功德院。南宋绍兴年间，宋高宗又赐给信安郡王孟忠厚。

元末明初，寺庙屡遭火灾，多次重建。明永乐五年（1407年）重建大雄宝殿，始称惠山寺禅院。明正统十年（1445年）又毁于火。

风水家认为，惠山寺坐西朝东，右前方锡山高耸，左前方却是平地，右有青龙而左缺白虎，因此火灾频发。于是巡抚周忱用烧毁的瓦石在寺庙左前方堆筑了一座护山，即今寄畅园西部假山的前身。

当时惠山寺的发展达到巅峰，寺前左右遍布僧房，有14座之多，后来的碧山吟社、寄畅园、愚公谷等都是在这些僧房的基础上改建而成。明天顺四年（1460年）僧楚光重修惠山寺，明万历年间又毁于火，邹迪光修复。

明清之际寺庙遭到破坏，清康熙年间修复，到乾隆年间达到鼎盛。清咸丰十年（1860年）四月，湘军与太平军在惠山激战，寺庙又毁。

清同治四年（1865年）李鸿章在寺庙废墟上建昭忠祠，祭祀激战中牺牲的湘军将士。2002年开始修复惠山寺，2004年开放。

惠山寺背倚惠山，从东面的古华山门起，向西依次有唐宋经幢、金刚殿、日月池、天王殿、金莲桥、御碑亭、听松石床、古银杏树和大雄宝殿等景点。寺庙南北分布着大量的园林和祠堂。

古华山门：为惠山寺正门，始建于清乾隆十五年（1750年），以迎接次年乾隆临幸惠山。外面悬"古华山门"匾，背面悬"胜地名泉"匾，皆为古砖刻。今门为2008年重建。

2. 唐宋经幢：位于惠山寺山门外，2013年（第七批）列为国保单位。

南侧经幢为唐乾符三年（876年）李端符建，高6.26米，底径1.48米，塔身刻《佛顶尊胜陀罗尼经》，李端符书。

北侧经幢为北宋熙宁三年（1070年）刘元规仿唐幢建，高6.22米，底径1.40米，塔身刻《大白伞盖神咒》。

刻咒而不刻经，是宋代以后的流行做法。两幢大小、形制基本相同，皆分为幢基9级、幢身1级和幢顶9级三部分，每级都由整块青石雕成，共19级。幢基有三层束腰，底层为须弥山，中层为四只狮子，上层为八座佛龛，龛上有仰莲座，上立八角形幢身，高1.6米，遍刻经文。

幢身上部的垫石和圆扁石上托仰莲瓣，其上立束腰柱，也刻有八座佛龛，其上覆宝盖，角隅雕力士头像。其上又为一圆扁石，上覆八角攒尖顶，檐角高翘，最上部为宝珠。两座经幢幢身高大，雕刻精美，是江苏保存最好的经幢，代表了唐、宋石雕的艺术风格。

3. 寄畅园：过香花桥向北为寄畅园南门，门匾集自乾隆书法，1988年（第三批）列为国保单位。

寄畅园前身是明嘉靖六年（1527年）尚书秦金在"沤寓"僧房旧址修筑的凤谷行窝，明嘉靖三十九年（1560年）凤谷行窝转给同宗的秦瀚、秦梁父子。

明万历二十年（1592年）都察院右副都御史秦燿罢官，回无锡大加拓建，万历二十七年（1599年）完工，取王羲之"取欢仁智乐，寄畅山水阴"诗意，改名寄畅园。秦燿卒后，园林分归四个儿子管理。

清康熙七年（1668年）前后，秦德藻、秦松龄父子聘请张南垣之侄张鉽合并改筑，基本形成今日园貌。雍正年间，九王爷胤糖被治罪，秦松龄长子秦道然担任王府总管，受此牵连，寄畅园没官，南部被划出卖。

清乾隆元年（1736年）秦道然长子秦蕙田考中探花，上书陈情，乾隆将寄畅园发还，由族中富户秦瑞熙出资修葺。

清乾隆十一年（1748年）秦道然聚族合议，改园中嘉树堂为双孝祠，将寄畅园变作宗祠成为公产，避免再次没官。清咸丰十年（1860年）兵火延烧，园中建筑仅剩双孝祠和凌虚阁。

清光绪九年（1883年）秦宝瓒重建知鱼槛、凌虚阁。民国初拆掉倾圮的凌虚阁，改建三层西式楼房。此后陆续修复了清响斋、清籁轩、涵碧亭、郁盘和含贞斋等。1937年园林遭到日机轰炸，北部破坏严重。

1952年秦氏将寄畅园捐给国家，进行修复，2000年又复建了园林东南部的凌虚阁、卧云堂、先月榭和游廊等。

秦燿时期园门朝北，清康熙年间将园门改为朝东，1954年拓宽惠山横街时，园墙向西缩进3—7米，园门也向北移动。1955年开始以贞节祠南门作为主入口，东门留而不开。进入南门是一处庭院，西侧墙上嵌康熙"山色溪光"和乾隆"玉戛金枞"原刻。

院中正堂外悬"凤谷行窝"匾，内悬康熙"松风水月"匾，为仿香雪海康熙同名碑刻重题。由堂前游廊向西，过洞门为秉礼堂庭院，以水池为中心，池南为秉礼堂，其他三面设游廊，廊壁嵌《寄畅园法帖》及续刻84方。游廊西侧辟门通二泉书院，经游廊东北角小门则可达含贞斋，是当年园主的书房。

含贞斋东面对着近代堆筑的九狮峰，峰南是二层的临梵阁，可由假山登阁。阁东为园林南部正堂卧云堂，是主人雅集会客之所，堂东尽处是一座方池，池内有龙头吐水，为园林的出水口。池东特置造型优美的介如峰。庭园南部建有御碑亭，碑上刻乾隆所绘《介如峰图》和题诗。院北是二层的凌虚阁，可登阁欣赏园林内外景色。

寄畅园分为南部起居和北部山池两区，以上为南部起居区，园林的精华则在北部山池区。过凌虚阁沿游廊向西是先月榭。明代先月榭在池西，可向东隔池欣赏月色，到乾隆年间已移至池南。站在榭前平台上北望，南北狭长的锦汇漪景深丰富，池东是知鱼槛、七星桥、桥后的水湾和挑出水面的涵碧亭，池西是人工与天然相衬相映。

沿游廊折回东岸，一路向北，先后穿过郁盘和知鱼槛，右侧墙壁嵌有《寄畅园东岸刻》，左侧则可欣赏对岸的假山与矶岸。东岸知鱼槛和西岸鹤步滩双双伸向水面，将水池拦腰束住，宛如腰身纤细的少女，婀娜多姿。清代园主常在知鱼槛欣赏优伶们在鹤步滩上演奏昆曲。

槛北一道长长的七星桥将池面隔为一大一小，小池东北岸有涵碧亭和清籁廊，掩住水尾，悠远不尽。过七星桥，北岸为园林正厅嘉树堂。站在堂前南望，景致绝佳，锦汇漪、知鱼槛、郁盘亭、园中树木逐层呈现，在它们后方，远处山巅上还矗立着一座高塔，将游人的思绪带出园外，为园林借景的经典之笔。

寄畅园的高潮是水池西岸的大假山，沿山共有四条路径。一条在假山东侧，贴山临池，有石桥、滩头和古树等，突隐曲折，为山水结合部位处理之佳例。沿此路走回水池南岸，可重温池边景致；其西另有一条入山小径，景致相对平淡。行至山南右转，向西走尽头，一折又豁然开朗。

置身其中，眼前是浑厚兀立的石壁，脚下是叮咚流淌的清泉，头顶是遮天蔽日的古木，仿佛与尘世隔绝，置身幽谷深林之间。从山谷走出，又回到嘉树堂前。堂西有小路可登至山顶梅亭，是全园的制高点和收束处，坐在亭中，园林内外的美景尽收眼底。4. 天下第二泉：庭院占地805平方米，2006年（第六批）列为国保单位。

二泉开凿于唐大历五年（770年）左右。惠山泉水来自降雨，经岩根松隙过滤，含矿物质丰富，色清味醇，被茶圣陆羽（733—804）品定为天下第二。稍后刘伯刍（755—815）再评天下名泉，又将其定为第二，从此奠定了"天下第二泉"的地位。李绅曾向李德裕推荐二泉水，李德裕千里运水煮茶。

宋徽宗将二泉水列为贡品，每月进贡100坛。元代很多人不远千里汲水，"舟车络绎，水陆并运，但见瓶盎樽缶，交错于道，汲取无虚日"（王永积《锡山景物略》）。

明正德十三年（1518年）文徵明与蔡羽、汤珍、王守、王宠等到惠山茶会，绘《惠山茶会图》。走下竹炉山房门厅，南面院中即为二泉亭，三面开敞，其西墙壁上镶三排石刻。

上为赵孟頫书"天下第二泉"，中为明万历四年（1576年）王球书《修泉亭记》，下为清雍正八年（1730年）杜诏记、王澍书《重修惠山泉亭记》、宋之晋《天下第二泉说》及清嘉庆八年（1803年）顾皋《天下第二泉碑记》。

亭中池为上池与中池。上池深1.94米，井口八边形，中池深约1米，井口四边形，象征天圆地方。两池相距0.65米，井壁间有孔相通，井口皆围以青石井栏。二泉亭向西拾级而上为陆子祠，供奉茶圣陆羽，祠南有山道，向西可登惠山头茅峰。二泉亭向东为漪澜堂，是院内主堂，近年重建，内设与二泉有关的11位历代名人展。

堂东为长方形的下池，凿于北宋明道年间（1032—1033），池西石螭首出自明代良工之手，雕刻精良。堂北院墙上镶清雍正六年（1728年）王澍"天下第二泉"等六篇题刻。

下池东侧墙边是一组太湖石，原在明人顾可学惠岩小筑中，乾隆年间移至二泉庭院，称鳌鱼观音石，上有三段铭文。墙东南角开门，为二泉庭院门头。

由漪澜堂向南为尤文简公祠，供南宋礼部尚书尤袤，清光绪十六年（1890年）尤侗筹建，为惠山祠堂群重点建筑，2006年被列为国保单位。

尤祠坐北朝南，最北一进为万卷楼，二楼面北设落地长窗，为观赏二泉庭院佳处，楼西堆假山，楼南天井中有遂初泉。天井南为遂初堂，堂南为祠门。出祠门向南为碧山吟社。

5. 碧山吟社：明成化十八年（1482年）秦旭等十人在龙泉僧房旧址创建吟社，效仿白居易等"香山九老"，号为"碧山十老"，尚书王恕、王亻舆和吴宽都常与诸老唱和，沈周为之绘《碧山吟社雅集图》，成为当地的文化盛事。

明弘治七年（1494年）秦旭父子相继过世，碧山吟社被豪家霸占。

1521年秦金与潘绪、邵宝谋划重开吟社，但豪家不肯松动，直到明嘉靖三十三年（1554年）秦旭曾孙秦瀚协同当地士绅19人，终于从豪家手中购回吟社，大学士徐阶撰《重复碧山吟社记》，陈彦生作《复碧山吟社序》，文徵明题"碧山吟社"匾，再次轰动县邑。

此后，碧山吟社成为无锡的重要文化记忆，不断有文士名流重开吟社，文风诗韵延续至今，2005年全面复建。碧山吟社坐北朝南，有两进庭院。从尤祠向南，先进入最北面的十老堂，内有漆绘文徵明《兰亭修禊图》。沿堂前檐廊向西为望益楼，出楼向南为流觞山房。

由山房南门向西出庭院，可看到秦瀚等人的摩崖石刻，南侧是涵碧池，东岸临水建濯缨轩，池水向北伏流进入龙缝泉，流向望益楼西北。回到庭院进入碧山吟社正堂，堂前庭院对假山，南面是正门门厅，东厢是诗台。沿诗舍前廊一直向北，东侧开吟社门，仅设门头，门外嵌文徵明"碧山吟社"砖刻。碧山吟社南为春申涧，相传春申君曾在此饮马，是观瀑佳处。

继续向南通往阿炳墓和杜鹃园（杜鹃是无锡市花），皆为近年所建公园。碧山吟社东面是胡文昭公祠，祀宋代理学大家胡瑗，清顺治年间借愚公谷旧址营建，2005年重建。祠北有莲池，向东为映山湖，传说秦始皇东巡时，"望气者以金陵太湖之间有天子气，故掘而厌之"（陆羽《游惠山寺记》），因此民间称此湖为秦王坞。

胡祠北为尊贤祠，原在今陆子祠附近，始建于宋元年间，祀陆羽、湛挺、李绅三贤，后陆续增祀华宝、秦观、尤袤、倪瓒、王绂、邵宝和秦旭等，改称尊贤祠，清乾隆十六年（1751年）迁今址，2005年重建。

华孝子祠：尊贤祠北为华孝子祠，祀东晋孝子华宝，原在二泉西侧，唐代迁今址，为惠山祠堂群重点建筑，2006年列为国保单位。祠庙坐西朝东，沿轴线展开。

东首为四面牌坊，清乾隆十二年（1747年）建，是一座盈顶方亭，四面都为牌坊，内外皆有题刻，盈顶中央开天窗，便于采光看清内部榜文。亭内水井凿于1959年。

这种牌坊在无锡曾有四座，包括史家弄顾可久祠顾氏牌坊（已复建）、仓桥东堍秦金北四牌坊、凤光桥秦氏世科南四牌坊，今仅存一座，具有较高的价值。

向西为一楼一门牌坊，坊内为永锡堂，始建于明成化二十一年（1485），2004年重建。堂西为承泽池和溯源桥，建于明成化年间。桥西为鼋池，八角形，池内南面螭首吐水，北面螭首吸水，通向金莲池，故称双龙泉，是惠山水系的重要枢纽。

池西为孝祖享堂，建于明成化二十一年（1485年），清乾隆二十七年（1762年）重修。

享堂南壁嵌12方1982年重刻的《真赏斋帖》，此帖当年是华夏请文徵明父子钩摹、章藻刻石，被誉为"明代第一刻帖"，文徵明曾为华夏绘《真赏斋图》。2005年在享堂北面增建碑廊。

享堂西面为成志楼，始建于明弘治十七年（1504年），2005年重建，楼前庭院花石秀美，登楼可眺望锡山。

华孝子祠东南为至德祠，祀泰伯，始建于清乾隆三十年（1765年），1959年复建，为惠山祠堂群重点建筑，2006年列为国保单位。

至德祠北面，自西向东还有李忠定祠，祀抗金名将李纲，始建于清康熙五年（1666年），2005年复建；邹忠公祠祀宋学士邹浩，附祀邹迪光、邹德基父子，邹迪光始建，2005年复建；张义士祠、嵇留山祠祀清代忠烈嵇永仁，始建于清雍正七年（1729年），2005年复建；过郡马祠祀宋郡马过孟玉，2005年复建。

由嵇留山祠北门出，即回到惠山寺金刚殿，结束游览。

· · · · ·
English

Xihui Park is located in Huishan Ancient Town, Beitang District, named after Xishan (Tin Mountain) and Huishan (Kindness Mountain).

It includes all of Xishan, the eastern foot of Huishan, and the Yingshan Lake connecting the two mountains.

Important scenic spots include Huishan Temple and its gardens and ancestral halls, Jichang Garden, and Xishan scenic spots.1.Huishan Temple: Huishan has several ancient names.

According to Tang Lu Yu's "Record of Visiting Huishan Temple": Laozi's "Record of the Pillow" called it Wuxi West Divine Mountain; during the Southern Dynasties, names from northern mountains and commanderies were often adopted, taking the meaning of Shun plowing at Lishan, it was called Lishan; Gu Huan's "Record of Wu Region" called it Huashan (Flower Mountain); because the mountain has nine peaks, it was also called Jiulong Mountain (Nine Dragons) or Doulong Mountain; legend says Jin monk Huizhao once propagated Buddhism here, so it was also called Huishan (Wisdom Mountain).

The last name spread most widely; because hui (wisdom) and hui (kindness) are interchangeable, it was finally named Huishan.

Huishan Temple's predecessor was the Lishan Thatched Cottage of Zhan Ting, Chief Clerk of the Liu Song in the Southern Dynasties; in the 1st year of Jingping of the Liu Song (423), he donated his residence as a temple, called Huashan Jingshe (Flower Mountain Retreat).

In the 3rd year of Datong of the Southern Dynasties Liang (537), the Mahavira Hall was built, with the temple name Fayun Chan Yuan, also called Huishan Temple because green lotuses grew in the mountain.

During the Huichang reign of the Tang, the temple was destroyed; rebuilt in the 1st year of Dazhong (847).

In the 3rd year of Qianfu of the Tang (876), the Dharani Pillar was built.

In the 2nd year of Zhidao of the Northern Song (996), the temple was granted the plaque "Puli Courtyard"; in the 3rd year of Xining of the Northern Song (1070), the Great White Umbrella Divine Spell Pillar was built.

In the 1st year of Jingkang of the Northern Song (1126), Emperor Qinzong granted Puli Chan Courtyard to Li Gang as a merit courtyard.

During the Shaoxing reign of the Southern Song, Emperor Gaozong granted it to Meng Zhonghou, Prince of Xin'an.

At the end of the Yuan and beginning of the Ming, the temple suffered repeated fires and was rebuilt multiple times.

In the 5th year of Yongle of the Ming (1407), the Mahavira Hall was rebuilt, beginning to be called Huishan Temple Chan Courtyard.

In the 10th year of Zhengtong of the Ming (1445), it was destroyed by fire again.

Fengshui masters believed that Huishan Temple faces west with its back to east, with Xishan towering at the right front but flat ground at the left front—having the Azure Dragon on the right but lacking the White Tiger on the left, hence frequent fires.

So Governor Zhou Xun piled the burned tiles and stones into a protective mountain in front of the temple's left side—the predecessor of today's western rockery in Jichang Garden.

At that time Huishan Temple reached its peak, with monk rooms spread all around in front of the temple, as many as 14; later Bishan Poetry Society, Jichang Garden, and Yugong Valley were all rebuilt on the basis of these monk rooms.

In the 4th year of Tianshun of the Ming (1460), monk Chuguang repaired Huishan Temple; during the Wanli reign it was destroyed by fire again and repaired by Zou Diguang.

At the Ming-Qing transition the temple was damaged; repaired during the Kangxi reign of the Qing, reaching its peak during the Qianlong reign.

In the 10th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1860), in April, the Xiang Army and Taiping Army fought fiercely at Huishan, and the temple was destroyed again.

In the 4th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1865), Li Hongzhang built the Zhaozhong (Loyal Martyrs) Shrine on the temple ruins, sacrificing to the Xiang Army soldiers who died in the fierce battle.

Restoration of Huishan Temple began in 2002 and opened in 2004.

Huishan Temple backs onto Huishan; starting from the ancient Huashan Gate on the east, going west are successively the Tang-Song Dharani Pillars, Vajra Hall, Sun-Moon Pond, Heavenly King Hall, Golden Lotus Bridge, Imperial Stele Pavilion, Listening-to-Pine Stone Bed, Ancient Ginkgo Tree, and Mahavira Hall.

North and south of the temple are distributed numerous gardens and ancestral halls.

Ancient Huashan Gate: the main gate of Huishan Temple, first built in the 15th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1750) to welcome Emperor Qianlong's visit to Huishan the following year.

Outside hangs the plaque "Ancient Huashan Gate," inside hangs the plaque "Famous Scenic Spot and Famous Spring," both ancient brick carvings.Today's gate was rebuilt in 2008.2.

Tang-Song Dharani Pillars: located outside the Huishan Temple gate, designated a national protected site in 2013 (7th batch).

The south pillar was built by Li Duanfu in the 3rd year of Qianfu of the Tang (876), 6.26 meters high, base diameter 1.

48 meters, with the pillar body carved with the "Buddha's Top Superior Victorious Dharani Sutra," written by Li Duanfu.

The north pillar was built by Liu Yuangui in imitation of the Tang pillar in the 3rd year of Xining of the Northern Song (1070), 6.

22 meters high, base diameter 1.40 meters, with the pillar body carved with the "Great White Umbrella Divine Spell.

" Carving spells rather than sutras was a popular practice after the Song Dynasty.

The two pillars are basically the same in size and form, each divided into three parts: 9-level pillar base, 1-level pillar body, and 9-level pillar top, each level carved from a single piece of bluestone, totaling 19 levels.

The pillar base has three layers of waisted sections: the bottom layer is Mount Sumeru, the middle layer is four lions, the upper layer is eight Buddhist niches; above the niches is an upward-lotus seat, on which stands the octagonal pillar body, 1.

6 meters high, covered with carved scriptures.

Above the pillar body, the cushion stone and round flat stone support upward-lotus petals, on which stands a waisted column also carved with eight Buddhist niches, covered by a treasure canopy with guardian deity head carvings at the corners.

Above that is another round flat stone, covered by an octagonal pyramidal roof with high upturned eaves, and at the very top is a precious pearl.

The two dharani pillars are tall with exquisite carvings—the best-preserved dharani pillars in Jiangsu, representing the artistic style of Tang and Song stone carving.

3.

Jichang Garden: Crossing the Fragrant Flower Bridge northward is the south gate of Jichang Garden, with the gate plaque collected from Qianlong's calligraphy, designated a national protected site in 1988 (3rd batch).

Jichang Garden's predecessor was the Fenggu Xingwo (Phoenix Valley Travel Nest) built in the 6th year of Jiajing of the Ming (1527) by Minister Qin Jin on the site of the "Ouyu" monk room.

In the 39th year of Jiajing (1560), Fenggu Xingwo was transferred to his clansmen Qin Han and Qin Liang.

In the 20th year of Wanli of the Ming (1592), Qin Yao, Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, was dismissed from office and returned to Wuxi to greatly expand it, completed in the 27th year of Wanli (1599), taking the meaning from Wang Xizhi's "finding joy in benevolence and wisdom, finding comfort in mountains and waters" poetry, renaming it Jichang Garden (Comfortable Garden).

After Qin Yao's death, the garden was divided among four sons.

Around the 7th year of Kangxi of the Qing (1668), Qin Dezao and Qin Songling father and son hired Zhang Shi, nephew of Zhang Nanyuan, to merge and rebuild it, basically forming today's garden appearance.

During the Yongzheng reign, the Ninth Prince Yintang was convicted; Qin Songling's eldest son Qin Daoran served as the prince's steward and was implicated, so Jichang Garden was confiscated and its southern part sold off.

In the 1st year of Qianlong of the Qing (1736), Qin Daoran's eldest son Qin Huitian passed the third-place exam (tanhua) and submitted a memorial appealing; Qianlong returned Jichang Garden, with wealthy clansman Qin Ruixi funding the repair.

In the 11th year of Qianlong (1748), Qin Daoran gathered the clan to discuss and changed the Jiashu Hall in the garden into the Shuangxiao (Double Filial Piety) Shrine, turning Jichang Garden into a clan ancestral hall as public property to avoid future confiscation.

In the 10th year of Xianfeng (1860), war fires spread, leaving only the Shuangxiao Shrine and Lingxu Pavilion in the garden.

In the 9th year of Guangxu (1883), Qin Baozan rebuilt the Zhiyu (Knowing Fish) Threshold and Lingxu Pavilion.

In the early Republic, the crumbling Lingxu Pavilion was demolished and replaced with a three-story Western-style building.

Thereafter, Qingxiang Studio, Qinglai Studio, Hanbi Pavilion, Yupan, and Hanzhen Studio were successively restored.

In 1937 the garden was bombed by Japanese aircraft, with severe damage to the northern part.

In 1952 the Qin family donated Jichang Garden to the state for restoration; in 2000 the Lingxu Pavilion, Woyun Hall, Xianyue Pavilion, and corridors in the southeastern part of the garden were rebuilt.

During Qin Yao's period the garden gate faced north; during the Kangxi reign it was changed to face east; in 1954 when widening Huishan Heng Street, the garden wall was indented 3-7 meters westward and the gate moved northward.

From 1955, the south gate of the Chastity Shrine was used as the main entrance, with the east gate kept but not opened.

Entering the south gate is a courtyard, with the west wall embedded with Kangxi's "Mountain Colors and Stream Light" and Qianlong's "Jade Clacking and Gold Thumping" original carvings.

The main hall in the courtyard hangs the plaque "Fenggu Xingwo" outside, and inside hangs Kangxi's "Pine Wind and Water Moon" plaque, re-inscribed in imitation of Kangxi's same-named stele at Xiangxuehai.

From the hall's front corridor westward, through a cave gate is the Bingli Hall courtyard, centered on a pond, with Bingli Hall south of the pond and corridors on the other three sides; the corridor walls are embedded with 84 pieces of the "Jichang Garden Calligraphy Album" and its continuation.

A door on the west side of the corridor leads to the Erquan (Second Spring) Academy; through a small door at the northeast corner of the corridor reaches Hanzhen Studio, the garden master's study in those years.

East of Hanzhen Studio faces the modernly piled Nine Lions Peak; south of the peak is the two-story Linfan Pavilion, climbable via rockery.

East of the pavilion is the southern main hall Woyun Hall, where the master entertained guests; at the east end of the hall is a square pond with a dragon head spouting water—the garden's water outlet.

East of the pond is the exquisitely shaped Jieru Peak.

In the southern part of the courtyard is the Imperial Stele Pavilion, with the stele carved with Qianlong's painting "Jieru Peak" and inscribed poems.

North of the courtyard is the two-story Lingxu Pavilion, climbable to appreciate the scenery inside and outside the garden.

Jichang Garden is divided into the southern living quarters and the northern mountain-pond area; the above is the southern living area, while the essence of the garden is in the northern mountain-pond area.

Passing Lingxu Pavilion and following the corridor westward is the Xianyue (First Moon) Pavilion.

In the Ming, Xianyue Pavilion was west of the pond, allowing appreciation of the moonlight across the pond eastward; by the Qianlong reign it had been moved south of the pond.

Standing on the platform in front of the pavilion and looking north, the north-south elongated Jinhui Yi (Splendid Gathering Ripple) has rich depth; east of the pond are the Zhiyu Threshold, Seven-Star Bridge, the water bay behind the bridge, and the Hanbi Pavilion cantilevering over the water; west of the pond is the contrast between artificial and natural.

Following the corridor back to the east bank, going northward, one passes successively through Yupan and Zhiyu Threshold; the right wall is embedded with the "Jichang Garden East Bank Carvings," while the left side allows appreciation of the opposite rockery and rocky shore.

The east bank's Zhiyu Threshold and the west bank's Hebu (Crane Step) Beach both extend toward the water, cinching the pond at the waist like a slender-waisted young girl, graceful and charming.

Qing-dynasty garden masters often enjoyed actors performing Kunqu opera on Hebu Beach from the Zhiyu Threshold.

North of the threshold, a long Seven-Star Bridge divides the pond into a large and small part; on the northeast bank of the small pond are the Hanbi Pavilion and Qinglai Corridor, concealing the water's end with distant endlessness.

Crossing the Seven-Star Bridge, the north bank is the garden's main hall Jiashu Hall.

Standing in front of the hall and looking south, the scenery is superb: Jinhui Yi, Zhiyu Threshold, Yupan Pavilion, and garden trees appear layer by layer; behind them, a tall pagoda still stands on the distant mountain peak, carrying the visitor's thoughts beyond the garden—a classic example of garden borrowed scenery.

The climax of Jichang Garden is the large rockery west of the pond, with four paths along the mountain.

One path is on the east side of the rockery, hugging the mountain by the pond, with stone bridges, beaches, and ancient trees, hidden and winding—an excellent example of handling the mountain-water junction.

Following this path back to the south bank of the pond allows revisiting the pond-side scenery; west of it is another mountain path with relatively plain scenery.

Reaching the south of the mountain and turning right, going west to the end, a turn suddenly opens up.

Inside, one sees thick and towering stone walls, gurgling clear springs underfoot, and ancient trees blocking the sky overhead—as if cut off from the mortal world, placed in a deep valley and dense forest.

Exiting the valley, one returns to Jiashu Hall.

West of the hall is a path to climb to the Plum Pavilion at the mountain top—the highest point and concluding place of the whole garden; sitting in the pavilion, the beautiful scenery inside and outside the garden is fully visible.

4.The Second Spring Under Heaven: The courtyard covers 805 square meters, designated a national protected site in 2006 (6th batch).

The Second Spring was excavated around the 5th year of Dali of the Tang (770).

Huishan spring water comes from rainfall, filtered through rock roots and pine gaps, rich in minerals, clear in color and mellow in taste, ranked as the second best under heaven by the Tea Sage Lu Yu (733-804).

Later Liu Bochou (755-815) re-evaluated famous springs under heaven and also ranked it second, hence establishing its status as "The Second Spring Under Heaven.

" Li Shen once recommended the Second Spring water to Li Deyu, who transported water a thousand li to boil tea.

Emperor Huizong of the Northern Song listed the Second Spring water as a tribute, paying 100 jars monthly.

In the Yuan Dynasty, many people traveled a thousand li to draw water: "boats and carts came and went, transported by land and water, only to see jars and bottles crisscrossing the road, drawing water without an empty day" (Wang Yongji, "Record of Scenic Spots of Xishan").

In the 13th year of Zhengde of the Ming (1518), Wen Zhengming, together with Cai Yu, Tang Zhen, Wang Shou, and Wang Chong, had a tea gathering at Huishan and painted the "Huishan Tea Gathering Painting.

" Descending the Zhulu Mountain Cottage gate hall, the south courtyard is the Second Spring Pavilion, open on three sides; its west wall is embedded with three rows of stone carvings.

The top is Zhao Mengfu's calligraphy "The Second Spring Under Heaven"; the middle is Wang Qiu's "Record of Repairing the Spring Pavilion" in the 4th year of Wanli of the Ming (1576); the bottom is Du Zhao's record and Wang Shu's calligraphy "Record of Rebuilding the Huishan Spring Pavilion" in the 8th year of Yongzheng of the Qing (1730), Song Zhijin's "On the Second Spring Under Heaven," and Gu Gao's "Record of the Second Spring Under Heaven Stele" in the 8th year of Jiaqing of the Qing (1803).

The pond in the pavilion is the upper pond and middle pond.The upper pond is 1.

94 meters deep with an octagonal well mouth; the middle pond is about 1 meter deep with a quadrilateral well mouth—symbolizing the round heaven and square earth.The two ponds are 0.

65 meters apart, with holes connecting the well walls, and both well mouths surrounded by bluestone railings.

From the Second Spring Pavilion, climbing steps westward is the Luzi (Lu Yu) Shrine, enshrining the Tea Sage Lu Yu; south of the shrine is a mountain path, westward可 climb to the first peak of Huishan.

East of the Second Spring Pavilion is the Yilan (Ripple) Hall, the main hall of the courtyard, rebuilt in recent years, with an exhibition of 11 historical figures related to the Second Spring.

East of the hall is the rectangular lower pond, excavated during the Mingdao reign of the Northern Song (1032-1033); the stone chi-dragon head on the west side of the pond was made by a skilled Ming craftsman, exquisitely carved.

On the north courtyard wall are embedded six inscriptions including Wang Shu's "The Second Spring Under Heaven" in the 6th year of Yongzheng of the Qing (1728).

By the east wall of the lower pond is a group of Taihu rocks, originally in Gu Kexue's Huiyan Small Cottage of the Ming, moved to the Second Spring courtyard during the Qianlong reign, called the Ao Fish Guanyin Stone, with three inscriptions.

A door opens at the southeast corner of the wall, serving as the courtyard gate.

From Yilan Hall southward is the You Wenjian (You Mao) Shrine, enshrining You Mao, Minister of Rites of the Southern Song, built by You Dong in the 16th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1890), a key building of the Huishan Ancestral Hall Complex, designated a national protected site in 2006.

The You Shrine faces south, with the northernmost bay being the Wanjuan (Ten Thousand Volumes) Building, with floor-to-ceiling windows on the north side of the second floor—an excellent place to view the Second Spring courtyard; rockery is piled west of the building, and in the courtyard south of the building is the Suichu (Returning to Beginnings) Spring.

South of the courtyard is the Suichu Hall, and south of the hall is the shrine gate.Exiting the shrine gate southward is the Bishan Poetry Society.5.

Bishan Poetry Society: In the 18th year of Chenghua of the Ming (1482), Qin Xu and nine others founded a poetry society on the site of the Longquan monk room, imitating Bai Juyi's "Nine Elders of Xiangshan," calling themselves the "Ten Elders of Bishan"; Ministers Wang Shu, Wang Yu, and Wu Kuan often joined the elders in poetry exchanges, and Shen Zhou painted the "Bishan Poetry Society Elegant Gathering Painting" for them—becoming a local cultural event.

In the 7th year of Hongzhi of the Ming (1494), Qin Xu and his son passed away successively, and the Bishan Poetry Society was seized by a powerful family.

In 1521, Qin Jin, together with Pan Xu and Shao Bao, planned to reopen the poetry society, but the powerful family refused to yield; it was not until the 33rd year of Jiajing of the Ming (1554) that Qin Xu's great-grandson Qin Han, together with 19 local gentry, finally purchased the poetry society back from the powerful family.

Grand Secretary Xu Jie wrote the "Record of Re-establishing the Bishan Poetry Society," Chen Yansheng wrote the "Preface to Re-establishing the Bishan Poetry Society," and Wen Zhengming inscribed the plaque "Bishan Poetry Society"—causing a sensation in the county again.

Thereafter, the Bishan Poetry Society became an important cultural memory of Wuxi, with literati and celebrities continuously reopening the poetry society, and the literary style and poetic charm continuing to this day; it was fully rebuilt in 2005.

The Bishan Poetry Society faces south, with two courtyards.

From the You Shrine southward, one first enters the northernmost Shilao (Ten Elders) Hall, with a lacquer painting of Wen Zhengming's "Orchid Pavilion Gathering.

" Following the hall's front eave corridor westward is the Wangyi (Looking at Benefit) Tower; exiting the tower southward is the Liushang (Floating Wine Cups) Mountain Room.

From the mountain room's south gate westward out of the courtyard, one can see the cliff carvings by Qin Han and others; south of it is the Hanbi (Green Jade) Pond, with the Zhuoying (Washing Tassel) Pavilion built by the water on the east bank; the pond water flows northward underground into the Longfeng (Dragon Seam) Spring, flowing toward the northwest of Wangyi Tower.

Returning to the courtyard and entering the Bishan Poetry Society main hall, the courtyard in front of the hall faces the rockery; south of it is the main gate hall, and the east wing is the Poetry Platform.

Following the poetry room's front corridor northward, the east side opens the poetry society gate, only a gate head, with Wen Zhengming's brick carving "Bishan Poetry Society" embedded outside.

South of the Bishan Poetry Society is the Chunshen (Lord Chunshen) Stream, legend says Lord Chunshen once watered horses here, an excellent place for viewing waterfalls.

Continuing southward leads to A Bing's Tomb and the Azalea Garden (azalea is Wuxi's city flower), both recently built parks.

East of the Bishan Poetry Society is the Hu Wenzhao (Hu Yuan) Shrine, enshrining the great Song Neo-Confucian Hu Yuan, built during the Shunzhi reign of the Qing on the former site of Yugong Valley, rebuilt in 2005.

North of the shrine is the Lotus Pond, eastward is the Yingshan (Reflecting Mountain) Lake; legend says when Qin Shi Huang made his eastern tour, "a qi-watcher said there was son-of-heaven qi between Jinling and Taihu, so he dug to suppress it" (Lu Yu, "Record of Visiting Huishan Temple"), hence folk call this lake the Qin King Dock.

North of the Hu Shrine is the Zunxian (Honoring Worthies) Shrine, originally near today's Luzi Shrine, first built during the Song-Yuan period, enshrining Lu Yu, Zhan Ting, and Li Shen; later successively adding Hua Bao, Qin Guan, You Mao, Ni Zan, Wang Fu, Shao Bao, and Qin Xu, renamed the Zunxian Shrine, moved to today's site in the 16th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1751), rebuilt in 2005.

Hua Xiaozi (Hua the Filial Son) Shrine: North of the Zunxian Shrine is the Hua Xiaozi Shrine, enshrining the Eastern Jin filial son Hua Bao, originally west of the Second Spring, moved to today's site in the Tang Dynasty—a key building of the Huishan Ancestral Hall Complex, designated a national protected site in 2006.

The shrine faces west, with its back to east, unfolding along the axis.

At the east end is the Four-Sided Archway, built in the 12th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1747), a square pavilion with a flat top, with archways on all four sides and inscriptions inside and outside; a skylight opens in the center of the flat top for lighting to clearly see the internal plaques.

The well inside the pavilion was dug in 1959.

This type of archway once existed in four places in Wuxi, including the Gu family archway at Gu Kejiu's Shrine in Shijia Lane (rebuilt), the Qin Jin North Four Archways at the east end of Cangqiao Bridge, and the Qin Family Shike South Four Archways at Fengguang Bridge—today only one survives, with relatively high value.

Westward is a one-story one-door archway; inside the archway is the Yongxi (Eternal Blessing) Hall, first built in the 21st year of Chenghua of the Ming (1485), rebuilt in 2004.

West of the hall is the Chengze (Inheriting Grace) Pond and Sanyuan (Tracing Origins) Bridge, built during the Chenghua reign of the Ming.

West of the bridge is the Yuan (Soft-Shelled Turtle) Pond, octagonal, with a chi-dragon head spouting water on the south side inside the pond and a chi-dragon head absorbing water on the north side, leading to the Golden Lotus Pond—hence called the Double Dragon Spring, an important hub of the Huishan water system.

West of the pond is the Xiaozu (Filial Ancestor) Enjoyment Hall, built in the 21st year of Chenghua of the Ming (1485), repaired in the 27th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1762).

The south wall of the enjoyment hall is embedded with 12 pieces of the 1982 re-carved "Zhenshang Studio Album"; this album was originally carved by Hua Xia asking Wen Zhengming father and son to trace and Zhang Zao to carve, hailed as the "number one carved album of the Ming Dynasty"; Wen Zhengming once painted the "Zhenshang Studio Painting" for Hua Xia.

In 2005, a stele corridor was added north of the enjoyment hall.

West of the enjoyment hall is the Chengzhi (Aspiring to Ambition) Tower, first built in the 17th year of Hongzhi of the Ming (1504), rebuilt in 2005; the courtyard in front of the tower has beautiful flowers and rocks, and climbing the tower offers a view of Xishan.

Southeast of the Hua Xiaozi Shrine is the Zhide (Ultimate Virtue) Shrine, enshrining Taibo, first built in the 30th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1765), rebuilt in 1959—a key building of the Huishan Ancestral Hall Complex, designated a national protected site in 2006.

North of the Zhide Shrine, from west to east, are also the Li Zhongding Shrine, enshrining the anti-Jin general Li Gang, first built in the 5th year of Kangxi of the Qing (1666), rebuilt in 2005; the Zhou Zhonggong Shrine enshrines the Song scholar Zhou Hao, with Zhou Diguang and Zhou Deji father and son as accompanying deities, first built by Zhou Diguang, rebuilt in 2005; the Zhang Yishi Shrine; the Ji Liushan Shrine enshrines the Qing loyal martyr Ji Yongren, first built in the 7th year of Yongzheng of the Qing (1729), rebuilt in 2005; the Guo Junma Shrine enshrines the Song commandery prince consort Guo Mengyu, rebuilt in 2005.

Exiting through the north gate of the Ji Liushan Shrine, one returns to the Vajra Hall of Huishan Temple, ending the tour.

建筑要点 / Key Features
锡惠公园位于北塘区惠山古镇以锡山惠山命名包括锡山全部、惠山东麓及连接两山的映山湖重要景点有惠山寺及其园林祠堂、寄畅园和锡山名胜等；惠山有多个古称据唐代陆羽游惠山寺记载老子枕中记作吴西神山南朝时多取北方山川郡邑之名取舜耕于历山之意称作历山顾欢吴地记作华山因山有九峰又称作九龙山或斗龙山传说晋僧慧照曾在此弘法还称作慧山最后一种称呼流传最广因慧惠相通最后定名惠山；惠山寺前身是南朝宋长史湛挺的历山草堂南朝宋景平元年423年舍宅为寺称华山精舍南朝梁大同三年537年建大雄宝殿寺名法云禅院因山中出青莲花又称慧山寺唐会昌年间寺毁大中元年847年重建唐乾符三年876年建陀罗尼经幢北宋至道二年996年赐额普利院北宋熙宁三年1070年建大白伞盖神咒幢北宋靖康元年1126年钦宗将普利禅院赐给李纲为功德院南宋绍兴年间宋高宗又赐给信安郡王孟忠厚元末明初寺庙屡遭火灾多次重建明永乐五年1407年重建大雄宝殿始称惠山寺禅院明正统十年1445年又毁于火风水家认为惠山寺坐西朝东右前方锡山高耸左前方却是平地右有青龙而左缺白虎因此火灾频发于是巡抚周忱用烧毁的瓦石在寺庙左前方堆筑了一座护山即今寄畅园西部假山的前身当时惠山寺的发展达
11 惠山祠堂群
Ancestral Hall Complex at Huishan Mountain
唐—清
级别 Level
第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年），其中华孝子祠、至德祠、尤文简公祠、钱武肃王祠、淮湘昭忠祠（以上在锡惠公园内）、潜庐（留耕草堂）、王恩绶祠（武愍公）、杨藕芳祠、顾可久祠（洞阳先生）、陆宣公祠10座为重点祠堂
地址 Address
惠山寺南北，向东延伸到直街、横街、寺塘泾和惠山浜一带
类型 Type
祠堂群/历史文化街区
门票 Ticket
通票30元，可参观任何已开放的祠堂；单座祠堂门票10元
中文原文

从唐代开始，惠山就建有华孝子祠和春申君祠等；明清以来民间立祠，出现了大量家祠，无锡皆以能在惠山占得一席之地祭祀先贤、先祖为荣。如今在惠山寺南北，向东延伸到直街、横街、寺塘泾和惠山浜一带，建有大小祠堂118处。

这些祠堂时间跨度近500年，主要包括钦定官设和民间联宗立庙两大类，细分为神祠、先贤祠、墓祠、寺院祠、贞节祠、宗祠、专祠、书院祠、园林祠、行会祠十小类，祭祀人物之多、建筑密度之大、祠堂类型之全，为国内外所罕见，生动地诠释了中国的忠孝文化。

1. 潜庐（留耕草堂）：位于上河塘20号，西与2008年复建的寄畅园朝房相通，为惠山祠堂群重点建筑。杨宗濂（字艺芳，1832—1905）曾先后追随曾国藩、李鸿章攻伐太平军、捻军，军功卓著，《清史稿·列传239》有传。

清光绪八年（1882年）其母病重，他潜行回乡探视，遭到政敌弹劾罢官，于是在惠山脚构筑园亭，取《易经》"潜龙勿用"之意命名潜庐，并在庐旁祭祀父亲杨延望。留耕草堂为园中主厅，向南隔池对着戏台，另有望山亭、丛桂轩诸景。

清光绪十一年（1885年）杨宗濂复出，先后为李鸿章筹建北洋武备学堂，与人合办天津自来火公司等；清光绪二十一年（1895年）与其弟杨宗瀚筹办无锡第一家纺织企业——业勤纱厂。杨宗濂任官期间，胞弟杨以退隐居潜庐，教授子弟读书，间与士绅雅集，名声颇著。

潜庐后传杨翰西、杨彦斌之手，得以修复保存。杨翰西另在鼋头渚修筑了横云草堂。2. 王恩绶祠（武愍公）：位于下河塘8号，为惠山祠堂群重点建筑。王恩绶（1804—1855）字乐山，太平军攻克武昌时死于武昌知县任上，清同治十三年（1874年）状元洪钧奏请敕建祠堂。

祠园分为东、中、西三组院落，中院由门厅、碑亭、二门和工字殿组成，西院祭祀王恩绶之子，东院有月洞门、水池、戏台和介福堂。今为无锡非遗展览馆，主要展示无锡泥人。3. 杨藕芳祠：位于下河塘，为惠山祠堂群重点建筑。

杨宗瀚（字藕芳，1839—1910）是杨宗濂胞弟，曾入李鸿章、刘铭传幕府，到台湾担任台北道员，总办水陆商务、洋务，他开发建设了台湾第一条铁路，后又创办了上海机器织布厂和无锡业勤纱厂，是我国近代工业的创始人。这座祠堂建于1911年，采用青砖拱券的西洋风格，在惠山祠堂中独具特色。4. 顾可久祠（洞阳先生）：与杨藕芳祠相连，为惠山祠堂群重点建筑。

顾可久（1485—1561）字与新，号洞阳，明正德九年（1514年）进士。他为官耿直，曾两次因进谏遭受廷杖，可同官至广东按察司副使，督学粤东时注意选拔人才，举荐了海瑞。后来他受到权臣中伤，罢官回乡，明隆庆四年复碧山吟社，参与赋诗雅集，度过晚年。

明万历元年（1573年）海瑞亲临谒拜，题诗曰："两朝崇祀庙谟新，抗疏名传骨鲠臣。志矢回天曾叩马，功同浴日再批鳞。庭留训诲留余泽，史阙忠贞忆旧臣。功同浴日再批鳞……"从中可见顾可久对海瑞的影响。

清康熙二十七年（1688年）祠庙毁于火，次年重建，乾隆年间两次重修。祠中有拜石山房、丈人峰、浴日泉和四面牌坊（近年复建）等。以丈人峰最为珍贵，此石原在明代冯夔的竹素园中，乾隆年间顾光旭将其移至祠内，请秦瀛作《拜石山房记》。

此石高近4米，与拜石山房隔水相望，犹如伟岸的丈人，顾光旭借此象征先祖的精神与品格。5. 李公祠（惠山园）：入口在百岁街，祭祀李鸿章之弟、淮军将领李鹤章。李鹤章（1825—1880）是李鸿章创办淮军时的骨干，攻伐太平军期间，"躬冒矢石，奋勇争先"，战功显赫，获赐黄马褂和三品甘凉道台。后因李鸿章"避嫌不举"，李鹤章辞官不就，隐居故里。

无锡是李鹤章与太平军激战并取得成功之地，他去世后曾国荃上疏为其在惠山建造专祠。祠堂为徽派风格，集木、砖、石三雕和彩绘于一体。1929年合并改筑为惠山公园，1950年李鸿章、李鹤章被视为镇压太平军的刽子手，祠、园被拆除。2008年复建李公祠和惠山园。

6. 惠山泥人厂旧址：位于古华路，今为中国泥人博物馆，隈研吾设计。2006年惠山泥人入选国家级非物质质文保名录。惠山北坡出产黑泥，质地细腻，塑性极强，从明代起附近守祠堂的祠丁就在闲暇时做泥人。每到庙会期间，香客游人络绎不绝，祠丁多在门口出摊或沿街叫卖，形成惠山泥人一条街。

孩子买阿福，老人买寿星，恋人买和合二仙，商人买财神……精巧的泥人成为最受欢迎的无锡特产。7. 陆宣公祠：位于直街（绣嶂街）43号，祭祀唐代宰相陆贽（754—805），为惠山祠堂群重点建筑。

北宋建中靖国元年（1101年），陆氏迁锡始祖陆棐在惠山为陆贽建祠。明代毁坏，清康熙年间陆慧玉奉檄复建，嘉庆年间重修。

今祠共三进，有戏楼、池沼、石桥和仰贤堂、大殿和后殿等。陆宣公祠东为范文正公祠，西为倪云林祠。

8. 张中丞庙：位于直街120号，祀唐代安史之乱中抗击叛军殉职的御史中丞张巡，始建于南宋建炎二年（1128年），明成化九年（1473年）重建，清道光十一年（1831年）毁后又建，并增筑许远祠。

太平天国时期庙毁，清同治八年（1869年）重建，1995年列为省保单位。庙坐南朝北，背倚锡山，由北向南依次为门厅、二层戏台、大殿和后殿等。

大殿前院有两株400多年的古银杏，院东有明万历十五年（1587年）所凿云泉古井。主殿西侧为许远殿，其西有花篮厅和古鲁班殿。9. 龙光塔：张中丞庙后殿有山道通向锡山山顶。锡山龙光塔为无锡的地标建筑，是一座文峰塔，塔下建龙光寺。

惠山又称九龙山，锡山在其东侧，被风水家视为龙角，建议在山顶建塔，能使无锡文风昌盛。明嘉靖元年（1522年）顾懋章、顾可学父子在山顶建石塔。但无锡科举未见起色。风水家又说，龙靠角来听，中空才能听音，实心的石塔并不相宜。

明万历四年（1576年），常州知府施观民又在石塔旁建了一座八角七层砖塔，题名龙光塔。在明代万历年间绘制的《寄畅园图册》中，有三幅图表现了山顶一石一砖两塔共存的景致。康熙、雍正、道光年间龙光塔多次重修，1999年再次大修。

· · · · ·
English

From the Tang Dynasty, Huishan already had the Hua Xiaozi (Hua the Filial Son) Shrine and Chunshen Jun Shrine; during the Ming and Qing,民间 established shrines, with numerous family shrines appearing, and Wuxi people all took pride in being able to occupy a place at Huishan to sacrifice to former worthies and ancestors.

Today, north and south of Huishan Temple, extending eastward to Zhijie, Hengjie, Sitangjing, and Huishanbang areas, there are 118 ancestral halls of various sizes.

These ancestral halls span nearly 500 years, mainly including two categories: officially established by imperial decree and jointly established by clans; subdivided into ten minor categories: deity shrines, former-worthy shrines, tomb shrines, temple shrines, chastity shrines, clan shrines, special shrines, academy shrines, garden shrines, and guild shrines.

The number of people sacrificed to, the density of buildings, and the completeness of shrine types are rare at home and abroad, vividly interpreting Chinese culture of loyalty and filial piety.1.

Qianlu (Liugeng Caotang): Located at No.20 Shanghetang, connected westward to the Jichang Garden audience hall rebuilt in 2008, a key building of the Huishan Ancestral Hall Complex.

Yang Zonglian (style name Yifang, 1832-1905) successively followed Zeng Guofan and Li Hongzhang to attack the Taiping Army and Nian Army, with outstanding military merits, recorded in "Draft History of Qing·Biography 239.

" In the 8th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1882), when his mother was seriously ill, he secretly returned home to visit, was impeached by political opponents and dismissed, so he built pavilions and gardens at the foot of Huishan, taking the meaning of "a hidden dragon should not act" from the "Book of Changes" to name it Qianlu (Hidden Cottage), and sacrificed to his father Yang Yanwang beside the cottage.

Liugeng Caotang (Plowing-Gone Thatched Hall) is the main hall of the garden, facing a stage across a pond to the south, with other scenic spots such as Wangshan Pavilion and Conggui Studio.

In the 11th year of Guangxu (1885), Yang Zonglian returned to office, successively preparing to build the Beiyang Military Academy for Li Hongzhang and co-founding the Tianjin Self-Match Company etc.

; in the 21st year of Guangxu (1895), together with his younger brother Yang Zonghan, he prepared to establish Wuxi's first textile enterprise—Yiqin Cotton Mill.

During Yang Zonglian's official tenure, his younger brother Yang Yi retired to live in seclusion at Qianlu, teaching children to read and occasionally gathering with gentry for elegant gatherings, with a considerable reputation.

Qianlu later passed to Yang Hanxi and Yang Yanbin,得以 repaired and preserved.Yang Hanxi also built the Hengyun Thatched Hall at Yuantouzhu.2.

Wang Enshou Shrine (Wumin Gong): Located at No.8 Xiahetang, a key building of the Huishan Ancestral Hall Complex.

Wang Enshou (1804-1855), style name Leshan, died in office as magistrate of Wuchang when the Taiping Army captured Wuchang; in the 13th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1874), zhuangyuan Hong Jun petitioned for an imperial decree to build the shrine.

The shrine garden is divided into east, middle, and west groups of courtyards; the middle courtyard consists of the gate hall, stele pavilion, second gate, and I-shaped hall; the west courtyard sacrifices to Wang Enshou's son; the east courtyard has a moon gate, pond, stage, and Jiefu Hall.

Today it is the Wuxi Intangible Cultural Heritage Exhibition Hall, mainly displaying Wuxi clay figures.3.Yang Oufang Shrine: Located at Xiahetang, a key building of the Huishan Ancestral Hall Complex.

Yang Zonghan (style name Oufang, 1839-1910) was Yang Zonglian's younger brother, once served in the shogunates of Li Hongzhang and Liu Mingchuan, went to Taiwan as Taipei Circuit Intendant, in charge of land and water commerce and foreign affairs; he developed and built Taiwan's first railway, later founded the Shanghai Machine Weaving Factory and Wuxi Yiqin Cotton Mill—a founder of China's modern industry.

This shrine was built in 1911, adopting the Western style of blue brick arches, unique among the Huishan ancestral halls.4.

Gu Kejiu Shrine (Dongyang Xiansheng): Connected to the Yang Oufang Shrine, a key building of the Huishan Ancestral Hall Complex.

Gu Kejiu (1485-1561), style name Yuxin, hao Dongyang, passed the jinshi examination in the 9th year of Zhengde of the Ming (1514).

He was upright in office, twice suffered court flogging for remonstrating; Gu Ke served as Vice Commissioner of the Guangdong Provincial Surveillance Commission, paying attention to selecting talents when supervising education in eastern Guangdong, recommending Hai Rui.

Later he was maligned by powerful officials and dismissed, returning home; in the 4th year of Longqing of the Ming (1570) he revived the Bishan Poetry Society, participating in poetry gatherings and elegant assemblies, spending his later years.

In the 1st year of Wanli of the Ming (1573), Hai Rui personally came to pay homage, inscribing a poem: "Two dynasties worship the temple with new plans, his name of upright remonstrance spreads like a bone-loyal minister.

His will aimed to turn back heaven and he once knocked the horse, his merit same as bathing the sun and he again scaled the scales.

The courtyard retains teachings and remaining grace, history lacks loyalty but recalls the old minister..." From this one can see Gu Kejiu's influence on Hai Rui.

In the 27th year of Kangxi of the Qing (1688), the shrine was destroyed by fire, rebuilt the following year, and repaired twice during the Qianlong reign.

In the shrine are the Baishi (Worshiping Stone) Mountain Room, Zhangren (Elder) Peak, Yuri (Bathing Sun) Spring, and Four-Sided Archway (recently rebuilt) etc.

The Zhangren Peak is the most precious; this stone was originally in Feng Kui's Zhusu Garden of the Ming, and during the Qianlong reign Gu Guangxu moved it into the shrine, asking Qin Ying to write the "Record of the Baishi Mountain Room.

" This stone is nearly 4 meters high, facing the Baishi Mountain Room across the water, like a towering elder; Gu Guangxu used it to symbolize the spirit and character of his ancestors.5.

Li Gong Shrine (Huishan Garden): The entrance is on Baisui Street, sacrificing to Li Hezhang, younger brother of Li Hongzhang and a Huai Army general.

Li Hezhang (1825-1880) was a backbone when Li Hongzhang founded the Huai Army; during the campaign against the Taiping Army, he "braved arrows and stones, fighting bravely in the vanguard," with outstanding military merits, awarded the Yellow Riding Jacket and the third-rank Ganliang Circuit Intendant.

Later, because Li Hongzhang "avoided suspicion and did not recommend," Li Hezhang resigned and lived in seclusion in his hometown.

Wuxi was the place where Li Hezhang fought fiercely against the Taiping Army and achieved success; after his death, Zeng Guoquan petitioned to build a special shrine for him at Huishan.

The shrine is in Huizhou style, integrating wood, brick, and stone carvings and painted decorations.

In 1929 it was merged and rebuilt into Huishan Park; in 1950, Li Hongzhang and Li Hezhang were regarded as executioners suppressing the Taiping Army, and the shrine and garden were demolished.

In 2008, Li Gong Shrine and Huishan Garden were rebuilt.6.Former Site of Huishan Clay Figure Factory: Located on Guhua Road, today the China Clay Figure Museum, designed by Kengo Kuma.

In 2006, Huishan clay figures were included in the national intangible cultural heritage list.

The north slope of Huishan produces black clay, fine in texture and highly plastic; from the Ming Dynasty, shrine servants guarding nearby ancestral halls made clay figures in their spare time.

During temple fairs, pilgrims and tourists came in an endless stream, and shrine servants mostly set up stalls at the gate or sold along the street, forming a Huishan clay figure street.

Children bought Afu, the elderly bought the God of Longevity, lovers bought the He-He Twins, merchants bought the God of Wealth...exquisite clay figures became the most popular Wuxi specialty.7.

Lu Xuangong Shrine: Located at No.43 Zhijie (Xiuzhang Street), sacrificing to Tang Dynasty Chancellor Lu Zhi (754-805), a key building of the Huishan Ancestral Hall Complex.

In the 1st year of Jianzhong Jingguo of the Northern Song (1101), Lu Fei, the ancestor of the Lu family who moved to Wuxi, built a shrine for Lu Zhi at Huishan.

Destroyed in the Ming, rebuilt by Lu Huiyu under imperial decree during the Kangxi reign of the Qing, and repaired during the Jiaqing reign.

Today the shrine has three bays, with a stage, pond, stone bridge, Yangxian Hall, main hall, and rear hall etc.East of the Lu Xuangong Shrine is the Fan Wenzheng Shrine, west is the Ni Yunlin Shrine.

8.Zhang Zhongcheng Temple: Located at No.

120 Zhijie, sacrificing to Zhang Xun, Censorate Vice Censor-in-Chief who died fighting the rebel army during the An Lushan Rebellion of the Tang, first built in the 2nd year of Jianyan of the Southern Song (1128), rebuilt in the 9th year of Chenghua of the Ming (1473), destroyed and rebuilt in the 11th year of Daoguang of the Qing (1831), with the Xu Yuan Shrine added.

Destroyed during the Taiping Rebellion, rebuilt in the 8th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1869), designated a provincial protected site in 1995.

The temple faces south with its back to Xishan, from north to south successively the gate hall, two-story stage, main hall, and rear hall etc.

In the front courtyard of the main hall are two ancient ginkgo trees over 400 years old; east of the courtyard is the Yunquan ancient well dug in the 15th year of Wanli of the Ming (1587).

West of the main hall is the Xu Yuan Hall, west of which are the Flower Basket Hall and Ancient Luban Hall.9.

Longguang Pagoda: From the rear hall of the Zhang Zhongcheng Temple, a mountain path leads to the top of Xishan.

The Xishan Longguang Pagoda is Wuxi's landmark building, a cultural-prosperity (wenfeng) pagoda, with the Longguang Temple built below it.

Huishan is also called Jiulong (Nine Dragons) Mountain; Xishan is on its east side, regarded by fengshui masters as the dragon's horn, suggesting that building a pagoda on the mountain top would make Wuxi's literary culture prosper.

In the 1st year of Jiajing of the Ming (1522), Gu Maozhang and Gu Kexue father and son built a stone pagoda on the mountain top.

But Wuxi's imperial examination success did not improve.

Fengshui masters then said that dragons hear through their horns, and hollow horns can hear, while a solid stone pagoda is not suitable.

In the 4th year of Wanli of the Ming (1576), Shi Guanmin, Prefect of Changzhou, built an octagonal seven-story brick pagoda beside the stone pagoda, named Longguang (Dragon Light) Pagoda.

In the "Jichang Garden Album" painted during the Wanli reign of the Ming, three paintings show the scene of one stone and one brick pagoda coexisting on the mountain top.

During the Kangxi, Yongzheng, and Daoguang reigns, the Longguang Pagoda was repaired multiple times, and again majorly repaired in 1999.

建筑要点 / Key Features
从唐代开始惠山就建有华孝子祠和春申君祠等明清以来民间立祠出现了大量家祠无锡皆以能在惠山占得一席之地祭祀先贤先祖为荣如今在惠山寺南北向东延伸到直街横街寺塘泾和惠山浜一带有大小祠堂118处这些祠堂时间跨度近500年主要包括钦定官设和民间联宗立庙两大类细分为神祠先贤祠墓祠寺院祠贞节祠宗祠专祠书院祠园林祠行会祠十小类祭祀人物之多建筑密度之大祠堂类型之全为国内外所罕见生动地诠释了中国的忠孝文化；潜庐留耕草堂位于上河塘20号西与2008年复建的寄畅园朝房相通为惠山祠堂群重点建筑杨宗濂字艺芳1832-1905曾先后追随曾国藩李鸿章攻伐太平军捻军军功卓著清史稿列传239有传清光绪八年1882年其母病重他潜行回乡探视遭到政敌弹劾罢官于是在惠山脚构筑园亭取易经潜龙勿用之意命名潜庐并在庐旁祭祀父亲杨延望留耕草堂为园中主厅向南隔池对着戏台另有望山亭丛桂轩诸景清光绪十一年1885年杨宗濂复出先后为李鸿章筹建北洋武备学堂与人合办天津自来火公司等清光绪二十一年1895年与其弟杨宗瀚筹办无锡第一家纺织企业业勤纱厂杨宗濂任官期间胞弟杨以退隐居潜庐教授子弟读书间与士绅雅集名声颇著潜庐后传杨翰西杨彦斌之手得以修复保存杨翰西
12 荣氏梅园
Rong's Plum Garden
1912—1934
级别 Level
第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
地址 Address
滨湖区梁溪西路卞家湾13号
类型 Type
近代园林
门票 Ticket
60元（或购买五园联票，见锡惠公园）
中文原文

1906年工商实业家荣德生游览苏州留园，萌生造园之念，1912年他购得荣巷以西的东山坡地种植梅花，并开筑连接梅园与城区的公路，方便人们游赏。此后陆续盖房、凿泉、建寺、立塔，1934年基本建成，在中国近代公园史上具有重要意义。

梅园入口原在今大门之西，入门有荣德生手植紫藤，右侧墙角为洗心泉，沿紫藤棚架向前可见荣德生手书"梅园"刻石。向北，一座高台掩映在繁密的梅林中，其上点缀六角小亭，为天心台，台基用黄石垒砌，登台入亭可周赏园景。台南屹立三块湖石，题名"米襄阳拜石"，为乾隆朝大学士兼军机大臣、曾编著《日下旧闻考》的金坛人于敏中（1714—1779）园中旧物。台西为揖蠡亭，向商界之祖范蠡致敬。

继续向北为香海轩，轩前有荣德生铜像，轩后建楠木正厅诵豳堂，堂后为招鹤亭与乐农别墅。别墅前安放着三片石磨，乃荣家始创面粉厂时从法国进口，后来改用粉机，拆下的石磨被安放在新建的梅园中。沿山路向北，迎面耸立一塔，八角三层，乃1930年荣氏兄弟为纪念母亲80冥寿建造的"念劬塔"。

塔位于高处，成为园中的标志建筑，在多处都可见到；登塔可俯瞰园内景色，北倚惠山群峰，南对太湖万顷，借景绝佳。塔东为建于1923年的宗敬别墅，采用西洋风格；更东为建于1926年的秋丹阁，荣氏子弟求学的读书处、豁然洞，以及建于1933年的开原寺。

出寺沿山路折而向西，经植物博览馆可达古梅奇石圃、远香堂、花溪和积雪堂等，返回景区入口。以上为梅园主景区，此外，北区为梅品种登录园，展示梅品种和梅桩造型等；东区为中日梅花观赏园，由吟风阁、纮齐苑和畹芬堂等组成。

· · · · ·
English

In 1906, industrialist Rong Desheng visited Suzhou's Lingering Garden and conceived the idea of building a garden.

In 1912, he purchased the east hillside land west of Rongxiang to plant plum blossoms, and built a road connecting the Plum Garden with the city to facilitate people's visits.

Thereafter he successively built houses, dug springs, built temples, and erected pagodas, basically completed in 1934, with important significance in the history of modern Chinese parks.

The Plum Garden entrance was originally west of today's main gate; entering, there is a wisteria planted by Rong Desheng himself, the Xixin (Heart-Cleansing) Spring at the right corner, and along the wisteria trellis forward one can see the "Plum Garden" stone carving in Rong Desheng's own handwriting.

Northward, a high terrace is hidden among dense plum forests, with a hexagonal small pavilion on it—the Tianxin (Heavenly Heart) Terrace; the terrace base is built of yellow stone, and climbing onto the terrace and entering the pavilion allows one to enjoy the garden scenery all around.

South of the terrace stand three Taihu rocks, titled "Mi Xiangyang Worshiping Rocks," originally from the garden of Yu Minzhong (1714-1779) of Jintan, a Grand Secretary and Grand Councilor of the Qianlong reign who compiled the "Investigations into Old News under the Sun.

" West of the terrace is the Yili (Saluting Li) Pavilion, paying tribute to Fan Li, the ancestor of the business world.

Continuing northward is the Xianghai (Fragrant Sea) Studio, with a bronze statue of Rong Desheng in front; behind the studio is the nanmu main hall Songbin (Reciting Bin) Hall, and behind the hall are the Zhahe (Crane-Calling) Pavilion and Lenong (Happy Farmer) Villa.

In front of the villa are placed three stone millstones, imported from France when the Rong family first founded the flour mill; later switching to powder machines, the removed stone millstones were placed in the newly built Plum Garden.

Following the mountain path northward, a pagoda rises head-on, octagonal and three-story—the "Nianqu (Remembering Toil) Pagoda" built by the Rong brothers in 1930 to commemorate their mother's 80th posthumous birthday.

The pagoda is located at a high place, becoming the landmark building of the garden, visible from many places; climbing the pagoda offers a bird's-eye view of the garden scenery, backed by the Huishan peaks to the north and facing the vast Taihu Lake to the south—excellent borrowed scenery.

East of the pagoda is the Zongjing Villa built in 1923, adopting Western style; further east is the Qiudan Pavilion built in 1926, the study place for the Rong family's children, the Huoran (Suddenly Enlightened) Cave, and the Kaiyuan Temple built in 1933.

Exiting the temple and turning west along the mountain path, passing the Plant Expo Hall, one reaches the Ancient Plum and Strange Rock Garden, Yuanxiang (Distant Fragrance) Hall, Flower Stream, and Jixue (Accumulated Snow) Hall etc.

, returning to the scenic area entrance.

The above is the main scenic area of the Plum Garden; in addition, the north area is the Plum Variety Registration Garden, displaying plum varieties and plum stump shapes etc.

; the east area is the Sino-Japanese Plum Blossom Viewing Garden, composed of the Yinfeng Pavilion, Hongqi Garden, and Wanfen Hall etc.

建筑要点 / Key Features
1906年工商实业家荣德生游览苏州留园萌生造园之念1912年他购得荣巷以西的东山坡地种植梅花并开筑连接梅园与城区的公路方便人们游赏此后陆续盖房凿泉建寺立塔1934年基本建成在中国近代公园史上具有重要意义；梅园入口原在今大门之西入门有荣德生手植紫藤右侧墙角为洗心泉沿紫藤棚架向前可见荣德生手书梅园刻石向北一座高台掩映在繁密的梅林中其上点缀六角小亭为天心台台基用黄石垒砌登台入亭可周赏园景台南屹立三块湖石题名米襄阳拜石为乾隆朝大学士兼军机大臣曾编著日下旧闻考的金坛人于敏中1714-1779园中旧物台西为揖蠡亭向商界之祖范蠡致敬继续向北为香海轩轩前有荣德生铜像轩后建楠木正厅诵豳堂堂后为招鹤亭与乐农别墅别墅前安放着三片石磨乃荣家始创面粉厂时从法国进口后来改用粉机拆下的石磨被安放在新建的梅园中沿山路向北迎面耸立一塔八角三层乃1930年荣氏兄弟为纪念母亲80冥寿建造的念劬塔塔位于高处成为园中的标志建筑在多处都可见到登塔可俯瞰园内景色北倚惠山群峰南对太湖万顷借景绝佳塔东为建于1923年的宗敬别墅采用西洋风格更东为建于1926年的秋丹阁荣氏子弟求学的读书处豁然洞以及建于1933年的开原寺出寺沿山路折而向西
13 荣巷
Modern Building Complex in Rongxiang
清
级别 Level
第五批江苏省文物保护单位（2002年）
地址 Address
滨湖区荣巷街
类型 Type
历史街区/近代建筑群
中文原文

明正统初年（1436年）无锡荣氏始祖荣清从金陵迁居此地，繁衍为荣氏家族。太平天国时期荣巷大半被毁，1896年荣宗敬、荣德生兄弟随父亲到上海开设钱庄，后回无锡创办茂新面粉厂和振新纱厂，成为中国民族工业巨擘。

荣德生之子荣毅仁被称为红色资本家，1993年至1998年担任国家副主席。荣巷是中国近代民族工商业发祥地之一，长约380米，街道集市各业齐全，有150多幢老宅，包括祠堂、学校、图书馆、钱庄、医院等，是一处保存完整的历史街区。

· · · · ·
English

In the early years of Zhengtong of the Ming (1436), Rong Qing, the ancestor of the Wuxi Rong family, moved here from Jinling (Nanjing), multiplying into the Rong family clan.

During the Taiping Rebellion, most of Rongxiang was destroyed.

In 1896, brothers Rong Zongjing and Rong Desheng followed their father to Shanghai to open a money shop, later returning to Wuxi to found the Maoxin Flour Mill and Zhenxin Cotton Mill, becoming giants of Chinese national industry.

Rong Desheng's son Rong Yiren was called a "red capitalist," serving as Vice President of the People's Republic of China from 1993 to 1998.

Rongxiang is one of the birthplaces of modern Chinese national industry and commerce, about 380 meters long, with complete streets and markets of all trades, over 150 old houses including ancestral halls, schools, libraries, money shops, and hospitals—a well-preserved historical block.

建筑要点 / Key Features
明正统初年1436年无锡荣氏始祖荣清从金陵迁居此地繁衍为荣氏家族太平天国时期荣巷大半被毁1896年荣宗敬荣德生兄弟随父亲到上海开设钱庄后回无锡创办茂新面粉厂和振新纱厂成为中国民族工业巨擘荣德生之子荣毅仁被称为红色资本家1993年至1998年担任国家副主席荣巷是中国近代民族工商业发祥地之一长约380米街道集市各业齐全有150多幢老宅包括祠堂学校图书馆钱庄医院等是一处保存完整的历史街区
14 蠡园
Scenic Area of Li Lake
民国
级别 Level
第五批江苏省文物保护单位（2002年）
地址 Address
滨湖区环湖路青祁路70号
类型 Type
近代园林/风景名胜
门票 Ticket
门票60元（或购买五园联票，见锡惠公园）
开放时间 Hours
6:00 — 17:30
中文原文

由梅园沿环湖路直到金城湾公园为蠡湖风景区，主要景点有管社山庄、万顷堂、渤公岛、鸥鹭岛、渔父岛、蠡湖中央公园、双虹园、宝界公园、茹经堂、蠡园及渔庄、蠡湖公园、西施庄、水居苑和大桥公园等。其中渤公岛与蠡园及渔庄较为精彩。蠡湖是太湖伸入无锡的内湖，相传范蠡引退后偕西施隐居于此，又名五里湖、漆湖或小五湖。

1927年至1937年间王禹卿父子建蠡园，1930年至1937年间陈梅芳建渔庄，又名"赛蠡园"，1952年将两园连通，成为一处景区。

2002年"蠡园及渔庄"成为省保单位，2005年成为4A景区。游览蠡园最好的时节是三月的桃花节或七八月的荷花展。园中较精彩的是归云峰假山，为陈梅芳聘请浙江东阳叠山家蒋家元所叠，用大量的湖石和笋石堆出山峦洞窟，人行其中，如入迷宫。

此外，在千步长廊和湖心亭欣赏湖景和凝春塔也别有趣味。

· · · · ·
English

From the Plum Garden along Huanhu Road to Jinchengwan Park is the Li Lake Scenic Area, with main scenic spots including Guanshe Villa, Wanqing Hall, Bogong Island, Oulu Island, Yufu Island, Li Lake Central Park, Shuanghong Garden, Baojie Park, Rujing Hall, Li Garden and Fishing Villa, Li Lake Park, Xishi Village, Shuiju Garden, and Daqiao Park etc.

Among them, Bogong Island and Li Garden & Fishing Villa are more splendid.

Li Lake is an inner lake of Taihu extending into Wuxi; legend says that after Fan Li retired, he lived in seclusion here with Xishi, hence also called Wuli Lake, Qi Lake, or Xiaowu Lake.

From 1927 to 1937, Wang Yuqing father and son built Li Garden; from 1930 to 1937, Chen Meifang built the Fishing Villa, also called "Sai Li Garden" (Surpassing Li Garden); in 1952 the two gardens were connected into one scenic area.

In 2002 "Li Garden and Fishing Villa" became a provincial protected site, and in 2005 became a 4A scenic area.

The best seasons to visit Li Garden are the Peach Blossom Festival in March or the Lotus Exhibition in July-August.

The most splendid part of the garden is the Guiyun Peak rockery, piled by Jiang Jiayuan, a rockery master from Dongyang, Zhejiang, hired by Chen Meifang, using large amounts of Taihu rocks and bamboo shoot stones to pile up mountains and caves—walking through it is like entering a labyrinth.

In addition, enjoying the lake scenery and the Ningchun Pagoda from the Thousand-Step Corridor and the Lake Center Pavilion is also quite interesting.

建筑要点 / Key Features
由梅园沿环湖路直到金城湾公园为蠡湖风景区主要景点有管社山庄万顷堂渤公岛鸥鹭岛渔父岛蠡湖中央公园双虹园宝界公园茹经堂蠡园及渔庄蠡湖公园西施庄水居苑和大桥公园等其中渤公岛与蠡园及渔庄较为精彩蠡湖是太湖伸入无锡的内湖相传范蠡引退后偕西施隐居于此又名五里湖漆湖或小五湖1927年至1937年间王禹卿父子建蠡园1930年至1937年间陈梅芳建渔庄又名赛蠡园1952年将两园连通成为一处景区2002年蠡园及渔庄成为省保单位2005年成为4A景区游览蠡园最好的时节是三月的桃花节或七八月的荷花展园中较精彩的是归云峰假山为陈梅芳聘请浙江东阳叠山家蒋家元所叠用大量的湖石和笋石堆出山峦洞窟人行其中如入迷宫此外在千步长廊和湖心亭欣赏湖景和凝春塔也别有趣味
15 鼋头渚
Turtle Head Isle
西汉—民国
级别 Level
国家5A景区，2006年列为江苏省文物保护单位
地址 Address
滨湖区鼋头渚风景区
类型 Type
风景名胜
门票 Ticket
105元（或购买五园联票，见锡惠公园），学生票50元，含园内游览车门票和往返太湖仙岛船票
中文原文

鼋头渚位于滨湖区，是充山西南麓深入太湖中的半岛，因状如鼋头而得名，被誉为"太湖第一名胜"。锡惠公园荟萃了无锡的人文名胜，鼋头渚则是无锡天然山水的代表。西汉末期王莽篡位，无锡人虞俊不肯附逆而殉难，归葬宝界山，刘秀登基后赐朱衣覆盖坟茔，"朱衣宝界"渐成名胜。南朝萧梁时僧人在充山北麓建广福庵。

北宋末期钱绅（康熙《无锡县志》卷20有传）在宝界山筑别业、构通惠亭，蒋瑑为作《通惠亭记》。元明以来，文人墨客到此游玩题诗者络绎不绝，明代著名画家王问、王鉴父子在钱绅别业旧址筑湖山草堂。

鼋头渚的大规模开发始于民国。1918年乡绅杨翰西建横云山庄，1924年又捐地助僧人迁建广福寺于今址，1934年荣德生捐出六十寿辰寿金建造宝界桥（2011年列为省保单位），共60孔，将鼋头渚与东岸相连。

此后陆续修建各类建筑，2002年鼋头渚被列为国家5A景区，2006年列为省保单位。

· · · · ·
English

Yuantouzhu (Turtle Head Isle) is located in Binhu District, a peninsula extending into Taihu Lake from the southwestern foot of Chongshan Mountain, named for its turtle-head shape, hailed as "the number one scenic spot of Taihu.

" While Xihui Park gathers Wuxi's cultural and historical scenic spots, Yuantouzhu is the representative of Wuxi's natural mountains and waters.

At the end of the Western Han, when Wang Mang usurped the throne, Wuxi native Yu Jun refused to submit to the traitor and died for his cause, buried at Baojie Mountain; after Liu Xiu ascended the throne, he bestowed red garments to cover the tomb, and "Red Garment Baojie" gradually became a famous scenic spot.

During the Southern Dynasties Liang, monks built the Guangfu Nunnery at the northern foot of Chongshan.

At the end of the Northern Song, Qian Shen (with a biography in Kangxi's "Wuxi County Gazetteer" vol.

20) built a villa and the Tonghui Pavilion at Baojie Mountain, and Jiang Zhuan wrote the "Record of the Tonghui Pavilion.

" Since the Yuan and Ming, literati and poets have come here to play and inscribe poems in an endless stream; the famous Ming painters Wang Wen and Wang Jian father and son built the Hushan Thatched Hall on the site of Qian Shen's villa.

The large-scale development of Yuantouzhu began in the Republic of China.

In 1918, local gentry Yang Hanxi built the Hengyun Mountain Villa; in 1924 he donated land to help monks relocate the Guangfu Temple to today's site; in 1934, Rong Desheng donated his 60th birthday celebration funds to build the Baojie Bridge (designated a provincial protected site in 2011), with 60 arches, connecting Yuantouzhu with the east bank.

Thereafter various buildings were successively constructed; in 2002 Yuantouzhu was listed as a national 5A scenic area, and in 2006 designated a provincial protected site.

建筑要点 / Key Features
鼋头渚位于滨湖区是充山西南麓深入太湖中的半岛因状如鼋头而得名被誉为太湖第一名胜锡惠公园荟萃了无锡的人文名胜鼋头渚则是无锡天然山水的代表西汉末期王莽篡位无锡人虞俊不肯附逆而殉难归葬宝界山刘秀登基后赐朱衣覆盖坟茔朱衣宝界渐成名胜南朝萧梁时僧人在充山北麓建广福庵北宋末期钱绅康熙无锡县志卷20有传在宝界山筑别业构通惠亭蒋瑑为作通惠亭记元明以来文人墨客到此游玩题诗者络绎不绝明代著名画家王问王鉴父子在钱绅别业旧址筑湖山草堂鼋头渚的大规模开发始于民国1918年乡绅杨翰西建横云山庄1924年又捐地助僧人迁建广福寺于今址1934年荣德生捐出六十寿辰寿金建造宝界桥2011年列为省保单位共60孔将鼋头渚与东岸相连此后陆续修建各类建筑2002年鼋头渚被列为国家5A景区2006年列为省保单位

9:00 — 17:00
中文原文

阖闾城位于无锡市滨湖区胡埭镇和常州市武进区雪堰桥交界处。吴王阖闾在位期间（前515—前496）为进攻越国建造阖闾城，此城北倚胥山，南临太湖，西阻越国，北拒楚兵，可攻可守，筑城取土后形成的闾江穿城而过汇入太湖。外围有大城，内包东、西两城，西城规格较高，又分成南城和北城，反映了吴国以西为尊的传统，建有阖庐宫、南城宫、东宫和西宫。

今大城城垣已无，仅存长方形环濠，东、西小城尚存城墙、高土台及部分环濠，以及练兵场、点将台、伍子胥屯兵处和兵器库遗址。如今将建成吴都阖闾城遗址公园。另外在无锡滨湖区马山闾江2号有阖闾城遗址博物馆。

· · · · ·
English

Helv City Site is located at the junction of Hudai Town, Binhu District, Wuxi and Xueyanqiao, Wujin District, Changzhou.

During the reign of King Helü of Wu (515-496 BC), Helü City was built to attack the State of Yue; this city backs onto Xu Mountain to the north, faces Taihu Lake to the south, blocks Yue to the west, and resists Chu troops to the north—able to attack and defend.

The Lüjiang River formed by excavating earth for the city walls passes through the city and flows into Taihu.

The outer part has a large city, containing east and west small cities; the west small city has higher specifications, divided into south and north cities, reflecting the Wu tradition of honoring the west, with the Helü Palace, South City Palace, East Palace, and West Palace built.

Today the large city's walls are gone, only a rectangular moat remains; the east and west small cities still preserve walls, high earth platforms, and parts of the moat, as well as a training ground, general's platform, Wu Zixu's troop station, and armory ruins.

It will now be developed into the Wu Capital Helü City Site Park.Additionally, there is the Helü City Site Museum at No.2 Lüjiang, Mashan, Binhu District, Wuxi.

建筑要点 / Key Features
阖闾城位于无锡市滨湖区胡埭镇和常州市武进区雪堰桥交界处吴王阖闾在位期间前515-前496为进攻越国建造阖闾城此城北倚胥山南临太湖西阻越囯北拒楚兵可攻可守筑城取土后形成的闾江穿城而过汇入太湖外围有大城内包东西两城西城规格较高又分成南城和北城反映了吴国以西为尊的传统建有阖庐宫南城宫东宫和西宫今大城城垣已无仅存长方形环濠东西小城尚存城墙高土台及部分环濠以及练兵场点将台伍子胥屯兵处和兵器库遗址如今将建成吴都阖闾城遗址公园另外在无锡滨湖区马山闾江2号有阖闾城遗址博物馆
17 泰伯庙和墓
Taibo Temple and Tomb
明—清

第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）

滨湖区泰伯中路21号
类型 Type
祠庙/墓葬
门票 Ticket
10元

中文原文

商末泰伯在梅里建立勾吴，开挖最早的人工运河伯渎河。东汉永兴二年（154年）桓帝命吴郡太守糜豹修泰伯庙，并在鸿山立泰伯墓。

北宋元符三年（1100年）谥泰伯为"至德侯"，崇宁年间扩建泰伯庙，明清多次重修，《泰伯梅里志》"泰伯庙图"反映了明弘治年间的格局。

太平天国战争中庙被毁，仅存正殿至德殿。今庙前立照池，上架香花桥，北依次为"至德名邦"牌坊、棂星门、享堂和至德殿。至德殿建于明代，前出青石月台，三面环以栏杆，台上置宝鼎，正面铸"泰伯庙至德殿"六个金字。

大殿面阔五间，进深六架，采用单檐歇山顶，外部有檐廊，檐柱皆用石柱，殿内立14根楠木柱。大殿正中设汉白玉石座，供奉泰伯坐像。殿内嵌有清代历朝修庙碑记13方，是重要的史料。泰伯墓位于鸿山南麓，距梅村三公里。

依山而筑，由月牙池、棂星门、享堂、丹陛、甬道、拜坛、月台、泰伯墓四面碑、罗城和墓墩组成。

· · · · ·
English

At the end of the Shang Dynasty, Taibo established Gouwu in Meili and excavated the earliest artificial canal, the Bodu River.

In the 2nd year of Yongxing of the Eastern Han (154), Emperor Huan ordered Mi Bao, Governor of Wu Commandery, to repair the Taibo Temple and establish the Taibo Tomb at Hongshan.

In the 3rd year of Yuanfu of the Northern Song (1100), Taibo was posthumously titled "Marquis of Ultimate Virtue"; during the Chongning reign the Taibo Temple was expanded, and repaired multiple times during the Ming and Qing.

The "Taibo Meili Gazetteer"'s "Map of Taibo Temple" reflects the layout during the Hongzhi reign of the Ming.

During the Taiping Rebellion war the temple was destroyed, only the main hall Zhide (Ultimate Virtue) Hall survived.

Today in front of the temple stands a reflection pond with a Fragrant Flower Bridge over it; northward are successively the "Ultimate Virtue and Famous State" archway, Lingxing Gate, Enjoyment Hall, and Zhide Hall.

The Zhide Hall was built in the Ming, with a bluestone platform projecting in front, surrounded by railings on three sides; a precious tripod is placed on the platform, with the six golden characters "Taibo Temple Zhide Hall" cast on the front.

The main hall is five bays wide and six rafters deep, adopting a single-eave hip-and-gable roof, with an eave corridor outside, all eave columns made of stone, and 14 nanmu columns inside the hall.

In the center of the main hall is a white marble seat, enshrining a seated statue of Taibo.

Embedded in the hall are 13 stele records of temple repairs from various Qing dynasties—important historical materials.

The Taibo Tomb is located at the southern foot of Hongshan, three kilometers from Meicun.

Built along the mountain, it consists of the Crescent Pond, Lingxing Gate, Enjoyment Hall, Imperial Steps, Path, Worship Altar, Platform, Four-Sided Stele of Taibo Tomb, Enclosing Wall, and Tomb Mound.

建筑要点 / Key Features
商末泰伯在梅里建立勾吴开挖最早的人工运河伯渎河东汉永兴二年154年桓帝命吴郡太守糜豹修泰伯庙并在鸿山立泰伯墓北宋元符三年1100年谥泰伯为至德侯崇宁年间扩建泰伯庙明清多次重修泰伯梅里志泰伯庙图反映了明弘治年间的格局太平天国战争中庙被毁仅存正殿至德殿今庙前立照池上架香花桥北依次为至德名邦牌坊棂星门享堂和至德殿至德殿建于明代前出青石月台三面环以栏杆台上置宝鼎正面铸泰伯庙至德殿六个金字大殿面阔五间进深六架采用单檐歇山顶外部有檐廊檐柱皆用石柱殿内立14根楠木柱大殿正中设汉白玉石座供奉泰伯坐像殿内嵌有清代历朝修庙碑记13方是重要的史料泰伯墓位于鸿山南麓距梅村三公里依山而筑由月牙池棂星门享堂丹陛甬道拜坛月台泰伯墓四面碑罗城和墓墩组成
18 荡口古镇
Dangkou Ancient Town
明—清
级别 Level
含4处13座省保，1处市保，50处历史建筑
地址 Address
无锡市锡山区鹅湖镇荡口
类型 Type
历史文化名镇/古镇
中文原文

荡口古镇位于无锡、苏州交界处，古名丁舍，相传是东汉孝子丁兰故里，后因位于鹅肫荡口得名。明洪武年间华贞固迁居此地，名声渐显。

明中期荡口所在的南延乡成为江南缴纳粮赋第一乡，华氏也发展成无锡的煌煌大族，明、清两代出了37名进士，著名人物如明代侍读学士华察、出版家华燧、收藏家华夏、东林党人、复社成员华允诚、著名音乐家华秋苹、著名数学家华蘅芳、华世芳兄弟等。

镇上有4处13座省保，1处市保，50处历史建筑，多与华氏家族有关。

1. 华氏建筑群：包括漫画家华君武旧居；新当里花沿街北侧的"数学双星"华蘅芳、华世芳故居；进步街北仓河的华氏老义庄，庄内有楠木厅，被誉为"江南第一义庄"；学海路上有果育鸿模小学和荡口中学；和平街小巷内的明代华氏进士第，尚存振始堂和明代假山石；旺儿桥旁的华氏始迁祖祠，以及锡甘路旁的华氏真赏斋遗址等，2002年列为省保单位。

2. 荡口义庄群：荡口古建筑以义庄最具特色，自清初以来，先后兴建了10余处，以华氏为主，过、殷、徐氏为辅，义庄数量之多、义田规模之大、善举范围之广，均为国内罕见。

荡口义庄从单一封建田租发展为多元化收益办庄，从义田、义仓拓展为义庄、义学，从本族慈善事业推向社会慈善义举，从济贫扶弱、救急解困扩展为崇文兴教、办学兴国，为荡口做出了重要贡献。如今保存较好的有华氏老义庄、永喜义庄、华氏襄义庄、徐氏义庄和须义庄五座，2002年列为省保单位。

华氏老义庄位于进步街，清乾隆年间华进思、华公弼父子创建，是当地的第一座义庄，规模也最大。现存四进房屋，自南向北依次为隔河照壁、码头、八字照壁、门厅、轿厅、楠木正厅和后厅。西路辟有花园，有水池假山、亭桥廊榭。

目前筹建为荡口义庄展示馆。永喜义庄位于青虹路，清道光二十四年（1845年）华永喜妻华锡鳞建。现存四进房屋，由南向北依次为前屋、前厅、大厅和后屋。义庄三面环水，建筑精美，墙中夹有金山石柱，河埠设有闸门，防盗功能完善。华氏襄义庄位于生产街，1924年华襄云建。现存门厅、前厅和后厅共三进和两座侧厢。

徐氏义庄位于新桥村老湖桥，清光绪初年进士徐焕后裔所建，俗称红墙门。清光绪三十三年（1907年）在庄内创办湖桥小学堂，新中国成立前曾遭火灾。现存门厅、前厅、大厅和后厅共四进，每进9间，两侧皆有备弄。

其中大厅规模较大，梁柱粗壮，雕工细致，体现了苏州民居营造技术对荡口的影响。须义庄位于团结街，今存门厅、前厅和后厅共三进，原为须家祠堂，后改为米行。现为私人宅院。3. 三公祠（含步弓石刻）：位于荡口镇鹅湖新桥边三公路，2006年列为省保单位。

三公祠是明嘉靖三十六年（1557年）华察为孙慎、翁大立、王其勤所立生祠，赞颂三人丈量土地，厘清田赋，造福百姓，清代多次重修。祠内有思泉亭、学海书院、望月楼、遗爱堂、致斋所和衍庆道院等。丈量工具"步弓石刻"嵌在遗爱堂前院西墙上。

· · · · ·
English

Dangkou Ancient Town is located at the junction of Wuxi and Suzhou, anciently named Dingshe, legend says it was the hometown of the Eastern Han filial son Ding Lan, later named for being at the mouth of Ezhun Dang.

During the Hongwu reign of the Ming, Hua Zhenggu moved here, and its fame gradually grew.

In the mid-Ming, Nanyan Township where Dangkou was located became the number one township in Jiangnan for paying grain taxes, and the Hua family developed into a prominent clan in Wuxi, producing 37 jinshi during the Ming and Qing dynasties.

Famous figures include Ming Reader-in-Waiting Hua Cha, publisher Hua Sui, collector Hua Xia, Donglin Party members, Fushe member Hua Yuncheng, famous musician Hua Qiuping, and famous mathematicians Hua Hengfang and Hua Shifang brothers etc.

The town has 4 sites with 13 provincial protected buildings, 1 municipal protected building, and 50 historical buildings, mostly related to the Hua family.1.

Hua Family Building Complex: Includes the former residence of cartoonist Hua Junwu; the former residences of "mathematics twin stars" Hua Hengfang and Hua Shifang on the north side of Huayan Street in Xindangli; the Hua Family Old Charity Estate on Beicang River, Jinbu Street, with a nanmu hall inside, hailed as "the number one charity estate in Jiangnan"; on Xuehai Road are Guoyu Hongmo Primary School and Dangkou Middle School; the Ming Hua Family Jinshi Mansion in the alley of Heping Street, with the Zhenshi Hall and Ming rockery stones still preserved; the Hua Family First Ancestor Shrine beside Wang'er Bridge, and the site of the Hua Family Zhenshang Studio on Xigan Road etc.

, designated a provincial protected site in 2002.2.

Dangkou Charity Estate Group: Dangkou's ancient buildings are most distinctive for their charity estates (yizhuang); since the early Qing, more than 10 have been successively built, mainly by the Hua family, supplemented by the Guo, Yin, and Xu families.

The number of charity estates, the scale of charity fields, and the breadth of charitable acts are rare in China.

Dangkou charity estates developed from single feudal land rent to diversified income management; from charity fields and charity granaries to charity estates and charity schools; from clan charity to social charity; from helping the poor and rescuing the needy to advocating culture and education and running schools for national rejuvenation—making important contributions to Dangkou.

Today, five are well preserved: Hua Family Old Charity Estate, Yongxi Charity Estate, Hua Family Xiang Charity Estate, Xu Family Charity Estate, and Xu Family Charity Estate, designated provincial protected sites in 2002.

The Hua Family Old Charity Estate is located on Jinbu Street, founded by Hua Jinsi and Hua Gongbi father and son during the Qianlong reign of the Qing—the first charity estate in the area and also the largest.

It preserves four rows of houses, from south to north successively: riverside screen wall, dock,八字 screen wall, gate hall, sedan hall, nanmu main hall, and rear hall.

The west road has a garden with pond, rockery, pavilions, bridges, and corridors.It is currently being prepared as the Dangkou Charity Estate Exhibition Hall.

The Yongxi Charity Estate is located on Qinghong Road, built by Hua Yongxi's wife Hua Xilin in the 24th year of Daoguang of the Qing (1845).

It preserves four rows of houses, from south to north successively: front house, front hall, main hall, and rear house.

The charity estate is surrounded by water on three sides, with exquisite architecture, Jinshan stone pillars embedded in the walls, and gates at the river landings with complete anti-theft functions.

The Hua Family Xiang Charity Estate is located on Shengchan Street, built by Hua Xiangyun in 1924.It preserves three rows: gate hall, front hall, and rear hall, plus two side wings.

The Xu Family Charity Estate is located at Laohu Bridge, Xinqiao Village, built by the descendants of jinshi Xu Huan in the early Guangxu reign of the Qing, commonly called the Red Wall Gate.

In the 33rd year of Guangxu (1907), the Huqiao Primary School was founded inside the estate; before the founding of New China it suffered a fire.

It preserves four rows: gate hall, front hall, main hall, and rear hall, each row with 9 bays, with service corridors on both sides.

The main hall is relatively large, with thick beams and columns and exquisite carvings, reflecting the influence of Suzhou residential construction techniques on Dangkou.

The Xu Family Charity Estate is located on Tuanjie Street, today preserving three rows: gate hall, front hall, and rear hall, originally the Xu family ancestral hall, later changed to a rice shop.

Now a private residence.3.Sangong (Three Dukes) Shrine (including Step-Bow Stone Carving): Located on Sangong Road by Ehu New Bridge in Dangkou Town, designated a provincial protected site in 2006.

The Sangong Shrine was a living shrine established by Hua Cha in the 36th year of Jiajing of the Ming (1557) for Sun Shen, Weng Dali, and Wang Qinqin, praising the three for measuring land, clarifying field taxes, and benefiting the people; repaired multiple times during the Qing.

Inside the shrine are the Siquan Pavilion, Xuehai Academy, Wangyue Tower, Yi'ai (Remaining Love) Hall, Zhai Studio, and Yanqing Daoist Temple etc.

The surveying tool "Step-Bow Stone Carving" is embedded in the west wall of the front courtyard of the Yi'ai Hall.

建筑要点 / Key Features
荡口古镇位于无锡苏州交界处古名丁舍相传是东汉孝子丁兰故里后因位于鹅肫荡口得名明洪武年间华贞固迁居此地名声渐显明中期荡口所在的南延乡成为江南缴纳粮赋第一乡华氏也发展成无锡的煌煌大族明清两代出了37名进士著名人物如明代侍读学士华察出版家华燧收藏家华夏东林党人复社成员华允诚著名音乐家华秋苹著名数学家华蘅芳华世芳兄弟等镇上有4处13座省保1处市保50处历史建筑多与华氏家族有关；华氏建筑群包括漫画家华君武旧居新当里花沿街北侧的数学双星华蘅芳华世芳故居进步街北仓河的华氏老义庄庄内有楠木厅被誉为江南第一义庄学海路上有果育鸿模小学和荡口中学和平街小巷内的明代华氏进士第尚存振始堂和明代假山石旺儿桥旁的华氏始迁祖祠以及锡甘路旁的华氏真赏斋遗址等2002年列为省保单位；荡口义庄群荡口古建筑以义庄最具特色自清初以来先后兴建了10余处以华氏为主过殷徐氏为辅义庄数量之多义田规模之大善举范围之广均为国内罕见荡口义庄从单一封建田租发展为多元化收益办庄从义田义仓拓展为义庄义学从本族慈善事业推向社会慈善义举从济贫扶弱救急解困扩展为崇文兴教办学兴国为荡口做出了重要贡献如今保存较好的有华氏老义庄永喜义庄华氏襄义庄徐氏义庄和须
19 昭嗣堂
Zhaosi Ancestral Hall
明—清
级别 Level
第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
地址 Address
滨湖区硕放街裕安路
类型 Type
祠堂/楠木建筑
中文原文

明嘉靖七年（1528年）进士曹察建，清乾隆十三年（1748年）改为曹氏家祠，名昭嗣堂，现存门厅、过厅和正厅昭嗣堂。庭院前窄后宽呈"凸"字形，是当地流行的吉宅形制。

昭嗣堂是明代原构，面阔五间，进深十一架，全用上等金丝楠木建成，又名香楠厅，是江苏保存最完整的明代楠木建筑。厅内明间有草架、双脊，梁枋等处施彩画，檐下砖雕纹样细致。

曹察女为嘉靖端妃曹氏，因宫变牵连被处死，据说曹察回乡后为纪念女儿倾尽财产建造了这座香楠厅，寓意"香囡之厅"，厅内北面正中的两根青石柱则代表"双亲（青）"。

· · · · ·
English

Built by jinshi Cao Cha in the 7th year of Jiajing of the Ming (1528), changed to the Cao family ancestral hall in the 13th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1748), named Zhaosi Hall; today preserves the gate hall, passage hall, and main hall Zhaosi Hall.

The courtyard is narrow in front and wide at the back,呈 a "convex" shape—a popular auspicious house form in the area.

Zhaosi Hall is an original Ming structure, five bays wide and eleven rafters deep, entirely built of high-quality golden-thread nanmu, also called the Fragrant Nanmu Hall—the best-preserved Ming nanmu building in Jiangsu.

Inside the hall, the central bay has a hidden frame and double ridges, with painted decorations on beams and lintels, and exquisite brick carving patterns under the eaves.

Cao Cha's daughter was Consort Duan of the Jiajing Emperor, surnamed Cao, who was executed due to implication in a palace coup; it is said that after returning home, Cao Cha exhausted his fortune to build this fragrant nanmu hall in memory of his daughter, meaning "Hall of the Fragrant Daughter," and the two bluestone columns in the center of the north side of the hall represent "parents (qing/bluestone).

"

建筑要点 / Key Features
明嘉靖七年1528年进士曹察建清乾隆十三年1748年改为曹氏家祠名昭嗣堂现存门厅过厅和正厅昭嗣堂庭院前窄后宽呈凸字形是当地流行的吉宅形制昭嗣堂是明代原构面阔五间进深十一架全用上等金丝楠木建成又名香楠厅是江苏保存最完整的明代楠木建筑厅内明间有草架双脊梁枋等处施彩画檐下砖雕纹样细致曹察女为嘉靖端妃曹氏因宫变牵连被处死据说曹察回乡后为纪念女儿倾尽财产建造了这座香楠厅寓意香囡之厅厅内北面正中的两根青石柱则代表双亲青

中文原文

兴国寺塔始建于北宋太平兴国（796—983）年间，原属太平教寺，后来寺庙荒废唯塔尚存。塔原高七层，外壁呈八边形，内壁呈四边形，塔内有转角木梯，可登高临眺。各层皆开壶门和直棂假窗，上下相错。

元至正年间塔遭毁坏，明正统年间修复，增高为九层木檐砖身楼阁式塔。清嘉庆二十二年（1817年），塔内木构和塔顶毁于火，仅存砖壁塔身。1925年直奉军阀混战时，炮弹削去顶层西南半侧，塔颠变成钢笔尖状。

1985年重修，塔现高42.83米，6层以下为宋代原物。2002年围绕寺塔拓建为宋代风格的兴国园。

塔东有经幢亭，内置唐咸通十一年（870年）所刻经幢。

· · · · ·
English

Xingguo Temple Pagoda was first built during the Taiping Xingguo reign of the Northern Song (976-983), originally belonging to the Taipingjiao Temple; later the temple fell into disrepair and only the pagoda survived.

The pagoda was originally seven stories high, with an octagonal outer wall and a quadrilateral inner wall, with a corner wooden ladder inside allowing climbing to overlook.

Each story has pot-door openings and straight-lattice false windows, alternating up and down.

During the Zhizheng reign of the Yuan, the pagoda was damaged; repaired during the Zhengtong reign of the Ming, raised to a nine-story wooden-eave brick-body pavilion-style pagoda.

In the 22nd year of Jiaqing of the Qing (1817), the wooden structure and pagoda top were destroyed by fire, leaving only the brick wall body.

In 1925 during the Zhili-Fengtian warlord melee, a shell削去 the southwest half of the top story, and the pagoda top became pen-nib shaped.

Repaired in 1985, the pagoda is now 42.83 meters high, with the six lower stories being original Song structures.

In 2002, the area around the temple pagoda was expanded into the Song-style Xingguo Garden.

East of the pagoda is a dharani pillar pavilion, containing a dharani pillar carved in the 11th year of Xiantong of the Tang (870).

建筑要点 / Key Features
兴国寺塔始建于北宋太平兴国796-983年间原属太平教寺后来寺庙荒废唯塔尚存塔原高七层外壁呈八边形内壁呈四边形塔内有转角木梯可登高临眺各层皆开壶门和直棂假窗上下相错元至正年间塔遭毁坏明正统年间修复增高为九层木檐砖身楼阁式塔清嘉庆二十二年1817年塔内木构和塔顶毁于火仅存砖壁塔身1925年直奉军阀混战时炮弹削去顶层西南半侧塔颠变成钢笔尖状1985年重修塔现高42.83米6层以下为宋代原物2002年围绕寺塔拓建为宋代风格的兴国园塔东有经幢亭内置唐咸通十一年870年所刻经幢

中文原文

刘氏兄弟故居是文学家、教育学家、语言学家刘半农，音乐家刘天华和刘北茂三兄弟出生和青少年时期生活和学习的场所，他们被冰心誉为"刘氏三杰"，是中国近代文化界的杰出人物。

这处故居由他们的曾祖父刘荣建于清末，坐西朝东，现存三间两进及后院的两座厢房，今为刘氏兄弟纪念馆，展示他们少年生活的细节和后来的成就，清丽朴素的建筑和器物，配着细腻生动的解说，古朴而别具情趣。

在城市扩建过程中，周围老宅已被拆光，只留下这组院落处在人民路中央，两侧车水马龙、行客匆匆，刘氏故居则环绕在青草绿树间，粉墙黛瓦、老井深院、腊梅月桂……在喧嚣和繁华中显得幽静安详。

· · · · ·
English

The Former Residence of the Liu Brothers is the place where writer, educator, and linguist Liu Bannong, and musicians Liu Tianhua and Liu Beimao, three brothers, were born and lived and studied during their youth; they were hailed by Bing Xin as the "Three Outstanding Liu Brothers," distinguished figures in modern Chinese cultural circles.

This residence was built by their great-grandfather Liu Rong in the late Qing, facing west with its back to east, today preserving three bays in two rows and two wing rooms in the rear courtyard, now the Liu Brothers Memorial Hall, displaying details of their teenage life and later achievements; the elegant and simple buildings and objects, paired with delicate and vivid explanations, are quaint and uniquely charming.

During urban expansion, the surrounding old houses were all demolished, leaving only this courtyard complex in the center of Renmin Road, with heavy traffic and hurrying pedestrians on both sides; the Liu residence, surrounded by green grass and trees, with white walls and black tiles, old well and deep courtyard, wintersweet and cassia.

..appears serene and peaceful amid the noise and prosperity.

中文原文

这处文庙始建于北宋淳化三年（992年），原在监狱旁边，北宋景祐三年（1036年）在范仲淹"庆历新政"带动下，江阴守令范宗古在今址重建文庙，并邀请范仲淹撰写《景祐重建文宣王庙记》。

南宋绍熙年间此庙已具较大规模，此后屡毁屡建，今存建筑多建于明清两代。江阴文庙坐北朝南，由南向北依次为棂星门、泮池、大成门、大成殿和明伦堂。

南部的半月形泮池及池上三桥皆为明正统二年（1437）旧物。居中的大成殿面阔五间，进深十架，采用重檐歇山顶，内供孔子塑像，殿内梁架皆施彩绘，古朴可观。

· · · · ·
English

This Confucian Temple was first built in the 3rd year of Chunhua of the Northern Song (992), originally beside the prison; in the 3rd year of Jingyou of the Northern Song (1036), driven by Fan Zhongyan's "Qingli New Policies," Jiangyin magistrate Fan Zonggu rebuilt the Confucian Temple at today's site and invited Fan Zhongyan to write the "Record of Rebuilding the Temple of King Wenxuan in Jingyou.

" During the Shaoxi reign of the Southern Song, this temple already had a relatively large scale; thereafter it was repeatedly destroyed and rebuilt, and today's surviving buildings were mostly built during the Ming and Qing dynasties.

Jiangyin Confucian Temple faces south, from south to north successively the Lingxing Gate, Pan Pond, Dacheng Gate, Dacheng Hall, and Minglun Hall.

The crescent-shaped Pan Pond in the south and the three bridges over it are all original objects from the 2nd year of Zhengtong of the Ming (1437).

The central Dacheng Hall is five bays wide and ten rafters deep, adopting a double-eave hip-and-gable roof, with a seated statue of Confucius inside; the beam frames inside the hall are all painted, quaint and viewable.

建筑要点 / Key Features
这处文庙始建于北宋淳化三年992年原在监狱旁边北宋景祐三年1036年在范仲淹庆历新政带动下江阴守令范宗古在今址重建文庙并邀请范仲淹撰写景祐重建文宣王庙记南宋绍熙年间此庙已具较大规模此后屡毁屡建今存建筑多建于明清两代江阴文庙坐北朝南由南向北依次为棂星门泮池大成门大成殿和明伦堂南部的半月形泮池及池上三桥皆为明正统二年1437旧物居中的大成殿面阔五间进深十架采用重檐歇山顶内供孔子塑像殿内梁架皆施彩绘古朴可观
23 中山公园（季园）
Dr. Sun Yat-sen Park (Jiyuan Garden)

虹桥北路东侧
类型 Type
