The stage faces south with its back to north, with a two-story hip-and-gable roof, and the plan呈 a "convex" shape, with the stage opening directly facing the City God Temple main hall (demolished in 1988).

Between the stage and the main hall, there were originally 9 viewing towers on each side, upper and lower.

On the east wall of the stage is embedded the "Record of Adding to and Repairing the City God Temple of Yanghu County" carved in the 22nd year of Guangxu of the Qing (1896), stating: "The theatrical tower is especially tall; in spring and autumn sacrifices, music is played to entertain the gods.

Furthermore, stories of ancient and modern loyalty, filial piety, chastity, and righteousness are taken for opera performers to enact." 3.

Wansui Dongyue Temple Theatrical Tower: Located inside the Wansui Dongyue Temple in Menghe Town, Xinbei District.

The Dongyue Temple was first built during the Zhenguan reign of the Tang, repaired during the Daoguang reign of the Qing.

The theatrical tower is attached to the Dongyue Temple, built during the Daoguang reign, facing west with its back to east, with the stage opening directly facing the Dongyue Temple main hall.

The theatrical tower plan呈 a "convex" shape; the main stage eaves extend outward, higher than the roof, forming an octagonal roof with a coffered ceiling inside.

The backstage is three bays wide, with dressing rooms on both sides, and on the left there is also a rack platform for the band to perform.

The stage board walls record the opera troupes, plays, and leading actor names that performed here from the late Qing to early Republic, with relatively high historical value.4.

Xixiashu Meicun Theatrical Tower: Located in Meilin Village, Xixiashu Town, Xinbei District, attached to the Zhenwu Temple (the temple no longer exists).

The theatrical tower was first built in the Ming, rebuilt in 1688, and repaired twice in 1863 and 2004.

The theatrical tower faces south with its back to north, with a two-story hip-and-gable roof, three bays upper and lower, and the plan呈 a "convex" shape.5.

Lijia Theatrical Tower: Located inside Lijia Middle School, Wujin District.This stage opening faces north, directly facing the Liedi Temple main hall.

During the Taiping Rebellion the theatrical tower was destroyed by war fires, rebuilt during the Guangxu reign.

Two stories with three bays each, the plan呈 a "convex" shape, with stage columns on both sides supporting the arched upturned eaves upward, and the lower part stabilizing the floor slab and stage corners.

The architectural style is quite similar to the Suzhou towers built by the Xiangshan Gang.In front of the theatrical tower is an open square that can accommodate over 2000 spectators.6.

Shunzhuang Theatrical Tower: Located at the west end of Zhangjia Natural Village, Shunzhuang Village, Henglin Town, Wujin District, attached to the Dongyue Temple.

The theatrical tower was built in the Qing, facing south with its back to north, with a two-story hip-and-gable roof, the plan呈 a "convex" shape, with the front stage three bays relatively narrow and the backstage three bays relatively wide.

建筑要点 / Key Features
常州地区现有6座古代戏楼2006年第六批列为国保单位杨氏家庭戏楼位于钟楼区东下塘75号紧邻青果巷此戏楼建于清同治光绪年间又称杨氏雕花楼有上下两层一层存放乐器等二层为舞台除东面外三面临空周置20扇长窗雕刻虫鱼花鸟工艺精细平时长窗关闭自成一室演戏时将窗撤下露出舞台楼前建有花园和假山阳湖县城隍庙戏楼位于和平南路与青果巷交汇处的新坊桥小学内城隍庙建于清乾隆二十四年1759年戏台建于清同治九年1870年1896年重修戏台坐南朝北两层歇山顶平面呈凸字形台口正对城隍庙大殿1988年拆除戏台与大殿之间两侧原有上下各9间看戏楼戏台东墙上嵌清光绪二十二年1896年所刻阳湖县增修城隍庙记称戏楼特高春秋致祭作乐以娱神复取古今忠孝节义故事俾梨园子弟演之万绥东岳庙戏楼位于新北区孟河镇万绥东岳庙内东岳庙始建于唐贞观年间清道光年间重修戏楼附属于东岳庙建于道光年间坐东朝西台口正对东岳庙大殿戏楼平面呈凸字形正台屋檐外伸高出屋面做成八角屋顶内架藻井后台宽三间两侧设化妆间左侧还有供乐队演奏的架子台台板壁上记载了清末民初来此演出的戏班戏目和主角姓名等具有较高的史料价值西夏墅梅村戏楼位于新北区西夏墅镇梅林村附属于真武庙庙已不存戏

镇江

Zhenjiang
11
处建筑

地区概述 / Regional Overview

镇江市位于江苏省西南部，地处长江三角洲的顶端，西邻南京，南接常州，东北临长江黄金水道段。早在旧石器时代中期，镇江沿江一带就有古人类繁衍生息。镇江有文字记载的历史可上溯到3000年前的西周时期为谷阳。秦始皇统一七国后，认为谷阳有"天子气"，遂凿断京岘山阻断，并改谷阳为丹徒，一直沿用至今。

北宋政和三年（1113年）升润州为镇江府，丹徒属镇江府。镇江襟山带江，自然风光雄伟壮丽，地上地下文物、人文景观十分丰富。

作为江防重镇，三国东吴孙权筑铁瓮城以固守，东晋郗鉴、王恭在京口花山湾筑晋陵城，延续至隋、唐又修缮加筑，今尚存城墙遗址2300米。

镇江所辖丹阳市为东晋南朝齐梁帝王祖籍地，这些帝王死后多归葬丹阳，现丹阳、句容地区共存有南朝帝陵石刻12处，为六朝艺术精品。镇江焦山有六朝石刻《瘗鹤铭》，被誉为"大字之祖""书家冠冕"，为书法瑰宝。

隋唐运河的开凿使镇江成为交通冲衢，漕运咽喉，唐代润州城西北蒜山下的渡口——蒜山渡逐渐兴盛，唐以后称西津渡，即今西津渡古街所在地。

唐代后期大臣李德裕三次出任浙西观察使，在北固山后峰扩建寺庙，寺成后天降甘露，因名甘露寺，又在甘露寺入口处建石塔一座，瘗埋舍利子，北宋时改为铁塔，现为江苏省仅存的铁塔。唐代寺庙兴盛，城南创于东晋的鹤林寺后来成为禅系牛头宗的重要据点。

中晚唐时期金山寺已成规模，处在江渡中是往来香客的方便去处。如今丹阳市内的唐中和铜钟，即为唐普宁寺遗物。宋代建炎南渡后，镇江成为屏障都城临安的重镇，城内水网密集，建桥甚多。名士苏轼多次游览镇江，在金山寺留下晒经台之佳话。

沈括曾担任镇江知州，在京口置梦溪园，今其地犹存。元代在西津渡建造过街石塔。近代是镇江又一个繁荣时期，1858年《天津条约》规定镇江要在一年后通商，1861年设立租界，1964年在云台山坡建成英国领事馆。

民国时期镇江曾作为江苏省会，长达20年之久。晚清至民国初年镇江租界及沿江地带洋行林立，洋楼栉比，建造了大量品质优良的近代建筑，以及马路、邮政、电讯和自来水等公共设施，大多保存在今赵伯先路沿线。1986年镇江成为国务院颁布的第二批国家历史文化名城。

镇江今辖京口区（市政府驻地）、润州区和丹徒区3个区，代管丹阳市、扬中市和句容市3个县级市，有国家级文物保护单位17处，省级文物保护单位47处，本书介绍国保建筑6处，省保建筑4处，其他建筑1处。

Zhenjiang City is located in the southwestern part of Jiangsu Province, at the top of the Yangtze River Delta, bordering Nanjing to the west, Changzhou to the south, and the golden waterway section of the Yangtze River to the northeast.

As early as the middle Paleolithic period, ancient humans already lived and multiplied along the Zhenjiang river area.

Zhenjiang's recorded history can be traced back 3000 years to the Western Zhou period, when it was called Guyang.

After Qin Shi Huang unified the seven states, believing that Guyang had "son-of-heaven qi," he cut through Jingxian Mountain to block it and renamed Guyang to Dantu, a name used to this day.

In the 3rd year of Zhenghe of the Northern Song (1113), Runzhou was promoted to Zhenjiang Prefecture, with Dantu belonging to Zhenjiang Prefecture.

Zhenjiang embraces mountains and the river, with magnificent natural scenery and rich above-ground and underground cultural relics and human landscapes.

As a river defense stronghold, Sun Quan of Eastern Wu in the Three Kingdoms built the Tieweng (Iron Urn) City for defense; in the Eastern Jin, Chi Jian and Wang Gong built the Jinling City at Huashan Bay in Jingkou, continuing to the Sui and Tang when it was repaired and reinforced, with 2300 meters of city wall ruins surviving today.

Danyang City under Zhenjiang's jurisdiction was the ancestral home of the emperors of the Qi and Liang dynasties of the Eastern Jin and Southern Dynasties; after death, these emperors were mostly buried in Danyang, and today there are 12 Southern Dynasties imperial tomb stone carvings in the Danyang and Jurong areas—fine artworks of the Six Dynasties.

Jiaoshan in Zhenjiang has the Six Dynasties stone carving "Crane Burial Inscription," hailed as the "ancestor of large characters" and "crown of calligraphers," a calligraphic treasure.

The excavation of the Sui-Tang Grand Canal made Zhenjiang a transportation hub and grain transport throat; the ferry at the foot of Suan Mountain northwest of Runzhou City in the Tang—Suan Mountain Ferry—gradually flourished, called Xijin Ferry after the Tang, today's location of the Xijin Ferry Ancient Street.

Li Deyu, a late-Tang minister, served three times as Governor of Western Zhejiang, expanding a temple on the rear peak of Beigu Mountain; after its completion, sweet dew fell from heaven, hence named Ganlu (Sweet Dew) Temple; he also built a stone pagoda at the entrance of Ganlu Temple to bury relics, changed to an iron pagoda in the Northern Song—today the only surviving iron pagoda in Jiangsu Province.

Tang Dynasty temples flourished; the Helin Temple south of the city, founded in the Eastern Jin, later became an important stronghold of the Niutou Sect of Chan Buddhism.

In the mid-to-late Tang, Jinshan Temple had already taken shape, located in the river crossing as a convenient place for pilgrims coming and going.

Today the Tang Zhonghe bronze bell in Danyang City is a relic of the Tang Puning Temple.

After the Jianyan southern crossing of the Song, Zhenjiang became a strategic town shielding the capital Lin'an, with dense water networks inside the city and numerous bridges built.

The famous scholar Su Shi visited Zhenjiang multiple times, leaving the fine story of the scripture-drying platform at Jinshan Temple.

Shen Kuo once served as Governor of Zhenjiang, establishing the Mengxi Garden in Jingkou, whose site still exists today.

In the Yuan Dynasty, a street-crossing stone pagoda was built at Xijin Ferry.

Modern times were another prosperous period for Zhenjiang; the 1858 "Treaty of Tianjin" stipulated that Zhenjiang should open for trade a year later, a concession was established in 1861, and the British Consulate was built on the slope of Yuntai Mountain in 1964.

During the Republic period, Zhenjiang served as the capital of Jiangsu Province for as long as 20 years.

From the late Qing to early Republic, foreign firms stood in rows in the Zhenjiang concession and along the river, with Western-style buildings closely packed, constructing a large number of high-quality modern buildings, as well as public facilities such as roads, postal services, telecommunications, and tap water—mostly preserved along today's Zhao Boxian Road.

In 1986, Zhenjiang became the second batch of National Historical and Cultural Cities promulgated by the State Council.

Zhenjiang today administers 3 districts: Jingkou (municipal government seat), Runzhou, and Dantu, and代管 3 county-level cities: Danyang, Yangzhong, and Jurong; it has 17 national-level cultural heritage protection units and 47 provincial-level cultural heritage protection units; this book introduces 6 national-protected buildings, 4 provincial-protected buildings, and 1 other building.

01 焦山
Jiaoshan Mountain
南朝—清
级别 Level
含定慧寺（省保2011年）、焦山碑林与瘗鹤铭（第三批国保1988年）
地址 Address
京口区东吴路83号，镇江东北长江江心
类型 Type
风景名胜/佛教寺院/碑林
门票 Ticket
旺季65元，淡季50元（含渡船）
开放时间 Hours
7:15 — 17:30，需乘坐渡船，7:30 — 凌晨1:00不间断
中文原文

原称樵山，相传东汉末年焦光隐居于此，改名焦山，又称浮玉山。焦山与金山相距十余里，遥遥相对，山上有寺，因焦山比金山高，竹木丰茂，寺庙掩映其中，又有"金山寺裹山，焦山山裹寺"之谚。

1. 焦山定慧寺：2011年列为省保单位，相传始建于东汉，宋代改称普济禅院，之后通称焦山寺，元代被焚毁，明宣德年间重建，清康熙二十年（1681年）重修，康熙南巡时改名定慧寺，取"由戒生定，因定发慧"之意。

抗战期间定慧寺遭日军炮击，部分被毁，新中国成立初期曾予修葺，"文革"期间又遭到严重破坏。1979年6月整修大殿和天王殿。寺庙坐北朝南，依次为山门、天王殿和大雄宝殿，寺西有华严阁。

天王殿始建于明正统年间，清光绪二十九年（1903年）重建，1983年因木柱衰朽拆除重建。

大雄宝殿为重檐庑殿顶，出檐深远，始建于唐，自宋以来多次重建，"文革"中破坏严重，大殿倾斜，1976年拨正，1979年再加修缮。

华严阁位于焦山西麓，清代僧人元漕创建，新中国成立后重修。1979年，中国佛教协会会长赵朴初为题"无尽藏"匾。"华严月色"为焦山十六景之一。2. 焦山碑林与瘗鹤铭：第三批国保（1988年）。

焦山碑林由摩崖石刻和碑刻陈列两部分组成，其中摩崖石刻环绕在焦山西侧悬崖边的浮玉岩、观音岩、罗汉岩（距公崖）、雷轰岩和栈道岩一带，绵延200余米，有六朝以来刻石百余方。受到历代书法家尊崇的《瘗鹤铭》原址在雷轰岩，今已移入碑林陈列。

现存著名摩崖石刻有罗汉岩前唐贞观年间僧人书写的《金刚经偈句》，宋代米芾瘗鹤铭铭书体写的"仲宣、法芝、米芾元祐辛未孟夏观山樵书"，在西南转角处崖上的"浮玉"二字，为北宋汴京（今开封）人赵孟奎题，另有陆游与友人同观《瘗鹤铭》后书写的短文等。

碑刻陈列在焦山东麓。宋庆历八年（1048年）在焦山建宝墨亭，收藏王羲之字刻的唐代经幢和《瘗鹤铭》，明代改为宝墨轩，清代以来屡遭兵燹，损毁严重。

1960年集合南郊鹤林寺等处的石碑，共收碑刻265方，移至定慧寺东自然庵、香林庵和玉峰庵旧址陈列，称为"焦山碑林"，藏自六朝至民国碑500方，展出400方。

除《瘗鹤铭》外，著名碑刻还有南齐《刘岱墓志》、唐《魏法师碑》、宋米芾临《兰亭序帖》、张即之《金刚经》、徐铉临《秦峄石门刻石》、元赵孟頫《赤壁赋及东坡小像》、明文徵明《千字文》、清套帖《澄鉴堂石刻》和《乾隆御碑》等。

《瘗鹤铭》原刻在焦山西麓石壁上，铭文题记称华阳真逸撰，上皇山樵书，通常认为此铭刻于南朝梁时期。铭文为大字楷书，十分精美，黄庭坚曾称赞"大字无过《瘗鹤铭》"。宋代时山体滑移，《瘗鹤铭》崩落江中，清康熙五十年（1711年）从江中捞出残石五块，移置寺中。

1960年在宝墨轩园内建亭，按前人考证的位置，依照当年摩崖原样将石块嵌入石壁中。

· · · · ·
English

Originally called Qiaoshan (Firewood Mountain), legend says Jiao Guang lived in seclusion here at the end of the Eastern Han, hence renamed Jiaoshan (Jiao Mountain), also called Fuyu Mountain (Floating Jade Mountain).

Jiaoshan and Jinshan are over ten li apart, facing each other from afar; there is a temple on the mountain, and because Jiaoshan is higher than Jinshan with abundant bamboo and trees, the temple is hidden among them, hence the proverb "Jinshan Temple wraps the mountain, Jiaoshan Mountain wraps the temple.

" 1.

Jiaoshan Dinghui Temple: Designated a provincial protected unit in 2011, traditionally founded in the Eastern Han; in the Song it was renamed Puji Chan Courtyard, thereafter commonly called Jiaoshan Temple; destroyed by fire in the Yuan, rebuilt during the Xuande reign of the Ming, repaired in the 20th year of Kangxi of the Qing (1681), and during Kangxi's southern tour renamed Dinghui Temple, taking the meaning of "from precepts arises samadhi, from samadhi arises wisdom.

" During the War of Resistance against Japan, Dinghui Temple was shelled by Japanese troops and partially destroyed; in the early days of New China it was repaired, and during the Cultural Revolution it suffered severe damage again.

In June 1979, the main hall and Heavenly King Hall were renovated.

The temple faces south, with the mountain gate, Heavenly King Hall, and Mahavira Hall in sequence, and the Huayan Pavilion west of the temple.

The Heavenly King Hall was first built during the Zhengtong reign of the Ming, rebuilt in the 29th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1903), and demolished and rebuilt in 1983 due to decaying wooden columns.

The Mahavira Hall has a double-eave hip roof with deep eaves, first built in the Tang, rebuilt multiple times since the Song; severely damaged during the Cultural Revolution with the hall tilting, it was straightened in 1976 and further repaired in 1979.

The Huayan Pavilion is located at the western foot of Jiaoshan, founded by Qing monk Yuan Cao, rebuilt after the founding of New China.

In 1979, Zhao Puchu, President of the Buddhist Association of China, inscribed the plaque "Endless Treasury." "Huayan Moonlight" is one of the sixteen scenes of Jiaoshan.2.

Jiaoshan Stele Forest and Crane Burial Inscription: 3rd Batch National Protected (1988).The Jiaoshan Stele Forest consists of two parts: cliff carvings and stele display.

The cliff carvings surround Fuyu Rock, Guanyin Rock, Luohan Rock (Jugong Rock), Leihong Rock, and Plank Road Rock along the cliff on the west side of Jiaoshan, stretching over 200 meters, with over a hundred carved stones since the Six Dynasties.

The "Crane Burial Inscription," revered by calligraphers of all dynasties, was originally at Leihong Rock and has now been moved into the stele forest display.

Existing famous cliff carvings include the "Vajra Sutra Verse" written by a monk during the Zhenguan reign of the Tang in front of Luohan Rock; the Song Mi Fu's inscription in the calligraphic style of the Crane Burial Inscription: "Zhongxuan, Fazhi, Mi Fu viewed the mountain woodcutter's writing in the early summer of Yuanyou Xinwei"; the two characters "Fuyu" (Floating Jade) on the cliff at the southwest corner, inscribed by Zhao Mengkui, a native of Bianjing (today's Kaifeng) in the Northern Song; and a short essay written by Lu You after viewing the "Crane Burial Inscription" with friends etc.

The stele display is at the eastern foot of Jiaoshan.

In the 8th year of Qingli of the Northern Song (1048), the Baomo (Precious Ink) Pavilion was built on Jiaoshan, collecting the Tang dharani pillar with Wang Xizhi's characters and the "Crane Burial Inscription"; in the Ming it was changed to the Baomo Studio, and since the Qing it has repeatedly suffered from wars with severe damage.

In 1960, stone steles from places such as Helin Temple in the southern suburbs were gathered, collecting 265 stele carvings in total, moved to the former sites of Ziran Temple, Xianglin Temple, and Yufeng Temple east of Dinghui Temple for display, called the "Jiaoshan Stele Forest," housing 500 steles from the Six Dynasties to the Republic, with 400 on display.

Besides the "Crane Burial Inscription," famous stele carvings include the Southern Qi "Epitaph of Liu Dai," Tang "Stele of Master Wei," Song Mi Fu's copy of the "Preface to the Orchid Pavilion," Zhang Jizhi's "Vajra Sutra," Xu Xuan's copy of the "Stone Carving at Yi Gate of Qin," Yuan Zhao Mengfu's "Ode to the Red Cliff and Portrait of Dongpo," Ming Wen Zhengming's "Thousand Character Classic," Qing multi-model album "Chengjian Hall Stone Carvings," and "Qianlong Imperial Stele" etc.

The "Crane Burial Inscription" was originally carved on the stone wall at the western foot of Jiaoshan; the inscription's colophon says it was composed by Huayang Zhenyi and written by Shanghuang Shanqiao, and it is generally believed this inscription was carved during the Liang Dynasty of the Southern Dynasties.

The inscription is in large-character regular script, extremely exquisite; Huang Tingjian once praised that "no large characters surpass the 'Crane Burial Inscription.

'" During the Song, the mountain body shifted and the "Crane Burial Inscription" collapsed into the river; in the 50th year of Kangxi of the Qing (1711), five remnant stones were fished out of the river and moved into the temple.

In 1960, a pavilion was built in the Baomo Studio garden, and according to the location verified by predecessors, the stones were embedded into the stone wall in the original cliff-carving style of that year.

建筑要点 / Key Features
原称樵山相传东汉末年焦光隐居于此改名焦山又称浮玉山焦山与金山相距十余里遥遥相对山上有寺因焦山比金山高竹木丰茂寺庙掩映其中又有金山寺裹山焦山山裹寺之谚定慧寺2011年列为省保单位相传始建于东汉宋代改称普济禅院之后通称焦山寺元代被焚毁明宣德年间重建清康熙二十年1681年重修康熙南巡时改名定慧寺取由戒生定因定发慧之意抗战期间定慧寺遭日军炮击部分被毁新中国成立初期曾予修葺文革期间又遭到严重破坏1979年6月整修大殿和天王殿寺庙坐北朝南依次为山门天王殿和大雄宝殿寺西有华严阁天王殿始建于明正统年间清光绪二十九年1903年重建1983年因木柱衰朽拆除重建大雄宝殿为重檐庑殿顶出檐深远始建于唐自宋以来多次重建文革中破坏严重大殿倾斜1976年拨正1979年再加修缮华严阁位于焦山西麓清代僧人元漕创建新中国成立后重修1979年中国佛教协会会长赵朴初为题无尽藏匾华严月色为焦山十六景之一焦山碑林与瘗鹤铭第三批国保1988年焦山碑林由摩崖石刻和碑刻陈列两部分组成其中摩崖石刻环绕在焦山西侧悬崖边的浮玉岩观音岩罗汉岩距公崖雷轰岩和栈道岩一带绵延200余米有六朝以来刻石百余方受到历代书法家尊崇的瘗鹤铭原址在雷轰岩今已移入
02 北固山
Beigu Mountain
宋—明
级别 Level
含甘露寺铁塔（第七批国保2013年）
地址 Address
京口区东吴路
类型 Type
风景名胜/佛教寺院
门票 Ticket
40元，或购与金山、焦山联票
开放时间 Hours
7:30 — 17:30
中文原文

北固山北临长江，由前峰、中峰和后峰三部分组成，前峰三面皆是悬崖，地势险固，山上多建亭台楼阁，古迹众多，有"天下第一江山"之誉。1. 甘露寺铁塔：第七批国保（2013年）。铁塔在后峰东部甘露寺长廊入口。

唐长庆四年（824年）11月19日，长干寺发现佛舍利，李德裕在甘露寺建石塔，长庆五年（825年）瘗下；唐大和三年（829年）正月二十四日禅众寺又出土佛舍利，也葬在塔下。

唐乾符年间石塔倒塌，北宋熙宁二年（1069年）在原址挖出李德裕所葬遗物，由信徒焦巽出钱200万铸铁塔，北宋熙宁九年（1076年）五月开工，元丰元年（1078年）完工，同时葬入一些宋代物品。

这座铁塔原有九级。据康熙《镇江府志》记载，明万历十一年（1583年）"塔颓海啸"，可能在重建时减了两层，因为在高从龙摹绘的《甘露寺图》和清代嘉庆、道光年间画家张夕庵和周镐的册页中，铁塔都只有七层。

19世纪末铁塔遭遇雷击，塔刹被英军掠走。1960年对塔基进行发掘，出土了两千多件珍贵文物。当时残存明代铸造的四、五层塔身，第四层从腰间折去一半，上有两处残缺铭文。

今铁塔的莲花座和第一、二层为宋代原构，第三、第四层为明代补铸。铁塔残高约8米，每层高约5尺，直径约8尺。塔身八面，四面辟门，上下相闪，铸有佛像飞天，犹存唐风。檐口置斗栱，柱头有卷杀，都是宋代风格。

下部铁铸须弥座八面饰海水波浪纹，上铸力士像及龙凤戏珠图。第二层铸楷书"国泰安宁""法轮常转"及僧人姓名。第四层有"中宪大夫"等明代官名。

· · · · ·
English

Beigu Mountain faces the Yangtze River to the north, composed of three parts: front peak, middle peak, and rear peak; the front peak has cliffs on three sides, with a strategic and solid terrain; the mountain has many pavilions, terraces, and towers, with numerous historical sites, hailed as "the number one mountain and river under heaven.

" 1.Ganlu Temple Iron Pagoda: 7th Batch National Protected (2013).The iron pagoda is at the entrance of the Ganlu Temple corridor on the eastern part of the rear peak.

On November 19, the 4th year of Changqing of the Tang (824), Buddha relics were discovered at Changgan Temple; Li Deyu built a stone pagoda at Ganlu Temple, burying them in the 5th year of Changqing (825); on January 24, the 3rd year of Dahe of the Tang (829), Buddha relics were unearthed again at Chanzhong Temple and also buried under the pagoda.

The stone pagoda collapsed during the Qianfu reign of the Tang; in the 2nd year of Xining of the Northern Song (1069), the relics buried by Li Deyu were excavated at the original site, and believer Jiao Xun donated 2 million coins to cast an iron pagoda; construction began in May of the 9th year of Xining (1076) and was completed in the 1st year of Yuanfeng (1078), with some Song objects buried at the same time.

This iron pagoda originally had nine stories.

According to Kangxi's "Zhenjiang Prefecture Gazetteer," in the 11th year of Wanli of the Ming (1583) "the pagoda collapsed in a sea tsunami," and two stories may have been reduced during reconstruction, because in Gao Conglong's copied "Painting of Ganlu Temple" and in the albums of painters Zhang Xi'an and Zhou Gao during the Jiaqing and Daoguang reigns of the Qing, the iron pagoda has only seven stories.

At the end of the 19th century, the iron pagoda was struck by lightning, and the pagoda finial was taken away by British troops.

In 1960, the pagoda base was excavated, yielding over two thousand precious cultural relics.

At that time, the fourth and fifth story bodies cast in the Ming remained, with the fourth story broken in half from the waist and two incomplete inscriptions on it.

Today the lotus base and the first and second stories of the iron pagoda are original Song structures, while the third and fourth stories were recast in the Ming.

The iron pagoda has a residual height of about 8 meters, each story about 5 chi high and about 8 chi in diameter.

The pagoda body is octagonal, with doors opened on four sides, alternating up and down, cast with Buddha statues and flying apsaras, still retaining the Tang style.

Bracket sets are placed at the eaves, and the column heads have entasis—both Song style.

The lower iron-cast Sumeru base is decorated on eight sides with sea wave patterns, cast with guardian deity figures and dragon-phoenix playing-with-pearl designs.

The second story is cast with regular script "National Peace and Tranquility," "Dharma Wheel Always Turning," and the names of monks.

The fourth story has Ming official titles such as "Zhongxian Dafu" (Grand Master of Palace Rectitude).

建筑要点 / Key Features
北固山北临长江由前峰中峰和后峰三部分组成前峰三面皆是悬崖地势险固山上多建亭台楼阁古迹众多有天下第一江山之誉甘露寺铁塔第七批国保2013年铁塔在后峰东部甘露寺长廊入口唐长庆四年824年11月19日长干寺发现佛舍利李德裕在甘露寺建石塔长庆五年825年瘗下唐大和三年829年正月二十四日禅众寺又出土佛舍利也葬在塔下唐乾符年间石塔倒塌北宋熙宁二年1069年在原址挖出李德裕所葬遗物由信徒焦巽出钱200万铸铁塔北宋熙宁九年1076年五月开工元丰元年1078年完工同时葬入一些宋代物品这座铁塔原有九级据康熙镇江府志记载明万历十一年1583年塔颓海啸可能在重建时减了两层因为在高从龙摹绘的甘露寺图和清代嘉庆道光年间画家张夕庵和周镐的册页中铁塔都只有七层19世纪末铁塔遭遇雷击塔刹被英军掠走1960年对塔基进行发掘出土了两千多件珍贵文物当时残存明代铸造的四五层塔身第四层从腰间折去一半上有两处残缺铭文今铁塔的莲花座和第一二层为宋代原构第三第四层为明代补铸铁塔残高约8米每层高约5尺直径约8尺塔身八面四面辟门上下相闪铸有佛像飞天犹存唐风檐口置斗栱柱头有卷杀都是宋代风格下部铁铸须弥座八面饰海水波浪纹上铸力士像及龙凤戏珠
03 金山
Jinshan Mountain
东晋—清
级别 Level
第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2011年）
地址 Address
润州区金山路62号金山公园内
类型 Type
风景名胜/佛教寺院
门票 Ticket
淡季50元，旺季65元，可购与焦山、北固山联票
开放时间 Hours
8:00 — 17:00
中文原文

金山是镇江三大名山之一，高44米，主要因山上的金山寺而驰誉天下，建筑密度大，有"金山寺裹山"之谚。除金山寺外，金山周围还有众多古迹，如法海洞、白龙洞和楞伽台等。南侧笔架山上据传有郭璞衣冠冢，现只剩巨石标志。金山还有号称"天下第一泉"的中泠泉，位于塔影湖中小岛上，需乘船前往，泉水今已干涸，泉边石栏为20世纪50年代重修。

1. 金山寺：金山寺位于镇江西北长江南岸，东晋时在江中小岛建寺，称泽心寺。佛教经忏法事中最隆重的水陆法会，相传便起源于梁武帝时期的此寺。传说唐代宰相裴休之子出家为僧，法号法海，在此开山得金，大肆扩建寺院，始称金山寺，唐代已成为游览胜地，《白蛇传》即以此为背景。

宋真宗曾梦游金山，诏改寺名为龙游寺；宋徽宗崇尚道教，又改寺为道观，称神霄玉清万寿宫；宋代靖康之变后复称金山寺。宋将韩世忠和虞允文曾先后在此据天险成功抵御金兵。

清代康熙南巡登金山，见水天一色，赐"江天禅寺"匾。乾隆时期曾在金山寺文宗阁皮藏《四库全书》。经过历代增修，金山上殿阁密布，从明代就有"金山寺裹山"之说。太平天国期间寺庙毁于战火，殿堂荡然无存，文宗阁和藏书也付之一炬。

清同治十年（1871年）重修完毕，清光绪二十六年（1900年）修复山北七层慈寿塔。1948年又发生火灾，寺内三百余间殿阁被焚，仅存慈寿塔、天王殿、楞伽台、观音阁和留云阁等处。

清光绪年间江水淤塞，金山岛逐渐与陆地相连。今寺中建筑多为70年代以后重修，寺门朝西，沿山西麓依次排列山门、天王殿和大雄宝殿等。留云山门建于民国初年，上悬康熙御题"江天禅寺"匾。

山门外有牌坊，坐东朝西，为四柱三门式，系民国初年用混凝土模板浇铸而成，牌坊外有一对石狮。

天王殿始建于明正统年间，清同治八年（1869年）重建。

大雄宝殿始建于明正统年间，1948年毁于火灾，1985年至1990年重建。

大雄宝殿后部山崖上为观音阁，明永乐八年（1410年）郑和创建，清同治年间重建，今为寺内文物陈列室。观音阁后部有近年重修的藏经阁。

慈寿塔位于金山西北角，始建于南朝齐梁时期，宋代曾立双塔，明隆庆三年（1569年）在原北塔遗址重建，改名慈寿塔。

清咸丰三年（1853年）毁于战火，清光绪二十六年（1900年）复建。新中国成立后将改木制栏杆改为钢筋混凝土结构，"文革"期间遭破坏，1989年塔身倾斜，进行了扶正修缮。

山巅妙高峰有留云亭，始建于宋，清咸丰三年（1853年）毁于战火，清同治十年（1871年）重建，两江总督曾国荃将康熙手书"江天一览"四字石碑供享亭内，改名江天一览亭。

"文革"时期石碑被毁，1977年重新刻石。

金山寺藏有清代学者叶志诜赠送的周鼎、传为苏东坡遗留的玉带、镇江知府魁元赠送的铜鼓和明代画家文徵明所绘《金山图》四件珍贵文物，并有宋佛顶尊胜陀罗尼经幢、雪浪石和宋代名将宗泽画像等，目前仅展示复制品。

· · · · ·
English

Jinshan (Gold Mountain) is one of the three famous mountains of Zhenjiang, 44 meters high, mainly renowned throughout the world for the Jinshan Temple on the mountain, with high building density, hence the proverb "Jinshan Temple wraps the mountain.

" Besides Jinshan Temple, there are numerous historical sites around Jinshan, such as Fahai Cave, White Dragon Cave, and Lengjia Terrace etc.

On the southern Bijia (Pen Rack) Mountain, it is said there is Guo Pu's cenotaph, now only a giant stone marker remains.

Jinshan also has the Zhongling Spring, known as "the number one spring under heaven," located on a small island in Taying Lake, requiring a boat to reach; the spring water has now dried up, and the stone railing by the spring was rebuilt in the 1950s.

1.Jinshan Temple: Jinshan Temple is located on the south bank of the Yangtze River northwest of Zhenjiang; in the Eastern Jin, a temple was built on a small island in the river, called Zexin Temple.

The most solemn of Buddhist repentance ceremonies, the Water-Land Ceremony, is traditionally said to have originated at this temple during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Liang.

Legend says the son of Tang Prime Minister Pei Xiu became a monk with the dharma name Fahai, who opened the mountain and found gold here, greatly expanding the temple, hence called Jinshan Temple; by the Tang it had become a tourist attraction, and the "Legend of the White Snake" takes this as its background.

Emperor Zhenzong of the Song once dreamed of Jinshan and issued an edict to rename the temple Longyou Temple; Emperor Huizong of the Song, advocating Daoism, changed the temple into a Daoist temple, called the Shenxiao Yuqing Wanshou Palace; after the Jingkang Incident of the Song, it was again called Jinshan Temple.

Song generals Han Shizhong and Yu Yunwen successively relied on the natural barrier here to successfully resist Jin troops.

During the Qing, Kangxi's southern tour climbed Jinshan and, seeing the water and sky as one color, bestowed the plaque "Jiangtian Chan Temple.

" During the Qianlong reign, the "Complete Library in Four Sections" was stored in the Wenzong Pavilion of Jinshan Temple.

Through successive dynasties' additions and repairs, Jinshan was densely covered with halls and pavilions, and from the Ming there was the saying "Jinshan Temple wraps the mountain.

" During the Taiping Rebellion the temple was destroyed by war fires, with halls completely gone, and the Wenzong Pavilion and its book collection were also burned to ashes.

Repairs were completed in the 10th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1871), and the seven-story Cishou (Longevity) Pagoda north of the mountain was restored in the 26th year of Guangxu (1900).

Another fire broke out in 1948, burning over three hundred halls and pavilions in the temple, leaving only the Cishou Pagoda, Heavenly King Hall, Lengjia Terrace, Guanyin Pavilion, and Liuyun Pavilion etc.

During the Guangxu reign of the Qing, the river silted up, and Jinshan Island gradually connected with the land.

Today's temple buildings were mostly rebuilt after the 1970s, with the temple gate facing west, and the mountain gate, Heavenly King Hall, and Mahavira Hall etc.

arranged in sequence along the western foot of the mountain.The Liuyun Mountain Gate was built in the early Republic, with Kangxi's imperial inscription "Jiangtian Chan Temple" plaque hanging above.

Outside the mountain gate is an archway, facing west with its back to east, of four-column three-gate style, cast with concrete formwork in the early Republic, with a pair of stone lions outside the archway.

The Heavenly King Hall was first built during the Zhengtong reign of the Ming, rebuilt in the 8th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1869).

The Mahavira Hall was first built during the Zhengtong reign of the Ming, destroyed by fire in 1948, and rebuilt from 1985 to 1990.

On the cliff behind the Mahavira Hall is the Guanyin Pavilion, founded by Zheng He in the 8th year of Yongle of the Ming (1410), rebuilt during the Tongzhi reign of the Qing, today the temple's cultural relics exhibition room.

Behind the Guanyin Pavilion is the recently restored Scripture Library.

The Cishou Pagoda is located at the northwest corner of Jinshan, first built during the Qi-Liang period of the Southern Dynasties; twin pagodas were erected in the Song, and in the 3rd year of Longqing of the Ming (1569) it was rebuilt on the site of the original north pagoda, renamed Cishou Pagoda.

Destroyed by war fires in the 3rd year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1853), it was rebuilt in the 26th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1900).

After the founding of New China, the wooden railings were changed to reinforced concrete structures; damaged during the Cultural Revolution, in 1989 the pagoda body tilted and was straightened and repaired.

At the mountain peak Miaogao Peak is the Liuyun (Remaining Cloud) Pavilion, first built in the Song, destroyed by war fires in the 3rd year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1853), rebuilt in the 10th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1871); Zeng Guoquan, Viceroy of Liangjiang, placed a stone stele with Kangxi's handwritten four characters "Jiangtian Yilan" (River and Sky in One View) inside the pavilion, renaming it the Jiangtian Yilan Pavilion.

The stele was destroyed during the Cultural Revolution, and re-carved in 1977.

Jinshan Temple houses four precious cultural relics: the Zhou Ding (bronze vessel) donated by Qing scholar Ye Zhishen, the jade belt traditionally left by Su Dongpo, the bronze drum donated by Zhenjiang Prefect Kui Yuan, and the "Painting of Jinshan" by Ming painter Wen Zhengming; it also has the Song Buddha's Top Superior Victorious Dharani Pillar, Xuelang Stone, and a portrait of Song general Zong Ze etc.

, currently only displaying replicas.

建筑要点 / Key Features
金山是镇江三大名山之一高44米主要因山上的金山寺而驰誉天下建筑密度大有金山寺裹山之谚除金山寺外金山周围还有众多古迹如法海洞白龙洞和楞伽台等南侧笔架山上据传有郭璞衣冠冢现只剩巨石标志金山还有号称天下第一泉的中泠泉位于塔影湖中小岛上需乘船前往泉水今已干涸泉边石栏为20世纪50年代重修金山寺金山寺位于镇江西北长江南岸东晋时在江中小岛建寺称泽心寺佛教经忏法事中最隆重的水陆法会相传便起源于梁武帝时期的此寺传说唐代宰相裴休之子出家为僧法号法海在此开山得金大肆扩建寺院始称金山寺唐代已成为游览胜地白蛇传即以此为背景宋真宗曾梦游金山诏改寺名为龙游寺宋徽宗崇尚道教又改寺为道观称神霄玉清万寿宫宋代靖康之变后复称金山寺宋将韩世忠和虞允文曾先后在此据天险成功抵御金兵清代康熙南巡登金山见水天一色赐江天禅寺匾乾隆时期曾在金山寺文宗阁皮藏四库全书经过历代增修金山上殿阁密布从明代就有金山寺裹山之说太平天国期间寺庙毁于战火殿堂荡然无存文宗阁和藏书也付之一炬清同治十年1871年重修完毕清光绪二十六年1900年修复山北七层慈寿塔1948年又发生火灾寺内三百余间殿阁被焚仅存慈寿塔天王殿楞伽台观音阁和留云阁等处清光绪年间江水淤塞
04 西津渡街
Xijindu Street
元—清
级别 Level
含昭关石塔（第六批国保2006年）、救生会（第七批省保2011年）、旧生会旧址（省保）
地址 Address
镇江城西云台山北麓
类型 Type
历史文化街区/古街
门票 Ticket
街道全天免费开放，观音洞和救生会需购票
中文原文

西津渡街，又称观音洞一条街或小码头一条街，东至大西路，西至苏北路与小铁路交接处，东西长484米，宽3米。街道全天免费开放，观音洞和救生会需购票。此街原为沿山壁开辟的栈道，下临长江，后来在此设古渡口，因靠近蒜山，名蒜山渡。

六朝时称西津渡，唐代称金陵渡，元代成为交通命脉，江浙闽海运货物由此达京师，清代被誉为银码头，一直是镇江南北驿道要冲上的主要渡口。清道光以降，长江主航道北移，街区功能由渡口转变为区域商贸中心。石板路上至今仍保留着深深的车辙印。

街上现存多处古迹，包括元代昭关石塔，清代观音洞、救生会和待渡亭等。其中昭关石塔为国保单位，旧生会旧址为省保单位。

街道东端为五十三坡，即东侧坡道上的53级台阶，坡上街南有观音洞，乃宋代借天然洞穴扩建成的庙宇，今存清咸丰九年（1859年）依山重建的三层楼。西侧渡口边有清同治七年（1868年）所建待渡亭。

云台山北麓有清末形成的传统民居街区。镇江开埠后，西津渡银山门一带被占为英租界，现存英国领事馆、美国领事馆、英工部局大楼、税务司公馆、亚细亚火油公司和美孚火油公司等租界建筑。1. 昭关石塔：第六批国保（2006年）。

昭关石塔立于观音洞和救生会之间，是一座过街塔，下部开圭形门洞，类似城关，门外是通往江北瓜州和江中金山的西津渡古渡口。塔始建于元代，为喇嘛塔形制，明万历十年（1582年）重修塔基，1959年、1980年两次修整。

洞顶横额东西两面均刻"昭关"二字，附会伍子胥逃离楚国时所过的昭关（实际在今安徽省含山县）。过街塔发源于西藏地区，中国始见于元代，是藏传佛教的重要建筑类型。昭关石塔与武汉胜像宝塔、北京妙应寺白塔风格接近，应为建于元代的"噶当觉顿式"喇嘛塔。

元代喇嘛塔塔身低，相轮粗，天盘宽，称"噶当觉顿式"，昭关石塔为典型代表。明代中叶以后国内所建喇嘛塔塔身较高，相轮较细，天盘较小，称为"觉顿式"。

昭关石塔下部是用青石砌筑的四根石柱，南北洞口较低，仅东西贯通行人，柱顶有雕刻精美的石雀替，上架石枋搭成平台，地面至台顶高3.9米。台上立喇嘛塔，全用青石雕垒成，高4.69米。

塔下部是两层的亚字形须弥座，四角各形成五个转角，上置莲花金刚座，座上为覆钵形塔身，其上又为亚字形平座，上托周套重圈的圆锥形"十三轮"，顶部是仰莲伞盖、法轮和宝瓶形塔刹，内置镇塔之宝佛镜等。出石塔西门可望见渡口码头，这段长江水道狭窄，水流湍急，常发生翻船溺水事件，因而在此建塔保佑平安。

2. 救生会：第七批省保（2011年）。救生会是古代救护各种船只和渡江人员的慈善机构。清康熙四十二年（1703年），京口蒋元鼐、朱用载、蒋尚忠等十五人力劝"邑中输钱，救涉江覆舟者"。他们捐助白金若干，在西津渡观音阁成立"京口救生会"。

康熙四十七年（1708年），救生会购得西津渡昭关晏公庙旧址，建屋三间作为会址。救生会南部临街为砖木结构二层楼房，三开间，坐北朝南，为办公之所。清光绪二十一年（1895年）在正门上置办"救生会"石额。

其内为庭院，院北建连廊和附属用房，西南有角门出入。整组建筑为清代风格，保存完好。京口救生会影响遍及大江南北，江西、湖北、安徽各省纷纷效仿，打造救生红船，实施救助措施。该会成立后持续活动长达200年之久，在我国水上救生史以及古代民间慈善事业中均堪称奇迹。

· · · · ·
English

Xijindu Street, also called Guanyin Cave Street or Small Wharf Street, extends east to Daxi Road and west to the junction of Subei Road and the Small Railway, 484 meters long east-west and 3 meters wide.

The street is open free all day; Guanyin Cave and the Rescue Society require tickets.

This street was originally a plank road carved along the mountain cliff, overlooking the Yangtze River below; later an ancient ferry was established here, called Suanshan Ferry because it was near Suan Mountain.

In the Six Dynasties it was called Xijin Ferry, in the Tang Jinling Ferry, and in the Yuan it became a transportation lifeline, with sea transport goods from Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and Fujian reaching the capital through here; in the Qing it was hailed as the Silver Wharf, always the main ferry on the key north-south post road of Zhenjiang.

From the Daoguang reign of the Qing onward, the main channel of the Yangtze shifted north, and the district's function transformed from a ferry to a regional trade center.

Deep wheel ruts are still preserved on the stone slab road today.

Many historical sites exist on the street, including the Yuan Zhaoguan Stone Pagoda, and the Qing Guanyin Cave, Rescue Society, and Waiting-for-Ferry Pavilion etc.

Among them, the Zhaoguan Stone Pagoda is a national protected unit, and the former Rescue Society site is a provincial protected unit.The east end of the street is the Fifty-Three Slope, i.e.

, the 53 stone steps on the east side ramp; south of the street on the slope is Guanyin Cave, a temple expanded from a natural cave in the Song, today preserving a three-story building rebuilt against the mountain in the 9th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1859).

By the ferry on the west side is the Waiting-for-Ferry Pavilion built in the 7th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1868).

At the northern foot of Yuntai Mountain is a traditional residential district formed in the late Qing.

After Zhenjiang opened as a treaty port, the area around Yinshan Gate of Xijin Ferry was occupied as the British concession, today preserving concession buildings such as the British Consulate, American Consulate, British Municipal Council Building, Tax Commissioner's Residence, Asiatic Petroleum Company, and Standard Oil Company etc.

1.Zhaoguan Stone Pagoda: 6th Batch National Protected (2006).

The Zhaoguan Stone Pagoda stands between Guanyin Cave and the Rescue Society; it is a street-crossing pagoda, with a guiform (sword-shaped) gate opening at the lower part, similar to a city gate; outside the gate is the ancient Xijin Ferry crossing leading to Guazhou north of the river and Jinshan in the river.

The pagoda was first built in the Yuan, in the form of a Lamaist pagoda; its base was rebuilt in the 10th year of Wanli of the Ming (1582), and repaired twice in 1959 and 1980.

The horizontal plaque above the cave opening is engraved with the two characters "Zhaoguan" on both east and west sides, associated with the Zhaoguan Pass that Wu Zixu passed when fleeing the State of Chu (actually in today's Hanshan County, Anhui Province).

Street-crossing pagodas originated in Tibet and first appeared in China in the Yuan, an important architectural type of Tibetan Buddhism.

The Zhaoguan Stone Pagoda is close in style to the Shengxiang Pagoda in Wuhan and the White Pagoda of Miaoying Temple in Beijing, and should be a "Kadam-Jokton-style" Lamaist pagoda built in the Yuan.

Yuan Lamaist pagodas have a low body, thick harmika (ring of circles), and wide heaven disc, called "Kadam-Jokton style," with the Zhaoguan Stone Pagoda as a typical representative.

After the mid-Ming, Lamaist pagodas built in China have a taller body, thinner harmika, and smaller heaven disc, called "Jokton style.

" The lower part of the Zhaoguan Stone Pagoda consists of four stone pillars built of bluestone; the north and south gate openings are low, only allowing pedestrians to pass east-west; the pillar tops have exquisitely carved stone spandrel brackets, with stone beams above forming a platform, 3.

9 meters high from ground to platform top.On the platform stands the Lamaist pagoda, entirely carved and stacked from bluestone, 4.69 meters high.

The lower part of the pagoda is a two-story ya-shaped (cross-shaped) Sumeru base, with five corners formed at each of the four corners; above it is a lotus vajra seat, on which is the overturned-bowl-shaped pagoda body, above which is another ya-shaped flat seat, supporting the conical "thirteen rings" wrapped with repeated circles; the top is an upward-lotus umbrella canopy, dharma wheel, and vase-shaped pagoda finial, with the pagoda-suppressing treasure Buddha mirror etc.

placed inside.

Exiting the west gate of the stone pagoda, one can see the ferry wharf; this section of the Yangtze waterway is narrow with rapid currents, and boat-capsizing and drowning incidents often occurred, hence a pagoda was built here to bless safety.

2.Rescue Society: 7th Batch Provincial Protected (2011).The Rescue Society was a charitable institution in ancient times for rescuing various boats and people crossing the river.

In the 42nd year of Kangxi of the Qing (1703), fifteen people including Jiang Yuannai, Zhu Yongzai, and Jiang Shangzhong of Jingkou strongly urged "the county to contribute money to rescue those who capsize boats crossing the river.

" They donated several taels of platinum and established the "Jingkou Rescue Society" at the Guanyin Pavilion of Xijin Ferry.

In the 47th year of Kangxi (1708), the Rescue Society purchased the former site of the Zhaoguan Yan Gong Temple at Xijin Ferry and built three rooms as its headquarters.

The southern part of the Rescue Society facing the street is a two-story brick-wood building, three bays wide, facing south with its back to north, serving as office space.

In the 21st year of Guangxu of the Qing (1895), a stone plaque "Rescue Society" was placed on the main gate.

Inside is a courtyard, with a covered corridor and auxiliary rooms built north of the courtyard, and a corner gate for entry and exit in the southwest.

The entire building complex is in Qing style and well preserved.

The Jingkou Rescue Society's influence spread throughout the country, with provinces such as Jiangxi, Hubei, and Anhui following suit, building rescue red boats and implementing rescue measures.

After its establishment, the society continued its activities for as long as 200 years, truly a miracle in the history of water rescue and ancient folk philanthropy in China.

建筑要点 / Key Features
西津渡街又称观音洞一条街或小码头一条街东至大西路西至苏北路与小铁路交接处东西长484米宽3米此街原为沿山壁开辟的栈道下临长江后来在此设古渡口因靠近蒜山名蒜山渡六朝时称西津渡唐代称金陵渡元代成为交通命脉江浙闽海运货物由此达京师清代被誉为银码头一直是镇江南北驿道要冲上的主要渡口清道光以降长江主航道北移街区功能由渡口转变为区域商贸中心石板路上至今仍保留着深深的车辙印街上现存多处古迹包括元代昭关石塔清代观音洞救生会和待渡亭等其中昭关石塔为国保单位旧生会旧址为省保单位街道东端为五十三坡即东侧坡道上的53级台阶坡上街南有观音洞乃宋代借天然洞穴扩建成的庙宇今存清咸丰九年1859年依山重建的三层楼西侧渡口边有清同治七年1868年所建待渡亭云台山北麓有清末形成的传统民居街区镇江开埠后西津渡银山门一带被占为英租界现存英国领事馆美国领事馆英工部局大楼税务司公馆亚细亚火油公司和美孚火油公司等租界建筑昭关石塔第六批国保2006年昭关石塔立于观音洞和救生会之间是一座过街塔下部开圭形门洞类似城关门外是通往江北瓜州和江中金山的西津渡古渡口塔始建于元代为喇嘛塔形制明万历十年1582年重修塔基1959年1980年两次修整
05 镇江英国领事馆旧址
Former British Consulate of Zhenjiang
清（1889—1890）
级别 Level
第四批全国重点文物保护单位（1996年）
地址 Address
润州区云台山北麓五十三坡，小码头街1号
类型 Type
近代建筑/领事馆
中文原文

清同治元年（1862年）英国在镇江设立租界，清同治三年（1864年）建领事馆，清光绪十五年（1889年）因巡捕殴毙华人，英人裁判不公，激怒民众放火烧了领事馆和巡捕房。

清政府赔款4万两白银，次年（1890年）用赔款重建。原建筑群由5栋建筑组成，分别为办公楼、西北的员工宿舍、南坡的正、副领事官府邸和北面的工部局巡捕房。均为砖木结构，用青砖砌筑，夹杂红砖装饰。

1933年售予江苏省民政厅长赵启騄，现为镇江市博物馆。办公大楼在最高处，采用外廊式风格，屋顶三角形山花中央刻有"1890"字样。楼高三层，沿台地布置，首层仅有东侧一间，北向开门。二层为过厅和三个房间，东侧券门额首两侧各嵌圆形花岗岩，雕刻"IR"两字，由过厅楼梯可至三层。

三层可从正门进入，面积最大，有8个房间，五间带壁炉，西侧过廊有地下室。屋外以连廊通向辅助平房。建筑采用木屋架、瓦楞铁皮顶，墙面以红砖为主，用青砖砌出花纹。券廊下的栏杆用宜兴产绿色琉璃瓷宝瓶。室内地面先用砖做地垄，上架密肋木梁，再铺钉企口木地板。楼板用密肋木梁，上铺木地板，天花及券廊用石膏抹面平顶，四周做天花灯圈与线脚。

东面底层与二层券廊为砖砌弧形拱券天花，二层底拱券廊天花用工字钢小梁，上砌弧形砖拱券。北侧云台山下是工部局巡捕房，为东西向三层楼房，用青砖砌筑，红砖装饰。南立面二、三层有券廊，底层为墙面，开8个拱券窗。办公楼南部东西两侧有两座三层小楼，为正、副领事住所。

东北方的白色二层楼房原为美国领事馆，清光绪二十六年（1900年）美国领事馆迁往江宁（今南京），该建筑成为职员宿舍、餐厅和娱乐房间，东南两面有券廊，现用玻璃封闭。

· · · · ·
English

In the 1st year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1862), Britain established a concession in Zhenjiang; in the 3rd year of Tongzhi (1864) the consulate was built; in the 15th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1889), because a patrolman beat a Chinese person to death and the British judged unfairly, the enraged people set fire to the consulate and police station.

The Qing government paid 40,000 taels of silver in compensation, and the following year (1890) rebuilt it with the compensation.

The original building complex consisted of 5 buildings: the office building, the staff dormitory to the northwest, the residences of the consul and vice-consul on the southern slope, and the Municipal Council police station to the north.

All are brick-wood structures, built with grey bricks and interspersed with red brick decoration.

In 1933 it was sold to Zhao Qilu, Director of the Civil Affairs Department of Jiangsu Province, and is now the Zhenjiang City Museum.

The office building is at the highest point, adopting the veranda style, with the characters "1890" engraved in the center of the triangular gable of the roof.

It is three stories high, arranged along the terrace; the first floor has only one room on the east side, with the door opening north.

The second floor is a hallway and three rooms; on both sides of the arch door lintel on the east side are embedded round granites engraved with the two letters "IR"; from the hallway stairs one can reach the third floor.

The third floor can be entered from the main gate, with the largest area, 8 rooms, 5 with fireplaces, and a basement in the west hallway.Outside, a covered corridor leads to auxiliary bungalows.

The building uses wooden roof trusses and corrugated iron roofs; the walls are mainly red brick, with patterns laid in grey brick.

The railings under the veranda use green glazed porcelain vases produced in Yixing.

The indoor floor first uses bricks to make floor joists, with dense ribbed wooden beams above, then nailed tongue-and-groove wooden flooring.

The floor slabs use dense ribbed wooden beams with wooden flooring above; the ceilings and verandas use plastered flat ceilings, with ceiling lamp rings and moldings around.

The east ground and second-floor verandas have brick-built arched vaulted ceilings; the second-floor bottom veranda ceiling uses I-beam small girders with arched brick vaults above.

North of Yuntai Mountain below is the Municipal Council police station, an east-west three-story building, built with grey bricks and decorated with red bricks.

The south facade has verandas on the second and third floors, with the ground floor as a wall with 8 arched windows.

On the east and west sides south of the office building are two three-story small buildings, the residences of the consul and vice-consul.

The white two-story building to the northeast was originally the American Consulate; in the 26th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1900) the American Consulate moved to Jiangning (today's Nanjing), and this building became staff dormitory, dining room, and entertainment rooms, with verandas on the southeast sides, now enclosed with glass.

建筑要点 / Key Features
清同治元年1862年英国在镇江设立租界清同治三年1864年建领事馆清光绪十五年1889年因巡捕殴毙华人英人裁判不公激怒民众放火烧了领事馆和巡捕房清政府赔款4万两白银次年1890年用赔款重建原建筑群由5栋建筑组成分别为办公楼西北的员工宿舍南坡的正副领事官府邸和北面的工部局巡捕房均为砖木结构用青砖砌筑夹杂红砖装饰1933年售予江苏省民政厅长赵启騄现为镇江市博物馆办公大楼在最高处采用外廊式风格屋顶三角形山花中央刻有1890字样楼高三层沿台地布置首层仅有东侧一间北向开门二层为过厅和三个房间东侧券门额首两侧各嵌圆形花岗岩雕刻IR两字由过厅楼梯可至三层三层可从正门进入面积最大有8个房间五间带壁炉西侧过廊有地下室屋外以连廊通向辅助平房建筑采用木屋架瓦楞铁皮顶墙面以红砖为主用青砖砌出花纹券廊下的栏杆用宜兴产绿色琉璃瓷宝瓶室内地面先用砖做地垄上架密肋木梁再铺钉企口木地板楼板用密肋木梁上铺木地板天花及券廊用石膏抹面平顶四周做天花灯圈与线脚东面底层与二层券廊为砖砌弧形拱券天花二层底拱券廊天花用工字钢小梁上砌弧形砖拱券北侧云台山下是工部局巡捕房为东西向三层楼房用青砖砌筑红砖装饰南立面二三层有券廊底层为墙面开8
06 伯先路近代建筑群
Modern Building Complex on Boxian Road
晚清—民国
级别 Level
含广肇公所（第七批省保2011年）、镇江商会旧址（第六批省保2006年）、五卅演讲厅（第三批省保1982年）
地址 Address
润州区伯先路延伸至京畿路
类型 Type
近代建筑群
中文原文

伯先路近代建筑群从润州区伯先路延伸至京畿路，保存有大量晚清、民国建筑，类型多样，质量上乘。主要建筑有广肇公所、浸礼会教堂、镇江商会、怀仁诊所、屠家骅公馆、内地会教堂、镇江老邮政局、世界红字会江苏省会、定福寺旧址和伯先公园等。1. 广肇公所：第七批省保（2011年）。

广肇公所是广东肇庆地区来镇江经商的同乡会所。原在运粮河旁中华路菜场南，清光绪三十三年（1907年）由卓翼堂主持在现址重建。公所坐东朝西，面积约600余平方米，内有厅房、正房、偏房和厢房20多间。厅南厢房内壁嵌"广肇公所记"碑，记载公所历史及重建始末。

大门用磨砖砌成，上有挑檐，装饰"五福盘寿"砖雕，白石横额镌刻"广肇公所"四字，落款为"前护川督陈橘书"。门上有"福禄寿"三星，"琴棋书画"和"渔樵耕读"等砖雕装饰，大门两侧磨砖倚柱底部有石刻蝙蝠纹样等。2. 镇江商会旧址：第六批省保（2006年）。镇江商会旧址现为镇江市工商业联合会。

1929年北伐军归还镇江工商联借款20万银圆，实业家陆小波（1882—1973）等用其中4万元建造商会。建筑为砖木结构，青砖建造，共三进院落，外立面有中华巴洛克式门楼，内部院落为中式风格。

正门朝南，迎街朝东另建一座大门楼，两座门楼都用方砖柱砌出西式牌楼，南门较为正式，入口有砖砌罗马式拱券叠涩，门上嵌于右任题写的"镇江商会"白石横额。门内共有三进，第一进院北为大厅，宽三间，南面采用中式槅扇门，两侧为厢房；第二进后部为二层楼，第三进由东大门进入，为三层楼房，有走廊与第二进相连。屋顶用平瓦，坡度较缓。

3. 五卅演讲厅：第三批省保（1982年），位于伯先路18号伯先公园内。

· · · · ·
English

The Modern Building Complex on Boxian Road extends from Boxian Road to Jingji Road in Runzhou District, preserving a large number of late Qing and Republic buildings, diverse in type and high in quality.

The main buildings include the Guangzhao Guild Hall, Baptist Church, Zhenjiang Chamber of Commerce, Huairen Clinic, Tu Jiahua Mansion, China Inland Mission Church, Old Zhenjiang Post Office, World Red Swastika Society Jiangsu Provincial Association, former site of Dingfu Temple, and Boxian Park etc.

1.Guangzhao Guild Hall: 7th Batch Provincial Protected (2011).The Guangzhao Guild Hall was a fellow-townsmen's club for merchants from Zhaoqing area of Guangdong who came to do business in Zhenjiang.

Originally located south of the Zhonghua Road vegetable market beside the grain transport river, in the 33rd year of Guangxu of the Qing (1907) it was rebuilt at the current site under the direction of Zhuo Yitang.

The guild hall faces west with its back to east, with an area of about 600 square meters, containing over 20 rooms including halls, main rooms, side rooms, and wing rooms.

On the inner wall of the south wing room of the hall is embedded the "Record of the Guangzhao Guild Hall" stele, recording the history of the guild hall and the process of its reconstruction.

The main gate is built of ground bricks, with overhanging eaves above, decorated with "Five Blessings Surrounding Longevity" brick carvings; the white stone horizontal plaque is engraved with the four characters "Guangzhao Guild Hall," with the signature "Written by Chen Ju, former acting Governor of Sichuan.

" On the gate are brick-carving decorations such as the "Fu Lu Shou" (Fortune, Prosperity, Longevity) Three Stars, "Qin Qi Shu Hua" (Lute, Chess, Calligraphy, Painting), and "Yu Qiao Geng Du" (Fisherman, Woodcutter, Farmer, Scholar) etc.

; at the bottom of the ground-brick pilasters on both sides of the main gate are stone-carved bat patterns etc.2.Former Zhenjiang Chamber of Commerce: 6th Batch Provincial Protected (2006).

The former Zhenjiang Chamber of Commerce is now the Zhenjiang City Federation of Industry and Commerce.

In 1929, the Northern Expeditionary Army repaid the 200,000 silver dollars borrowed by the Zhenjiang Federation of Industry and Commerce; industrialist Lu Xiaobo (1882-1973) etc.

used 40,000 yuan of it to build the chamber.

The building is brick-wood structure, built with grey bricks, with a total of three courtyards; the exterior facade has a Chinese-Baroque style gate tower, and the internal courtyards are in Chinese style.

The main gate faces south, and another large gate tower was built facing east toward the street; both gate towers use square brick columns to build Western-style archways; the south gate is more formal, with a brick Roman-style arch corbel entrance, and a white stone horizontal plaque with "Zhenjiang Chamber of Commerce" inscribed by Yu Youren embedded on the gate.

Inside the gate there are three courtyards in total: the north of the first courtyard is a main hall, three bays wide, with Chinese lattice doors on the south side and wing rooms on both sides; the rear of the second courtyard is a two-story building; the third courtyard, entered from the east main gate, is a three-story building with a corridor connecting to the second courtyard.

The roof uses flat tiles with a relatively gentle slope.3.May 30th Lecture Hall: 3rd Batch Provincial Protected (1982), located inside Boxian Park at No.18 Boxian Road.

建筑要点 / Key Features
伯先路近代建筑群从润州区伯先路延伸至京畿路保存有大量晚清民国建筑类型多样质量上乘主要建筑有广肇公所浸礼会教堂镇江商会怀仁诊所屠家骅公馆内地会教堂镇江老邮政局世界红字会江苏省会定福寺旧址和伯先公园等广肇公所第七批省保2011年广肇公所是广东肇庆地区来镇江经商的同乡会所原在运粮河旁中华路菜场南清光绪三十三年1907年由卓翼堂主持在现址重建公所坐东朝西面积约600余平方米内有厅房正房偏房和厢房20多间厅南厢房内壁嵌广肇公所记碑记载公所历史及重建始末大门用磨砖砌成上有挑檐装饰五福盘寿砖雕白石横额镌刻广肇公所四字落款为前护川督陈橘书门上有福禄寿三星琴棋书画和渔樵耕读等砖雕装饰大门两侧磨砖倚柱底部有石刻蝙蝠纹样等镇江商会旧址第六批省保2006年镇江商会旧址现为镇江市工商业联合会1929年北伐军归还镇江工商联借款20万银圆实业家陆小波18821973等用其中4万元建造商会建筑为砖木结构青砖建造共三进院落外立面有中华巴洛克式门楼内部院落为中式风格正门朝南朝东另建一座大门楼两座门楼都用方砖柱砌出西式牌楼南门较为正式入口有砖砌罗马式拱券叠涩门上嵌于右任题写的镇江商会白石横额门内共有三进第一进院北为大厅宽三
07 山巷清真寺
Shanxiang Mosque
清
级别 Level
第七批省级文物保护单位（2011年）
地址 Address
镇江城西清真寺街84号
类型 Type
清真寺/伊斯兰教建筑
门票 Ticket
免费开放
中文原文

山巷清真寺又称"城西清真寺"或"西大寺"，因位于山巷东侧，故名"山巷清真寺"。初建时仅有三间茅舍，清康熙年间扩建，咸丰三年（1853年）毁于兵燹，同治十二年（1873年）重建。

后由穆斯林信众集资，光绪二十八年（1902年）大规模扩建，"文革"前期被学校占用，"文革"中期遭到破坏，1982年市政府拨款修缮。这是江苏省现存规模最大的清真寺之一，也是全国三大伊斯兰印经处之一。

山巷清真寺坐东朝西，占地三亩左右，有门楼、前厅、天井、大殿、南讲堂、对厅和望月楼，围以条石基础的青砖围墙。寺门对面有照壁，门宽三间，深两间，中部有斗栱装饰。门内经天井有宽三间的过廊，折向西为第二道门，两旁立雕花石鼓；入门经巷道折向北有第三道门，门内为主庭院。

庭院南侧是院门和游廊，东侧为信一堂，北侧为讲堂，望月楼位于庭院东北角，是一座两层六角攒尖顶小楼，下部与庭院连为一体。庭院西侧是礼拜殿，由窑殿、正殿和辅殿（备殿）组成。殿前出卷棚前廊，前后殿相连，均为硬山式，西边两角挑出长檐，檐角翘起，后部正中向西又伸出一间，歇山式屋顶，外部为半亭阁式墙身。

大殿正面用隔扇门，宽、深皆为五间，内有52根圆木立柱，梁上彩绘华丽精细。殿内悬挂多块匾额，西墙正中砌"米哈拉布"（凹龛），右首有红漆"敏拜尔"（宣讲台），两侧开明窗，采光极佳，使祭坛和讲坛显得格外明亮。

· · · · ·
English

Shanxiang Mosque, also called "West City Mosque" or "West Great Mosque," is named "Shanxiang Mosque" because it is located on the east side of Shanxiang Lane.

When first built it had only three thatched rooms; it was expanded during the Kangxi reign of the Qing, destroyed by war fires in the 3rd year of Xianfeng (1853), and rebuilt in the 12th year of Tongzhi (1873).

Later, with funds raised by Muslim believers, it was greatly expanded in the 28th year of Guangxu (1902); in the early Cultural Revolution it was occupied by a school, and in the mid-Cultural Revolution it was damaged; in 1982 the municipal government allocated funds for repair.

This is one of the largest existing mosques in Jiangsu Province and one of the three major Islamic scripture-printing establishments in China.

Shanxiang Mosque faces west with its back to east, covering about three mu, with a gate tower, front hall, courtyard, main hall, south lecture hall, opposite hall, and moon-watching tower, enclosed by a grey-brick wall on a strip-stone foundation.

Opposite the temple gate is a screen wall; the gate is three bays wide and two bays deep, with bracket decoration in the middle.

Inside the gate, through the courtyard, is a three-bay-wide corridor; turning west is the second gate, with carved stone drums on both sides; entering through a lane and turning north is the third gate, inside which is the main courtyard.

South of the courtyard are the courtyard gate and covered corridor; east is the Xinyi Hall; north is the lecture hall; the moon-watching tower is at the northeast corner of the courtyard, a two-story hexagonal pyramidal-roof small building, with its lower part integrated with the courtyard.

West of the courtyard is the prayer hall, composed of the mihrab hall, main hall, and auxiliary hall (reserve hall).

In front of the hall is a rolling-roof front porch; the front and rear halls are connected, both of yingshan (gable) style; the two western corners project long eaves with upturned corners; at the rear center, extending westward, is another room with a xieshan (hip-and-gable) roof, externally a semi-pavilion wall body.

The front of the main hall uses lattice doors, five bays wide and five bays deep, with 52 round wooden columns inside, and the beams are painted with ornate and delicate colors.

Many plaques hang inside the hall; in the center of the west wall is built the "mihrab" (recessed niche), and on the right is the red-lacquered "minbar" (preaching platform); bright windows on both sides provide excellent lighting, making the altar and pulpit appear especially bright.

建筑要点 / Key Features
山巷清真寺又称城西清真寺或西大寺因位于山巷东侧故名山巷清真寺初建时仅有三间茅舍清康熙年间扩建咸丰三年1853年毁于兵燹同治十二年1873年重建后由穆斯林信众集资光绪二十八年1902年大规模扩建文革前期被学校占用文革中期遭到破坏1982年市政府拨款修缮这是江苏省现存规模最大的清真寺之一也是全国三大伊斯兰印经处之一山巷清真寺坐东朝西占地三亩左右有门楼前天井大殿南讲堂对厅和望月楼围以条石基础的青砖围墙寺门对面有照壁门宽三间深两间中部有斗栱装饰门内经天井有宽三间的过廊折向西为第二道门两旁立雕花石鼓入门经巷道折向北有第三道门门内为主庭院庭院南侧是院门和游廊东侧为信一堂北侧为讲堂望月楼位于庭院东北角是一座两层六角攒尖顶小楼下部与庭院连为一体庭院西侧是礼拜殿由窑殿正殿和辅殿备殿组成殿前出卷棚前廊前后殿相连均为硬山式西边两角挑出长檐檐角翘起后部正中向西又伸出一间歇山式屋顶外部为半亭阁式墙身大殿正面用隔扇门宽深皆为五间内有52根圆木立柱梁上彩绘华丽精细殿内悬挂多块匾额西墙正中砌米哈拉布凹龛右首有红漆敏拜尔宣讲台两侧开明窗采光极佳使祭坛和讲坛显得格外明亮

Former Residence of Pearl Buck

中文原文

美国著名作家赛珍珠（Pearl Sydenstricker Buck，1892—1973）曾经在中国长期生活，以中国为背景的长篇小说《大地》先后获得普利策文学奖和诺贝尔文学奖。赛珍珠的父亲赛兆祥为美国南长老会传教士，她出生四个月就随父母来到中国，在镇江生活到18岁。

赛珍珠故居建于清光绪中期，为青砖砌筑的二层西式楼房，可能由美国南长老会传教士设计建造，占地259平方米。正立面朝南，向前伸出一间"凸"字形两层外廊，上层用玻璃封闭，下为门廊。入门迎面为木楼梯，可登至二楼。走廊两旁各有大小三个房间，上下基本相似，为会客室和卧室。室内均铺木地板，石灰抹面平顶天花，原有四座壁炉。

东西两侧用长方形直高窗，顶部平梁上砌券拱装饰。东立面地势较低，砌有地下室，北立面上下均用连续高窗。屋顶原为瓦楞铁皮，今已改为平瓦。故居现对外开放，展览赛珍珠的著作、物品、资料和镇江与外国友好交流的展品。

· · · · ·
English

The famous American writer Pearl Buck (Pearl Sydenstricker Buck, 1892-1973) lived in China for a long time; her novel "The Good Earth," set in China, successively won the Pulitzer Prize for Literature and the Nobel Prize in Literature.

Pearl Buck's father, Absalom Sydenstricker, was a missionary of the American Southern Presbyterian Church; she came to China with her parents at four months old and lived in Zhenjiang until she was 18.

The former residence of Pearl Buck was built in the mid-Guangxu reign of the Qing, a two-story Western-style building of grey brick, possibly designed and built by missionaries of the American Southern Presbyterian Church, covering 259 square meters.

The main facade faces south, projecting forward a "convex"-shaped two-story veranda; the upper story is enclosed with glass, and the lower is a porch.

Entering the gate, facing you is a wooden staircase leading to the second floor.

On both sides of the corridor are three rooms of various sizes each, basically similar upstairs and downstairs, serving as reception rooms and bedrooms.

The interiors are all paved with wooden floors, with plastered flat ceilings, and originally had four fireplaces.

The east and west sides use rectangular tall straight windows, with arch vault decorations built on the top flat beams.

The east facade has lower terrain, with a basement built; the north facade uses continuous tall windows both upstairs and downstairs.The roof was originally corrugated iron, now changed to flat tiles.

The former residence is now open to the public, exhibiting Pearl Buck's works, objects, materials, and exhibits of friendly exchanges between Zhenjiang and foreign countries.

建筑要点 / Key Features
美国著名作家赛珍珠Pearl Sydenstricker Buck18921973曾经在中国长期生活以中国为背景的长篇小说大地先后获得普利策文学奖和诺贝尔文学奖赛珍珠的父亲赛兆祥为美国南长老会传教士她出生四个月就随父母来到中国在镇江生活到18岁赛珍珠故居建于清光绪中期为青砖砌筑的二层西式楼房可能由美国南长老会传教士设计建造占地259平方米正立面朝南向前伸出一间凸字形两层外廊上层用玻璃封闭下为门廊入门迎面为木楼梯可登至二楼走廊两旁各有大小三个房间上下基本相似为会客室和卧室室内均铺木地板石灰抹面平顶天花原有四座壁炉东西两侧用长方形直高窗顶部平梁上砌券拱装饰东立面地势较低砌有地下室北立面上下均用连续高窗屋顶原为瓦楞铁皮今已改为平瓦故居现对外开放展览赛珍珠的著作物资料和镇江与外国友好交流的展品
09 南山
Nanshan Mountain
东晋—清
级别 Level
含招隐寺、竹林寺、鹤林寺、赵伯先墓
地址 Address
镇江城南约2.5公里
类型 Type
风景名胜/佛教寺院
门票 Ticket
旺季40元，淡季30元
开放时间 Hours
7:30 — 17:30
中文原文

南山景区内重峦叠翠，茂林修竹，被北宋书画家米芾誉为"城市山林"，其中主要名胜为鹤林、竹林和招隐三座古寺。鹤林寺和竹林寺皆创建于东晋，招隐寺建于南朝宋。南山景区屡有兴废，太平天国和抗日战争时期遭遇战火，"文革"前后也受到毁坏，今大部分殿宇为毁后重建。

1. 招隐寺：招隐寺在南郊招隐山中，据传戴颙曾在山中隐居，后来其女舍宅为寺，称招隐寺。南朝宋时金山寺高僧普慈住持该寺，曾以其法号作为寺名。南朝梁时萧统在此读书。明万历二十六年（1598年），为与鹤林寺呼应，改名鹿泉寺。

清咸丰年间毁于战火，同治、光绪时期相继重建，1923年在今址复建，抗日期间被毁，新中国成立前被国民党军队占驻，"文革"又遭破坏。目前景点多为1980年以后陆续复建，有招隐坊、听鹂山房、虎跑泉、鹿跑泉、玉蕊亭、珍珠泉和鸟外亭等。2. 竹林寺：竹林寺在夹山北麓。

始建于东晋，初名夹山禅院，唐代曾作为鹤林寺下院，后圮废。明崇祯年间（1635年前后）重建，独立成寺，因四周修竹环抱，改名竹林寺。清康熙三十八年（1699年）康熙帝南巡时曾在此驻跸，亲题寺匾。

清雍正十一年（1733年）诏令重建，规模宏大，为其鼎盛时期。

清咸丰六年（1856年）毁于战火，清咸丰八年（1858年）建后又毁，同治三年（1864年）重建，但规模已不如前。抗日战争时期部分被日军烧毁，"文革"中破坏殆尽。

1981年部分修复，主要景点有林公泉和挹江亭等。3. 鹤林寺：鹤林寺在南郊磨笄山北麓，始建于东晋，初名竹林寺。传说南朝宋开国皇帝刘裕年轻时常在寺内劳作休息，时有黄鹤飞舞其上，他即位后改名为鹤林寺。

南宋绍兴年间重建，咸淳年间迁至山南，明永乐十年（1412年）又毁，僧人就原古竹院稍加修缮为寺，即今址。

明弘治八年（1495年）和万历二十四年（1596年）、清康熙四年（1665年）多次重建，清咸丰年间毁于战火，"文革"时期破坏严重，景致大多湮没，今存杜鹃花、杜鹃楼和米芾墓等。

4. 赵伯先墓：赵伯先墓在竹林寺东侧文苑景区。赵声（1881—1911）字伯先，镇江大港人，同盟会主要领导人之一。1912年葬在镇江南郊，墓碑刻"大烈士赵伯先之墓"。后来又在墓道前方丘地上树赵声戎装骑马画像石碑亭一座，与坟包、墓道构成中轴线。抗日战争前曾扩建陵墓，因战争爆发中止。

1966年陵墓被破坏，1981年重树"辛亥烈士赵声伯先之墓"碑，除石像外，基本恢复原貌。陵墓长330米，宽90米，坟包建在圆形台基上，前列石供桌，有凭吊场地、墓道和石牌坊，坊额篆刻"浩气长存"四字。

牌坊前有3座小石拱桥。

· · · · ·
English

In the Nanshan (South Mountain) scenic area, layered peaks are covered in green, with dense forests and tall bamboo, hailed by Northern Song calligrapher-painter Mi Fu as "urban mountain forest"; the main scenic spots are the three ancient temples of Helin, Zhulin, and Zhaoyin.

Both Helin Temple and Zhulin Temple were founded in the Eastern Jin, and Zhaoyin Temple was built in the Liu Song of the Southern Dynasties.

The Nanshan scenic area has repeatedly risen and fallen; it suffered war fires during the Taiping Rebellion and the War of Resistance against Japan, and was also damaged before and after the Cultural Revolution; today most halls were rebuilt after destruction.

1.

Zhaoyin Temple: Zhaoyin Temple is in Zhaoyin Mountain in the southern suburbs; legend says Dai Yong once lived in seclusion in the mountain, and later his daughter donated her residence as a temple, called Zhaoyin Temple.

In the Liu Song of the Southern Dynasties, the eminent monk Puci of Jinshan Temple served as abbot of this temple, and it was once named after his dharma name.

In the Liang of the Southern Dynasties, Xiao Tong studied here.In the 26th year of Wanli of the Ming (1598), to echo Helin Temple, it was renamed Luquan Temple.

Destroyed by war fires during the Xianfeng reign of the Qing, it was successively rebuilt during the Tongzhi and Guangxu periods, rebuilt at the current site in 1923, destroyed during the War of Resistance against Japan, occupied by Kuomintang troops before the founding of New China, and damaged again during the Cultural Revolution.

Currently most scenic spots were successively rebuilt after 1980, including Zhaoyin Archway, Tingli (Listening to Orioles) Mountain Room, Hupao (Tiger Running) Spring, Lupao (Deer Running) Spring, Yurui (Jade Stamen) Pavilion, Pearl Spring, and Niaowai (Beyond Birds) Pavilion etc.

2.Zhulin Temple: Zhulin Temple is at the northern foot of Jia Mountain.

First built in the Eastern Jin, originally named Jiashan Chan Courtyard; in the Tang it served as a sub-temple of Helin Temple, later fell into ruin.

Rebuilt during the Chongzhen reign of the Ming (around 1635), becoming an independent temple, renamed Zhulin (Bamboo Forest) Temple because surrounded by tall bamboo.

In the 38th year of Kangxi of the Qing (1699), during his southern tour, Emperor Kangxi stayed here and personally inscribed the temple plaque.

In the 11th year of Yongzheng of the Qing (1733), an imperial edict ordered its reconstruction, with a grand scale, marking its heyday.

Destroyed by war fires in the 6th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1856), rebuilt in the 8th year of Xianfeng (1858) then destroyed again, rebuilt in the 3rd year of Tongzhi (1864), but the scale was no longer as before.

During the War of Resistance against Japan, part was burned by Japanese troops, and during the Cultural Revolution it was completely destroyed.

Partially restored in 1981, the main scenic spots include Lingong Spring and Yijiang (Embracing the River) Pavilion etc.3.

Helin Temple: Helin Temple is at the northern foot of Moji Mountain in the southern suburbs, first built in the Eastern Jin, originally named Zhulin Temple.

Legend says Liu Yu, the founding emperor of the Liu Song of the Southern Dynasties, often worked and rested in the temple when young, with yellow cranes flying above it; after he ascended the throne, he renamed it Helin (Crane Forest) Temple.

Rebuilt during the Shaoxing reign of the Southern Song, moved to the south of the mountain during the Xianchun reign; destroyed again in the 10th year of Yongle of the Ming (1412), and monks slightly repaired the original Ancient Bamboo Courtyard as a temple, i.

e., today's site.

Rebuilt multiple times in the 8th year of Hongzhi of the Ming (1495), the 24th year of Wanli (1596), and the 4th year of Kangxi of the Qing (1665); destroyed by war fires during the Xianfeng reign of the Qing, severely damaged during the Cultural Revolution, with most scenes lost; today surviving are azaleas, Azalea Tower, and Mi Fu's Tomb etc.

4.Zhao Boxian Tomb: Zhao Boxian Tomb is in the Wenyuan scenic area east of Zhulin Temple.

Zhao Sheng (1881-1911), courtesy name Boxian, a native of Dagang, Zhenjiang, was one of the main leaders of the Tongmenghui (Chinese Revolutionary Alliance).

Buried in the southern suburbs of Zhenjiang in 1912, with the tombstone engraved "Tomb of the Great Martyr Zhao Boxian.

" Later, a stone stele pavilion with a portrait of Zhao Sheng in military uniform riding a horse was erected on the mound in front of the tomb path, forming a central axis with the grave mound and tomb path.

Before the War of Resistance against Japan, the tomb was once expanded, but stopped due to the outbreak of war.

The tomb was destroyed in 1966, and in 1981 the stele "Tomb of Zhao Sheng (Boxian), Martyr of the 1911 Revolution" was re-erected; except for the stone statues, it basically restored its original appearance.

The tomb is 330 meters long and 90 meters wide; the grave mound is built on a circular platform base, with a stone altar table in front, a mourning ground, tomb path, and stone archway; the archway plaque is engraved with the four characters "Noble Spirit Endures Forever.

" In front of the archway are 3 small stone arch bridges.

建筑要点 / Key Features

10 南朝陵墓石刻
Stone Sculptures at Mausoleums of Southern Dynasties
南朝
级别 Level
第三批全国重点文物保护单位（1988年）
地址 Address
丹阳市
类型 Type
陵墓石刻/古建筑
中文原文

丹阳在南朝时期称"南兰陵"，为齐、梁两代帝王的祖籍地，两代帝王多归葬于此，丹阳有帝陵11处，句容有1处（详见列表），墓前布置精美石刻。石刻中以陵口二石兽最雄伟，是一对麒麟和天禄。

东为天禄，双角，四足损缺，长4米，残高3.6米；西为麒麟，独角，四足残损，身长3.95米，残高2.9米。两只石兽精雕细刻，纹饰华丽，两翼造型巧丽，翼上鳞纹凸出翼面，是体型最大、最为秀美的一对石刻。

诸陵中保存石刻最多的是梁文帝萧顺的建陵，现存石兽、石柱础、石柱和石龟跌各一对。其他石刻还有齐宣帝萧承之永安陵、齐武帝萧赜景安陵各存石麒麟、天禄一对，均为东侧完整天禄，永安陵西侧麒麟失去头部，景安陵失去四足。齐景帝萧道生修安陵尚存麒麟、天禄一对。齐明帝萧鸾兴安陵有石麒麟、天禄一对，北为天禄，肢体残断，半身湮没于土中，仅存部分前躯；南为麒麟，四足全失。

金王陈南齐失名墓有麒麟、天禄一对。烂石弄南齐失名墓有石辟邪一对，一完整，一残缺。水经山南齐失名墓有石辟邪一对，这两个墓的主人可能为废帝。梁武帝萧衍修陵有一石麒麟，已残。梁简文帝萧纲庄陵有一麒麟。句容的梁南康简王萧绩墓存有一对石辟邪，西雌东雄，东西相向而立一对石柱，东石柱完好无损，西石柱上的小辟邪遭雷击破损。

丹阳、句容南朝陵墓石刻一览表（参考梁白泉《南京的六朝石刻》）：1. 齐宣帝萧承之永安陵石刻（447年），丹阳市东北胡桥镇狮子湾张庄村东北水田里，石麒麟、天禄各一；2. 齐武帝萧赜景安陵石刻（493年），丹阳市云阳镇田家村南400米处，石麒麟、天禄各一，石柱一；3. 齐景帝萧道生修安陵石刻（494年），丹阳市胡桥镇仙塘湾（又称鹤仙塘）以东约一公里，石麒麟、天禄各一；4. 齐明帝萧鸾兴安陵石刻（498年），丹阳市城东荆林镇三城巷东北，石麒麟、天禄各一；5. 金王陈南齐失名陵墓石刻（南朝齐），丹阳市后巷镇陈家村西南，石麒麟、天禄各一；6. 烂石弄南朝失名墓石刻（494年），丹阳市后巷镇烂石弄北，石辟邪二；7. 水经山村南朝失名墓石刻（494年），丹阳市埤城水经山村东南，石辟邪二；8. 齐梁陵口陵墓石刻（南朝），丹阳市陵口镇东，石麒麟、天禄各一；9. 梁文帝萧顺之建陵石刻（502年），丹阳市城东荆林镇三城巷东北，石麒麟、天禄各一，石柱二，石碑座二，石台基二；10. 梁武帝萧衍修陵石刻（549年），丹阳市城东荆林镇三城刘家庄，石天禄一；11. 梁简文帝萧纲庄陵石刻（551年），丹阳市城东荆林镇三城刘家庄，石天禄一；12. 梁南康简王萧绩墓石刻（566年），栖霞区栖霞镇新合村狮子冲，石辟邪二，石柱二。

· · · · ·
English

Danyang was called "Southern Lanling" during the Southern Dynasties, the ancestral home of the emperors of the Qi and Liang dynasties; emperors of both dynasties were mostly buried here, with 11 imperial tombs in Danyang and 1 in Jurong (see list for details), with exquisite stone carvings arranged in front of the tombs.

Among the stone carvings, the two stone beasts at Lingkou are the most majestic—a pair of qilin and tianlu.

The east one is a tianlu, with double horns, four feet damaged, 4 meters long, with a residual height of 3.6 meters; the west one is a qilin, with a single horn, four feet damaged, 3.

95 meters long, with a residual height of 2.9 meters.

The two stone beasts are exquisitely carved with ornate patterns, with cleverly shaped wings, and the scale patterns on the wings protrude from the wing surface—they are the largest and most graceful pair of stone carvings.

Among all the tombs, the one preserving the most stone carvings is the Jianling Tomb of Emperor Wen of Liang, Xiao Shunzhi, currently preserving one pair each of stone beasts, stone column bases, stone columns, and stone tortoise pedestals.

Other stone carvings include: the Yong'an Tomb of Emperor Xuan of Qi, Xiao Chengzhi, and the Jing'an Tomb of Emperor Wu of Qi, Xiao Ze, each preserving one pair of stone qilin and tianlu—both with the east tianlu intact; the west qilin of Yong'an Tomb lost its head, and Jing'an Tomb lost its four feet.

The Xiu'an Tomb of Emperor Jing of Qi, Xiao Daosheng, still preserves one pair of qilin and tianlu.

The Xing'an Tomb of Emperor Ming of Qi, Xiao Luan, has one pair of stone qilin and tianlu; the north one is a tianlu, with limbs broken and half body buried in soil, only part of the forebody remaining; the south one is a qilin, with all four feet lost.

The unnamed Jinwangchen Tomb of the Southern Qi has one pair of qilin and tianlu.The unnamed Lanshinong Tomb of the Southern Qi has one pair of stone bixie, one intact and one damaged.

The unnamed Shuijingshan Tomb of the Southern Qi has one pair of stone bixie; the owners of these two tombs may have been deposed emperors.

The Xiuling Tomb of Emperor Wu of Liang, Xiao Yan, has one stone qilin, already damaged.The Zhuangling Tomb of Emperor Jianwen of Liang, Xiao Gang, has one qilin.

The tomb of Xiao Ji, Prince Jian of Nankang of Liang, in Jurong preserves one pair of stone bixie, west female and east male, facing each other east-west; one pair of stone columns, with the east column intact and the small bixie on the west column damaged by lightning.

List of Southern Dynasties Tomb Stone Carvings in Danyang and Jurong (referencing Liang Baiquan's "Six Dynasties Stone Carvings of Nanjing"): 1.

Yong'an Tomb Stone Carvings of Emperor Xuan of Qi, Xiao Chengzhi (447), in the paddy field northeast of Zhangzhuang Village, Shiziwan, Huqiao Town, northeast of Danyang City—one each of stone qilin and tianlu; 2.

Jing'an Tomb Stone Carvings of Emperor Wu of Qi, Xiao Ze (493), 400 meters south of Tianjia Village, Yunyang Town, Danyang City—one each of stone qilin and tianlu, one stone column; 3.

Xiu'an Tomb Stone Carvings of Emperor Jing of Qi, Xiao Daosheng (494), about one kilometer east of Xiantang Bay (also called Hexian Pond), Huqiao Town, Danyang City—one each of stone qilin and tianlu; 4.

Xing'an Tomb Stone Carvings of Emperor Ming of Qi, Xiao Luan (498), northeast of Sancheng Lane, Jinglin Town, east of Danyang City—one each of stone qilin and tianlu; 5.

Unnamed Jinwangchen Tomb Stone Carvings of Southern Qi, southwest of Chenjia Village, Houxiang Town, Danyang City—one each of stone qilin and tianlu; 6.

Unnamed Lanshinong Tomb Stone Carvings of Southern Dynasties (494), north of Lanshinong, Houxiang Town, Danyang City—two stone bixie; 7.

Unnamed Shuijingshan Village Tomb Stone Carvings of Southern Dynasties (494), southeast of Shuijingshan Village, Picheng, Danyang City—two stone bixie; 8.

Lingkou Tomb Stone Carvings of Qi-Liang (Southern Dynasties), east of Lingkou Town, Danyang City—one each of stone qilin and tianlu; 9.

Jianling Tomb Stone Carvings of Emperor Wen of Liang, Xiao Shunzhi (502), northeast of Sancheng Lane, Jinglin Town, east of Danyang City—one each of stone qilin and tianlu, two stone columns, two stele bases, two stone platform bases; 10.

Xiuling Tomb Stone Carvings of Emperor Wu of Liang, Xiao Yan (549), Liujiazhuang, Sancheng, Jinglin Town, east of Danyang City—one stone tianlu; 11.

Zhuangling Tomb Stone Carvings of Emperor Jianwen of Liang, Xiao Gang (551), Liujiazhuang, Sancheng, Jinglin Town, east of Danyang City—one stone tianlu; 12.

Tomb Stone Carvings of Xiao Ji, Prince Jian of Nankang of Liang (566), Shizichong, Xinhe Village, Qixia Town, Qixia District—two stone bixie, two stone columns.
