清真寺/伊斯兰教建筑
中文原文

仙鹤寺是一座历史悠久的清真寺，南宋咸淳年间伊斯兰先贤普哈丁筑，明洪武二十三年（1390年）重建，与广州怀圣寺、泉州麒麟寺和杭州凤凰寺并称中国伊斯兰教四大名寺。

寺门朝东，建筑格局有似仙鹤亮翅，因而得名：门如鹤首，甬道为鹤颈，大殿为鹤身，两侧之半亭则如鹤翼，殿后植两株古柏象征鹤腿，最后以翠竹作为鹤尾。寺内有传为南宋年间所植的银杏。

· · · · ·
English

Crane Mosque is a mosque with a long history, built by the Islamic sage Puhaddin during the Xianchun reign of the Southern Song, and rebuilt in the 23rd year of Hongwu of the Ming (1390); together with the Huaisheng Mosque in Guangzhou, the Qilin Mosque in Quanzhou, and the Fenghuang Mosque in Hangzhou, it is called one of the four famous mosques of Chinese Islam.

The temple gate faces east, and the architectural layout resembles a crane spreading its wings, hence the name: the gate is like the crane's head, the corridor is the crane's neck, the main hall is the crane's body, the half-pavilions on both sides are like the crane's wings, two ancient cypresses planted behind the hall symbolize the crane's legs, and finally green bamboo serves as the crane's tail.

Inside the temple there is a ginkgo tree traditionally said to have been planted during the Southern Song.

建筑要点 / Key Features
仙鹤寺是一座历史悠久的清真寺南宋咸淳年间伊斯兰先贤普哈丁筑明洪武二十三年1390年重建与广州怀圣寺泉州麒麟寺和杭州凤凰寺并称中国伊斯兰教四大名寺寺门朝东建筑格局有似仙鹤亮翅因而得名门如鹤首甬道为鹤颈大殿为鹤身两侧之半亭则如鹤翼殿后植两株古柏象征鹤腿最后以翠竹作为鹤尾寺内有传为南宋年间所植的银杏
19 阮元家庙及宅第
Ruan Yuan's Family Temple and Residence
清
级别 Level
第五批省级文物保护单位（2002年）
地址 Address
毓贤街8号
类型 Type
家庙/官宦宅第
中文原文

阮元（1764—1849），字伯元，为清代名臣，曾任湖广、两广、云贵总督，体仁阁大学士，清道光十八年（1838年）致仕退休时，由于他是乾嘉道三朝元老、九省疆臣、文经武纬，加太子太保衔。

道光帝称赞他"极三朝之宠遇，为一代之完人"，清道光二十六年（1846年）阮元晋升太傅，位列三公。阮元在政事、经史、金石等方面都成就极高，他的名字曾引起嘉庆皇帝的兴趣，问古代可有类似的名字，他答曰"伊尹"，帝嘉其志（《冷庐杂识·卷一》）。

阮元家庙位于住宅西侧，清嘉庆八年（1803年）建，坐北朝南，有临街照壁、头门厅、二门厅、享堂和文选井等。庙前毓贤街原名太傅街，因阮元官至太傅而得名。在家庙东侧，毓贤街12号有扬州市保单位怡庐，正在修缮，庭院颇为精雅。

家庙南侧旌忠巷2号有市保单位旌忠寺，传为文选楼旧址。在公道桥清嘉庆五年（1800年）建有阮家祠堂，今已不存。

阮元及其家族墓地位于邗江区槐泗镇槐子村，始建于明天启年间，前后共安葬阮氏五代及附葬者20余人，是清代一处重要墓葬群。墓群北面1里左右为阮元误定的隋炀帝陵。

· · · · ·
English

Ruan Yuan (1764-1849), courtesy name Boyuan, was a famous official of the Qing Dynasty, having served as Governor-General of Huguang, Liangguang, and Yun-Gui, and Grand Secretary of the Tiren Cabinet; when he retired in the 18th year of Daoguang of the Qing (1838), because he was a senior official of three reigns (Qianlong, Jiaqing, Daoguang), governor of nine provinces, and both literary and military, he was given the title of Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

Emperor Daoguang praised him as "enjoying the utmost favor of three reigns, a complete man of his generation"; in the 26th year of Daoguang (1846), Ruan Yuan was promoted to Grand Tutor, ranking among the Three Dukes.

Ruan Yuan achieved extremely high accomplishments in government affairs, classics and history, and epigraphy etc.

; his name once aroused the interest of Emperor Jiaqing, who asked if there were similar names in ancient times; he answered "Yi Yin," and the emperor praised his ambition ("Lenglu Zashi" Volume 1).

Ruan Yuan's Family Temple is located west of the residence, built in the 8th year of Jiaqing of the Qing (1803), facing south with its back to north, with a street-facing screen wall, first gate hall, second gate hall, worship hall, and Wenxuan Well etc.

Yuxian Street in front of the temple was originally named Taifu (Grand Tutor) Street, named because Ruan Yuan rose to the rank of Grand Tutor.East of the family temple, at No.

12 Yuxian Street, is the Yangzhou municipal protected unit Yilu, currently under renovation, with a quite elegant courtyard.South of the family temple, at No.

2 Jingzhong Lane, is the municipal protected unit Jingzhong Temple, traditionally said to be the former site of the Wenxuan (Literary Selection) Tower.

At Gongdao Bridge, in the 5th year of Jiaqing of the Qing (1800), the Ruan Family Ancestral Hall was built, today no longer existing.

Ruan Yuan and his family's cemetery is located in Huaizi Village, Huaisi Town, Hanjiang District, first built during the Tianqi reign of the Ming, burying five generations of the Ruan family and over 20 accompanying burials in total—an important Qing Dynasty burial group.

About 1 li north of the burial group is the Tomb of Emperor Yang of Sui, mistakenly identified by Ruan Yuan.

建筑要点 / Key Features
阮元17641849字伯元为清代名臣曾任湖广两广云贵总督体仁阁大学士清道光十八年1838年致仕退休时由于他是乾嘉道三朝元老九省疆臣文经武纬加太子太保衔道光帝称赞他极三朝之宠遇为一代之完人清道光二十六年1846年阮元晋升太傅位列三公阮元在政事经史金石等方面都成就极高他的名字曾引起嘉庆皇帝的兴趣问古代可有类似的名字他答曰伊尹帝嘉其志冷庐杂识卷一阮元家庙位于住宅西侧清嘉庆八年1803年建坐北朝南有临街照壁头门厅二门厅享堂和文选井等庙前毓贤街原名太傅街因阮元官至太傅而得名在家庙东侧毓贤街12号有扬州市保单位怡庐正在修缮庭院颇为精雅家庙南侧旌忠巷2号有市保单位旌忠寺传为文选楼旧址在公道桥清嘉庆五年1800年建有阮家祠堂今已不存阮元及其家族墓地位于邗江区槐泗镇槐子村始建于明天启年间前后共安葬阮氏五代及附葬者20余人是清代一处重要墓葬群墓群北面1里左右为阮元误定的隋炀帝陵
20 文昌阁—舍利塔—四望亭
Wenchang Pavilion, Sarira Pagoda, Siwang Pavilion
唐—明
级别 Level
省保单位（2011年）
地址 Address
汶河路、文昌路、石塔路、四望亭路
类型 Type
楼阁/塔/古建筑
中文原文

1. 文昌阁：位于汶河路、文昌路交叉处，始建于明万历十三年（1585年），万历二十四年（1596年）重建，清代重修，阁为八角三层，形似天坛祈年殿，2011年列为省保单位。

2. 舍利塔：木兰院舍利塔位于石塔路，为市保建筑，始建于唐开成三年（838年），原在扬州西门外古木兰院内，南宋移建于今址，清乾隆年间重修，增建石栏。这是一座仿木楼阁式青石塔，六角五层，较为精美。3. 四望亭：四望亭位于四望亭路东首，汶河路西侧，为市保建筑。

据明万历《江都县志》引宋《宝佑志》记载"四望亭在州治南，宁宗嘉定年间特授直宝谟阁、权发遣扬州事、主管淮东安抚司事崔与之建"，认为此亭为南宋崔与之所建。

但清乾隆《江都县志》则认为此亭始建于明嘉靖三十八年（1559年），也称文奎楼、魁星阁，是江都县学的一部分。四望亭为砖木结构，八角三层攒尖顶。底层四面开门与街道相通，又称"过街亭"。二、三层可供登临，欣赏市区景色。

· · · · ·
English

1.

Wenchang Pavilion: Located at the intersection of Wenhe Road and Wenchang Road, first built in the 13th year of Wanli of the Ming (1585), rebuilt in the 24th year of Wanli (1596), and repaired in the Qing; the pavilion is octagonal with three stories, resembling the Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests at the Temple of Heaven, designated a provincial protected unit in 2011.

2.

Sarira Pagoda: The Mulan Courtyard Sarira Pagoda is located on Shita Road, a municipal protected building, first built in the 3rd year of Kaicheng of the Tang (838), originally in the ancient Mulan Courtyard outside the west gate of Yangzhou, moved to today's site in the Southern Song, repaired during the Qianlong reign of the Qing with a stone railing added.

This is an imitation-wood pavilion-style bluestone pagoda, hexagonal with five stories, quite exquisite.3.

Siwang (Four-View) Pavilion: Siwang Pavilion is located at the east end of Siwangting Road, west of Wenhe Road, a municipal protected building.

According to the Ming Wanli "Jiangdu County Gazetteer" quoting the Song "Baoyou Records," "Siwang Pavilion is south of the prefectural government; during the Jiading reign of Emperor Ningzong, it was built by Cui Yuzhi, who was specially appointed as Direct Baomo Ge, Acting Prefect of Yangzhou, and Director of the Huaidong Pacification Commission," believing this pavilion was built by Cui Yuzhi of the Southern Song.

But the Qing Qianlong "Jiangdu County Gazetteer" believes this pavilion was first built in the 38th year of Jiajing of the Ming (1559), also called Wenkui Tower or Kuixing Pavilion, part of the Jiangdu County School.

Siwang Pavilion is a brick-wood structure, octagonal with a three-story pyramidal roof.

The ground floor has doors on all four sides connecting with the streets, also called the "Street-Crossing Pavilion." The second and third floors can be climbed to admire the city scenery.

建筑要点 / Key Features
文昌阁位于汶河路文昌路交叉处始建于明万历十三年1585年万历二十四年1596年重建清代重修阁为八角三层形似天坛祈年殿2011年列为省保单位舍利塔木兰院舍利塔位于石塔路为市保建筑始建于唐开成三年838年原在扬州西门外古木兰院内南宋移建于今址清乾隆年间重修增建石栏这是一座仿木楼阁式青石塔六角五层较为精美四望亭四望亭位于四望亭路东首汶河路西侧为市保建筑据明万历江都县志引宋宝佑志记载四望亭在州治南宁宗嘉定年间特授直宝谟阁权发遣扬州事主管淮东安抚司事崔与之建认为此亭为南宋崔与之所建但清乾隆江都县志则认为此亭始建于明嘉靖三十八年1559年也称文奎楼魁星阁是江都县学的一部分四望亭为砖木结构八角三层攒尖顶底层四面开门与街道相通又称过街亭二三层可供登临欣赏市区景色
21 西方寺大殿（扬州八怪纪念馆）
Main Hall of Xifang Temple (Shrine of Yangzhou Eight Eccentrics)
唐—明
级别 Level
第三批省级文物保护单位（1982年）
地址 Address
驼岭巷18号
类型 Type
佛教寺院/大殿
门票 Ticket
淡季15元，旺季25元
开放时间 Hours
8:00 — 17:00
中文原文

西方寺为扬州八大名刹之一，始建于唐永贞元年（805年），明洪武五年（1372年）重建，清咸丰三年（1853年）除大殿外皆毁于火。

这座大殿采用重檐歇山顶，楠木梁柱保存完好，局部有明代彩绘。平面接近方形，宽五间，深五进。外圈柱距很小，有似于周围廊，但墙壁、隔扇皆设在四周檐柱上，使立面梢间显得很窄，反映了江南殿堂建筑的典型特征。

清乾隆年间，扬州八怪之一的金农曾在寺内度过晚年，今辟为扬州八怪纪念馆。

· · · · ·
English

Xifang (Western) Temple is one of the eight famous temples of Yangzhou, first built in the 1st year of Yongzhen of the Tang (805), rebuilt in the 5th year of Hongwu of the Ming (1372); in the 3rd year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1853), everything except the main hall was destroyed by fire.

This main hall adopts a double-eave hip-and-gable roof, with nanmu beams and columns well preserved, and local Ming Dynasty painted decorations.

The plan is nearly square, five bays wide and five bays deep.

The outer column spacing is very small, resembling a surrounding corridor, but the walls and lattice doors are all set on the surrounding eave columns, making the end bays of the facade appear very narrow—reflecting the typical characteristics of Jiangnan hall architecture.

During the Qianlong reign of the Qing, Jin Nong, one of the Eight Eccentrics of Yangzhou, spent his later years in the temple; today it has been opened as the Memorial Hall of the Eight Eccentrics of Yangzhou.

建筑要点 / Key Features
西方寺为扬州八大名刹之一始建于唐永贞元年805年明洪武五年1372年重建清咸丰三年1853年除大殿外皆毁于火这座大殿采用重檐歇山顶楠木梁柱保存完好局部有明代彩绘平面接近方形宽五间深五进外圈柱距很小有似于周围廊但墙壁隔扇皆设在四周檐柱上使立面梢间显得很窄反映了江南殿堂建筑的典型特征清乾隆年间扬州八怪之一的金农曾在寺内度过晚今年今辟为扬州八怪纪念馆
22 罗聘故居（朱草诗林）
Former Residence of Luo Pin (Alkanet and Poetic Realm)
清
级别 Level
第七批省级文物保护单位（2011年）
地址 Address
广陵区弥陀巷46号
类型 Type
名人故居
门票 Ticket
10元
开放时间 Hours
8:20 — 11:30, 14:00 — 17:30（周一闭馆）
中文原文

罗聘（1733—1799）是"扬州八怪"之一，年纪最小，有"八怪殿军"之称，擅画人物佛像与山水花卉，最出色的是《鬼趣图》。这处故居建于清乾隆年间，罗聘自题"朱草诗林"，与夫人方婉仪（1732—1779）在此吟诗作画，被誉为"画坛伉俪"。当时金农、郑燮、高翔、汪士慎等都住在附近，常到此雅集论画。

如今故居中的书斋"香叶草堂"和半亭"倦鸟巢"保存良好，已辟为罗聘纪念馆，展览罗聘的生平和作品。

· · · · ·
English

Luo Pin (1733-1799) was one of the "Eight Eccentrics of Yangzhou," the youngest, known as the "rear guard of the Eight Eccentrics"; he excelled in painting figures, Buddhist images, landscapes, flowers, and plants, with his most outstanding work being the "Ghost Amusement Paintings.

" This former residence was built during the Qianlong reign of the Qing; Luo Pin himself inscribed it "Zhucao Shilin" (Alkanet and Poetic Realm), and with his wife Fang Wanyi (1732-1779) he composed poetry and painted here, hailed as a "couple in the art world.

" At that time, Jin Nong, Zheng Xie, Gao Xiang, Wang Shishen etc.all lived nearby and often came here for elegant gatherings to discuss painting.

Today the study "Xiangye Thatched Hall" and the half-pavilion "Juanniao Chao" (Tired Bird's Nest) in the former residence are well preserved, and it has been opened as the Luo Pin Memorial Hall, exhibiting Luo Pin's life and works.

建筑要点 / Key Features
罗聘17331799是扬州八怪之一年纪最小有八怪殿军之称擅画人物佛像与山水花卉最出色的是鬼趣图这处故居建于清乾隆年间罗聘自题朱草诗林与夫人方婉仪17321779在此吟诗作画被誉为画坛伉俪当时金农郑燮高翔汪士慎等都住在附近常到此雅集论画如今故居中的书斋香叶草堂和半亭倦鸟巢保存良好已辟为罗聘纪念馆展览罗聘的生平和作品
23 史可法墓祠
Tomb and Shrine of Shi Kefa
清
级别 Level
第七批省级文物保护单位（2011年）
地址 Address
维扬区广储门外梅花岭西麓
类型 Type
名人墓祠/园林
门票 Ticket
20元
开放时间 Hours
8:30 — 17:30
中文原文

明万历二十年（1592年）扬州守令吴秀以浚河之土堆筑成山，环山种梅，民间呼为梅花岭。岭周围布置楼台池沼，总名偕乐园，是当时一处游览胜地，"每佳晨韶景，士女游观者轮蹄摩击无虚日"。后来官府压制冶游之风，改作崇雅书院（万历《扬州府志》卷21）。

史可法（1602—1645）字宪之，明末任南京兵部尚书，北京沦陷后以兵部尚书兼东阁大学士督师扬州。清顺治二年（1645年）清军包围扬州，战前史可法嘱托嗣子史德威："我死，当葬梅花岭上。"扬州城破后，史可法被执拒降，不屈而死。

史德威遍寻遗骸不可得，只好将其衣冠葬在岭上。此地遂成为后人缅怀史公之地，如清代全祖望《梅花岭记》所言："圣贤家法，其气浩然，长留天地之间。……百年而后，予登岭上，与客述忠烈遗言，无不泪下如雨，想见当日围城光景，此即忠烈之面目，宛然可遇。"当年在刚攻克扬州后，清军将领多铎就在城内建祠纪念史可法。

清雍正十二年（1734年）个园主人马曰琯在岭东捐建"梅花书院"，增建祠宇亭榭。乾隆皇帝将史可法作为忠君忠国的榜样，谥为"忠正"，并在墓西建祠。李斗《扬州画舫录》卷四描述了乾隆年间此地的景致："古梅花岭旧址无考，今因重宁寺旁土阜增而成岭。

皆土山间石，石骨暴露，任石之怪，不加斧凿，锋棱如削，飘然有云姿鹤态。栽梅花数百株，皆玉蝶种，花比十亩梅园迟开一月，极高处有山亭，六角，花时便不见亭。"太平天国时期墓祠毁于战火，清同治九年（1870年）重建，"文革"时期墓冢被夷平，后来复原。今包括墓、祠、园三部分。东部为墓，南侧大门临河，门额书"史公墓"三字。

入门庭院两侧为碑廊，北部正中是飨堂，门外悬张尔荩撰写的名联"数点梅花亡国泪，二分明月故臣心"，堂内置1985年塑的史可法坐像，两边的"生有自来文信国，死而后已武乡侯"楹联，将史可法与文天祥、诸葛亮并称。堂东偏院有百年金桂，桂前建桂花厅，厅南是一处小园，黄石花坛内植紫藤、木香、芍药、丛桂等，绿荫满庭，并建有芍药亭和牡丹阁。

飨堂北为史可法衣冠墓，墓前立牌坊，与三面围墙形成墓地，牌坊北部正中立青石墓碑，上镌"明督师兵部尚书兼东阁大学士史可法之墓"。墓后两边院墙各开一道月洞门，额题"梅花岭"，即为门后的土岭。岭上遍植梅花，象征史可法的铮铮风骨。

岭东为二层歇山顶的梅花仙馆，可循石级登上二层，欣赏腊梅、湖石；岭西北是单檐歇山顶的晴雪轩，轩内墙壁上嵌史可法的"复睿亲王多尔衮书"、遗书、肖像及墨迹石刻等，又称"遗墨厅"。梅花岭东西横亘，中部叠筑假山，下有石洞可供穿行，岭南开凿水池，构成一处宜人的花园。

由花园西侧向南是史公祠，南为祠门，北为祠堂，内悬史可法遗像，向东与响堂相通。史可法与岳飞、文天祥齐名，这处墓祠集建筑、园林于一体，是开展爱国主义和民族气节教育的重要场所。

· · · · ·
English

In the 20th year of Wanli of the Ming (1592), Wu Xiu, Magistrate of Yangzhou, piled the soil from dredging the river into a mountain, planting plum trees around it, commonly called Meihua (Plum Blossom) Ridge.

Around the ridge, towers, terraces, ponds, and marshes were arranged, collectively named Xiele (Joy Together) Garden, a tourist attraction at that time: "Every fine morning and beautiful scene, scholars and women tourists came with wheels and hooves rubbing against each other, without an empty day.

" Later, the authorities suppressed the atmosphere of pleasure-seeking and changed it into the Chongya Academy (Wanli "Yangzhou Prefecture Gazetteer" Volume 21).

Shi Kefa (1602-1645), courtesy name Xianzhi, served as Minister of War of Nanjing in the late Ming; after the fall of Beijing, he supervised the army in Yangzhou as Minister of War and Grand Secretary of the Dongge Cabinet.

In the 2nd year of Shunzhi of the Qing (1645), Qing troops surrounded Yangzhou; before the battle, Shi Kefa instructed his adopted son Shi Dewei: "When I die, bury me on Plum Blossom Ridge.

" After Yangzhou fell, Shi Kefa was captured, refused to surrender, and died unyielding.

Shi Dewei searched everywhere for his remains but could not find them, so he had to bury his official hat and robes on the ridge.

This place thus became a site for later generations to remember Lord Shi, as stated in Qing person Quan Zuwang's "Record of Plum Blossom Ridge": "The sage's family code, his qi is浩然 and remains between heaven and earth for a long time.

..

A hundred years later, I climbed the ridge and, with guests, recounted the loyal martyr's last words; none did not weep like rain, imagining the scene of the city under siege that day—this is the loyal martyr's face, as if vividly encountered.

" That year, just after capturing Yangzhou, the Qing general Dodo built a shrine in the city to commemorate Shi Kefa.

In the 12th year of Yongzheng of the Qing (1734), Ma Yueguan, owner of Geyuan Garden, donated to build the "Plum Blossom Academy" east of the ridge, adding shrine buildings and pavilions.

Emperor Qianlong took Shi Kefa as a model of loyalty to the monarch and country, posthumously titling him "Zhongzheng" (Loyal and Upright), and built a shrine west of the tomb.

Li Dou's "Yangzhou Huafang Lu" Volume 4 describes the scenery here during the Qianlong reign: "The old site of Plum Blossom Ridge is untraceable; today it was increased into a ridge because of the earth mound beside Chongning Temple.

It is all earth mountain with interspersed stones, with stone bones exposed; letting the stones be strange, without chiseling, the edges and corners are as if cut, floating with cloud posture and crane demeanor.

Several hundred plum trees are planted, all of the Yudie (Jade Butterfly) variety; their flowers bloom a month later than the ten-mu plum garden; at the highest point there is a hexagonal mountain pavilion, and when flowers bloom the pavilion cannot be seen.

" During the Taiping Rebellion the tomb and shrine were destroyed by war fires, rebuilt in the 9th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1870); during the Cultural Revolution the tomb was leveled, later restored.

Today it includes three parts: tomb, shrine, and garden.The eastern part is the tomb; the south gate faces the river, with the gate lintel inscribed with the three characters "Shi Gong's Tomb.

" Entering the gate, both sides of the courtyard are stele corridors; in the center north is the Xiangtang (Banquet Hall), with the famous couplet written by Zhang Erjin hanging outside: "A few dots of plum blossoms—tears of a fallen nation; two parts of bright moonlight—the heart of a loyal former minister"; inside the hall is a seated statue of Shi Kefa sculpted in 1985, and on both sides the couplet "Born like Wen Tianxiang, died like Zhuge Liang" compares Shi Kefa with Wen Tianxiang and Zhuge Liang.

East of the hall, in a side courtyard, is a century-old golden osmanthus; in front of the osmanthus is the Osmanthus Hall; south of the hall is a small garden, with yellow-stone flower terraces planted with wisteria, rosewood, peonies, and clustered osmanthus etc.

, with green shade filling the courtyard, and a Peony Pavilion and Peony Pavilion built.

North of the Xiangtang is Shi Kefa's cenotaph (hat-and-robe tomb); in front of the tomb stands an archway, forming a burial ground with three-sided walls; in the center north of the archway stands a bluestone tombstone, engraved with "Tomb of Shi Kefa, Ming Supervisor of Army, Minister of War, and Grand Secretary of the Dongge Cabinet.

" Behind the tomb, each side of the courtyard wall opens a moon gate, inscribed "Plum Blossom Ridge," which is the earth mound behind the gate.

Plum trees are planted all over the ridge, symbolizing Shi Kefa's unyielding integrity.

East of the ridge is the two-story hip-and-gable roof Plum Blossom Immortal Hall, where one can climb stone steps to the second floor to admire wintersweet and Taihu stones; northwest of the ridge is the single-eave hip-and-gable roof Qingxue (Clear Snow) Studio, whose inner walls are embedded with Shi Kefa's "Letter in Reply to Prince Regent Dorgon," last letters, portraits, and calligraphy stone carvings etc.

, also called the "Posthumous Ink Hall.

" Plum Blossom Ridge stretches east-west, with a rockery stacked in the middle, and a stone cave below for passage; south of the ridge a pond is dug, forming a pleasant garden.

From the west side of the garden southward is the Shi Gong Shrine, with the shrine gate to the south and the shrine hall to the north, hanging a portrait of Shi Kefa, connected eastward to the Xiangtang.

Shi Kefa is as famous as Yue Fei and Wen Tianxiang; this tomb and shrine integrates architecture and garden, an important place for patriotism and national integrity education.

建筑要点 / Key Features
明万历二十年1592年扬州守令吴秀以浚河之土堆筑成山环山种梅民间呼为梅花岭岭周围布置楼台池沼总名偕乐园是当时一处游览胜地每佳晨韶景士女游观者轮蹄摩击无虚日后来官府压制冶游之风改作崇雅书院万历扬州府志卷21史可法16021645字宪之明末任南京兵部尚书北京沦陷后以兵部尚书兼东阁大学士督师扬州清顺治二年1645年清军包围扬州战前史可法嘱托嗣子史德威我死当葬梅花岭上扬州城破后史可法被执拒降不屈而死史德威遍寻遗骸不可得只好将其衣冠葬在岭上此地遂成为后人缅怀史公之地如清代全祖望梅花岭记所言圣贤家法其气浩然长留天地之间……百年而后予登岭上与客述忠烈遗言无不泪下如雨想见当日围城光景此即忠烈之面目宛然可遇当年在刚攻克扬州后清军将领多铎就在城内建祠纪念史可法清雍正十二年1734年个园主人马曰琯在岭东捐建梅花书院增建祠宇亭榭乾隆皇帝将史可法作为忠君忠国的榜样谥为忠正并在墓西建祠李斗扬州画舫录卷四描述了乾隆年间此地的景致古梅花岭旧址无考今因重宁寺旁土阜增而成岭皆土山间石石骨暴露任石之怪不加斧凿锋棱如削飘然有云姿鹤态栽梅花数百株皆玉蝶种花比十亩梅园迟开一月极高处有山亭六角花时便不见亭太平天国时期墓祠毁于战火清
24 扬州重宁寺
Chongning Temple of Yangzhou
清
级别 Level

地址 Address
长征西路15号

中文原文

清乾隆四十八年（1783年），扬州盐商为庆祝乾隆帝寿辰，集资筹建重宁寺，次年乾隆第六次南巡即驻跸于此，赐《万寿重宁寺碑记》，称"合万姓之寿以为寿，所以万寿也；以下民之宁以为宁，所以为重宁也"。八怪中的罗聘曾绘制寺内壁画。清咸丰年间寺庙毁于兵火，晚清重建。

寺内大雄宝殿建于清光绪十七年（1891年），五开间，重檐歇山顶，内有八根名贵的铁梨木方柱，皆高15米以上，殿内天花、藻井上有精美彩绘。

今为某单位办公场所，不开放。

· · · · ·
English

In the 48th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1783), Yangzhou salt merchants, to celebrate Emperor Qianlong's birthday, raised funds to build Chongning Temple; the following year, on his sixth southern tour, Qianlong stayed here, bestowing the "Stele Record of Wanshou Chongning Temple," stating: "Combining the longevity of all surnames as longevity, hence ten thousand longevity; combining the peace of the lower people as peace, hence heavy peace.

" Luo Pin, one of the Eight Eccentrics, once painted murals inside the temple.

During the Xianfeng reign of the Qing, the temple was destroyed by war fires and rebuilt in the late Qing.

The Mahavira Hall in the temple was built in the 17th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1891), five bays wide with a double-eave hip-and-gable roof; inside are eight precious iron pear wood square columns, all over 15 meters high, with exquisite painted decorations on the ceiling and coffered ceiling.

Today it is the office of a certain unit and not open to the public.

建筑要点 / Key Features
清乾隆四十八年1783年扬州盐商为庆祝乾隆帝寿辰集资筹建重宁寺次年乾隆第六次南巡即驻跸于此赐万寿重宁寺碑记称合万姓之寿以为寿所以万寿也以下民之宁以为宁所以为重宁也八怪中的罗聘曾绘制寺内壁画清咸丰年间寺庙毁于兵火晚清重建寺内大雄宝殿建于清光绪十七年1891年五开间重檐歇山顶内有八根名贵的铁梨木方柱皆高15米以上殿内天花藻井上有精美彩绘今为某单位办公场所不开放

Tianning Temple

中文原文

天宁寺为扬州八大古刹之首。据传东晋太元十年（385年）谢安镇守广陵曾在此居住，后来舍宅为寺。东晋义熙十四年（418年）尼泊尔高僧在此译《华严经》。北宋政和二年（1112年），宋徽宗赐名"天宁禅寺"。

康熙六次南巡皆驻跸天宁寺，并命曹寅在寺内设书局，刊刻《全唐诗》。乾隆在寺西建御码头（乾隆游瘦西湖登船处）、行宫和御花园，以及储藏《四库全书》《古今图书集成》的文汇阁。

众多建筑和图书皆毁于太平天国战火，今寺重建于清同治四年（1865年），有山门、天王殿、大雄宝殿、华严阁和藏经楼（万佛楼）等，现为扬州博物馆。

· · · · ·
English

Tianning Temple is the first of the eight ancient temples of Yangzhou.

Legend says that in the 10th year of Taiyuan of the Eastern Jin (385), Xie An, when guarding Guangling, once lived here and later donated his residence as a temple.

In the 14th year of Yixi of the Eastern Jin (418), a Nepalese eminent monk translated the "Avatamsaka Sutra" here.

In the 2nd year of Zhenghe of the Northern Song (1112), Emperor Huizong bestowed the name "Tianning Chan Temple.

" On all six of his southern tours, Kangxi stayed at Tianning Temple and ordered Cao Yin to set up a book bureau in the temple to print the "Complete Tang Poems.

" Qianlong built an imperial dock (where Qianlong boarded a boat to tour Slender West Lake), an imperial palace, and an imperial garden west of the temple, as well as the Wenhui Pavilion storing the "Complete Library in Four Sections" and the "Gujin Tushu Jicheng" (Complete Collection of Ancient and Modern Books).

Many buildings and books were destroyed in the Taiping Rebellion wars; today's temple was rebuilt in the 4th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1865), with a mountain gate, Heavenly King Hall, Mahavira Hall, Huayan Pavilion, and Scripture Library (Ten-Thousand-Buddha Tower) etc.

, now the Yangzhou Museum.

建筑要点 / Key Features
天宁寺为扬州八大古刹之首据传东晋太元十年385年谢安镇守广陵曾在此居住后来舍宅为寺东晋义熙十四年418年尼泊尔高僧在此译华严经北宋政和二年1112年宋徽宗赐名天宁禅寺康熙六次南巡皆驻跸天宁寺并命曹寅在寺内设书局刊刻全唐诗乾隆在寺西建御码头乾隆游瘦西湖登船处行宫和御花园以及储藏四库全书古今图书集成的文汇阁众多建筑和图书皆毁于太平天国战火今寺重建于清同治四年1865年有山门天王殿大雄宝殿华严阁和藏经楼万佛楼等现为扬州博物馆
26 瘦西湖
Slender West Lake
清
级别 Level
国家重点风景名胜区
地址 Address
扬州市西北郊
类型 Type
风景名胜/园林
中文原文

瘦西湖原名保障河，扬州西北郊的山洪雨水经此汇入大运河，很早就成为郊游胜地。到清代乾隆年间，盐商趁皇帝南巡之际极力兴造，最称繁盛。扬州人通常乘舟从城北门出，欣赏沿途风光。清代文人沈复（1763—1825？）在《浮生六记》中点评道："行其途有八九里，虽全是人功，而奇思幻想，点缀天然，即阆苑瑶池，琼楼玉宇，谅不过此！

其妙处在十余家之园亭合而为一，联络至山，气势俱贯。"金安清（1817—1880？）《水窗春呓》也称"两岸数十里楼台相接，无一处重复"，并认为最佳处"在虹桥迤西一转，小金山矗其南，五亭桥镇其中，而白塔一区，雄伟古朴。往往夕阳返照，萧鼓灯船，如入汉宫图画"。瘦西湖、小秦淮、小金山，这些名字贴切形容出扬州风景的灵秀之美。

今瘦西湖风景区东起天宁寺前御码头，经冶春园、卷石洞天、西园曲水为第一段，水道较窄；折向北由虹桥揽胜经长堤春柳、荷浦薰风、桃花坞—冶春后社—徐园和四桥烟雨（长春桥、春波桥、莲花桥和玉版桥）为第二段，水面渐宽；由四桥烟雨折向西，先后经过小金山、钓鱼台、凫庄、五亭桥和莲性寺白塔，直抵西端熙春台为第三段，景致最为集中；水系由此再度向北，经二十四桥、石壁流淙、蜀冈朝旭和小吹台为第四段，较为疏野，有天然风味。

其中梅岭春深、莲花桥和熙春台为三大景观节点，以中段的吹台、白塔、凫庄和莲花桥最为精彩。莲花桥和白塔：莲性寺建于元代，当时叫法海寺，市民出城游玩常先在此泊舟拜佛。寺址四周环水，形如莲花，更奇的是寺北高起一座土丘，风水家称山脉来自北边蜀冈，迤逦穿水而过与寺址相接，宛如莲花的枝茎。这条莲茎最初是座河堤，称莲花堤，人们相信其为寺庙命脉所系。

晚明之际一名杨姓宦官筑保扬城，废堤为桥，并阻断了寺西河水，导致"堤断脉伤，而寺之殿宇，日渐圮废"。入清后人们挖开河障，改桥为堤，并培高被视作寺脉的土丘，次第兴建楼殿，使寺庙粲然复兴，乡人感慨"地脉效灵，形象之言不爽也"。1705年康熙南巡，正式赐名"莲性寺"。

白塔位于寺北，建于清乾隆年间，模仿北京北海的白塔。下为方形台座，有梯可登；中为喇嘛式白色塔身，南面设龛室；顶上是由十三重相轮、伞盖和宝珠组成的塔刹。

徐珂《清稗类钞》讲述了建造白塔的戏剧性过程：据说乾隆南巡时游玩至此，对左右随从说，此地景致颇似西苑的"琼岛春阴"，可惜缺座白塔。当时负责接驾的盐商江春听闻此言，"亟以千金贿近侍"，请他们画出北海白塔的状貌，然后依图修建，一夜就建成了。第二天乾隆又来游玩，"见塔巍然，大异之，以为伪。既至，果砖石所成。询知其故，叹曰：'盐商之财力伟哉！

'"这个故事有夸张之处，但却恰当地表现了扬州盐商的富足，令皇帝都感到惊佩。莲花桥位于原莲花堤的位置，1757年为迎接乾隆南巡，方便御舟行驶，两淮盐政高恒改堤为桥。为了延续莲脉又不阻断水上行舟，采用了罕见的十五孔桥形式，桥身和四翼下部各有3个桥洞，总共15个。

《扬州揽胜录》描述了满月之夜的奇观："三五之夕，皓月当空，每洞各衔一月，计十五洞，共得十五月，金色漾藻，众月争辉，倒悬波心，不可捉摸。西湖之三潭印月，不能专美于前。"此景特令扬州人自豪，认为足可媲美西湖的三潭映月。高恒还请名匠在桥上建了五座亭子，因此又称五亭桥。今桥为光绪年间重建。

· · · · ·
English

Slender West Lake was originally called Baozhang River; the mountain flood and rainwater from the northwest suburb of Yangzhou flows through it into the Grand Canal, and it early became an outing scenic spot.

By the Qianlong reign of the Qing, salt merchants took advantage of the emperor's southern tours to vigorously build it, reaching its greatest prosperity.

Yangzhou people usually took boats from the north gate of the city to admire the scenery along the way.Qing scholar Shen Fu (1763-1825?

) commented in "Six Records of a Floating Life": "Traveling its path for eight or nine li, although entirely man-made, with wondrous thoughts and fantasies, embellished naturally—even the fairyland of Langyuan and Jade Pool, or the jade towers and jade pavilions, could hardly surpass this!

Its beauty lies in the gardens and pavilions of over ten families merging into one, connecting to the mountain, with momentum all penetrating." Jin Anqing (1817-1880?

) in "Shuichun Chuiyi" also said "for tens of li on both banks, towers and terraces connect, with no place repeated," and believed the best place is "at a turn west of Hongqiao, with Xiaojinshan standing tall to its south, Wuting Bridge in its middle, and the White Pagoda area, majestic and simple.

Often at sunset with reflected light, with flute and drum lantern boats, it is like entering a Han palace painting.

" Slender West Lake, Xiaoqinhuai (Small Qinhuai), Xiaojinshan (Small Gold Mountain)—these names aptly describe the graceful beauty of Yangzhou's scenery.

Today's Slender West Lake scenic area starts east at the imperial dock in front of Tianning Temple, passing through Yechun Garden, Juanshi Dongtian (Rolling Stone Cave Heaven), and Xiyuan Qushui (West Garden Winding Water) as the first section, with a relatively narrow waterway; turning north, from Hongqiao Lansheng (Hongqiao Embracing Scenery) through Changdi Chunliu (Long Embankment Spring Willows), Hepu Xunfeng (Lotus Pond Fragrant Wind), Taohuawu—Yechun Houshe—Xuyuan, and Siqiao Yanyu (Four Bridges Misty Rain) (Changchun Bridge, Chunbo Bridge, Lianhua Bridge, and Yuban Bridge) as the second section, with the water surface gradually widening; turning west from Siqiao Yanyu, successively passing Xiaojinshan, Diaoyutai (Fishing Terrace), Fuzhuang, Wuting Bridge, and the White Pagoda of Lianxing Temple, straight to Xichun Terrace at the west end as the third section, with the most concentrated scenery; from there the water system again goes north, through Ershisi Bridge (Twenty-Four Bridge), Shibi Liucong (Stone Wall Flowing Water), Shugang Zhaoxu (Shugang Morning Sun), and Xiaochuitai as the fourth section, relatively sparse and wild with natural flavor.

Among them, Meiling Chunshen (Plum Ridge Deep Spring), Lianhua Bridge, and Xichun Terrace are three major scenic nodes, with the middle section's Chuitai, White Pagoda, Fuzhuang, and Lianhua Bridge the most wonderful.

Lianhua Bridge and White Pagoda: Lianxing Temple was built in the Yuan Dynasty, then called Fahai Temple; citizens going out of the city for outings often first moored boats and worshipped Buddha here.

The temple site is surrounded by water on all sides, shaped like a lotus; even more wonderful is a raised earth mound north of the temple, which feng shui experts say the mountain range comes from the northern Shugang, winding through the water to connect with the temple site, just like the stem of a lotus.

This lotus stem was originally a river embankment called Lianhua (Lotus) Embankment, and people believed it was the lifeblood of the temple.

In the late Ming, a eunuch surnamed Yang built the Baoyang City, abolishing the embankment and making it a bridge, and blocked the river west of the temple, causing "the embankment to break and the pulse to be injured, and the temple halls gradually fell into ruin.

" After entering the Qing, people dug open the river barrier, changed the bridge back to an embankment, and raised the earth mound regarded as the temple's pulse, successively building halls and pavilions, making the temple brilliantly revive; the townspeople sighed that "the earth pulse responds effectively, and the words of imagery are not wrong.

" In 1705, during Kangxi's southern tour, it was officially bestowed the name "Lianxing Temple.

" The White Pagoda is located north of the temple, built during the Qianlong reign of the Qing, imitating the White Pagoda of Beihai in Beijing.

Below is a square platform base with a ladder for climbing; in the middle is a Lamaist-style white pagoda body, with a niche room on the south; on top is a pagoda finial composed of thirteen layers of harmika, umbrella canopy, and precious pearl.

Xu Ke's "Qing Bai Lei Chao" tells the dramatic process of building the White Pagoda: It is said that during Qianlong's southern tour, when playing here, he said to his attendants that the scenery here is quite like the "Qiongdao Chunyin" (Jade Island Spring Shade) of the Western Garden, but unfortunately lacks a white pagoda.

The salt merchant Jiang Chun, in charge of receiving the emperor, hearing this, "urgently bribed the close attendants with a thousand gold," asking them to draw the appearance of the Beihai White Pagoda, then built it according to the drawing, completing it in one night.

The next day Qianlong came to play again, "seeing the pagoda towering, greatly surprised, thinking it was fake.Upon approaching, it was indeed made of bricks and stones.

After inquiring the reason, he sighed: 'The financial power of salt merchants is mighty!

'" This story has exaggerations, but it appropriately shows the wealth of Yangzhou salt merchants, which even the emperor found astonishing.

Lianhua Bridge is located at the original Lianhua Embankment; in 1757, to welcome Qianlong's southern tour and facilitate the passage of the imperial boat, Gao Heng, Salt Commissioner of Lianghuai, changed the embankment into a bridge.

To continue the lotus pulse without blocking water navigation, a rare fifteen-arch bridge form was adopted, with 3 arch holes each under the bridge body and four wings, totaling 15.

"Yangzhou Lansheng Lu" describes the wonder on a full-moon night: "On the night of the fifteenth, the bright moon hangs in the sky; each arch holds a moon, totaling fifteen arches and fifteen moons, with golden color rippling in the algae, many moons competing in brilliance, hanging upside down in the wave center, unfathomable.

The Three Pools Reflecting the Moon of West Lake cannot monopolize beauty before this.

" This scene especially makes Yangzhou people proud, believing it can rival the Three Pools Reflecting the Moon of West Lake.

Gao Heng also asked famous craftsmen to build five pavilions on the bridge, hence also called Wuting (Five-Pavilion) Bridge.Today's bridge was rebuilt during the Guangxu reign.

建筑要点 / Key Features
瘦西湖原名保障河扬州西北郊的山洪雨水经此汇入大运河很早就成为郊游胜地到清代乾隆年间盐商趁皇帝南巡之际极力兴造最称繁盛扬州人通常乘舟从城北门出欣赏沿途风光清代文人沈复17631825在浮生六记中点评道行其途有八九里虽全是人功而奇思幻想点缀天然即阆苑瑶池琼楼玉宇谅不过此其妙处在十余家之园亭合而为一联络至山气势俱贯金安清18171880水窗春呓也称两岸数十里楼台相接无一处重复并认为最佳处在虹桥迤西一转小金山矗其南五亭桥镇其中而白塔一区雄伟古朴往往夕阳返照萧鼓灯船如入汉宫图画瘦西湖小秦淮小金山这些名字贴切形容出扬州风景的灵秀之美今瘦西湖风景区东起天宁寺前御码头经冶春园卷石洞天西园曲水为第一段水道较窄折向北由虹桥揽胜经长堤春柳荷浦薰风桃花坞冶春后社徐园和四桥烟雨长春桥春波桥莲花桥和玉版桥为第二段水面渐宽由四桥烟雨折向西先后经过小金山钓鱼台凫庄五亭桥和莲性寺白塔直抵西端熙春台为第三段景致最为集中水系由此再度向北经二十四桥石壁流淙蜀冈朝旭和小吹台为第四段较为疏野有天然风味其中梅岭春深莲花桥和熙春台为三大景观节点以中段的吹台白塔凫庄和莲花桥最为精彩莲花桥和白塔莲性寺建于元代当时叫法海寺市民出城游玩常先
27 蜀冈
Shugang Scenic Area
南朝宋—清
级别 Level
含大明寺（第六批国保2006年）、平山堂、西园
地址 Address
邗江区蜀冈中峰
类型 Type
风景名胜/佛教寺院
门票 Ticket
45元
开放时间 Hours
7:30 — 17:15
中文原文

江苏地区以平原为主，由北自山东入境，一马平川，扬州城北的蜀冈是沿途所见的第一座高丘。蜀冈得名大致有三种说法。第一种是风水家的形势说，认为此冈是四川蜀山向东绵延的余脉，如北宋梅尧臣所称"冈形来自蜀，山色去连吴"。南宋祝穆《方舆胜览》称："旧传地脉通蜀，故曰蜀冈。

"第二种是江水说，明刘绩《霏雪录》称："山上有井，其水味如蜀江，号曰蜀冈。"第三种是字形说，《尔雅》认为蜀意为独，蜀冈的意思是一座独行之山。各种说法为这座小山增添了许多趣味，扬州人敝帚自珍，将其媲美于苏州虎丘，认为"隔江南北，两山相类"。

蜀冈作为扬州不多的几块高地之一，具有一定的防御优势，历代多选择在此建城，如春秋时期吴、楚的邗城，西汉的广陵城，隋唐的扬州城……也由于地势较高，蜀冈成为供人登高望远的风景胜地，今有大明寺、平山堂和西园等景点。1. 大明寺：第六批国保（2006年）。

大明寺始建于南朝宋孝武帝大明年间。隋仁寿元年（601年）隋文帝"诏海内立九层塔三十所"，庆祝他的六十大寿，其中一所便是立在大明寺的扬州栖灵塔，因此又称栖灵寺。

唐代高僧鉴真曾在此居住讲学，并于天宝年间东渡日本，创建唐招提寺，成为日本律宗初祖。1973年在寺东建造鉴真纪念堂，由建筑学家梁思成设计。唐末栖灵塔被火烧毁，复称大明寺。

清初因讳改称栖灵寺，清乾隆三十年（1765年）诏改法净寺。现存建筑多为清同治九年（1870年）重建，有山门、大雄宝殿和藏经楼等。

2. 平山堂：平山堂位于大明寺西侧。北宋庆历八年（1048年）欧阳修由滁州调任扬州，趁公事余暇，在蜀冈筑平山堂，因能平望江南诸山而得名。

1056年刘攽出任扬州，欧阳修填词相送，追忆当年在堂内的文酒盛事，称"平山栏槛倚晴空，山色有无中"。后有好事者调侃，平山堂望江南诸山甚近，拱列檐下，若可攀取，欧公言"有无中"，莫非因为近视？（严有翼《艺苑雌黄》）苏轼曾三过平山堂，缅思旧事，作《水调歌头》调笑好事者："长记平山堂上，欹枕江南烟雨，渺渺没孤鸿。

"认为山色有无是被烟雨所掩，正写出欧公幽澹情怀，岂是俗人能知？平山堂为敞口厅，宽五间，前有石铺的行春台，台前围以栏杆，下临深池，植有千竿修竹。游人可坐在堂内或倚在栏前，向南眺望江南群山。由于与欧、苏的关系，平山堂名重士林，历代游赏不绝，多次重修。

其中最重要的一次是清乾隆元年（1736年），时任两淮商总的汪应庚出资重建平山堂，并增建西园和远楼。事成后汪氏编纂《平山揽胜志》，收录历代题咏诗文，供人怀想往贤盛游。3. 西园：西园位于平山堂西。

清乾隆元年（1736年）汪应庚利用蜀冈的自然地势，开池叠山、布置亭榭，点缀而成。

园林占地数十亩，中央是一座巨大的水池，沿池建造亭台楼阁，主要位于南岸；池中有岛屿，上建单檐歇山顶房屋，是1963年从城内壶园迁来。池东叠黄石假山，高五丈许，极有气势；山内洞穴上下贯穿，可由山顶下至池边，幽深险怪。

假山东侧为康熙御碑亭，东壁嵌御碑；北侧是乾隆御碑亭，北壁嵌御碑。碑亭附近有著名的"天下第五泉"。

· · · · ·
English

The Jiangsu region is mainly plains; entering from the north from Shandong, it is a vast flat expanse, and Shugang north of Yangzhou city is the first high hill seen along the way.

The name Shugang (Shu Ridge) generally has three explanations.

The first is the feng shui situation theory, believing this ridge is the eastern extension of the Shu Mountains in Sichuan, as Northern Song Mei Yaochen said: "The ridge shape comes from Shu, the mountain color connects to Wu.

" Southern Song Zhu Mu's "Fangyu Shenglan" says: "Tradition says the earth pulse connects to Shu, hence called Shugang.

" The second is the river water theory; Ming Liu Ji's "Feixue Lu" says: "There is a well on the mountain, its water tastes like the Shu River, called Shugang.

" The third is the character-shape theory; "Erya" believes 'shu' means 'alone,' so Shugang means a solitary mountain.

Various explanations add much interest to this small hill; Yangzhou people, valuing their own, compare it to Suzhou's Tiger Hill, believing "across the river north and south, the two mountains are similar.

" As one of the few highlands in Yangzhou, Shugang has certain defensive advantages, and successive dynasties mostly chose to build cities here, such as the Han City of Wu and Chu in the Spring and Autumn period, the Guangling City of the Western Han, and the Yangzhou City of the Sui and Tang.

..Also due to its higher terrain, Shugang became a scenic spot for people to climb high and gaze into the distance; today it has Daming Temple, Pingshan Hall, West Garden, and other scenic spots.1.

Daming Temple: 6th Batch National Protected (2006).Daming Temple was first built during the Daming reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Liu Song of the Southern Dynasties.

In the 1st year of Renshou of the Sui (601), Emperor Wen of Sui "issued an edict to build thirty nine-story pagodas across the country" to celebrate his 60th birthday; one of them was the Yangzhou Qiling Pagoda built at Daming Temple, hence also called Qiling Temple.

The Tang eminent monk Jianzhen once lived and lectured here, and during the Tianbao reign crossed east to Japan, founding the Toshodai-ji Temple and becoming the first patriarch of Japanese Risshu Buddhism.

In 1973, the Jianzhen Memorial Hall was built east of the temple, designed by architect Liang Sicheng.

At the end of the Tang, the Qiling Pagoda was destroyed by fire, and it was again called Daming Temple.

In the early Qing, due to taboo, it was renamed Qiling Temple; in the 30th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1765), an edict renamed it Fajing Temple.

The existing buildings were mostly rebuilt in the 9th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1870), including the mountain gate, Mahavira Hall, and Scripture Library etc.2.

Pingshan Hall: Pingshan (Level Mountain) Hall is located west of Daming Temple.

In the 8th year of Qingli of the Northern Song (1048), Ouyang Xiu was transferred from Chuzhou to Yangzhou; taking advantage of his spare time from official duties, he built Pingshan Hall on Shugang, named because one can look levelly at the mountains south of the Yangtze.

In 1056, when Liu Ban was appointed to Yangzhou, Ouyang Xiu sent a ci poem to see him off, recalling the literary and drinking gatherings in the hall that year, saying "Pingshan's railings lean against the clear sky, mountain colors in being and non-being.

" Later, some busybody teased that from Pingshan Hall the mountains south of the Yangtze are very close, arching under the eaves as if reachable; Ouyang Gong saying 'in being and non-being'—could it be because he was nearsighted?

(Yan Youyi, "Yiyuan Cihuang") Su Shi passed Pingshan Hall three times, recalling old times, and wrote "Shuidiao Getou" mocking the busybody: "Long remember on Pingshan Hall, leaning on a pillow in the misty rain south of the Yangtze, the lone goose disappears faintly.

" Believing the mountain colors' 'being and non-being' was obscured by misty rain, precisely expressing Ouyang Gong's serene and indifferent sentiment—how could ordinary people understand?

Pingshan Hall is an open hall, five bays wide, with a stone-paved Xingchun (Spring-Walking) Terrace in front, surrounded by railings, overlooking a deep pool below with a thousand tall bamboos planted.

Visitors can sit inside the hall or lean on the railing, looking south at the mountains south of the Yangtze.

Due to its connection with Ouyang and Su, Pingshan Hall is highly regarded among scholars, with continuous visits through the dynasties and multiple renovations.

The most important one was in the 1st year of Qianlong of the Qing (1736), when Wang Yinggeng, then chief merchant of Lianghuai, funded the rebuilding of Pingshan Hall and added the West Garden and Yuanlou (Distant Tower).

After completion, Wang compiled the "Pingshan Lansheng Zhi," collecting inscriptions and poems through the dynasties for people to recall the elegant travels of former worthies.3.

West Garden: West Garden is located west of Pingshan Hall.

In the 1st year of Qianlong of the Qing (1736), Wang Yinggeng used the natural terrain of Shugang to dig ponds, stack rockeries, arrange pavilions and terraces, and embellish it into a garden.

The garden covers tens of mu, with a huge pond in the center; pavilions, terraces, and towers are built along the pond, mainly on the south bank; there is an island in the pond, with a single-eave hip-and-gable roof building on it, moved from the Huyuan Garden in the city in 1963.

East of the pond, a yellow-stone rockery is stacked, about five zhang high, very imposing; caves inside the mountain penetrate up and down, allowing passage from the mountain top to the pond edge, deep and perilously strange.

East of the rockery is the Kangxi Imperial Stele Pavilion, with an imperial stele embedded in the east wall; north is the Qianlong Imperial Stele Pavilion, with an imperial stele embedded in the north wall.

Near the stele pavilions is the famous "Fifth Spring Under Heaven."

建筑要点 / Key Features
江苏地区以平原为主由北自山东入境一马平川扬州城北的蜀冈是沿途所见的第一座高丘蜀冈得名大致有三种说法第一种是风水家的形势说认为此冈是四川蜀山向东绵延的余脉如北宋梅尧臣所称冈形来自蜀山色去连吴南宋祝穆方舆胜览称旧传地脉通蜀故曰蜀冈第二种是江水说明刘绩霏雪录称山上有井其水味如蜀江号曰蜀冈第三种是字形说尔雅认为蜀意为独蜀冈的意思是一座独行之山各种说法为这座小山增添了许多趣味扬州人敝帚自珍将其媲美于苏州虎丘认为隔江南北两山相类蜀冈作为扬州不多的几块高地之一具有一定的防御优势历代多选择在此建城如春秋时期吴楚的邗城西汉的广陵城隋唐的扬州城也由于地势较高蜀冈成为供人登高望远的风景胜地今有大明寺平山堂和西园等景点大明寺第六批国保2006年大明寺始建于南朝宋孝武帝大明年间隋仁寿元年601年隋文帝诏海内立九层塔三十所庆祝他的六十大寿其中一所便是立在大明寺的扬州栖灵塔因此又称栖灵寺唐代高僧鉴真曾在此居住讲学并于天宝年间东渡日本创建唐招提寺成为日本律宗初祖1973年在寺东建造鉴真纪念堂由建筑学家梁思成设计唐末栖灵塔被火烧毁复称大明寺清初因讳改称栖灵寺清乾隆三十年1765年诏改法净寺现存建筑多为清同治九年1870
28 扬州城遗址（唐城遗址博物馆）
Yangzhou City Site (The Ancient Tang City Ruins Museum)
隋—宋
级别 Level
第四批全国重点文物保护单位（1996年）
地址 Address
维扬区平山堂东路20号
类型 Type
古城遗址/博物馆
门票 Ticket
25元
开放时间 Hours
8:30 — 17:00
中文原文

春秋时期吴国已在蜀冈筑城，其最兴盛的时期则在隋唐两宋。隋在汉初广陵城的基础上扩建为江都宫城。唐代拓展为子城和罗城两部分：子城在蜀冈上，为衙署区，夯土筑墙，四面开门，城内以十字街贯通。罗城在蜀冈下，为工商业居民区。

宋代再次拓建，成为宋大城、堡城和夹城三城。扬州唐城遗址是国内保存最完好的古城遗址之一。唐代衙城的四周城垣、夯土城墙、城门和角楼至今仍高出地面5—10米，历历在目。

博物馆位于衙城遗址的西南角，复建了唐式城墙和阙楼，可登临观赏唐城遗址和扬州城。

馆内展览唐杜佑题名八角石柱、唐咸通十四年（873年）经幢和唐三绝碑等唐代文物精品，并辟有"崔志远史料陈列馆"。

· · · · ·
English

In the Spring and Autumn period, the State of Wu already built a city at Shugang, and its most prosperous period was in the Sui, Tang, and Song dynasties.

The Sui expanded it into the Jiangdu Palace City on the basis of the early Han Guangling City.The Tang expanded it into two parts: the Zicheng (Sub-city) and Luocheng (Outer City).

The Zicheng is on Shugang, serving as the government office area, with rammed-earth walls, gates on all four sides, and cross streets running through the city.

The Luocheng is below Shugang, serving as the industrial, commercial, and residential area.

The Song expanded again, forming three cities: the Song Great City, Fortress City, and Clamp City.

The Yangzhou Tang City Site is one of the best-preserved ancient city sites in China.

The surrounding city walls, rammed-earth walls, gates, and corner towers of the Tang yamen city still rise 5-10 meters above the ground today, clearly visible.

The museum is located at the southwest corner of the yamen city site, with rebuilt Tang-style city walls and gate towers, which can be climbed to view the Tang city site and Yangzhou city.

Inside the museum, fine Tang cultural relics such as the octagonal stone pillar inscribed by Du You of the Tang, the dharani pillar of the 14th year of Xiantong of the Tang (873), and the Tang Three Wonders Stele are exhibited, and a "Cui Zhiyuan Historical Materials Exhibition Hall" has been opened.

建筑要点 / Key Features
春秋时期吴国已在蜀冈筑城其最兴盛的时期则在隋唐两宋隋在汉初广陵城的基础上扩建为江都宫城唐代拓展为子城和罗城两部分子城在蜀冈上为衙署区夯土筑墙四面开门城内以十字街贯通罗城在蜀冈下为工商业居民区宋代再次拓建成为宋大城堡城和夹城三城扬州唐城遗址是国内保存最完好的古城遗址之一唐代衙城的四周城垣夯土城墙城门和角楼至今仍高出地面510米历历在目博物馆位于衙城遗址的西南角复建了唐式城墙和阙楼可登临观赏唐城遗址和扬州城馆内展览唐杜佑题名八角石柱唐咸通十四年873年经幢和唐三绝碑等唐代文物精品并辟有崔志远史料陈列馆
29 天山汉墓
Tianshan Mausoleum of Han Dynasty
汉
级别 Level
第三批省级文物保护单位（1982年）
地址 Address
平山堂东路97号
类型 Type
汉墓/博物馆
门票 Ticket
30元

8:00 — 17:00
中文原文

天山汉墓原在高邮市天山镇神居山上，是汉武帝之子刘胥（？—前54年）的陵墓。西汉元狩六年（前117年）刘胥封广陵王，卒后葬神居山。1979年发现了他与王后的合葬墓，1992年迁至扬州，又称汉陵苑。

汉陵苑馆内中央展厅陈列"神居山一号汉墓"（王墓），采用帝王级别的"黄肠题凑"木椁墓，是全国罕见的大型汉代墓葬。南北长16.65米，东西宽14.28米，是迄今发现的保存最完整的一座。东厅陈列"神居山二号汉墓"（后墓），也采用"黄肠题凑"形制。此外，在东西侧室还展有汉广陵国出土的木器、玉器、铜器、漆器、陶器等，供人了解汉代王侯生活。

· · · · ·
English

The Tianshan Han Tomb was originally on Shenju Mountain, Tianshan Town, Gaoyou City, and is the mausoleum of Liu Xu (?-54 BC), son of Emperor Wu of Han.

In the 6th year of Yuanshou of the Western Han (117 BC), Liu Xu was enfeoffed as King of Guangling and buried at Shenju Mountain after death.

In 1979, his joint tomb with the queen was discovered, and in 1992 it was moved to Yangzhou, also called the Han Mausoleum Garden.

The central exhibition hall of the Han Mausoleum Garden displays the "Shenju Mountain Han Tomb No.

1" (king's tomb), adopting the imperial-level "Huangchang Ticou" (cypress heart timber frame) wooden outer-coffin tomb—a rare large Han Dynasty tomb in China.It is 16.

65 meters long north-south and 14.28 meters wide east-west, the most completely preserved one discovered to date.The east hall displays the "Shenju Mountain Han Tomb No.

2" (queen's tomb), also adopting the "Huangchang Ticou" form.

In addition, the east and west side chambers display wooden artifacts, jade, bronze, lacquerware, and pottery unearthed from the Han Guangling Kingdom, allowing people to understand the life of Han Dynasty kings and marquises.

建筑要点 / Key Features
天山汉墓原在高邮市天山镇神居山上是汉武帝之子刘胥前54年的陵墓西汉元狩六年前117年刘胥封广陵王卒后葬神居山1979年发现了他与王后的合葬墓1992年迁至扬州又称汉陵苑汉陵苑馆内中央展厅陈列神居山一号汉墓王墓采用帝王级别的黄肠题凑木椁墓是全国罕见的大型汉代墓葬南北长16.65米东西宽14.28米是迄今发现的保存最完整的一座东厅陈列神居山二号汉墓后墓也采用黄肠题凑形制此外在东西侧室还展有汉广陵国出土的木器玉器铜器漆器陶器等供人了解汉代王侯生活
30 隋炀帝陵
Mausoleum of Emperor Yang of Sui
唐—清
级别 Level
第四批省级文物保护单位（1995年）
地址 Address
邗江区西湖镇隋炀西路102号
类型 Type
帝陵/古建筑
中文原文

隋代大业十四年（618年）隋炀帝杨广因困居在扬州行宫，夜夜笙歌，不久被部下勒死，年仅五十岁，萧皇后拆下床板作为棺木，将其草草埋葬。唐代平定江南后，按帝王之礼在雷塘改葬隋炀帝。陵墓规模狭小，唐人罗隐《隋炀帝陵》感慨："君王忍把平陈业，只换雷塘数亩田。

"清嘉庆十二年（1807年）阮元误将槐泗镇槐二村的一处土墩认作隋炀帝陵，为其立碑建石，1995年被列为省保单位。

2013年考古学家在西湖镇发现两座古墓，出土隋炀帝墓志和鎏金铜铺首，确定此处才是隋炀帝陵的真实位置，更正了阮元的错误。

· · · · ·
English

In the 14th year of Daye of the Sui Dynasty (618), Emperor Yang of Sui, Yang Guang, trapped in the Yangzhou palace with nightly singing and music, was soon strangled by his subordinates at the age of fifty; Empress Xiao removed the bed board as a coffin and hastily buried him.

After the Tang pacified Jiangnan, Emperor Yang of Sui was reburied at Leitang according to imperial rites.

The mausoleum is small in scale; Tang person Luo Yin's "Mausoleum of Emperor Yang of Sui" lamented: "The king endured to trade the achievement of pacifying Chen for only a few mu of fields at Leitang.

" In the 12th year of Jiaqing of the Qing (1807), Ruan Yuan mistakenly identified an earthen mound at Huai'er Village, Huaisi Town as the Mausoleum of Emperor Yang of Sui, erecting a stele and stone for it, and it was listed as a provincial protected unit in 1995.

In 2013, archaeologists discovered two ancient tombs in Xihu Town, unearthing the epitaph of Emperor Yang of Sui and gilded bronze door knockers, confirming that this place is the true location of the Mausoleum of Emperor Yang of Sui, correcting Ruan Yuan's error.

建筑要点 / Key Features
隋代大业十四年618年隋炀帝杨广因困居在扬州行宫夜夜笙歌不久被部下勒死年仅五十岁萧皇后拆下床板作为棺木将其草草埋葬唐代平定江南后按帝王之礼在雷塘改葬隋炀帝陵墓规模狭小人罗隐隋炀帝陵感慨君王忍把平陈业只换雷塘数亩田清嘉庆十二年1807年阮元误将槐泗镇槐二村的一处土墩认作隋炀帝陵为其立碑建石1995年被列为省保单位2013年考古学家在西湖镇发现两座古墓出土隋炀帝墓志和鎏金铜铺首确定此处才是隋炀帝陵的真实位置更正了阮元的错误
31 文峰塔
Wenfeng Pagoda
明—清
级别 Level
第六批省级文物保护单位（2006年）

中文原文

文峰塔是一座砖木结构的楼阁式塔，始建于明万历十年（1582年），清咸丰三年（1853年）寺毁仅剩塔心，1923年修复，2003年重修。

文峰塔与城市的文运攸关，通常结合地形和水流，选择甲（东偏北）、丙（南偏东）、丁（南偏西）等方位建塔。扬州文峰塔选在丁位，位于护城河出水口处，既可弘扬文风，又能锁住象征才华和财运的河水。塔为八边形平面，高七层，内墙砖砌，外檐与栏杆为木构。此塔既是地标性建筑，又可登塔南眺京口三山，北望蜀冈诸胜，被誉为扬州城南第一胜景。

塔下为文峰寺，有前殿、后殿及东西廊房等清代建筑。

· · · · ·
English

Wenfeng Pagoda is a pavilion-style pagoda of brick-wood structure, first built in the 10th year of Wanli of the Ming (1582); in the 3rd year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1853) the temple was destroyed leaving only the pagoda core, repaired in 1923 and rebuilt in 2003.

Wenfeng Pagoda is closely related to the city's literary fortune; usually, combining terrain and water flow, pagodas are built in positions such as Jia (east by north), Bing (south by east), and Ding (south by west).

Yangzhou's Wenfeng Pagoda was chosen at the Ding position, located at the outlet of the moat, both to promote literary style and to lock in the river water symbolizing talent and wealth.

The pagoda has an octagonal plan, seven stories high, with inner walls of brick and outer eaves and railings of wood.

This pagoda is both a landmark building and allows climbing to gaze south at the Three Mountains of Jingkou and north at the scenic spots of Shugang, hailed as the number one scenic spot south of Yangzhou city.

Below the pagoda is Wenfeng Temple, with Qing Dynasty buildings such as the front hall, rear hall, and east-west corridor rooms.

建筑要点 / Key Features
文峰塔是一座砖木结构的楼阁式塔始建于明万历十年1582年清咸丰三年1853年寺毁仅剩塔心1923年修复2003年重修文峰塔与城市的文运攸关通常结合地形和水流选择甲东偏北丙南偏东丁南偏西等方位建塔扬州文峰塔选在丁位位于护城河出水口处既可弘扬文风又能锁住象征才华和财运的河水塔为八边形平面高七层内墙砖砌外檐与栏杆为木构此塔既是地标性建筑又可登塔南眺京口三山北望蜀冈诸胜被誉为扬州城南第一胜景塔下为文峰寺有前殿后殿及东西廊房等清代建筑
32 盂城驿
Yucheng Post House
明—清
级别 Level

中文原文

盂城驿于2014年成为世界文化遗产京杭大运河的组成部分，盂城是高邮的别称，取秦观描写高邮"吾乡如覆盂"之意。盂城驿是全国保存最完整的古驿站之一，为研究古代邮驿和交通的重要实例。

这处驿站始建于明洪武八年（1375年），到嘉靖年间发展到很大规模，有厅房、库房、神祠等共50多间。

明嘉靖三十六年（1557年）倭寇入侵，驿站被毁，明隆庆元年（1567年）重建。现存建筑多建于清道光年间，近年修复。

中路自南而北包括大门、正厅皇华厅和后厅驻节堂等，正厅与后厅皆为明代遗构。皇华厅东南角建有鼓楼，是古代值更守夜的制高点。

· · · · ·
English

Yucheng Post House became part of the World Cultural Heritage Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal in 2014; Yucheng is another name for Gaoyou, taking the meaning of Qin Guan's description of Gaoyou "my hometown is like an overturned bowl.

" Yucheng Post House is one of the best-preserved ancient post stations in China, an important example for studying ancient postal services and transportation.

This post station was first built in the 8th year of Hongwu of the Ming (1375), and by the Jiajing reign it had developed to a large scale, with over 50 rooms including halls, warehouses, and shrines.

In the 36th year of Jiajing of the Ming (1557), Japanese pirates invaded and the post station was destroyed; it was rebuilt in the 1st year of Longqing of the Ming (1567).

The existing buildings were mostly built during the Daoguang reign of the Qing and restored in recent years.

The middle road from south to north includes the main gate, the main hall Huanghua Hall, and the rear hall Zhujie Hall etc.; both the main hall and rear hall are Ming Dynasty remains.

A drum tower is built at the southeast corner of Huanghua Hall, the high point for keeping watch at night in ancient times.

33 文游台
Wenyou Platform
北宋—清
级别 Level
其他
地址 Address
高邮市人民路507号
类型 Type
古建/园林
门票 Ticket
30元
开放时间 Hours
8:30 — 17:30
中文原文

文游台原为东岳行宫，始建于北宋太平兴国年间。北宋元丰七年（1084年）苏轼由黄州到汝州赴任，途经高邮，与秦观、孙觉和王巩登东山览眺，饮酒论文。

当时四人都不得志，"登是台以啸咏，发舒其无聊不平之气"（王士禛《重修文游台记》）。随后县令以群贤毕至，将他们的登临之地题为"文游台"，李公麟为之绘图纪胜；此后文游台屡废屡兴，因人而存，后世骚人墨客常到此遐想苏、秦诸公当时"接袂登台，挥麈剧谈"的风神气概（应武《重修文游台记》）。宋代曾几《文游台》诗曰："忆昔坡仙此地游，一时人物尽风流。

香莼紫蟹供杯酌，彩笔银钩人唱酬。"现存建筑多建于晚清。南部入口前立有牌坊，入门院落中央为秦观立像，东路偏院有汪曾祺文学馆、秦观词社和高邮名人园，西路偏院是一座园林，有荷花池、古鉴堂和水鉴馆等。

秦观立像北面拾阶而上为正堂益簪堂，堂内四壁嵌《秦邮帖》，乃清嘉庆年间高邮知州师兆龙集苏东坡、黄庭坚、米元章、秦少游、赵子昂、董其昌等名家法书，由著名金石学家钱泳勒刻而成，书艺精湛，刀法传神，具有较高的艺术价值。堂北为文游台主体楼，这座二层楼建在高台上，登高远眺，东望田畴，西观湖天，古城景象尽收眼底。

主体楼西侧有泰山庙、秦观读书台和建于明代的纪念苏轼、孙觉、秦观、王巩的古四贤祠。

· · · · ·
English

Wenyou Platform was originally the Dongyue (Eastern Marchmount) Temporary Palace, first built during the Taiping Xingguo reign of the Northern Song.

In the 7th year of Yuanfeng of the Northern Song (1084), Su Shi, traveling from Huangzhou to Ruzhou to take office, passed through Gaoyou and, with Qin Guan, Sun Jue, and Wang Gong, climbed East Mountain to gaze into the distance, drinking and discussing literature.

At that time all four were unfulfilled in their ambitions, "climbing this platform to whistle and chant, releasing their bored and indignant qi" (Wang Shizhen, "Record of Rebuilding Wenyou Platform").

Subsequently, the county magistrate, considering the gathering of many worthies, titled the place where they climbed "Wenyou Platform" (Literary Gathering Platform), and Li Gonglin drew a picture to record the occasion; thereafter Wenyou Platform was repeatedly abandoned and revived, surviving because of its people.

Later poets and scholars often came here to imagine the spirited bearing of Su, Qin and other gentlemen at that time, "walking arm in arm to the platform, waving horsetail whisks and discussing vigorously" (Ying Wu, "Record of Rebuilding Wenyou Platform").

Song Dynasty Zeng Ji's poem "Wenyou Platform" says: "Recalling the past when the Poet Immortal traveled here, the figures of that time were all romantic.

Fragrant water shield and purple crabs served cups and goblets, colorful brushes and silver hooks people sang in response." The existing buildings were mostly built in the late Qing.

In front of the southern entrance stands a memorial archway; in the center of the entrance courtyard is a standing statue of Qin Guan; the east side courtyard has the Wang Zengqi Literature Museum, Qin Guan Ci Poetry Society, and Gaoyou Celebrity Garden; the west side courtyard is a garden with a lotus pond, Gujian Hall, and Shuijian Hall etc.

North of the Qin Guan statue, climbing steps up is the main hall Yizan Hall; the four walls of the hall are embedded with the "Qinyou Stele Album," which was compiled by Shi Zhaolong, Prefect of Gaoyou during the Jiaqing reign of the Qing, collecting calligraphy by famous masters such as Su Dongpo, Huang Tingjian, Mi Yuanzhang, Qin Shaoyou, Zhao Ziang, and Dong Qichang, engraved by the famous epigrapher Qian Yong—with exquisite calligraphy and vivid carving, having relatively high artistic value.

North of the hall is the main building of Wenyou Platform, a two-story building built on a high platform; climbing high and looking far, one sees fields to the east and lake and sky to the west, with the ancient city scenery in full view.

West of the main building are the Taishan Temple, Qin Guan's Reading Platform, and the ancient Four Worthies Shrine built in the Ming Dynasty commemorating Su Shi, Sun Jue, Qin Guan, and Wang Gong.

建筑要点 / Key Features
文游台原为东岳行宫始建于北宋太平兴国年间北宋元丰七年1084年苏轼由黄州到汝州赴任途经高邮与秦观孙觉和王巩登东山览眺饮酒论文当时四人都不得志登是台以啸咏发舒其无聊不平之气王士禛重修文游台记随后县令以群贤毕至将他们的登临之地题为文游台李公麟为之绘图纪胜此后文游台屡废屡兴因人而存后世骚人墨客常到此遐想苏秦诸公当时接袂登台挥麈剧谈的风神气概应武重修文游台记宋代曾几文游台诗曰忆昔坡仙此地游一时人物尽风流香莼紫蟹供杯酌彩笔银钩人唱酬现存建筑多建于晚清南部入口前立有牌坊入门院落中央为秦观立像东路偏院有汪曾祺文学馆秦观词社和高邮名人园西路偏院是一座园林有荷花池古鉴堂和水鉴馆等秦观立像北面拾阶而上为正堂益簪堂堂内四壁嵌秦邮帖乃清嘉庆年间高邮知州师兆龙集苏东坡黄庭坚米元章秦少游赵子昂董其昌等名家法书由著名金石学家钱泳勒刻而成书艺精湛刀法传神具有较高的艺术价值堂北为文游台主体楼这座二层楼建在高台上登高远眺东望田畴西观湖天古城景象尽收眼底主体楼西侧有泰山庙秦观读书台和建于明代的纪念苏轼孙觉秦观王巩的古四贤祠

镇国寺塔位于城西京杭大运河河心岛上，1956年拓宽运河时，保留下河心岛的古塔。镇国寺塔又称西门宝塔，为七层方形砖塔，始建于晚唐，被誉为"江南大雁塔"。今塔一至三层为宋构，四至七层在明代重建。

· · · · ·
English

Zhenguo Temple Pagoda is located on the river island in the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal west of the city; in 1956, when widening the canal, the ancient pagoda on the river island was preserved.

Zhenguo Temple Pagoda, also called West Gate Pagoda, is a seven-story square brick pagoda, first built in the late Tang, hailed as the "Great Wild Goose Pagoda of Jiangnan.

" Today the first to third stories of the pagoda are Song structures, and the fourth to seventh stories were rebuilt in the Ming.

The pagoda finial is a bronze-cast gourd, engraved with the characters "favorable weather, peaceful country and safe people."

English

Jingtu Temple Pagoda, also called East Gate Pagoda, opposite Zhenguo Temple Pagoda, was first built in the 34th year of Wanli of the Ming (1606), heavily repaired during the Guangxu reign of the Qing, had one corner destroyed by a shell in 1945, and was repaired the following year.

City Wall and Kuilou Tower of Gaoyou

1. 宋城墙：宋城墙位于盂城路和琵琶路交叉口，北宋开宝四年（971年）高邮军知军高凝祐筑。

1972年大部分城墙被拆除，仅存东南角约120余米的一段，其中东西向51.7米，南北向71米，墙高6.6米，雉堞39座。城墙采用青砖叠筑，拐角处有楼梯可登墙顶。

墙下有古护城河、南北水关、东水门和穿心河，组成一套完整的城市防卫体系。

2. 明奎楼：明奎楼位于城墙东南角，建于明天启三年（1623年），明崇祯九年（1636年）重修，1984年大修，2002年列为省保单位。

奎楼采用砖木结构，八角三层，底层朝北开门，二、三层四面开门。原一、二层顶部有精美彩绘，今按清代图样恢复第一层重檐、回廊。登楼可眺望城内风光。

· · · · ·
English

1.

Song City Wall: The Song City Wall is located at the intersection of Yucheng Road and Pipa Road, built by Gao Ningyou, Military Commissioner of Gaoyou Army, in the 4th year of Kaibao of the Northern Song (971).

In 1972 most of the city wall was demolished, leaving only a section of about 120 meters at the southeast corner, of which 51.

7 meters runs east-west and 71 meters north-south, with a wall height of 6.6 meters and 39 crenellations.

The city wall is built with stacked grey bricks, with stairs at the corners to climb to the top of the wall.

Below the wall are the ancient moat, north and south water gates, east water gate, and Chuanxin River, forming a complete urban defense system.2.

Ming Kuilou (Kuixing Tower): The Ming Kuilou is located at the southeast corner of the city wall, built in the 3rd year of Tianqi of the Ming (1623), rebuilt in the 9th year of Chongzhen of the Ming (1636), heavily repaired in 1984, and listed as a provincial protected unit in 2002.

Kuilou adopts a brick-wood structure, octagonal with three stories; the ground floor opens to the north, and the second and third floors open on all four sides.

The original first and second floor tops had exquisite painted decorations; today the first floor's double eaves and corridors have been restored according to Qing Dynasty patterns.

Climbing the tower, one can overlook the scenery inside the city.

建筑要点 / Key Features
宋城墙宋城墙位于盂城路和琵琶路交叉口北宋开宝四年971年高邮军知军高凝祐筑1972年大部分城墙被拆除仅存东南角约120余米的一段其中东西向51.7米南北向71米墙高6.6米雉堞39座城墙采用青砖叠筑拐角处有楼梯可登墙顶墙下有古护城河南北水关东水门和穿心河组成一套完整的城市防卫体系明奎楼明奎楼位于城墙东南角建于明天启三年1623年明崇祯九年1636年重修1984年大修2002年列为省保单位奎楼采用砖木结构八角三层底层朝北开门二三层四面开门原一二层顶部有精美彩绘今按清代图样恢复第一层重檐回廊登楼可眺望城内风光

English

Gaoyou Pawnshop is located at the intersection of Renmin Road and Beimen Dajie in Gaoyou City, listed as a 6th Batch National Protected Ancient Building in 2006.

Gaoyou Pawnshop opened in the early Qing, originally with four courtyards, nearly square in plan, with a castle-like exterior.

泰州

Taizhou
8
处建筑

地区概述 / Regional Overview

历史上泰州曾长期隶属扬州府，得益于明清时期兵灾较少，保存至今的日涉园比扬州现存园林都要古老，被陈从周先生誉为"淮左第一园"。

此园原为明代陈鸢宅第，明万历年间其孙陈应芳（1543—1610）在宅旁造园，取陶渊明"园日涉以成趣"之意，题名日涉园。今园中假山主景，即为明代遗物。

清初园归田氏，后来又归高凤翥（1707—1771），精心扩建为14景，并更名"三峰园"，奠定了今日格局。传世有道光五年（1825年）周庠所绘《三峰园四面景图》，表现了当时的园貌。

清咸丰八年（1858年）园归吴文锡（1800—1870），改名蛰园，后又归两淮盐运使乔松年（1815—1875），俗称乔园。

乔园是长江以北罕见的明代园林遗存，具有重要的历史价值和艺术价值；园林中区的山池主景，被陈从周赞誉为小园中的佳作："水池横中，假山对峙，洞曲藏岩，石梁卧波等，用极简单的数物组合成之，不落常套，光景自新。"

Historically, Taizhou was long subordinate to Yangzhou Prefecture; benefiting from fewer military disasters during the Ming and Qing periods, the preserved Rishe Garden is older than any existing garden in Yangzhou, and was praised by Mr.

Chen Congzhou as the 'Number One Garden of Huaizuo.

' This garden was originally the residence of Chen Yuan of the Ming; during the Wanli reign of the Ming, his grandson Chen Yingfang (1543-1610) built a garden next to the residence, taking Tao Yuanming's meaning 'the garden, daily entered, becomes a delight,' and titled it Rishe Garden.

The main rockery scene in today's garden is a Ming Dynasty relic.

In the early Qing, the garden passed to the Tian family, then to Gao Fengzhu (1707-1771), who carefully expanded it into 14 scenes and renamed it 'Sanfeng Garden' (Three Peaks Garden), establishing today's layout.

A 'Four-Sided View of Sanfeng Garden' painted by Zhou Xiang in the 5th year of Daoguang (1825) survives, showing the garden's appearance at that time.

In the 8th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1858), the garden passed to Wu Wenxi (1800-1870), renamed Zhe Garden, then to Qiao Songnian (1815-1875), Salt Commissioner of Lianghuai, commonly called Qiao Garden.

Qiao Garden is a rare Ming Dynasty garden remnant north of the Yangtze River, with important historical and artistic value; the mountain-pool main scene in the central area of the garden was praised by Chen Congzhou as a masterpiece among small gardens: 'The water pool lies horizontally in the middle, rockeries face each other, winding caves hide in the rocks, stone beams lie over the waves etc.

, composed with extremely simple few elements, not falling into common patterns, with scenery ever new.'

01 日涉园
Rishe Garden
明—民国

类型 Type

中文原文

今乔园北、西、南三面皆有入口，需从西门购票入园。园林分为东、中、西三区，中区属旧园遗存，为园中精华；东、西两区皆为近年复建。走进西门是一处天井小院，向东直接通向西区，也可向南经游廊曲折进入。西区中部是一座大假山，其上建三层来青阁和皆绿山房。

东北角有一座大池，绕池设文桂之舫、午韵轩和蕉雨轩，皆紧临水面，互成对景；东南角有一座小池，掩在云墙之后，两池通过环绕在假山东侧的溪流相连，水脉相通。中区采用前宅后园格局，南部有宅门和大堂，堂北设廊面向北部园林。园中以山响草堂（又名三峰草堂）为主体，分为南北两区。

堂南为开敞的平地，绕着一湾溪流，东西各跨一座小桥，对面隔水是座大型石假山，为珍贵的明代遗存。假山下有石矶洞穴，上有山路平台，用黄石和湖石叠成：下部近水及山洞底部用黄石，规整古朴；上部用湖石，宛转多姿。

山顶树立三支石笋，是当年"三峰园"旧物；东侧的古柏是明代古树，苍劲多姿，为园景增色不少。假山东侧设六角数鱼亭，可俯临溪水，观赏游鱼；西侧贴墙设半亭，位置较高，可纵览园景。山响草堂北侧是数级台地，台上正中为书斋汲堂，西侧为因巢亭，京剧大师梅兰芳曾在此下榻；东侧是小楼松吹阁，可登阁临眺。东区以建筑为主，园景较为单调。

· · · · ·
English

Today's Qiao Garden has entrances on the north, west, and south sides; tickets must be purchased and entry from the west gate.

The garden is divided into east, central, and west areas; the central area belongs to the old garden remains and is the essence of the garden; the east and west areas were both rebuilt in recent years.

Entering the west gate is a small courtyard; going east directly leads to the west area, or one can go south through a winding covered corridor.

In the middle of the west area is a large rockery, on which the three-story Laiqing Pavilion and Jielü Mountain House are built.

In the northeast corner is a large pond; around the pond are set the Wengui Boat, Wuyun Pavilion, and Jiaoyu Pavilion, all close to the water, forming opposite scenes; in the southeast corner is a small pond, hidden behind a cloud wall, and the two ponds are connected by a stream winding around the east side of the rockery, with water veins connected.

The central area adopts a front-residence-back-garden layout, with a residence gate and main hall in the south, and a corridor north of the hall facing the northern garden.

The garden centers on Shanxiang Thatched Hall (also called Sanfeng Thatched Hall), divided into north and south areas.

South of the hall is open flat ground, winding around a bay of stream, with a small bridge spanning east and west each; across the water opposite is a large stone rockery, a precious Ming Dynasty relic.

Below the rockery are stone banks and caves, above are mountain paths and platforms, stacked with yellow stone and lake stone: the lower part near water and the bottom of the cave use yellow stone, regular and simple; the upper part uses lake stone, graceful and varied.

Three stone stalagmites stand on the mountain top, relics of the former 'Sanfeng Garden'; the ancient cypress on the east side is a Ming Dynasty ancient tree, vigorous and varied, adding much to the garden scenery.

On the east side of the rockery is a hexagonal Fish-Counting Pavilion, overlooking the stream to watch swimming fish; on the west side against the wall is a half-pavilion, positioned higher, allowing a panoramic view of the garden.

North of Shanxiang Thatched Hall are several terraces; in the center of the terrace is the study Jitang, west is Yinchao Pavilion, where Peking Opera master Mei Lanfang once stayed; east is the small building Songchui Pavilion, which can be climbed to overlook.

The east area is mainly buildings, with relatively monotonous garden scenery.

建筑要点 / Key Features
今乔园北西南三面皆有入口需从西门购票入园园林分为东中西三区中区属旧园遗存为园中精华东西两区皆为近年复建走进西门是一处天井小院向东直接通向西区也可向南经游廊曲折进入西区中部是一座大假山上建三层来青阁和皆绿山房东北角有一座大池绕池设文桂之舫午韵轩和蕉雨轩皆紧临水面互成对景东南角有一座小池掩在云墙之后两池通过环绕在假山东侧的溪流相连水脉相通中区采用前宅后园格局南部有宅门和大堂堂北设廊面向北部园林园中以山响草堂又名三峰草堂为主体分为南北两区堂南为开敞的平地绕着一湾溪流东西各跨一座小桥对面隔水是座大型石假山为珍贵的明代遗存假山下有石矶洞穴上有山路平台用黄石和湖石叠成下部近水及山洞底部用黄石规整古朴上部用湖石宛转多姿山顶树立三支石笋是当年三峰园旧物东侧的古柏是明代古树苍劲多姿为园景增色不少假山东侧设六角数鱼亭可俯临溪水观赏游鱼西侧贴墙设半亭位置较高可纵览园景山响草堂北侧是数级台地台上正中为书斋汲堂西侧为因巢亭京剧大师梅兰芳曾在此下榻东侧是小楼松吹阁可登阁临眺东区以建筑为主园景较为单调
02 学政试院
Xuezheng Examination Hall
清
级别 Level
第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
地址 Address
海陵区府前路府前路2号
类型 Type
古建筑/考试场所
门票 Ticket
30元
开放时间 Hours
8:00 — 17:30
中文原文

学政试院原为五代永宁宫旧址，南唐昇元三年（939年），烈祖李昪派迁杨行密子孙至泰州，建永宁宫。后周时，在永宁宫筑子城，建州治。明初，凤阳军抚使院因避水患迁至此地。

明万历二十九年（1601年），都御使李三才将其改作督察院。明末至清，为扬州府属八县考生员场所，即扬郡试院，由省学政主持考试，所以又称学政试院。民国初年，在这里设教育会与劝学所，后驻兵，称大营。抗日战争期间被日本宪兵队占据。

新中国成立后，泰州档案馆、团市委、市妇联、总工会、文化局、文联等机关团体先后设于试院办公。学政试院建筑群沿中轴线有四进院落，主体建筑依次为头门、仪门、四教堂、思补堂和上房。清光绪年间废科举，将后部东、西二楼，以及两厢考棚拆除，只留下头门、仪门和大堂。

1982年又拆除了仪门，故原建筑仅保留下头门和大堂。头门采用灰瓦硬山顶，宽五间，深两间，前后檐用五踩斗栱，前出向上翘曲的假昂，柱间梁枋上有花草、包袱图案清式彩绘，梁架间以明式一斗六升斗栱承托。

大堂"四教堂"也是灰瓦硬山顶，宽五间，前出深三檩的硬山顶前廊，殿身深七檩。脊檩下以一斗六升斗栱逐层承托。前檐采用带假昂的五踩斗栱，斗栱也是明代风格。正堂悬挂清乾隆督学款"四教堂"、知府衔知泰州事张兆鹿重修"墨书题记。

学政书院今为泰州科举院试博物馆，近年复建了其他建筑，大堂与仪门之间两侧为考棚，头门前的广场两侧有东、西辕门，辕门内有东、西吹鼓亭，头门对面是大照壁，照壁前东西两侧各竖一根旗杆。

· · · · ·
English

Xuezheng Examination Hall was originally the site of the Five Dynasties Yongning Palace; in the 3rd year of Shengyuan of the Southern Tang (939), Liezu Li Bian sent and relocated the descendants of Yang Xingmi to Taizhou, building Yongning Palace.

In the Later Zhou, a sub-city was built at Yongning Palace to establish the prefectural government.

In the early Ming, the Fengyang Military Commission moved here to avoid flood disasters.

In the 29th year of Wanli of the Ming (1601), Censor-in-Chief Li Sancai converted it into the Censorate.

From the late Ming to the Qing, it was the venue for the eight counties under Yangzhou Prefecture to take the student examination, i.e.

, the Yang Prefecture Examination Hall, with examinations presided over by the provincial education commissioner, hence also called Xuezheng Examination Hall.

In the early Republic of China, an education association and study-promotion office were set up here, later troops were stationed, called the Great Camp.

During the War of Resistance against Japan, it was occupied by the Japanese military police.

After the founding of New China, government organizations and groups such as the Taizhou Archives, Municipal Youth League Committee, Municipal Women's Federation, General Trade Union, Cultural Bureau, and Federation of Literary and Art Circles successively set up offices in the examination hall.

The Xuezheng Examination Hall building complex has four courtyards along the central axis; the main buildings are in sequence: the Outer Gate, Ceremonial Gate, Sijiao Hall, Sibu Hall, and Upper Quarters.

During the Guangxu reign of the Qing, the imperial examination was abolished, and the rear east and west two-story buildings, as well as the two-side examination sheds, were demolished, leaving only the Outer Gate, Ceremonial Gate, and Main Hall.

In 1982, the Ceremonial Gate was also demolished, so the original buildings only retain the Outer Gate and Main Hall.

The Outer Gate adopts a grey-tile flush-gable roof, five bays wide and two bays deep, with five-step bracket sets on the front and rear eaves, with upward-curving fake ang (bracket arms) protruding forward; on the beams and lintels between columns are Qing-style painted decorations of flowers, plants, and cloth-bundle patterns; between the beam frames are Ming-style one-dou-six-sheng bracket sets for support.

The Main Hall 'Sijiao Hall' also has a grey-tile flush-gable roof, five bays wide, with a front porch of flush-gable roof three purlins deep protruding forward, and the hall body is seven purlins deep.

Under the ridge purlin are one-dou-six-sheng bracket sets supporting layer by layer.

The front eaves adopt five-step bracket sets with fake ang, and the bracket sets are also in Ming style.

The main hall hangs an ink inscription of the Qing Qianlong education commissioner's 'Sijiao Hall' and 'Prefect-rank Taizhou Magistrate Zhang Zhaolu rebuilt' in ink calligraphy.

Xuezheng Academy is today the Taizhou Imperial Examination Hall Museum; other buildings were rebuilt in recent years, with examination sheds on both sides between the main hall and ceremonial gate, east and west yuan gates on both sides of the square in front of the outer gate, east and west drum-and-wind pavilions inside the yuan gates, a large screen wall opposite the outer gate, and a flagpole erected on each of the east and west sides in front of the screen wall.

建筑要点 / Key Features
学政试院原为五代永宁宫旧址南唐昇元三年939年烈祖李昪派迁杨行密子孙至泰州建永宁宫后周时在永宁宫筑子城建州治明初凤阳军抚使院因避水患迁至此地明万历二十九年1601年都御使李三才将其改作督察院明末至清为扬州府属八县考生员场所即扬郡试院由省学政主持考试所以又称学政试院民国初年在这里设教育会与劝学所后驻兵称大营抗日战争期间被日本宪兵队占据新中国成立后泰州档案馆团市委市妇联总工会文化局文联等机关团体先后设于试院办公学政试院建筑群沿中轴线有四进院落主体建筑依次为头门仪门四教堂思补堂和上房清光绪年间废科举将后部东西二楼以及两厢考棚拆除只留下头门仪门和大堂1982年又拆除了仪门故原建筑仅保留下头门和大堂头门采用灰瓦硬山顶宽五间深两间前后檐用五踩斗栱前出向上翘曲的假昂柱间梁枋上有花草包袱图案清式彩绘梁架间以明式一斗六升斗栱承托大堂四教堂也是灰瓦硬山顶宽五间前出深三檩的硬山顶前廊殿身深七檩脊檩下以一斗六升斗栱逐层承托前檐采用带假昂的五踩斗栱斗栱也是明代风格正堂悬挂清乾隆督学款四教堂知府衔知泰州事张兆鹿重修墨书题记学政书院今为泰州科举院试博物馆近年复建了其他建筑大堂与仪门之间两侧为考棚头门前的广场两侧有东
03 泰州城隍庙
City God Temple of Taizhou
明—清
级别 Level
第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
地址 Address
海陵区邑庙街22号
类型 Type
古建筑/城隍庙
门票 Ticket
8:00 — 17:30
开放时间 Hours
8:00 — 17:30
中文原文

泰州城隍庙又称邑庙，位于泰州老城东北隅邑庙街，是江苏省境内现存最大、保存最完好的城隍庙。

此庙相传始建于唐，北宋元符二年（1099年）重建，建炎元年（1127年）毁于兵燹，南宋重建，元兵南下时又焚于火，明洪武年间再建。

明正统四年（1439年）、万历二十七年（1599年）两次翻新建，清雍正初年、咸丰四年（1854年）重修。

清代城隍庙规模盛大，有山门、四值功曹殿、审事厅、大殿与后宫五进，左右各有配殿。

1929年神像被毁，1953年拆除四值功曹殿和后宫，1958年神像全部被毁，一度改为医院、民宅，所幸主体建筑未损，尚保留山门、审事厅、大殿和左右厢房等。

山门宽五间，深两间，灰瓦硬山顶，门前两侧出八字影壁。入门有青岗条石甬道通向审事厅，审事厅建于明代，灰瓦硬山顶，宽五间，深十檩，构架分为前轩后堂两部分，为圆堂半磕头轩做法。

前部四檩为轩廊，卷棚天花，后部七檩为明堂；从内部看为碰檐做法，外观则为整体屋面，用料粗壮，做工考究，是泰州保存较好的明代厅堂建筑。

大殿建于明末清初，宽五间，灰色筒瓦硬山顶，前出四檩硬山勾连搭前檐，后部殿身为单檐歇山顶。

· · · · ·
English

Taizhou City God Temple, also called Yimiao (County Temple), is located at Yimiao Street in the northeast corner of old Taizhou city, and is the largest and best-preserved City God Temple existing in Jiangsu Province.

This temple is said to have been first built in the Tang, rebuilt in the 2nd year of Yuanfu of the Northern Song (1099), destroyed by war in the 1st year of Jianyan (1127), rebuilt in the Southern Song, burned again when Yuan troops marched south, and rebuilt in the Hongwu reign of the Ming.

It was rebuilt twice in the 4th year of Zhengtong of the Ming (1439) and the 27th year of Wanli (1599), and repaired in the early Yongzheng and the 4th year of Xianfeng (1854) of the Qing.

The Qing City God Temple was grand in scale, with five courtyards: mountain gate, Four Duty Officials Hall, Trial Hall, Main Hall, and Rear Palace, with side halls on left and right.

In 1929 the statues were destroyed; in 1953 the Four Duty Officials Hall and Rear Palace were demolished; in 1958 all statues were destroyed, and it was once converted into a hospital and private residences; fortunately the main buildings were not damaged, still retaining the mountain gate, Trial Hall, Main Hall, and left and right wing rooms etc.

The mountain gate is five bays wide and two bays deep, with a grey-tile flush-gable roof, with splayed screen walls on both sides in front of the gate.

Entering the gate, a bluestone flagstone path leads to the Trial Hall; the Trial Hall was built in the Ming, with a grey-tile flush-gable roof, five bays wide and ten purlins deep, with the frame divided into front porch and rear hall two parts, adopting the round-hall half-kowtow porch method.

The front four purlins are a porch corridor with a curved ceiling; the rear seven purlins are the main hall; from the inside it appears as a touching-eaves method, while from the outside it is an integral roof, with sturdy materials and exquisite workmanship, a well-preserved Ming hall building in Taizhou.

The Main Hall was built in the late Ming and early Qing, five bays wide, with a grey tube-tile flush-gable roof, with a four-purlin flush-gable interlocking front eave protruding forward, and the rear hall body as a single-eave hip-and-gable roof.

建筑要点 / Key Features
泰州城隍庙又称邑庙位于泰州老城东北隅邑庙街是江苏省境内现存最大保存最完好的城隍庙此庙相传始建于唐北宋元符二年1099年重建建炎元年1127年毁于兵燹南宋重建元兵南下时又焚于火明洪武年间再建明正统四年1439年万历二十七年1599年两次翻新建清雍正初年咸丰四年1854年重修清代城隍庙规模盛大有山门四值功曹殿审事厅大殿与后宫五进左右各有配殿1929年神像被毁1953年拆除四值功曹殿和后宫1958年神像全部被毁一度改为医院民宅所幸主体建筑未损尚保留山门审事厅大殿和左右厢房等山门宽五间深两间灰瓦硬山顶门前两侧出八字影壁入门有青岗条石甬道通向审事厅审事厅建于明代灰瓦硬山顶宽五间深十檩构架分为前轩后堂两部分为圆堂半磕头轩做法前部四檩为轩廊卷棚天花后部七檩为明堂从内部看为碰檐做法外观则为整体屋面用料粗壮做工考究是泰州保存较好的明代厅堂建筑大殿建于明末清初宽五间灰色筒瓦硬山顶前出四檩硬山勾连搭前檐后部殿身为单檐歇山顶
04 南山寺大雄宝殿
Hall of Mahavira in Nanshan Temple
明
级别 Level
第四批省级文物保护单位（1995年）
地址 Address
海陵区南山寺路1号
类型 Type
古建筑/佛教寺院
中文原文

南山寺位于泰州老城东南隅，始建于唐乾符三年（876年），朝廷赐额"护国寺"，北宋治平元年（1064年）改为"资福禅院"。

北宋政和七年（1117年）改为道观"神霄玉清万寿宫"，北宋建炎元年（1127年）恢复为"资福禅寺"，南宋淳熙十年（1183年）寺毁，南宋绍熙年间（1190—1194）重建。

明洪武十五年（1382年）改为"祝圣道场"，1958年后寺院被逐渐拆除，仅存明天启六年（1626年）重建的大雄宝殿。

大殿采用重檐庑殿顶，正脊不做推山，宽五间，深六间。殿中金柱用楠木制成，柱头有卷杀，上插较细的木柱，承金檩，为插柱造，蜀柱上安叉手。枋为琴面梁，梁头下用丁头栱。梁枋上有菱形锦地格和缠枝花彩画。

大殿的等级较高，脊檩间枋下有明天顺七年（1463年）、清道光年间及1957年重修的题记。

梁架结构为明代中期风格，某些构件和做法带有宋元时期的特征，但由于近年维修安装了平棋天花，仅能看到梁枋间彩画，屋顶梁架已不得见。

· · · · ·
English

Nanshan Temple is located in the southeast corner of old Taizhou city, first built in the 3rd year of Qianfu of the Tang (876), with the court bestowing the plaque 'Huguo Temple' (Nation-Protecting Temple); in the 1st year of Zhiping of the Northern Song (1064) it was renamed 'Zifu Chan Monastery.

' In the 7th year of Zhenghe of the Northern Song (1117) it was converted into a Daoist temple 'Shenxiao Yuqing Wanshou Palace'; in the 1st year of Jianyan of the Northern Song (1127) it was restored to 'Zifu Chan Temple'; in the 10th year of Chunxi of the Southern Song (1183) the temple was destroyed, and rebuilt during the Shaoxi reign of the Southern Song (1190-1194).

In the 15th year of Hongwu of the Ming (1382) it was renamed 'Zhusheng Daochang' (Blessing the Sage Ritual Site); after 1958 the temple was gradually demolished, leaving only the Mahavira Hall rebuilt in the 6th year of Tianqi of the Ming (1626).

The Main Hall adopts a double-eave hip roof, with no mountain-push on the main ridge, five bays wide and six bays deep.

The golden pillars in the hall are made of nanmu, with entasis at the column tops, with thinner wooden pillars inserted above to support the golden purlins, adopting the inserted-pillar method, with crossed hands (chashou) installed on the subsidiary pillars.

The lintels are qinmian (lute-face) beams, with dingtou bracket sets under the beam heads.

On the beams and lintels are diamond-pattern lattice and interlocking-flower painted decorations.

The Main Hall has a relatively high grade; under the lintels between the ridge purlins are inscriptions of repairs in the 7th year of Tianshun of the Ming (1463), the Daoguang reign of the Qing, and 1957.

The beam-frame structure is in the mid-Ming style, with some components and methods bearing characteristics of the Song-Yuan period; however, due to the installation of a coffered ceiling during recent repairs, only the painted decorations between beams and lintels can be seen, and the roof beam frame is no longer visible.

建筑要点 / Key Features
南山寺位于泰州老城东南隅始建于唐乾符三年876年朝廷赐额护国寺北宋治平元年1064年改为资福禅院北宋政和七年1117年改为道观神霄玉清万寿宫北宋建炎元年1127年恢复为资福禅寺南宋淳熙十年1183年寺毁南宋绍熙年间11901194重建明洪武十五年1382年改为祝圣道场1958年后寺院被逐渐拆除仅存明天启六年1626年重建的大雄宝殿大殿采用重檐庑殿顶正脊不做推山宽五间深六间殿中金柱用楠木制成柱头有卷杀上插较细的木柱承金檩为插柱造蜀柱上安叉手枋为琴面梁梁头下用丁头栱梁枋上有菱形锦地格和缠枝花彩画大殿的等级较高脊檩间枋下有明天顺七年1463年清道光年间及1957年重修的题记梁架结构为明代中期风格某些构件和做法带有宋元时期的特征但由于近年维修安装了平棋天花仅能看到梁枋间彩画屋顶梁架已不得见

Confucius Temple (Chongru Shrine)

类型 Type

门票 Ticket

开放时间 Hours
