中文原文

崇儒祠现为王艮与泰州学派纪念馆，位于泰州老城西北，始建于明万历四年（1576年），是祭祀泰州学派创始人王艮的祠堂。王艮（1483—1541）号心斋，是泰州安丰场（今属东台市）人，出身于盐民家庭，幼年辍学，自学成为儒学大师。

他曾在泰州安定书院和立诚社讲学，创立"淮南格物"学说，认为"百姓日用即道"，在平民阶层影响广泛。他去世后，杭州府、应天府、宁国府、扬州府、泰县姜堰和海安等地都为他建造了祠堂。

明嘉靖四十三年（1564年）泰州在安定胡先生祠合祀王艮，明万历四年（1476年）建立专祀王艮的崇儒祠，其后多此重修。现存门厅、立本堂、乐学堂和贤人堂，南北共四进，西侧附设园圃。门厅宽三间，灰瓦硬山顶，两侧出八字影壁。

进入院落为仪门，宽三间，门在脊檩下。入仪门为祠堂，始建于明，清嘉庆年间曾大修，三间硬山顶，出前廊，平面布局、柱础和部分梁架仍为明代遗构。堂前檐东廊壁间有《心斋王先生祠堂记》碑，保存完好，是明代原物。

西廊壁间有《崇儒祠记》，为残碑修补而成，檐下有"乐学堂"横匾。最后一进也是三间硬山顶，悬"先觉堂"横匾，内祀王艮像。祠堂西侧新辟小园，沿墙面设置长廊，园内布置曲水、花石、修竹，设王艮讲学立像。

· · · · ·
English

Chongru Shrine is now the Wang Gen and Taizhou School Memorial Hall, located in the northwest of old Taizhou city, first built in the 4th year of Wanli of the Ming (1576), and is a shrine for sacrificing to Wang Gen, founder of the Taizhou School.

Wang Gen (1483-1541), hao Xinzhai, was from Anfengchang in Taizhou (now belonging to Dongtai City), born into a salt-worker family; he dropped out of school in childhood and self-studied to become a master of Confucianism.

He once lectured at Anding Academy and Licheng Society in Taizhou, founding the 'Huainan Gewu' (Huainan Investigation of Things) doctrine, believing that 'the daily use of the common people is the Way,' with wide influence among the common people.

After his death, Hangzhou Prefecture, Yingtian Prefecture, Ningguo Prefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, Jiangyan in Tai County, and Haian etc.all built shrines for him.

In the 43rd year of Jiajing of the Ming (1564), Taizhou jointly sacrificed to Wang Gen at the Anding Mr.

Hu Shrine; in the 4th year of Wanli of the Ming (1476), Chongru Shrine dedicated to Wang Gen was established, and subsequently repaired many times.

The existing gate hall, Liben Hall, Xuetang Hall, and Xianren Hall form four courtyards north-south, with a garden attached on the west side.

The gate hall is three bays wide, with a grey-tile flush-gable roof, with splayed screen walls on both sides.

Entering the courtyard is the Ceremonial Gate, three bays wide, with the door under the ridge purlin.

Entering the Ceremonial Gate is the shrine, first built in the Ming and heavily repaired during the Jiaqing reign of the Qing, three bays with a flush-gable roof and a front porch; the plan layout, column bases, and part of the beam frame are still Ming Dynasty remains.

On the east corridor wall under the front eave of the hall is the stele 'Record of the Shrine of Mr.Wang Xinzhai,' well preserved and an original Ming artifact.

On the west corridor wall is the 'Record of Chongru Shrine,' made from a repaired broken stele; under the eave is the horizontal plaque 'Xuetang Hall.

' The last courtyard is also three bays with a flush-gable roof, hanging the horizontal plaque 'Xianjue Hall' (Hall of the First Awakened), with a statue of Wang Gen inside for sacrifice.

West of the shrine, a small garden has been newly opened, with a long corridor along the wall; inside the garden are arranged winding water, flower rocks, and tall bamboos, with a standing statue of Wang Gen lecturing.

建筑要点 / Key Features
崇儒祠现为王艮与泰州学派纪念馆位于泰州老城西北始建于明万历四年1576年是祭祀泰州学派创始人王艮的祠堂王艮14831541号心斋是泰州安丰场今属东台市人出身于盐民家庭幼年辍学自学成为儒学大师他曾在泰州安定书院和立诚社讲学创立淮南格物学说认为百姓日用即道在平民阶层影响广泛他去世后杭州府应天府宁国府扬州府泰县姜堰和海安等地都为他建造了祠堂明嘉靖四十三年1564年泰州在安定胡先生祠合祀王艮明万历四年1476年建立专祀王艮的崇儒祠其后多此重修现存门厅立本堂乐学堂和贤人堂南北共四进西侧附设园圃门厅宽三间灰瓦硬山顶两侧出八字影壁进入院落为仪门宽三间门在脊檩下入仪门为祠堂始建于明清嘉庆年间曾大修三间硬山顶出前廊平面布局柱础和部分梁架仍为明代遗构堂前檐东廊壁间有心斋王先生祠堂记碑保存完好是明代原物西廊壁间有崇儒祠记为残碑修补而成檐下有乐学堂横匾最后一进也是三间硬山顶悬先觉堂横匾内祀王艮像祠堂西侧新辟小园沿墙面设置长廊园内布置曲水花石修竹设王艮讲学立像
06 北山寺大殿
Main Hall of Beishan Temple
明
级别 Level
第五批省级文物保护单位（2002年）
地址 Address
海陵区扬州路92号
类型 Type
古建筑/佛教寺院
中文原文

北山寺在泰州老城外向北一公里处，始建于唐宝历元年（825年），全称北山开化禅寺，古称开化寺、独佛寺。传说唐代此地有百尺高塔，百口水井，南宋建炎年间毁于兵燹，百口水井仅余卓锡泉。

南宋淳熙年间重建寺庙，明弘治年间重铸铜钟，明天启六年（1626年）重建大雄宝殿。据清代文献记载，因海陵城北地势低下，遂将寺名改为"北山"，以"阜地气，壮郡形"。

清顺治四年（1647年）整修寺院，顺治十八年（1661年）重铸铜钟，康熙初年在大雄宝殿后建大悲楼，道光年间寺又衰落，咸丰年间重修，清光绪四年（1878年）扩建为大寺，在泰州规模仅次于光孝寺。

抗日战争时期二殿被日机炸毁，1942年修茸大雄宝殿，后被军队占用。1960年拆除大悲楼，"文革"时期铜钟被毁，1984年拆除头殿和大部分寮屋，现只存大雄宝殿。

大雄宝殿重建于明天启六年（1626年），清乾隆五十六年（1791年）、咸丰二年（1852年）和1942年多次重修。

大殿坐北朝南，宽五间，深九檩，黑瓦重檐歇山顶，出前廊，覆盆柱础，梁架间承以斗栱，脊檩蜀柱左右用叉手。大殿西北角的卓锡泉已湮没难寻。

· · · · ·
English

Beishan Temple is located one kilometer north outside old Taizhou city, first built in the 1st year of Baoli of the Tang (825), fully called Beishan Kaihua Chan Temple, anciently called Kaihua Temple and Dufo Temple.

Legend says that in the Tang there was a hundred-chi-high pagoda and a hundred water wells here; during the Jianyan reign of the Southern Song it was destroyed by war, leaving only the Zhuoxi Spring among the hundred wells.

The temple was rebuilt during the Chunxi reign of the Southern Song, the bronze bell was recast during the Hongzhi reign of the Ming, and the Mahavira Hall was rebuilt in the 6th year of Tianqi of the Ming (1626).

According to Qing Dynasty documents, because the terrain north of Hailing city was low, the temple name was changed to 'Beishan' (North Mountain) to 'enrich the earth qi and strengthen the prefecture's form.

' In the 4th year of Shunzhi of the Qing (1647) the temple was renovated; in the 18th year of Shunzhi (1661) the bronze bell was recast; in the early Kangxi, the Dabei (Great Compassion) Building was built behind the Mahavira Hall; during the Daoguang reign the temple declined again; it was repaired during the Xianfeng reign; in the 4th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1878) it was expanded into a large temple, second in scale only to Guangxiao Temple in Taizhou.

During the War of Resistance against Japan, the second hall was bombed and destroyed by Japanese aircraft; in 1942 the Mahavira Hall was repaired, later occupied by the military.

In 1960 the Dabei Building was demolished; during the Cultural Revolution the bronze bell was destroyed; in 1984 the front hall and most monk quarters were demolished; now only the Mahavira Hall remains.

The Mahavira Hall was rebuilt in the 6th year of Tianqi of the Ming (1626), and repaired many times in the 56th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1791), the 2nd year of Xianfeng (1852), and 1942.

The Main Hall faces south, five bays wide and nine purlins deep, with a black-tile double-eave hip-and-gable roof, with a front porch, inverted-basin column bases, bracket sets supporting between beam frames, and crossed hands on left and right of the ridge purlin subsidiary pillars.

The Zhuoxi Spring at the northwest corner of the Main Hall has been buried and is hard to find.

建筑要点 / Key Features
北山寺在泰州老城外向北一公里处始建于唐宝历元年825年全称北山开化禅寺古称开化寺独佛寺传说唐代此地有百尺高塔百口水井南宋建炎年间毁于兵燹百口水井仅余卓锡泉南宋淳熙年间重建寺庙明弘治年间重铸铜钟明天启六年1626年重建大雄宝殿据清代文献记载因海陵城北地势低下遂将寺名改为北山以阜地气壮郡形清顺治四年1647年整修寺院顺治十八年1661年重铸铜钟康熙初年在大雄宝殿后建大悲楼道光年间寺又衰落咸丰年间重修清光绪四年1878年扩建为大寺在泰州规模仅次于光孝寺抗日战争时期二殿被日机炸毁1942年修茸大雄宝殿后被军队占用1960年拆除大悲楼文革时期铜钟被毁1984年拆除头殿和大部分寮屋现只存大雄宝殿大雄宝殿重建于明天启六年1626年清乾隆五十六年1791年咸丰二年1852年和1942年多次重修大殿坐北朝南宽五间深九檩黑瓦重檐歇山顶出前廊覆盆柱础梁架间承以斗栱脊檩蜀柱左右用叉手大殿西北角的卓锡泉已湮没难寻
07 周氏住宅（吴氏住宅）
Zhou's Family Residence (Wu's Family Residence)
清
级别 Level
第五批省级文物保护单位（2002年）
地址 Address
海陵区涵西街17号
类型 Type
古建筑/民居
中文原文

周氏住宅在泰州老城稻河古街区西侧，始建于清咸丰年间，原为富绅周彬的住宅，周氏传两代即败落，住宅转售给曾任广东监盐大使的吴希彭。吴希彭认为周氏没落与屋宅风水有关，清同治年间对住宅进行改造与扩建。

拆除原东向大门，改为东南方向，在门前新建高大影壁，门内立砖雕佛龛，并重建了大厅、大小堂屋、穿堂东西花厅、照厅中西式蝴蝶厅、花园、厢房和厨房等。改建工程浩大，建筑材料上乘，雕饰精细考究，为泰州现存规模最大的民居院落，号称九十九间半。新中国成立后住宅收归国有，曾作为机关、学校，沦为居民杂院。2009年修缮一新。

住宅坐北向南，包括东、西四路，14处天井，10余座院落。东南角的大门宽三间，雕花门楼，两侧为磨砖八字影壁。门内为小天井，内立带福祠的照壁。天井北侧为中部轴线，有男厅、女厅和堂屋三进院落。

男厅高大宽敞，采用抬梁式结构，五架梁，分为前后两部分，前为船篷式卷棚，后为仿古海棠如意卷棚，前后檐下都安装玻璃隔扇门。过天井为女厅，与男厅梁架结构相同，采用前后卷棚。男、女厅之间的庭院东侧有便门和厢房，进出女厅需走东侧便门，避免从男厅经过。女厅后部为堂屋，前后也用隔扇门。男厅西南侧有雕花仪门，门内为第二条轴线，依次布置照厅、厅屋、穿堂和堂屋，建筑比东侧更高大。

再向西为第三路前后四进院落和第四路西花园花厅。花厅为歇山顶，梁架有彩绘，内用彩色水磨石地板，中部刻水磨石拼花图案，花厅东北角有一口水井。

· · · · ·
English

Zhou's Family Residence is located west of the Daohe Ancient Block in old Taizhou city, first built during the Xianfeng reign of the Qing, originally the residence of wealthy gentry Zhou Bin; the Zhou family declined after two generations, and the residence was resold to Wu Xipeng, who had served as Guangdong Salt Supervisor.

Wu Xipeng believed the Zhou family's decline was related to the house's feng shui, and during the Tongzhi reign of the Qing he renovated and expanded the residence.

The original east-facing main gate was demolished and changed to the southeast direction; a tall screen wall was newly built in front of the gate, a brick-carved Buddhist niche was erected inside the gate, and the main hall, large and small main rooms, corridor halls, east and west flower halls, reception hall, Chinese-Western butterfly hall, garden, wing rooms, and kitchen etc.

were rebuilt.

The renovation project was vast, with high-quality building materials and exquisite carvings, making it the largest existing folk residence compound in Taizhou, known as 'ninety-nine and a half rooms.

' After the founding of New China, the residence was nationalized, once used as government offices and schools, and became a mixed residential courtyard.It was renovated anew in 2009.

The residence faces south, including east and west four routes, 14 courtyards, and over 10 compounds.

The main gate at the southeast corner is three bays wide, with a carved gate tower and ground-brick splayed screen walls on both sides.

Inside the gate is a small courtyard, with a screen wall bearing a blessing shrine.North of the courtyard is the central axis, with three courtyards: male hall, female hall, and main room.

The male hall is tall and spacious, adopting a post-and-lintel structure with five-frame beams, divided into front and rear parts: the front is a boat-awning curved ceiling, the rear is an antique crabapple-ruyi curved ceiling, with glass lattice doors installed under both front and rear eaves.

Across the courtyard is the female hall, with the same beam-frame structure as the male hall, adopting front and rear curved ceilings.

On the east side of the courtyard between the male and female halls are side doors and wing rooms; entering and exiting the female hall requires taking the east side door, avoiding passing through the male hall.

The rear of the female hall is the main room, also using lattice doors front and rear.

On the southwest side of the male hall is a carved ceremonial gate; inside the gate is the second axis, sequentially arranging the reception hall, hall room, corridor hall, and main room, with buildings taller and larger than the east side.

Further west are the third route with four front-and-rear courtyards and the fourth route west garden flower hall.

The flower hall has a hip-and-gable roof, with painted decorations on the beam frame, colored terrazzo flooring inside, with a terrazzo mosaic pattern carved in the center, and a water well at the northeast corner of the flower hall.

08 上池斋药店
Shangchizhai Pharmacy
清—民国
级别 Level
第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
地址 Address
昭阳镇文峰社区东城外大街10号
类型 Type
古建筑/药店
中文原文

清雍正初年，扬州药商方石川在兴化东城外大街购得旧屋改建为"上池斋"中药店，集名医坐诊、中药制作和销售于一体，是江淮地区店史最长、最负盛名的一家药店。店名取自《史记·扁鹊传》："饮是以上池之水。

"1932年业主方少泉为增强竞争力，参照上海等地药店式样，改建店面，用进口瓷砖等装饰地坪和柜台立面，并在店堂西壁安装进口玻璃镜面，使药店显得洋气而亮堂。1956年公私合营后，上池斋药店隶属兴化县医药公司，仍以"上池斋"为店名。"文革"期间改称长春药店，1983年恢复原名。

药店采用砖木结构，坐南朝北，前后两进，前为店铺，后为作坊。店铺是两幢二层楼房，面宽8.3米，进深15米，硬山顶。

底层为铺面，由石库门进入，东侧设曲尺柜台，竖有清代制作的木质抱柱招牌，上书"本斋拣选药料遵古炮制发兑"字样。柜台内依墙立有药柜山架。柜台外侧贴青花瓷方块，地坪用彩花水泥方砖，皆为1932年店主进口来的材料。

店堂立柱挂有"水饮上池""采芝寿世""橘井流芳"和"杏林长春"等牌匾，南北之间有大型镂空木雕挂落，内容为鹿鹤同春、葫芦缠枝等图案，前后隔而不断。店内靠南墙设后柜。东南隅朝东开拱券门，门外有一口古井，方便取水熬药；西北角外侧有平台，台上建四角方亭，用于晾晒药材。楼上为药材库房，四围壁板，中为回廊，以木质雕花栏杆围护，既增加了店堂采光，又便于库房内药材通风透气。前进店堂和后进作坊相互贯通。

作坊为三开间七檩平房，硬山顶，穿斗式结构，柱下用木础，系明代建筑。这里是加工药材之处，尚存部分传统制药工具。作坊向南有天井，通向主体建筑西侧的小花圃。

· · · · ·
English

In the early Yongzheng reign of the Qing, Yangzhou medicine merchant Fang Shichuan purchased an old house on Dongchengwai Dajie in Xinghua and converted it into the 'Shangchizhai' Chinese medicine pharmacy, integrating famous doctors' consultations, Chinese medicine production, and sales into one; it is the pharmacy with the longest history and greatest reputation in the Jianghuai region.

The store name is taken from 'Records of the Grand Historian · Biography of Bian Que': 'Drink this with water from the upper pool.

' In 1932, owner Fang Shaoquan, to enhance competitiveness,参照 the style of pharmacies in Shanghai and other places, renovated the storefront, using imported tiles etc.

to decorate the floor and counter facade, and installed imported glass mirrors on the west wall of the store hall, making the pharmacy look foreign-style and bright.

After public-private partnership in 1956, Shangchizhai Pharmacy was subordinate to the Xinghua County Pharmaceutical Company, still using 'Shangchizhai' as the store name.

During the Cultural Revolution it was renamed Changchun Pharmacy, and restored its original name in 1983.

The pharmacy adopts a brick-wood structure, facing south with north at the back, with two front-and-rear courtyards: the front is the shop, the rear is the workshop.

The shop is two two-story buildings, 8.3 meters wide and 15 meters deep, with a flush-gable roof.

The ground floor is the storefront, entered through a stone-framed door; on the east side is a carpenter's-square counter, with a Qing-made wooden pillar-hugging signboard vertically inscribed with 'This store selects medicinal materials, processes according to ancient methods, and distributes.

' Inside the counter against the wall stand medicine cabinet mountain racks.

Outside the counter are pasted blue-and-white porcelain squares, and the floor uses colored cement square bricks—all materials imported by the store owner in 1932.

The store hall pillars hang plaques such as 'Water Drunk from Upper Pool,' 'Gathering Mushrooms for Longevity,' 'Orange Well Flowing Fragrance,' and 'Apricot Forest Eternal Spring'; between north and south is a large openwork wood-carved valance, with patterns of deer and crane sharing spring, gourd interlocking branches etc.

, separating front and rear without blocking.Inside the store against the south wall is a rear counter.

In the southeast corner, an arched door opens east; outside the door is an ancient well, convenient for fetching water to boil medicine; outside the northwest corner is a platform, on which a four-corner square pavilion is built for drying medicinal materials.

Upstairs is the medicinal material warehouse, with wall panels on all sides and a corridor in the middle, enclosed by wooden carved railings—both increasing the store hall's lighting and facilitating ventilation of medicinal materials in the warehouse.

The front store hall and rear workshop are interconnected.

The workshop is a three-bay seven-purlin single-story house, with a flush-gable roof and a column-and-tie structure, with wooden column bases—being a Ming Dynasty building.

This is where medicinal materials are processed, with some traditional medicine-making tools still surviving.

South of the workshop is a courtyard, leading to a small flower garden west of the main building.

建筑要点 / Key Features
清雍正初年扬州药商方石川在兴化东城外大街购得旧屋改建为上池斋中药店集名医坐诊中药制作和销售于一体是江淮地区店史最长最负盛名的一家药店店名取自史记扁鹊传饮是以上池之水1932年业主方少泉为增强竞争力参照上海等地药店式样改建店面用进口瓷砖等装饰地坪和柜台立面并在店堂西壁安装进口玻璃镜面使药店显得洋气而亮堂1956年公私合营后上池斋药店隶属兴化县医药公司仍以上池斋为店名文革期间改称长春药店1983年恢复原名药店采用砖木结构坐南朝北前后两进前为店铺后为作坊店铺是两幢二层楼房面宽8.3米进深15米硬山顶底层为铺面由石库门进入东侧设曲尺柜台竖有清代制作的木质抱柱招牌上书本斋拣选药料遵古炮制发兑字样柜台内依墙立有药柜山架柜台外侧贴青花瓷方块地坪用彩花水泥方砖皆为1932年店主进口来的材料店堂立柱挂有水饮上池采芝寿世橘井流芳和杏林长春等牌匾南北之间有大型镂空木雕挂落内容为鹿鹤同春葫芦缠枝等图案前后隔而不断店内靠南墙设后柜东南隅朝东开拱券门门外有一口古井方便取水熬药西北角外侧有平台台上建四角方亭用于晾晒药材楼上为药材库房四围壁板中为回廊以木质雕花栏杆围护既增加了店堂采光又便于库房内药材通风透气前进店堂和

南通

Nantong
11
处建筑

地区概述 / Regional Overview

南通位于长江入海口北岸，古称通州，是中国近代第一城，由张謇先生一手规划建设。南通古建筑兼具江南园林之秀与近代建筑之新，南通博物苑是中国人自建的第一座公共博物馆，濠南别业是张謇故居，大生纱厂是中国近代民族工业的发祥地。

Nantong is located on the north bank of the Yangtze River estuary, anciently called Tongzhou, known as China's first modern city, planned and built single-handedly by Mr.Zhang Jian.

Nantong's ancient architecture combines the elegance of Jiangnan gardens with the novelty of modern architecture; Nantong Museum is the first public museum built by Chinese themselves, Haonan Villa is Zhang Jian's former residence, and Dasheng Cotton Mill is the birthplace of China's modern national industry.

01 南通博物苑（含张謇墓）
Nantong Museum (including Tomb of Zhang Jian)
清—民国
级别 Level
第三批全国重点文物保护单位（1988年），2001年并入张謇墓园为第五批国保单位
地址 Address
南通市崇川区濠南路19号
类型 Type
博物馆/园林/墓葬
门票 Ticket
免费开放
开放时间 Hours
9:00 — 17:00（周一闭馆）
中文原文

1. 南通博物苑：南通博物苑位于南通古城护城河"濠河"的东南角，清光绪三十一年（1905年）张謇将建设中的通州师范学校公共植物园规建为"博物苑"，张謇自任总理，聘孙钺为主任，是中国人自建的第一座公共博物馆。抗日战争期间博物苑被日军占为马厩，只转移走部分文物，大部分散失。

新中国成立后修复改称为"南通博物馆"，原博物苑园林部分划归人民公园。1984年恢复南通博物苑原名，1999年将人民公园并入博物苑，恢复为初创时期的格局。南通博物苑采用展馆与园林相结合的形式，室内陈列与露天展览并重。博物苑沿主轴线建有南、中、北三馆。

南馆是主要展馆，建于1906年，坐南朝北，为二层砖木洋楼，前出半圆形露台。原名矿物陈列室楼，后称博物馆，陈列天产、历史、美术和教育四部。楼上为历史文物，楼下为动物、植物和矿物标本。在二楼的半圆形月台上，悬挂张謇手书对联："设为庠序学校以教，多识鸟兽草木之名。"此联也是张謇创办博物苑的宗旨。

馆北两侧各有一座亭子，陈列古玄妙观的三清塑像。中馆建于1906年，初为测候所，是三间平房，中央顶部有平台，上置气象观测仪器，是中国最早的气象观测机构。1914年测候所迁至农校，建筑师孙支厦在平台上增建气楼，中馆成为金石碑帖陈列室。

北馆为二层歇山顶砖木小楼，建于1911年。原计划陈列金石书画，建设期间得到鲸鱼骨架，于是进行改建，楼下陈列鲸鱼骨架，还有许多动物的骨骼标本和化石，楼上用特制的格屏陈列名家书画。北馆西侧为国秀坛，建于1907年，又名国粹坛。

中部叠太湖石假山，立"美人石"，石上刻有张謇的记文。坛内散置各地的石材，以示中国物产之丰富。坛内栽植名品牡丹、兰蕙等珍贵花卉，坛外种植不同品种和产地的绿竹。坛南是1908年建造的国秀亭，曾改造为竹石陈列处，展览各种名贵竹石标本。坛西北原有三角形金鱼池和人造瀑布。

苑内还有苑事室、藤东水榭、国秀亭、相禽阁和花竹平安馆，以及假山、水池、兽室、鸟室、风车和水车等园林设施，实现了现代博物馆与园林的完美结合。2. 张謇墓园：张謇墓园位于崇川区南郊路150号，2001年并入南通博物苑成为第五批国保单位。张謇，号啬庵，晚年自号啬翁，世人敬称啬公。

该墓始建于1923年，张謇亲自选址，1926年他去世后归葬啬园，两年后家人树铜像，建飨堂。1935年张謇独子张孝若去世，葬在张謇墓东侧，前立"南通张公子墓"石碑。抗战期间墓园逐渐荒废，新中国成立后修整。

1956年张氏后人在墓园增建"憩厅"，1958年更名为"南郊公园"。"文革"期间张謇墓被毁，墓穴被挖开，石阙被拉倒，铜像也被砸碎。1976年修整墓园，1983年原地重建张氏父子墓茔并重建墓阙。

张謇墓为方形混凝土灵台，高2米，四周有混凝土浇制栏杆。墓椁位于灵台中央，长方形，后置方座墓碑，高3米，上刻"南通张謇先生墓"。1985年"南郊公园"改称"啬园"，重立铜像。园中的飨堂、憩堂现为张謇生平业绩陈列室。

3. 濠南别业：濠南别业位于博物苑东北角，1914年张謇委托孙支厦参照北京农事试验场的畅观楼设计，1915年建成。建筑坐北朝南，高三层，用青砖砌筑，红砖装饰拱券、线脚，上为红色铁皮屋顶，开老虎窗，设烟囱。因北临濠河大路，这处别业有南北两个主立面。

南面入口左右有弧形台阶直通二层，二层窗框用红砖砌成拱形装饰，三层设红色水磨石爱奥尼外廊，中部凸出露台作为入口门厅。底层处理成基座，内有储藏室，开方形窗。东西两侧二、三层有红色木构外廊。北面中部和左右两翼向前凸出，皆有山花和圆形天窗装饰，中部最大，为巴洛克式。中央设台阶直通二层，进门中央为议事大厅，装饰西式石柱，两侧为议事室和书记室。后部有推拉门，西为会客室，东为宴会厅。楼梯在北侧中部。

三楼中央为大客堂，北侧为祠堂，两侧为卧室、琴房和书房等，房内均有壁炉。别业西侧还有一楼，三层砖木结构，原有天桥与濠南别业相通，为张謇家人用房，后曾作为南通市图书馆。

English

1.

Nantong Museum: Nantong Museum is located at the southeast corner of the Hao River, the moat of old Nantong city; in the 31st year of Guangxu of the Qing (1905), Zhang Jian converted the public botanical garden of the Tongzhou Normal School under construction into a 'museum garden,' with Zhang Jian himself as director and Sun Yue as curator—it is the first public museum built by Chinese themselves.

During the War of Resistance against Japan, the museum was occupied by the Japanese army as a stable, with only some cultural relics transferred away and most lost.

After the founding of New China, it was restored and renamed 'Nantong Museum,' with the original museum garden part allocated to People's Park.

In 1984 the original name Nantong Museum was restored, and in 1999 People's Park was merged into the museum, restoring the layout of its founding period.

Nantong Museum adopts a form combining exhibition halls and gardens, with equal emphasis on indoor displays and open-air exhibitions.

Along the main axis, the museum has South, Central, and North Halls.

The South Hall is the main exhibition hall, built in 1906, facing south with north at the back, a two-story brick-wood Western-style building with a semicircular terrace protruding forward.

Originally named the Mineral Display Hall, later called the Museum, it displays four departments: natural products, history, fine arts, and education.

Upstairs are historical relics; downstairs are animal, plant, and mineral specimens.

On the semicircular terrace on the second floor hangs a couplet in Zhang Jian's own handwriting: 'Establish schools and academies to teach, and know more the names of birds, beasts, plants, and trees.

' This couplet is also Zhang Jian's purpose in founding the museum.On both sides north of the hall are pavilions displaying the Three Pure Ones statues from the ancient Xuanmiao Temple.

The Central Hall was built in 1906, originally a weather observatory, a three-bay single-story house with a platform on the central top equipped with meteorological observation instruments—it is China's earliest meteorological observation institution.

In 1914 the observatory moved to the agricultural school; architect Sun Zhixia added a clerestory on the platform, and the Central Hall became a bronze-stone and stele-calligraphy display room.

The North Hall is a two-story hip-and-gable roof brick-wood small building, built in 1911.

Originally planned to display bronze-stone and calligraphy-painting, a whale skeleton was obtained during construction, so it was renovated: downstairs displays the whale skeleton, plus many animal skeletal specimens and fossils; upstairs uses specially made lattice screens to display famous calligraphy and paintings.

West of the North Hall is the Guoxiu Altar, built in 1907, also called Guocui Altar.

In the center, a Taihu stone rockery is stacked, with a 'Beauty Stone' standing, on which Zhang Jian's inscription is carved.

Inside the altar, stone materials from various places are scattered to show China's rich products.

Inside the altar, precious flowers such as famous peonies and orchids are planted; outside the altar, green bamboos of different varieties and origins are planted.

South of the altar is the Guoxiu Pavilion built in 1908, once converted into a bamboo-stone display area exhibiting various precious bamboo and stone specimens.

Northwest of the altar originally had a triangular goldfish pond and artificial waterfall.

Inside the museum garden there are also the Administration Office, Tengdong Waterside Pavilion, Guoxiu Pavilion, Xiangqin Pavilion, and Huazhu Ping'an Hall, as well as rockeries, ponds, animal rooms, bird rooms, windmills, and waterwheels etc.

, achieving the perfect combination of modern museum and garden.2.Zhang Jian Cemetery: Zhang Jian Cemetery is located at No.

150 South Suburb Road, Chongchuan District; in 2001 it was merged into Nantong Museum as a 5th Batch National Protected Unit.

Zhang Jian, hao Se'an, in later years self-named Sengweng, respectfully called Sengong by the world.

The tomb was first built in 1923, with Zhang Jian personally selecting the site; after his death in 1926 he was buried in Seng Garden, and two years later his family erected a bronze statue and built a memorial hall.

In 1935, Zhang Jian's only son Zhang Xiaoruo died and was buried east of Zhang Jian's tomb, with a stele 'Tomb of Young Master Zhang of Nantong' erected in front.

During the War of Resistance the cemetery gradually fell into disrepair, and was renovated after the founding of New China.

In 1956 the Zhang descendants added a 'Rest Hall' in the cemetery, and in 1958 it was renamed 'South Suburb Park.

' During the Cultural Revolution, Zhang Jian's tomb was destroyed, the grave was dug open, the stone gate towers were pulled down, and the bronze statue was smashed.

In 1976 the cemetery was renovated, and in 1983 the father-and-son tombs were rebuilt in place and the gate towers reconstructed.

Zhang Jian's tomb is a square concrete spirit platform, 2 meters high, with concrete railings around it.

The tomb coffin is in the center of the spirit platform, rectangular, with a square-base tombstone behind it, 3 meters high, inscribed 'Tomb of Mr.Zhang Jian of Nantong.

' In 1985 'South Suburb Park' was renamed 'Seng Garden,' and the bronze statue was re-erected.

The memorial hall and rest hall in the garden are now exhibition rooms for Zhang Jian's life and achievements.3.

Haonan Villa: Haonan Villa is located at the northeast corner of the museum; in 1914 Zhang Jian commissioned Sun Zhixia to design it参照 the Changguan Tower of the Beijing Agricultural Experiment Station, and it was completed in 1915.

The building faces south, three stories high, built with grey bricks, with red bricks decorating arches and moldings, topped with a red iron-sheet roof, with dormer windows and chimneys.

Because it faces the Hao River Road to the north, this villa has two main facades, north and south.

At the south entrance, curved stairs on left and right lead directly to the second floor; the second-floor window frames are decorated with red-brick arches; the third floor has a red terrazzo Ionic exterior corridor, with a terrace protruding in the center as the entrance hall.

The ground floor is treated as a base, with storage rooms inside and square windows.On the east and west sides, the second and third floors have red wooden exterior corridors.

The north center and left and right wings protrude forward, all with gable ornaments and circular skylight decorations, with the center the largest, in Baroque style.

A central staircase leads directly to the second floor; entering the door, the center is a council hall decorated with Western-style stone columns, with council rooms and secretary rooms on both sides.

At the rear are sliding doors: west is a reception room, east is a banquet hall.The staircase is in the north center.

On the third floor, the center is a large guest hall; the north side is an ancestral hall; both sides are bedrooms, piano rooms, and studies etc., all with fireplaces.

West of the villa is another building, three stories of brick-wood structure, originally connected to Haonan Villa by a sky bridge, used as housing for Zhang Jian's family, later serving as Nantong City Library.

建筑要点 / Key Features
南通博物苑位于南通古城护城河濠河的东南角清光绪三十一年1905年张謇将建设中的通州师范学校公共植物园规建为博物苑张謇自任总理聘孙钺为主任是中国人自建的第一座公共博物馆抗日战争期间博物苑被日军占为马厩只转移走部分文物大部分散失新中国成立后修复改称为南通博物馆原博物苑园林部分划归人民公园1984年恢复南通博物苑原名1999年将人民公园并入博物苑恢复为初创时期的格局南通博物苑采用展馆与园林相结合的形式室内陈列与露天展览并重博物苑沿主轴线建有南中北三馆南馆是主要展馆建于1906年坐南朝北为二层砖木洋楼前出半圆形露台原名矿物陈列室楼后称博物馆陈列天产历史美术和教育四部楼上为历史文物楼下为动物植物和矿物标本在二楼的半圆形月台上悬挂张謇手书对联设为庠序学校以教多识鸟兽草木之名此联也是张謇创办博物苑的宗旨馆北两侧各有一座亭子陈列古玄妙观的三清塑像中馆建于1906年初为测候所是三间平房中央顶部有平台上置气象观测仪器是中国最早的气象观测机构1914年测候所迁至农校建筑师孙支厦在平台上增建气楼中馆成为金石碑帖陈列室北馆为二层歇山顶砖木小楼建于1911年原计划陈列金石书画建设期间得到鲸鱼骨架于是进行改建楼下陈
02 文峰塔
Wenfeng Pagoda
明—清
级别 Level
第七批省级文物保护单位（2011年）
地址 Address
崇川区濠西路19号
类型 Type
古塔/楼阁式塔
中文原文

文峰塔始建于明万历四十六年（1618年），清嘉庆二十五年（1820年）大修，新中国成立以后两度修缮。此原有五福寺，又名文峰禅院。据清光绪《通州志》记载，五福寺为张元芳所建，文峰塔为白文粹建。

塔为六角五层木檐楼阁式，高39米，内设扶梯，各层皆有厅室，每面开一门两窗，围以外廊、栏杆。门洞外为拱券式，内作壸门。塔顶为灰瓦屋檐，檐下有斗栱，饰以龙首、仙人和走兽等，系金铎，层有大披檐。文峰塔南部隔河为文峰公园，园东有纺织博物馆，免费开放，陈列从大生纱厂整体搬迁复建的锯齿形结构厂房车间。

· · · · ·
English

Wenfeng Pagoda was first built in the 46th year of Wanli of the Ming (1618), heavily repaired in the 25th year of Jiaqing of the Qing (1820), and renovated twice after the founding of New China.

Here originally had the Wufu (Five Blessings) Temple, also called Wenfeng Chan Monastery.

According to the 'Tongzhou Gazetteer' of Guangxu of the Qing, Wufu Temple was built by Zhang Yuanfang, and Wenfeng Pagoda was built by Bai Wencui.

The pagoda is a hexagonal five-story wooden-eave pavilion-style pagoda, 39 meters high, with internal stairs, halls and rooms on each floor, one door and two windows on each side, surrounded by exterior corridors and railings.

Outside the door opening is an arch form, inside is a niche door.

The pagoda top has grey-tile eaves, with bracket sets under the eaves, decorated with dragon heads, immortals, and walking beasts etc.

, with golden bells, and large overhanging eaves on each layer.

South of Wenfeng Pagoda across the river is Wenfeng Park; east of the park is the Textile Museum, open free of charge, displaying the sawtooth-structured factory workshops relocated and rebuilt as a whole from Dasheng Cotton Mill.

建筑要点 / Key Features
文峰塔始建于明万历四十六年1618年清嘉庆二十五年1820年大修新中国成立以后两度修缮此原有五福寺又名文峰禅院据清光绪通州志记载五福寺为张元芳所建文峰塔为白文粹建塔为六角五层木檐楼阁式高39米内设扶梯各层皆有厅室每面开一门两窗围以外廊栏杆门洞外为拱券式内作壸门塔顶为灰瓦屋檐檐下有斗栱饰以龙首仙人和走兽等系金铎层有大披檐文峰塔南部隔河为文峰公园园东有纺织博物馆免费开放陈列从大生纱厂整体搬迁复建的锯齿形结构厂房车间
03 太平兴国教寺大殿
Main Hall of Taiping Xingguo Temple
明
级别 Level
第三批省级文物保护单位（1982年）
地址 Address
崇川区启秀路17号，南通博物苑南侧
类型 Type
古建筑/佛教寺院
中文原文

兴国禅寺俗称东寺，始建于南宋乾道年间，原有金刚殿、地藏殿和朝宫殿等，现仅存大殿。

此殿元至正十四年（1354年）被火烧毁，明洪武十四年（1381年）重建，清道光年间重修。

大殿为灰瓦歇山顶，前出披檐，宽深各三间，明间的四根金柱较粗，下置浅雕覆盆式柱础。屋架坡度平缓，外檐斗栱较大，明间三朵，次间一朵，用琴面月梁。柱头铺作和补间铺作均为四铺作单下昂，用两层角昂。屋架平梁上置叉手等构件。

普柏枋伸出阑额之外，与宋代手法相似。

· · · · ·
English

Xingguo Chan Temple, commonly called East Temple, was first built during the Qiandao reign of the Southern Song, originally having the Vajra Hall, Ksitigarbha Hall, and Chaogong Hall etc.

; now only the Main Hall remains.

This hall was destroyed by fire in the 14th year of Zhizheng of the Yuan (1354), rebuilt in the 14th year of Hongwu of the Ming (1381), and repaired during the Daoguang reign of the Qing.

The Main Hall has a grey-tile hip-and-gable roof, with a front overhanging eave, three bays wide and three bays deep; the four golden pillars in the central bay are relatively thick, with shallow-carved inverted-basin column bases below.

The roof truss has a gentle slope; the exterior eave bracket sets are relatively large, three sets in the central bay and one set in the side bays, using qinmian (lute-face) crescent beams.

Both the column-top bracket sets and inter-column bracket sets are four-set single lower ang, using two layers of corner ang.

On the flat beam of the roof truss are components such as crossed hands.the pubai beam extends beyond the lintel, similar to Song Dynasty techniques.

建筑要点 / Key Features
兴国禅寺俗称东寺始建于南宋乾道年间原有金刚殿地藏殿和朝宫殿等现仅存大殿此殿元至正十四年1354年被火烧毁明洪武十四年1381年重建清道光年间重修大殿为灰瓦歇山顶前出披檐宽深各三间明间的四根金柱较粗下置浅雕覆盆式柱础屋架坡度平缓外檐斗栱较大明间三朵次间一朵用琴面月梁柱头铺作和补间铺作均为四铺作单下昂用两层角昂屋架平梁上置叉手等构件普柏枋伸出阑额之外与宋代手法相似
04 濠阳小筑
Haoyang Villa
民国
级别 Level
第六批省级文物保护单位（2006年）
地址 Address
崇川区环城南路21号
类型 Type
古建筑/名人故居
门票 Ticket
免费开放
开放时间 Hours
9:00—17:00（周一闭馆）
中文原文

濠阳小筑在南濠河北沿，是张謇童年嬉戏之所，也是他晚年的居所，现为张謇纪念馆。这组建筑建于1917年，占地1860平方米，为中国传统风格庭院，有东、西并立的两组建筑，其间以走廊相连。由于位于城河边，地势较低，院中建筑基础较高，庭院则深陷地下。正门朝东，穿过门厅是东西横长的庭院，尽端有一座六角亭与门正对，原为张謇棋室。

院落北部并立两座主要房屋，东侧为花厅，西侧为敞厅。花厅内三个房间皆设壁炉。穿过花厅可进入北部庭院，北侧为两层砖木楼房曼寿堂，院中有张謇从五山移植来的罗汉松，西侧有金鱼池，西屋内有壁炉。由曼寿堂向东为东侧小园，是以前的职员宿舍、办公室、厨房和储藏室等。宅院西南角原有药王庙，营建濠南小筑时将庙迁至北侧数十米的旧城下，仅留下一棵大皂荚树，建造因树斋庭院，今树已不存。

濠阳小筑刚建成时张謇曾借出曼寿堂一半房间给绣艺大师沈寿居住养病。1920年又在濠阳小筑西侧建造南通织绣局与女工传习所，沈寿则移居到与传习所相邻的因树斋，直至病逝。现女工传习所为沈寿艺术馆，展示沈寿的绣品。

· · · · ·
English

Haoyang Villa is on the north bank of the South Hao River, where Zhang Jian played in childhood and also his residence in later years; now it is the Zhang Jian Memorial Hall.

This group of buildings was built in 1917, covering 1,860 square meters, a traditional Chinese-style courtyard with two groups of buildings standing side by side east and west, connected by corridors.

Because it is located by the city river with low terrain, the building foundations in the courtyard are high, while the courtyard itself is deeply sunken below ground.

The main gate faces east; passing through the entrance hall is an east-west horizontally long courtyard, with a hexagonal pavilion at the end directly opposite the gate, originally Zhang Jian's chess room.

In the north of the courtyard stand two main buildings side by side: the east is a flower hall, the west is an open hall.The three rooms in the flower hall all have fireplaces.

Passing through the flower hall leads to the northern courtyard; on the north side is the two-story brick-wood building Manshou Hall, with a Buddhist pine transplanted by Zhang Jian from the Five Mountains in the courtyard, a goldfish pond on the west side, and a fireplace in the west room.

East from Manshou Hall is the east small garden, formerly staff dormitories, offices, kitchen, and storage rooms etc.

At the southwest corner of the residence originally was the Medicine King Temple; when building Haonan Villa, the temple was moved to the old city wall tens of meters north, leaving only a large honey locust tree, around which the Yinshu Zhai courtyard was built; today the tree no longer exists.

When Haoyang Villa was just completed, Zhang Jian lent half of the rooms of Manshou Hall to embroidery master Shen Shou to live and recuperate.

In 1920, the Nantong Weaving and Embroidery Bureau and Women Workers' Training Institute were built west of Haoyang Villa; Shen Shou then moved to Yinshu Zhai adjacent to the training institute until her death.

Today the Women Workers' Training Institute is the Shen Shou Art Museum, displaying Shen Shou's embroidery works.

建筑要点 / Key Features
濠阳小筑在南濠河北沿是张謇童年嬉戏之所也是他晚年的居所现为张謇纪念馆这组建筑建于1917年占地1860平方米为中国传统风格庭院有东西并立的两组建筑其间以走廊相连由于位于城河边地势较低院中建筑基础较高庭院则深陷地下正门朝东穿过门厅是东西横长的庭院尽端有一座六角亭与门正对原为张謇棋室院落北部并立两座主要房屋东侧为花厅西侧为敞厅花厅内三个房间皆设壁炉穿过花厅可进入北部庭院北侧为两层砖木楼房曼寿堂院中有张謇从五山移植来的罗汉松西侧有金鱼池西屋内有壁炉由曼寿堂向东为东侧小园是以前的职员宿舍办公室厨房和储藏室等宅院西南角原有药王庙营建濠南小筑时将庙迁至北侧数十米的旧城下仅留下一棵大皂荚树建造因树斋庭院今树已不存濠阳小筑刚建成时张謇曾借出曼寿堂一半房间给绣艺大师沈寿居住养病1920年又在濠阳小筑西侧建造南通织绣局与女工传习所沈寿则移居到与传习所相邻的因树斋直至病逝现女工传习所为沈寿艺术馆展示沈寿的绣品
05 钟楼、谯楼
Drum Tower and Watchtower
明
级别 Level
第五批省级文物保护单位（2002年）
地址 Address
通州区建设路1号
类型 Type
古建筑/钟楼
门票 Ticket
免费开放
开放时间 Hours
免费开放
中文原文

钟楼、谯楼处在南通老城中心，由中国传统风格的谯楼和近代西洋风格的钟楼结合而成。谯楼始建于南宋淳熙年间，原在州治南，后毁于火。

元至正七年（1347年）在今址重建，后又毁于火，明洪武三年（1370年）重建，此后多次重修。清道光年间知州周焘命名为星枢楼。新中国成立后谯楼常年失修，2000年修复。

谯楼下层为土台，外砌城砖，中部有拱型通道，以前直通州衙大堂。谯楼上层为木造城楼，灰瓦歇山顶，宽五间，前后用隔扇门窗，内部原设漏刻，并供值夜者居住。1914年至1915年在谯楼前建钟楼，由孙支厦设计，李顺记施工。

钟楼模仿伦敦大本钟，高22.6米，是民国时期南通建造的最高建筑物。楼高六层，顶部为小平台，上立旗杆；五层为气楼，四坡屋顶，四层开门和老虎窗，周设外廊，既可作瞭望台，又可发现火警。

三层内置巨型机械钟，四面有直径近2米的钟面，南向墙上有张謇留下的对联：畴昔是州今是县，江淮之委海之端。二层四面开窗，可供居住，北侧有门与谯楼城台相通，外墙原嵌刻石，为张謇撰写的钟楼题记，记载钟楼尺寸，施工时间和建楼缘起，今已佚失。底层四面开拱券门，北侧与谯楼门洞相接。

文革时期钟楼曾被改造，2000年修复谯楼时恢复原状。

· · · · ·
English

The Clock Tower and Watchtower are located in the center of old Nantong city, combining the Chinese traditional-style Watchtower with the modern Western-style Clock Tower.

The Watchtower was first built during the Chunxi reign of the Southern Song, originally south of the prefectural government, later destroyed by fire.

In the 7th year of Zhizheng of the Yuan (1347) it was rebuilt at the current site, later destroyed by fire again, and rebuilt in the 3rd year of Hongwu of the Ming (1370), subsequently repaired many times.

During the Daoguang reign of the Qing, Prefect Zhou Tao named it Xingshu Tower.After the founding of New China, the Watchtower fell into disrepair for years and was restored in 2000.

The lower layer of the Watchtower is an earthen platform, faced with city bricks, with an arched passage in the center that formerly led directly to the prefectural government hall.

The upper layer of the Watchtower is a wooden city tower, with a grey-tile hip-and-gable roof, five bays wide, with lattice doors and windows front and rear; inside originally had a water clock and housed night watchmen.

From 1914 to 1915, the Clock Tower was built in front of the Watchtower, designed by Sun Zhixia and constructed by Li Shunji.The Clock Tower imitates London Big Ben, 22.

6 meters high, and was the tallest building constructed in Nantong during the Republican period.

The tower is six stories high, with a small platform at the top and a flagpole erected on it; the fifth story is a clerestory with a four-slope roof; the fourth story has doors and dormer windows, with exterior corridors around, serving both as an observation deck and for detecting fires.

The third story contains a giant mechanical clock, with clock faces nearly 2 meters in diameter on all four sides; on the south-facing wall is a couplet left by Zhang Jian: Formerly a prefecture, now a county; the confluence of Jianghuai and the end of the sea.

The second story has windows on all four sides for habitation, with a door on the north side connecting to the Watchtower city platform; the exterior wall originally had an inscribed stone, a Clock Tower inscription written by Zhang Jian recording the tower dimensions, construction time, and origin of building the tower, now lost.

The ground floor has arched doors on all four sides, with the north side connecting to the Watchtower gate opening.

During the Cultural Revolution, the Clock Tower was modified; when restoring the Watchtower in 2000, it was restored to its original state.

建筑要点 / Key Features
钟楼谯楼处在南通老城中心由中国传统风格的谯楼和近代西洋风格的钟楼结合而成谯楼始建于南宋淳熙年间原在州治南后毁于火元至正七年1347年在今址重建后又毁于火明洪武三年1370年重建此后多次重修清道光年间知州周焘命名为星枢楼新中国成立后谯楼常年失修2000年修复谯楼下层为土台外砌城砖中部有拱型通道以前直通州衙大堂谯楼上层为木造城楼灰瓦歇山顶宽五间前后用隔扇门窗内部原设漏刻并供值夜者居住1914年至1915年在谯楼前建钟楼由孙支厦设计李顺记施工钟楼模仿伦敦大本钟高22.6米是民国时期南通建造的最高建筑物楼高六层顶部为小平台上立旗杆五层为气楼四坡屋顶四层开门和老虎窗周设外廊既可作瞭望台又可发现火警三层内置巨型机械钟四面有直径近2米的钟面南向墙上有张謇留下的对联畴昔是州今是县江淮之委海之端二层四面开窗可供居住北侧有门与谯楼城台相通外墙原嵌刻石为张謇撰写的钟楼题记记载钟楼尺寸施工时间和建楼缘起今已佚失底层四面开拱券门北侧与谯楼门洞相接文革时期钟楼曾被改造2000年修复谯楼时恢复原状
