02 将军崖岩画
Paintings on General Cliff
新石器时代
级别 Level
第三批全国重点文物保护单位（1988年）
地址 Address
锦屏山桃花涧景区内
类型 Type
岩画/新石器时代
门票 Ticket
桃花涧景区门票30元，参观岩画另需5元
开放时间 Hours
桃花涧景区门票30元，参观岩画另需5元
中文原文

将军崖岩画位于桃花涧景区内。桃花涧是锦屏山最大的自然山涧，距市区5公里，全长4.5公里，内部石壁陡峭，依山傍水。景区包括东、西两部分，西部有将军崖岩画、桃花涧旧石器遗址和石刻文化艺术园，东部为桃花涧，有马耳峰龙洞石刻和北宋确臼庵等。

将军崖岩画在锦屏山马耳峰南麓，万氏崖油头以南。岩画刻在长22米、宽15米的平整光亮黑色岩石上，分为三组，内容有人面、农作物、鸟兽、星云等图案以及各种符号。是我国迄今发现最早的原始社会岩画。

第一组（A组），在将军崖岩画遗址西侧，全长4米，高2.8米，以人面和农作物图案为主，其中有11个人面，2个兽面，13个农作物图案和9个符号。图案用阴线刻成，刻痕断面呈V形，面壁光滑。深度多为1厘米，宽度则在2厘米至3厘米之间，线条粗率劲直。人面上的饰纹以复线三角纹、弦纹和网纹为主题。最大的人面像有90厘米高，110厘米宽。

人像没有躯干四肢，仅有一条线延伸到下部的作物图案上。作物图案间夹杂许多似乎用于计算的圆点符号。这些岩画反映了早期人类社会对于农作物的崇拜，是我国目前发现唯一反映原始农业部落社会生产的石刻画面。第二组（B组），在将军崖岩画遗迹南侧，长8米，宽6米，以鸟兽纹、类星象图案为主。

大多数兽面头向北偏东60度，刻痕宽平，有的宽达4厘米，但比第一组要浅得多。刻痕上多布满麻点状的浅坑，是敲凿面成。兽面纹饰和动物头骨图案，画得比较集中，数量也多，其间还夹有各种图案符号，有类似贝壳或兽蹄印者、有排列直线者、有上半部作交叉十字者，也有由一根弯折的长线或数量不等的短线组成的图案。

其中两幅鸟头图案形象清楚，少昊之国居民以鸟为图腾，石刻中的鸟头图案可能是这种崇拜的产物。另有四幅类似日月星辰的画面，左上角还有一个14厘米宽的兽面，由于长期风化，有些刻痕已很模糊了。其中有三个太阳图案较引人注目，三个太阳成倒三角形排列，太阳边缘表示光芒的放射线数目不同，分别表现光线强度不同的早、中、晚三个太阳。

这样排列是为了根据太阳运行轨迹的位置测量冬至、夏至的时间，为我国天文史上的重要发现。太阳图案东侧有一条南北向直线，为子午线，与实际子午线误差4度左右。第三组（C组），在将军崖岩画遗迹东侧，是三组画面中最高的一组，以人面夹杂星象图案组成。这一组中有四个人面，面部没有杂乱的线条，用圆点和短线表示五官。人面之间以圆点和短线组成星象图案。这组图案可能是先民想象的天神形象，头戴五彩冠冕。

三组岩画中间有三块大石，一大三小，石面分布着对称的圆窝图案，窝径在3厘米至7厘米之间，共21个。这和文献中东方民族祭祀以石为社，大石为社主，三小石为社足的记载吻合，是东夷以大石为神的土地崇拜祭祀的遗迹。女阴刻石在将军崖西侧160米处的山坡上，面向东方，西部为女体，东部为女阴，有明显的人工凿刻痕迹，为原始时期生殖崇拜的遗存。

· · · · ·
English

The General Cliff rock paintings are located in the Taohuajian (Peach Blossom Gorge) Scenic Area.

Taohuajian is the largest natural mountain gorge on Jinping Mountain, 5 kilometers from the city center, with a total length of 4.

5 kilometers; inside, the stone walls are steep, with mountains and water.

The scenic area includes east and west two parts: the west has the General Cliff rock paintings, the Taohuajian Paleolithic site, and the Stone Carving Culture and Art Park; the east is Taohuajian, with the Ma'er Peak Longdong stone carvings and the Northern Song Quejiu Nunnery etc.

The General Cliff rock paintings are at the south foot of Ma'er Peak on Jinping Mountain, south of the Wanshi Cliff oil head.

The rock paintings are carved on flat, smooth, black rock 22 meters long and 15 meters wide, divided into three groups, with content including human faces, crops, birds and beasts, stars and clouds, and various symbols.

They are the earliest primitive society rock paintings discovered so far in China.

First Group (Group A), on the west side of the General Cliff rock painting site, with a total length of 4 meters and height of 2.

8 meters, mainly features human faces and crop patterns, including 11 human faces, 2 animal faces, 13 crop patterns, and 9 symbols.

The patterns are carved with incised lines, with the carving cross-section V-shaped and the wall surface smooth.

The depth is mostly 1 centimeter, and the width is between 2 and 3 centimeters, with rough and vigorous straight lines.

The decorative patterns on the human faces feature double-line triangular patterns, chord patterns, and mesh patterns.The largest human face is 90 centimeters high and 110 centimeters wide.

The human figures have no torso or limbs, only a line extending to the crop pattern below.Between the crop patterns are mixed many dot symbols that seem to be used for calculation.

These rock paintings reflect early human society's worship of crops, and are the only stone-carved picture surface discovered so far in China reflecting the social production of primitive agricultural tribes.

Second Group (Group B), on the south side of the General Cliff rock painting remains, 8 meters long and 6 meters wide, mainly features bird and beast patterns and star-like patterns.

Most animal faces have heads facing 60 degrees east of north, with wide and flat carving marks, some up to 4 centimeters wide, but much shallower than the first group.

The carving marks are mostly covered with pockmark-like shallow pits, formed by chiseling.

The animal face decorations and animal skull patterns are drawn relatively concentrated and numerous, with various pattern symbols mixed in between: some resembling shells or animal hoof prints, some arranged in straight lines, some with crossed upper halves, and some composed of a bent long line or varying numbers of short lines.

Among them, two bird head patterns have clear images; the residents of the Shaohao State used birds as totems, and the bird head patterns in the stone carvings may be a product of this worship.

There are also four pictures resembling the sun, moon, and stars, with a 14-centimeter-wide animal face in the upper left corner; due to long-term weathering, some carving marks have become very blurry.

Among them, three sun patterns are quite eye-catching; the three suns are arranged in an inverted triangle, with different numbers of radial lines representing light rays at the sun edges, respectively representing the three suns of morning, noon, and evening with different light intensities.

This arrangement was for measuring the times of the winter solstice and summer solstice according to the position of the sun's trajectory, an important discovery in the history of Chinese astronomy.

East of the sun pattern is a north-south straight line, a meridian line, with an error of about 4 degrees from the actual meridian.

Third Group (Group C), on the east side of the General Cliff rock painting remains, is the highest group among the three groups of pictures, composed of human faces mixed with star patterns.

This group has four human faces, with no messy lines on the faces, using dots and short lines to represent facial features.Between the human faces, star patterns are composed of dots and short lines.

This group of patterns may be the image of heavenly gods imagined by the ancestors, wearing colorful crowns.

Between the three groups of rock paintings are three large stones, one large and three small, with symmetrical circular pit patterns distributed on the stone surfaces, with pit diameters between 3 and 7 centimeters, totaling 21.

This matches the records in literature that Eastern peoples used stones as altars (she) in sacrifices, with the large stone as the altar master and the three small stones as the altar feet; it is a relic of the Dongyi people's land worship sacrifice using large stones as gods.

The female genital stone carving is on the hillside 160 meters west of General Cliff, facing east; the west part is a female body, the east part is female genitalia, with obvious artificial chiseling traces, a relic of primitive period reproductive worship.

建筑要点 / Key Features
将军崖岩画位于桃花涧景区内桃花涧是锦屏山最大的自然山涧距市区5公里全长4.5公里内部石壁陡峭依山傍水景区包括东西两部分西部有将军崖岩画桃花涧旧石器遗址和石刻文化艺术园东部为桃花涧有马耳峰龙洞石刻和北宋确臼庵等将军崖岩画在锦屏山马耳峰南麓万氏崖油头以南岩画刻在长22米宽15米的平整光亮黑色岩石上分为三组内容有人面农作物鸟兽星云等图案以及各种符号是我国迄今发现最早的原始社会岩画第一组A组在将军崖岩画遗址西侧全长4米高2.8米以人面和农作物图案为主其中有11个人面2个兽面13个农作物图案和9个符号图案用阴线刻成刻痕断面呈V形面壁光滑深度多为1厘米宽度则在2厘米至3厘米之间线条粗率劲直人面上的饰纹以复线三角纹弦纹和网纹为主题最大的人面像有90厘米高110厘米宽人像没有躯干四肢仅有一条线延伸到下部的作物图案上作物图案间夹杂许多似乎用于计算的圆点符号这些岩画反映了早期人类社会对于农作物的崇拜是我国目前发现唯一反映原始农业部落社会生产的石刻画面第二组B组在将军崖岩画遗迹南侧长8米宽6米以鸟兽纹类星象图案为主大多数兽面头向北偏东60度刻痕宽平有的宽达4厘米但比第一组要浅得多刻痕上多布满麻点状的浅坑是敲
03 锦屏山龙祠摩崖石刻
Cliffside Inscriptions and Stone Sculptures around Longci Shrine at Jinping Mountain
北宋
级别 Level
第五批省级文物保护单位（2002年）
地址 Address
海州城之南，高山之巅，地理位置特殊，属人迹罕至之处
类型 Type
摩崖石刻
中文原文

龙祠在宋代被称为石庵或玉泉庵，为宋金时期官民祈雨之处，直至清代，香火不断。

石刻共有9处，全部刻在洞内外石壁上，尚有7处字迹可辨，其中宋刻6处，金刻1处。

从东至西分别为：北宋宣和二年题记、北宋庆历七年题记、北宋崇宁壬午年题记、北宋皇祐癸巳年题记、北宋庆历珍成提题记、北宋绍圣四年题记和金大定忍气吞声年题记。

石刻内容多与祷雨有关。

· · · · ·
English

Longci (Dragon Shrine) was called Shi'an (Stone Hut) or Yuquan'an (Jade Spring Hut) in the Song Dynasty, a place where officials and people prayed for rain during the Song-Jin period, and the incense continued until the Qing Dynasty.

There are 9 stone carvings in total, all carved on the stone walls inside and outside the cave; 7 of them still have legible characters, including 6 Song carvings and 1 Jin carving.

From east to west they are respectively: the Northern Song Xuanhe 2nd year inscription, the Northern Song Qingli 7th year inscription, the Northern Song Chongning Renwu year inscription, the Northern Song Huangyou Guisi year inscription, the Northern Song Qingli Zhencheng ti inscription, the Northern Song Shaosheng 4th year inscription, and the Jin Dading year inscription.

The content of the stone carvings is mostly related to praying for rain.

建筑要点 / Key Features
龙祠在宋代被称为石庵或玉泉庵为宋金时期官民祈雨之处直至清代香火不断石刻共有9处全部刻在洞内外石壁上尚有7处字迹可辨其中宋刻6处金刻1处从东至西分别为北宋宣和二年题记北宋庆历七年题记北宋崇宁壬午年题记北宋皇祐癸巳年题记北宋庆历珍成提题记北宋绍圣四年题记和金大定忍气吞声年题记石刻内容多与祷雨有关
04 花果山
Huaguo Mountain
唐—清
级别 Level
其他
地址 Address
新浦区云台乡
类型 Type
风景名胜/古建筑遗址
门票 Ticket
旺季门票100元，淡季（11月—次年2月）50元。由于景区范围大，需乘车游览，上下全程需35元
开放时间 Hours
旺季门票100元，淡季（11月—次年2月）50元。由于景区范围大，需乘车游览，上下全程需35元
中文原文

花果山是连云港市最大的景区，以《西游记》花果山的传说为主题，结合原有古建筑遗址营造了诸多景观，景区风景秀丽，动植物种类丰富，并具有神话色彩，是连云港最受欢迎的景区。景区周围主要文物有海清寺塔、郁林观石刻等。清康熙年间之前，花果山还峙立在大海之中，隋唐以来，花果山号称东海第一胜景、海内灵山。

隋唐以来，墨客骚人游历遍至，吟咏题刻，遍布山间。这些题刻集中在郁林观、水帘洞、照海亭几处。景区内的古迹多已被破坏，近年重修复建。山腰九龙桥拱券为明代遗构，桥北多宝佛塔塔基曾出土大批古钱币，1995年重建宝塔。

山上主要寺庙为三元宫，始建于唐，宋、明两代重建，至清代规模宏大，由于寺中僧人参与抗日，所有殿宇都在抗日战争中被日军烧毁，仅留有山门底部，1979年重建。

此外山上的著名景观还有水帘洞，以及其后的七十二洞。水帘洞洞口周围有宋刻：大宋国海州州县遗字、明王同的榜书高山流水、神泉普润题刻以及清道光皇帝书赐给陶澍的印心石屋四字题刻。

水帘洞东南300米左右有照海亭，周围有10处石刻。其中以民国初年李瑞清魏书石刻环瀛仰镜的艺术价值最高，位于海天洞外东侧一处石台的南面，石面光滑如镜，石刻采用魏碑体，字大近二尺，峻峭奇崛，气韵简穆，是李瑞清晚年成熟时期的代表性作品。

这四个字是1920年李瑞清游览花果山为海天洞悟五和尚所书。山上有玉皇殿，始建于明，近年重建，石刻匾额仍为旧物。主峰玉女峰顶有迎曙亭，也是20世纪80年代在原址新建。

· · · · ·
English

Huaguo (Flower and Fruit) Mountain is the largest scenic area in Lianyungang City, themed on the legend of Huaguo Mountain in 'Journey to the West,' combining original ancient architecture ruins to create many landscapes; the scenic area has beautiful scenery, rich species of animals and plants, and has a mythological color, making it the most popular scenic area in Lianyungang.

The main cultural relics around the scenic area include Haiqing Temple Pagoda and Yulin Temple stone carvings etc.

Before the Kangxi reign of the Qing, Huaguo Mountain still stood in the middle of the sea; since the Sui and Tang dynasties, Huaguo Mountain has been known as the 'First Scenic Spot of the East Sea' and the 'Spiritual Mountain Within the Sea.

' Since the Sui and Tang dynasties, literati and poets have traveled everywhere, with poems and inscriptions spread throughout the mountains.

These inscriptions are concentrated in several places: Yulin Temple, Water Curtain Cave, and Zhaohai (Sea-Shining) Pavilion.

Most of the historic sites in the scenic area have been destroyed, and have been restored and rebuilt in recent years.

The arch of the Jiulong (Nine Dragons) Bridge on the mountainside is a Ming Dynasty remnant; at the base of the Duobao (Many Treasures) Buddha Pagoda north of the bridge, a large number of ancient coins were unearthed, and the pagoda was rebuilt in 1995.

The main temple on the mountain is Sanyuan (Three Primes) Palace, first built in the Tang, rebuilt in the Song and Ming dynasties, and by the Qing Dynasty it had a grand scale; because the monks in the temple participated in the anti-Japanese resistance, all halls were burned down by the Japanese army during the War of Resistance against Japan, leaving only the bottom of the mountain gate, which was rebuilt in 1979.

In addition, the famous landscapes on the mountain include the Water Curtain Cave and the Seventy-Two Caves behind it.

Around the entrance of the Water Curtain Cave are Song carvings: the remaining characters 'Great Song State Haizhou Prefecture and County,' the Ming Dynasty Wang Tong's large-character inscription 'High Mountains and Flowing Water,' the 'Divine Spring Universal Moisture' inscription, and the four-character inscription 'Seal Heart Stone House' written and bestowed by the Qing Daoguang Emperor to Tao Shu.

About 300 meters southeast of the Water Curtain Cave is Zhaohai Pavilion, with 10 stone carvings around it.

Among them, the Wei-style stone carving 'Huan Ying Yang Jing (Looking Up at the Mirror Surrounding the Ocean)' by Li Ruiqing in the early Republic of China has the highest artistic value; it is located on the south side of a stone platform east of the Haitian (Sea-Sky) Cave, with the stone surface smooth as a mirror; the stone carving uses the Wei stele style, with characters nearly two chi (about 66 cm) large, steep and奇特, with a simple and solemn aura, and is a representative work of Li Ruiqing's mature later years.

These four characters were written by Li Ruiqing in 1920 when he visited Huaguo Mountain for the monk Wu Wu of Haitian Cave.

On the mountain is the Jade Emperor Hall, first built in the Ming, rebuilt in recent years, with the stone carving plaque still being the original.

On the summit of the main peak Yunü (Jade Maiden) Peak is the Yingshu (Greeting Dawn) Pavilion, also newly built on the original site in the 1980s.

建筑要点 / Key Features
花果山是连云港市最大的景区以西游记花果山的传说为主题结合原有古建筑遗址营造了诸多景观景区风景秀丽动植物种类丰富并具有神话色彩是连云港最受欢迎的景区景区周围主要文物有海清寺塔郁林观石刻等清康熙年间之前花果山还峙立在大海之中隋唐以来花果山号称东海第一胜景海内灵山隋唐以来墨客骚人游历遍至吟咏题刻遍布山间这些题刻集中在郁林观水帘洞照海亭几处景区内的古迹多已被破坏近年重修复建山腰九龙桥拱券为明代遗构桥北多宝佛塔塔基曾出土大批古钱币1995年重建宝塔山上主要寺庙为三元宫始建于唐宋明两代重建至清代规模宏大由于寺中僧人参与抗日所有殿宇都在抗日战争中被日军烧毁仅留有山门底部1979年重建此外山上的著名景观还有水帘洞以及其后的七十二洞水帘洞洞口周围有宋刻大宋国海州州县遗字明王同的榜书高山流水神泉普润题刻以及清道光皇帝书赐给陶澍的印心石屋四字题刻水帘洞东南300米左右有照海亭周围有10处石刻其中以民国初年李瑞清魏书石刻环瀛仰镜的艺术价值最高位于海天洞外东侧一处石台的南面石面光滑如镜石刻采用魏碑体字大近二尺峻峭奇崛气韵简穆是李瑞清晚年成熟时期的代表性作品这四个字是1920年李瑞清游览花果山为海天洞悟五和尚所书
05 海清寺塔
Haiqing Temple Pagoda
宋
级别 Level
第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
地址 Address
新浦区云台乡大村水库旁
类型 Type
古塔/楼阁式塔
中文原文

海清寺塔是为供养释迦真身舍利和阿育王灵牙而建，因此又称阿育王塔，建于北宋天圣元年至九年（1023—1031）。

此塔原在寺庙山门前的中轴线上，与北魏及唐宋以后佛寺建筑的配置方式都不尽相同，是中国建筑史上佛寺嬗变过程重要的一例。1975年维修时曾在地宫内发现银匣、银棺等一大批文物。

塔为八面九层，仿楼阁式砖塔，高40.58米。该塔以青砖叠涩构筑出檐部，外观和构造方式与河北正定开元寺料敌塔相似。各层在东、西、南、北正向辟拱门，上下对齐，其余外壁开直棂窗。塔身曲线柔缓，向上逐渐收分，各层层高逐层减少，仅顶层为明代重建，比例略大，有失协调。

1975年维修时，参照河北开元寺塔修复了塔顶。塔身内部中央砌八角形塔心柱体，各层以砖叠涩连成走道，各层塔心柱四面辟佛龛。由于塔身尺度较小，登梯梯级比较陡峭，因此在两侧壁面留洞便于手攀。

· · · · ·
English

Haiqing Temple Pagoda was built to enshrine the true body relics of Shakyamuni and the spiritual tooth of Ashoka, hence also called the Ashoka Pagoda; it was built from the 1st to the 9th year of Tiansheng of the Northern Song (1023-1031).

This pagoda was originally on the central axis in front of the temple's mountain gate, which is not entirely the same as the configuration of Buddhist temple buildings after the Northern Wei and Tang-Song dynasties, making it an important example of the evolution of Buddhist temples in Chinese architectural history.

During maintenance in 1975, a large batch of cultural relics such as silver boxes and silver coffins were discovered in the underground palace.

The pagoda is an eight-sided, nine-story, pavilion-style brick pagoda, 40.58 meters high.

This pagoda uses grey bricks in corbel construction to form the eaves, with an appearance and construction method similar to the Liaodi (Enemy-Watching) Pagoda of Kaiyuan Temple in Zhengding, Hebei.

Each story has arched doors on the east, west, south, and north main directions, aligned vertically, with straight-lattice windows on the other outer walls.

The pagoda body has a gentle curve, tapering gradually upward, with the height of each story decreasing layer by layer; only the top story was rebuilt in the Ming Dynasty, with a slightly large proportion and lack of coordination.

During maintenance in 1975, the pagoda top was repaired with reference to the Kaiyuan Temple Pagoda in Hebei.

In the center of the interior of the pagoda body, an octagonal pagoda core column is built; each story is connected by brick corbels to form walkways, with Buddhist niches opened on four sides of the pagoda core column at each story.

Because the scale of the pagoda body is relatively small and the climbing stairs are relatively steep, holes are left on both side walls to facilitate hand climbing.

建筑要点 / Key Features
海清寺塔是为供养释迦真身舍利和阿育王灵牙而建因此又称阿育王塔建于北宋天圣元年至九年10231031此塔原在寺庙山门前的中轴线上与北魏及唐宋以后佛寺建筑的配置方式都不尽相同是中国建筑史上佛寺嬗变过程重要的一例1975年维修时曾在地宫内发现银匣银棺等一大批文物塔为八面九层仿楼阁式砖塔高40.58米该塔以青砖叠涩构筑出檐部外观和构造方式与河北正定开元寺料敌塔相似各层在东西南北正向辟拱门上下对齐其余外壁开直棂窗塔身曲线柔缓向上逐渐收分各层层高逐层减少仅顶层为明代重建比例略大有失协调1975年维修时参照河北开元寺塔修复了塔顶塔身内部中央砌八角形塔心柱体各层以砖叠涩连成走道各层塔心柱四面辟佛龛由于塔身尺度较小登梯梯级比较陡峭因此在两侧壁面留洞便于手攀
06 郁林观石刻群
Yulinguan Stone Sculptures
宋
级别 Level
第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
地址 Address
新浦区花果山乡飞泉村狮子岩下
类型 Type
摩崖石刻
门票 Ticket
5元
开放时间 Hours
5元
中文原文

郁林观在花果山下五圣广场南侧400米处的狮子崖。其西是隋开皇年间的旧址，题刻分别位于飞泉附近的崖壁、巨石上，主要有6处。

一是《东海郁林观东岩壁记》摩崖题刻，俗称唐隶，刻在飞泉前的巨石上，由唐开元七年（719年）海州司马崔惟怦之子崔逸撰文，是一篇文字优美的游记，书法风格颇似汉隶《石门颂》，但结体更为方整。文21行，行17字，字径11厘米，共392字八分书。

这处题刻受到历代金石家重视，宋赵明诚《金石录》、清吴玉搢《金石存》都有著录。

二是北宋庆历四年（1044年）祖无择的三言诗刻，俗称宋篆，刻在唐隶斜对面的突兀大石上，共12行，每行7字，篆书，字径25厘米。祖无择作诗，苏唐卿书，王君章刻。

三是谭亨甫宋人诗刻，长135厘米，高110厘米，11行，每行7字，楷书杂有魏意，字径7厘米。四是宋四士篆书题名，刘居石行书题名，王邦行楷题名，字径6.5厘米，刻于北宋崇宁四年（1104年）七月。

另外还有明王同和清黄道传、师亮采等人的题刻。

· · · · ·
English

Yulinguan (Yulin Temple) is at Shizi (Lion) Cliff, 400 meters south of Wusheng Square at the foot of Huaguo Mountain.

West of it is the old site from the Kaihuang reign of the Sui; the inscriptions are respectively located on the cliffs and boulders near Feiquan (Flying Spring), with 6 main ones.

First is the 'Record of the East Cliff of Yulin Temple in Donghai' cliff inscription, commonly called Tang Li (Tang Clerical Script), carved on the boulder in front of Feiquan; the text was written by Cui Yi, son of Cui Weipeng, Sima (Viceroy) of Haizhou, in the 7th year of Kaiyuan of the Tang (719); it is a beautifully written travel record, with a calligraphy style quite similar to the Han clerical script 'Ode to the Stone Gate,' but with a more square and neat structure.

The text has 21 lines, 17 characters per line, with a character diameter of 11 centimeters, totaling 392 characters in bafen (eight-part) clerical script.

This inscription has been valued by epigraphists of all dynasties; it is recorded in Zhao Mingcheng's 'Catalogue of Inscriptions on Metal and Stone' of the Song and Wu Yujin's 'Preserved Metal and Stone' of the Qing.

Second is the three-character poem inscription by Zu Wuze in the 4th year of Qingli of the Northern Song (1044), commonly called Song Zhuan (Song Seal Script), carved on the towering boulder diagonally opposite the Tang Li, with 12 lines, 7 characters per line, in seal script, with a character diameter of 25 centimeters.

Zu Wuze wrote the poem, Su Tangqing did the calligraphy, and Wang Junzhang did the carving.

Third is the Song Dynasty poem inscription by Tan Hengfu, 135 centimeters long and 110 centimeters high, with 11 lines, 7 characters per line, in regular script mixed with Wei style, with a character diameter of 7 centimeters.

Fourth is the four Song scholars' seal script inscriptions, Liu Jushi's running script inscription, and Wang Bang's running-regular script inscription, with a character diameter of 6.

5 centimeters, carved in the 4th year of Chongning of the Northern Song (1104), July.

In addition, there are inscriptions by Wang Tong of the Ming and Huang Daochuan, Shi Liangcai etc.of the Qing.

建筑要点 / Key Features
郁林观在花果山下五圣广场南侧400米处的狮子崖其西是隋开皇年间的旧址题刻分别位于飞泉附近的崖壁巨石上主要有6处一是东海郁林观东岩壁记摩崖题刻俗称唐隶刻在飞泉前的巨石上由唐开元七年719年海州司马崔惟怦之子崔逸撰文是一篇文字优美的游记书法风格颇似汉隶石门颂但结体更为方整文21行行17字字径11厘米共392字八分书这处题刻受到历代金石家重视宋赵明诚金石录清吴玉搢金石存都有著录二是北宋庆历四年1044年祖无择的三言诗刻俗称宋篆刻在唐隶斜对面的突兀大石上共12行每行7字篆字字径25厘米祖无择作诗苏唐卿书王君章刻三是谭亨甫宋人诗刻长135厘米高110厘米11行每行7字楷书杂有魏意字径7厘米四是宋四士篆书题名刘居石行书题名王邦行楷题名字径6.5厘米刻于北宋崇宁四年1104年七月另外还有明王同和清黄道传师亮采等人的题刻
07 东连岛东海琅琊郡界域刻石
Stone Sculptures at Border of Donghai and Langya Prefectures on Donglian Island
西汉
级别 Level
第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
地址 Address
连云区苏马湾海滨浴场内
类型 Type
摩崖刻石/界域刻石
门票 Ticket
浴场门票60元
开放时间 Hours
8:00 — 19:00
中文原文

东连岛东海琅琊郡界域刻石是我国迄今发现的时间最早、最为完整、内容明确、有确切纪年的西汉晚期界域刻石，其字体显示出从篆转变为隶书的初创阶段的风格，是现存西汉石刻中的珍品和瑰宝。刻石共有二处，一在苏马湾景区内沙滩附近，一在东连岛东段灯塔山羊窝头北山麓，均面海而立。

苏马湾刻石距海水低潮平面约5米，羊窝头刻石距海水低潮平面约8米。苏马湾刻石在沙滩南侧一块独立的花岗片麻岩石壁上，外覆一亭。北面总长5.5米，高约2米，厚约1米。刻面保存良好，字迹清晰。

文字依岩石西高东低的形势布局，共十二行60字。其中首行、二行、五行、六行、九行、十一行为5字，三行、四行、十行为6字，七行、八行、十二行为4字。行距、字距、字径皆不等。最小字高8厘米，宽10厘米，最大字高17厘米，宽24厘米。刻石文字内容如下：东海郡朐与琅琊郡柜为界，因诸山以南属朐，水以北属柜，西直况其，朐与柜分高柜为界，东各承无极。始建国四年二月朔乙卯，以使者徐州牧治所书造。

羊窝头刻石位置险要，人迹罕至，1987年发现时，刻石已因风化与母岩分离，断为左右二截紧密相依的楔形大石，右石与左石前后相错，左右北面伸入右石，造成左右部分刻字损坏。刻面布局自然，就着石壁西高东低的形势摩刻而成。由于长期遭海水侵蚀，多数字迹已模糊不清。右刻石高110厘米，宽70厘米，文四行；左刻石高110厘米，宽80厘米，文四行。

刻文为阴刻竖书隶书带篆意，行字、行距、字距、字径均不等，小字高8厘米，宽12厘米，大字高20厘米，宽14厘米。因有苏马湾刻石作比，目前羊窝头刻石文字尚可辨认出40字：东海郡朐[与]琅琊郡柜[为]界，朐北界[尽]□，因诸山山[南]水以北柜。西直况[其]，[朐]与柜分高□[为]界；东各承无极（不能确认的字加[]，无法辨认的用□代替）。

· · · · ·
English

The Donglian Island Donghai-Langya Prefecture Boundary Stone Carvings are the earliest, most complete, clear-content, and precisely-dated boundary stone carvings of the late Western Han Dynasty discovered so far in China; their font shows the style of the initial stage of transition from seal script to clerical script, and are treasures and gems among existing Western Han stone carvings.

There are two stone carvings in total: one near the beach in the Suma Bay Scenic Area, and one at the north foot of Yangwotou (Sheep's Head) on the lighthouse mountain at the eastern section of Donglian Island, both facing the sea.

The Suma Bay stone carving is about 5 meters from the low-tide sea level, and the Yangwotou stone carving is about 8 meters from the low-tide sea level.

The Suma Bay stone carving is on an independent granite gneiss cliff south of the beach, covered by a pavilion.The north face has a total length of 5.

5 meters, a height of about 2 meters, and a thickness of about 1 meter.The carved surface is well preserved with clear characters.

The text is laid out following the rock's terrain of high west and low east, with a total of 12 lines and 60 characters.

Among them, the 1st, 2nd, 5th, 6th, 9th, and 11th lines have 5 characters; the 3rd, 4th, and 10th lines have 6 characters; the 7th, 8th, and 12th lines have 4 characters.

Line spacing, character spacing, and character diameter all vary.The smallest character is 8 centimeters high and 10 centimeters wide, and the largest is 17 centimeters high and 24 centimeters wide.

The content of the stone carving text is as follows: 'The Qu County of Donghai Commandery and the Ju County of Langya Commandery are bounded; because the mountains south belong to Qu, and north of the water belongs to Ju; west directly to Kuangqi; Qu and Ju are divided by Gaoju as the boundary; east each inherits infinity.

In the 4th year of Shijianguo, 2nd month, first day Yimao, made by the envoy and governor of Xuzhou at the administrative office.

' The Yangwotou stone carving is in a strategic location rarely visited by people; when discovered in 1987, the stone carving had separated from the parent rock due to weathering, broken into left and right two sections of wedge-shaped large stones closely adjacent; the right stone and left stone are staggered front and back, with the left and right north faces extending into the right stone, causing damage to the left and right parts of the carved characters.

The carved surface layout is natural, carved following the cliff's terrain of high west and low east.Due to long-term seawater erosion, most characters have become blurry and unclear.

The right stone carving is 110 centimeters high and 70 centimeters wide, with 4 lines of text; the left stone carving is 110 centimeters high and 80 centimeters wide, with 4 lines of text.

The carved text is intaglio vertical clerical script with seal script overtones; line characters, line spacing, character spacing, and character diameter all vary; small characters are 8 centimeters high and 12 centimeters wide, large characters are 20 centimeters high and 14 centimeters wide.

Because the Suma Bay stone carving serves as a comparison, currently 40 characters of the Yangwotou stone carving text can still be recognized: 'The Qu County of Donghai [Commandery] and Ju County of Langya [Commandery are bounded]; Qu's north boundary [ends at] □, because the mountains [south] and north of the water [belong to] Ju.

West directly to Kuang[qi], [Qu] and Ju divide by Gao□ [as] boundary; east each inherits infinity' (unconfirmable characters are marked with [], unrecognizable ones are replaced with □).

建筑要点 / Key Features
东连岛东海琅琊郡界域刻石是我国迄今发现的时间最早最为完整内容明确有确切纪年的西汉晚期界域刻石其字体显示出从篆转变为隶书的初创阶段的风格是现存西汉石刻中的珍品和瑰宝刻石共有二处一在苏马湾景区内沙滩附近一在东连岛东段灯塔山羊窝头北山麓均面海而立苏马湾刻石距海水低潮平面约5米羊窝头刻石距海水低潮平面约8米苏马湾刻石在沙滩南侧一块独立的花岗片麻岩石壁上外覆一亭北面总长5.5米高约2米厚约1米刻面保存良好字迹清晰文字依岩石西高东低的形势布局共十二行60字其中首行二行五行六行九行十一行为5字三行四行十行为6字七行八行十二行为4字行距字距字径皆不等最小字高8厘米宽10厘米最大字高17厘米宽24厘米刻石文字内容如下东海郡朐与琅琊郡柜为界因诸山以南属朐水以北属柜西直况其朐与柜分高柜为界东各承无极始建国四年二月朔乙卯以使者徐州牧治所书造羊窝头刻石位置险要人迹罕至1987年发现时刻石已因风化与母岩分离断为左右二截紧密相依的楔形大石右石与左石前后相错左右北面伸入右石造成左右部分刻字损坏刻面布局自然就着石壁西高东低的形势摩刻而成由于长期遭海水侵蚀多数字迹已模糊不清右刻石高110厘米宽70厘米文四行左刻石高110

宿迁

Suqian
5
处建筑

地区概述 / Regional Overview

宿迁是西楚霸王项羽的故里，位于江苏省北部，京杭大运河沿岸。宿迁古建筑以清代行宫、寺庙和近代建筑为特色，乾隆行宫（龙王庙）是世界文化遗产京杭大运河的重要遗产点，极乐律院曾是苏北最大的佛教律院。

Suqian is the hometown of Xiang Yu, the Overlord of Western Chu, located in northern Jiangsu Province along the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal.

Suqian's ancient architecture features Qing Dynasty palaces, temples, and modern buildings; the Qianlong Auxiliary Palace (Dragon King Temple) is an important heritage site of the World Cultural Heritage Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal, and Jile Temple was once the largest Buddhist Vinaya temple in northern Jiangsu.

01 乾隆行宫（龙王庙）
Auxiliary Palace of Emperor Qianlong (Temple of Dragon King)
清
级别 Level
世界文化遗产，第五批全国重点文物保护单位（2001年）
地址 Address
宿迁西北20公里处宿豫区皂河镇
类型 Type
古建筑/行宫
门票 Ticket
60元（联票70元，含乾隆行宫、合善堂、陈家大院和财神庙）

中文原文

黄河在宿迁境内多次决口，为祈求保佑、消除水患，清顺治年间建龙王庙，清康熙二十三年（1684年）改建。乾隆六次南巡，主要目的是视察黄河，因而五次在此驻跸，俗称乾隆行宫，2014年随京杭大运河入选世界文化遗产名录。

行宫坐北朝南，包括东、中、西三路，以中路为主体，左右对称，轴线分明，布局严整，规模宏大。入口朝东，位于西南角，向东穿过一道三券式牌楼进入中路庭院。庭院东西各有一座牌楼，分别题河清、海晏，点明治水主旨。

院南为奏平成戏楼，坐南朝北，供龙王看戏，1976年拆除，后来重建。院北是三间歇山顶山门，是乾隆御题敕建安澜龙王庙匾额，门前有一对清代石狮，室内供哼哈二将。

门北庭院正中为御碑亭，六角攒尖重檐顶，覆黄色琉璃瓦，下部有两圈12根木柱。亭内碑高5米，正面刻圣旨全文，记叙建庙缘由和经过，背面刻乾隆五次巡视宿迁所写的诗文。

御碑亭前东西分别为钟楼和鼓楼，皆为重檐歇山顶，钟楼内悬清嘉庆十八年（1813年）马士魁所铸八角铁钟，重2000余斤，鼓楼置直径1.4米的大鼓。

亭北为怡殿，供四大金刚，象征风调雨顺。殿内院北为行宫主体建筑龙王殿，面阔七间，重檐歇山顶，用黄蓝绿等六色琉璃瓦覆面，正中供奉东海龙王，左右分列八大水神。殿前的东西配殿分别供五湖神和四海神，伺拜龙王。乾隆五次巡视，都是在龙王殿内议事敬神。

殿北有门通向最后一进院落，院北为禹王殿，宽七间，两层重檐硬山顶，一层明间供南海观音，二层明间供大禹像，两侧是乾隆皇帝的书房和寝宫。殿前左右是东、西两宫娘娘的寝殿。

院南入口两侧分别是东西庑殿和灵官殿，庑殿供文武官员侍驾，灵官殿又叫分宫厅，皇后妃嫔进入此院后，禁止官员入内。院内植有柏、柿、桐、椿、槐、杨6棵树，寓意百世同春、百世怀畅。禹王殿西侧小院为御膳房，东、西两路曾有御花园，现在做了简单修复。

在乾隆行宫东北60米为合善堂，建于清光绪二十年（1894年），有前后两进庭院，门票10元（或购买联票）。

出行宫沿通圣街向北约1000米有财神庙和陈家大院（门票20元），可乘坐观光车，往返5元。

陈家大院建于清嘉庆年间，包括南北2路6座庭院共66间房屋，是宿迁最大的清代民居，值得一看。

· · · · ·
English

The Yellow River breached its banks multiple times within Suqian; to pray for protection and eliminate flood disasters, the Dragon King Temple was built during the Shunzhi reign of the Qing, and rebuilt in the 23rd year of Kangxi of the Qing (1684).

Qianlong made six southern tours, the main purpose being to inspect the Yellow River, and thus stayed here five times, commonly called the Qianlong Auxiliary Palace; in 2014 it was included in the World Cultural Heritage List along with the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal.

The auxiliary palace faces south, including east, central, and west three routes, with the central route as the main body, symmetrical left and right, with clear axes, a rigorous layout, and a grand scale.

The entrance faces east, located at the southwest corner; going east through a three-arch paifang leads into the central courtyard.

On the east and west of the courtyard are a paifang each, respectively inscribed 'River Clear' and 'Sea Calm,' pointing out the main theme of water control.

South of the courtyard is the Zoupingcheng Opera Tower, facing north, for the Dragon King to watch opera; it was demolished in 1976 and later rebuilt.

North of the courtyard are three bays of a hip-and-gable mountain gate, with a plaque of the imperial title 'Imperially Built Anlan Dragon King Temple' by Qianlong; in front of the gate are a pair of Qing Dynasty stone lions, and inside are enshrined the Heng and Ha two generals.

In the center of the courtyard north of the gate is the Imperial Stele Pavilion, with a hexagonal pyramidal double-eave roof covered with yellow glazed tiles, and two rings of 12 wooden columns at the lower part.

Inside the pavilion, the stele is 5 meters high; the front is engraved with the full text of the imperial edict, narrating the reason and process of building the temple, and the back is engraved with poems and essays written by Qianlong during his five inspections of Suqian.

East and west in front of the Imperial Stele Pavilion are respectively the Bell Tower and Drum Tower, both with double-eave hip-and-gable roofs; inside the Bell Tower hangs an octagonal iron bell cast by Ma Shikui in the 18th year of Jiaqing of the Qing (1813), weighing over 2000 jin, and the Drum Tower has a large drum 1.

4 meters in diameter.North of the pavilion is the Yi Hall, enshrining the Four Heavenly Kings, symbolizing favorable weather.

North of the inner courtyard of the hall is the main building of the auxiliary palace, the Dragon King Hall, seven bays wide, with a double-eave hip-and-gable roof, covered with six colors of glazed tiles such as yellow, blue, and green; in the center is enshrined the Dragon King of the East Sea, with eight great water gods arranged on the left and right.

The east and west side halls in front of the hall respectively enshrine the Five Lake Gods and the Four Sea Gods, serving the Dragon King.

Qianlong's five inspections all involved discussing affairs and worshipping gods in the Dragon King Hall.

North of the hall there is a door leading to the last courtyard; north of the courtyard is the Yu King (King Yu) Hall, seven bays wide, a two-story double-eave flush-gable building; the first floor central bay enshrines the South Sea Guanyin, the second floor central bay enshrines the statue of Great Yu, and on both sides are Emperor Qianlong's study and bedroom.

Left and right in front of the hall are the bedchambers of the East and West Palace empresses.

On both sides of the south entrance of the courtyard are respectively the east and west side halls and the Lingguan Hall; the side halls enshrine civil and military officials attending the emperor, and the Lingguan Hall is also called the Fenghuang (Palace Division) Hall; after the empress and concubines enter this courtyard, officials are prohibited from entering.

In the courtyard are planted 6 trees: cypress, persimmon, paulownia, toon, locust, and poplar, symbolizing 'a hundred generations of spring together' and 'a hundred generations of cherished harmony.

' The small courtyard west of the Yu King Hall is the imperial kitchen; the east and west routes once had imperial gardens, now simply restored.

60 meters northeast of the Qianlong Auxiliary Palace is the Heshantang (Good Deeds Hall), built in the 20th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1894), with front and rear two courtyards, ticket 10 yuan (or buy a combined ticket).

Exiting the auxiliary palace and going north along Tongsheng Street for about 1000 meters are the God of Wealth Temple and the Chen Family Compound (ticket 20 yuan); one can take a sightseeing cart, 5 yuan round trip.

The Chen Family Compound was built during the Jiaqing reign of the Qing, including 6 courtyards on 2 north-south routes with a total of 66 rooms, the largest Qing Dynasty folk residence in Suqian, worth seeing.

建筑要点 / Key Features
黄河在宿迁境内多次决口为祈求保佑消除水患清顺治年间建龙王庙清康熙二十三年1684年改建乾隆六次南巡主要目的是视察黄河因而五次在此驻跸俗称乾隆行宫2014年随京杭大运河入选世界文化遗产名录行宫坐北朝南包括东中西三路以中路为主体左右对称轴线分明布局严整规模宏大入口朝东位于西南角向东穿过一道三券式牌楼进入中路庭院庭院东西各有一座牌楼分别题河清海晏点明治水主旨院南为奏平成戏楼坐南朝北供龙王看戏1976年拆除后来重建院北是三间歇山顶山门是乾隆御题敕建安澜龙王庙匾额门前有一对清代石狮室内供哼哈二将门北庭院正中为御碑亭六角攒尖重檐顶覆黄色琉璃瓦下部有两圈12根木柱亭内碑高5米正面刻圣旨全文记叙建庙缘由和经过背面刻乾隆五次巡视宿迁所写的诗文御碑亭前东西分别为钟楼和鼓楼皆为重檐歇山顶钟楼内悬清嘉庆十八年1813年马士魁所铸八角铁钟重2000余斤鼓楼置直径1.4米的大鼓亭北为怡殿供四大金刚象征风调雨顺殿内院北为行宫主体建筑龙王殿面阔七间重檐歇山顶用黄蓝绿等六色琉璃瓦覆面正中供奉东海龙王左右分列八大水神殿前的东西配殿分别供五湖神和四海神伺拜龙王乾隆五次巡视都是在龙王殿内议事敬神殿北有门通向最后一进院落院北为
02 项王故里
Homeland of King Xiang Yu

中文原文

宿迁是西楚霸王项羽的故里，即《史记》所称项羽，下相人也，当时叫作梧桐巷。唐宋时期人们在梧桐巷立坊，后因黄河泛滥而毁。清康熙四十二年（1703年）知县胡三俊在项羽手植槐旁立项王故里碑，1931年增建草厅等简易纪念建筑。

今尚存项羽手植槐（树龄2200年）、老梧桐树（树龄2300年）和项家古井三处古迹。1983年在原址重建项王故里，坐北朝南共三进，采用汉代建筑风格，有石牌坊、子母阙、英风阁等。

2012年在故里南侧建成项王故里景区，包括古城门、项羽雕像、项府、项园、将署、项羽故居、项家宗祠、霸王古今馆和虞家老宅等十余个主要景点，通过展览、影片、演出等全面生动地讲述了项羽波澜壮阔的一生。在重瞳宫可欣赏项王生平4D影片（散客需另购20元票，可用铜币），项氏府邸有楚女歌舞，免费且较为精彩。

景区东部为真如禅寺，俗称南大寺，免费开放。

真如寺前身为寿圣寺，始建于元大德四年（1300年），历代多次重修，1898年曾遭火灾，1976年全部拆除，2005年重建，有山门、玉佛殿和大雄宝殿等。

· · · · ·
English

Suqian is the hometown of Xiang Yu, the Overlord of Western Chu, as called in 'Records of the Grand Historian'—Xiang Yu was a man of Xiaxiang, at that time called Wutong (Phoenix Tree) Lane.

During the Tang and Song periods, people erected a paifang in Wutong Lane, which was later destroyed due to Yellow River flooding.

In the 42nd year of Kangxi of the Qing (1703), County Magistrate Hu Sanjun erected a 'Homeland of King Xiang' stele beside the locust tree planted by Xiang Yu himself; in 1931, simple memorial buildings such as a thatched hall were added.

Today, three historic sites still survive: the locust tree planted by Xiang Yu (2200 years old), the old phoenix tree (2300 years old), and the Xiang family ancient well.

In 1983, the Homeland of King Xiang Yu was rebuilt on the original site, facing south with three courtyards, adopting Han Dynasty architectural style, with stone paifang, mother-and-child watchtowers, and Yingfeng (Heroic Wind) Pavilion etc.

In 2012, the Homeland of King Xiang Yu Scenic Area was built south of the homeland, including over ten main attractions such as the ancient city gate, Xiang Yu statue, Xiang Mansion, Xiang Garden, General's Office, Xiang Yu's Former Residence, Xiang Family Ancestral Hall, Overlord Past and Present Hall, and Yu Family Old Residence etc.

; through exhibitions, films, and performances, it comprehensively and vividly tells the story of Xiang Yu's magnificent life.

In the Chongtong (Double Pupil) Palace, one can enjoy a 4D film of King Xiang's life (individual visitors need to buy an additional 20-yuan ticket, copper coins can be used); the Xiang Family Mansion has Chu female singing and dancing, free and quite精彩.

East of the scenic area is Zhenru Chan Temple, commonly called South Great Temple, free to enter.

Zhenru Temple's predecessor was Shousheng Temple, first built in the 4th year of Dade of the Yuan (1300), repeatedly rebuilt through the dynasties, suffered a fire in 1898, completely demolished in 1976, and rebuilt in 2005, with a mountain gate, Jade Buddha Hall, and Mahavira Hall etc.

建筑要点 / Key Features
宿迁是西楚霸王项羽的故里即史记所称项羽下相人也当时叫作梧桐巷唐宋时期人们在梧桐巷立坊后因黄河泛滥而毁清康熙四十二年1703年知县胡三俊在项羽手植槐旁立项王故里碑1931年增建草厅等简易纪念建筑今尚存项羽手植槐树龄2200年老梧桐树树龄2300年和项家古井三处古迹1983年在原址重建项王故里坐北朝南共三进采用汉代建筑风格有石牌坊子母阙英风阁等2012年在故里南侧建成项王故里景区包括古城门项羽雕像项府项园将署项羽故居项家宗祠霸王古今馆和虞家老宅等十余个主要景点通过展览影片演出等全面生动地讲述了项羽波澜壮阔的一生在重瞳宫可欣赏项王生平4D影片散客需另购20元票可用铜币项氏府邸有楚女歌舞免费且较为精彩景区东部为真如禅寺俗称南大寺免费开放真如寺前身为寿圣寺始建于元大德四年1300年历代多次重修1898年曾遭火灾1976年全部拆除2005年重建有山门玉佛殿和大雄宝殿等

中文原文

敕赐极乐律院坐落在马陵山余脉——灵赫山脊上，北依锅矿山，西邻黄河故道，东靠京杭大运河。始建于明万历五年（1577年），原名马神庙，后改称极乐庵；因住持僧人宗奉律宗，庙内有朝廷钦赐的《藏经》，又改称敕赐极乐律院。

寺院自康熙朝开始大规模扩建，到清末鼎盛时期有六进院落，近千间房屋，六七百名僧众，城外耕地10万亩，是苏北最大的佛教律院，曾领多处下院，以至清末流行上有五台山，下有极乐庵的谚语。1929年受小刀会起义牵连，庙产被查封，逐渐荒废。文革时期《藏经》藏本和木雕佛像被焚毁，寺庙建筑也被毁坏。

律院今存大雄宝殿、藏经楼、大方丈室、玉佛楼和僧房等，是典型的北方民间建筑。大雄宝殿宽五间，单檐硬山顶，内部的人字梁构架较为罕见，具有较高的建筑艺术价值。

· · · · ·
English

The Imperially Bestowed Jile Vinaya Temple is located on the Linghe Mountain ridge, a branch of the Maling Mountains, backed by Guokuang Mountain to the north, adjacent to the old Yellow River course to the west, and leaning on the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal to the east.

First built in the 5th year of Wanli of the Ming (1577), originally named Horse God Temple, later renamed Jile Nunnery; because the abbot monk followed the Vinaya school and the temple had an imperially bestowed 'Tripitaka,' it was renamed the Imperially Bestowed Jile Vinaya Temple.

The temple began large-scale expansion from the Kangxi reign, and by its peak at the end of the Qing it had six courtyards, nearly a thousand rooms, six to seven hundred monks, and 100,000 mu of farmland outside the city; it was the largest Buddhist Vinaya temple in northern Jiangsu, once heading multiple branch temples, so much so that at the end of the Qing the proverb 'Above there is Wutai Mountain, below there is Jile Temple' was popular.

In 1929, implicated in the Small Swords Society uprising, the temple property was sealed and gradually fell into disrepair.

During the Cultural Revolution, the 'Tripitaka' collection and wood-carved Buddha statues were burned, and the temple buildings were also destroyed.

Today the Vinaya temple preserves the Mahavira Hall, Sutra Repository, Great Abbot's Room, Jade Buddha Building, and monk rooms etc., typical northern folk architecture.

The Mahavira Hall is five bays wide, with a single-eave flush-gable roof, and its internal herringbone beam framework is relatively rare, with high architectural artistic value.

建筑要点 / Key Features
敕赐极乐律院坐落在马陵山余脉灵赫山脊上北依锅矿山西邻黄河故道东靠京杭大运河始建于明万历五年1577年原名马神庙后改称极乐庵因住持僧人宗奉律宗庙内有朝廷钦赐的藏经又改称敕赐极乐律院寺院自康熙朝开始大规模扩建到清末鼎盛时期有六进院落近千间房屋六七百名僧众城外耕地10万亩是苏北最大的佛教律院曾领多处下院以至清末流行上有五台山下有极乐庵的谚语1929年受小刀会起义牵连庙产被查封逐渐荒废文革时期经藏本和木雕佛像被焚毁寺庙建筑也被毁坏律院今存大雄宝殿藏经楼大方丈室玉佛楼和僧房等是典型的北方民间建筑大雄宝殿宽五间单檐硬山顶内部的人字梁构架较为罕见具有较高的建筑艺术价值

宿城区幸福中路26号
类型 Type
近代建筑/商业建筑
中文原文

1882年美国传教士到宿迁传教，最初外来洋教无人信奉，教士走在街头常被孩子欺负，宿迁人张道生出面维护，美国教士认为他诚实质朴，帮他谋得销售洋碱、洋油的机会。张道生后来成为美孚公司在宿迁的代理，富冠全城，他的致富也为美国人的传教打开了局面。1897年张道生建造了宿迁当时最高的商业建筑——道生碱店。

该店采用中西合璧风格，主体三层，采用平屋顶；中段高起为四层，采用四角盈顶。墙体主要使用青砖，在拱券和花饰等重点部位，则使用较珍贵的进口红砖。入口位于南侧，采用拱券外廊式，其他三面则开简单的方形长窗。这是由中国工匠自发设计建造的西式建筑，反映了100多年前中国对于西方建筑的效仿和借鉴。道生碱店于2009年修缮为宿迁文化名人馆。

· · · · ·
English

In 1882, American missionaries came to Suqian to preach; initially the foreign religion had no believers, and missionaries walking on the street were often bullied by children.

Zhang Daosheng, a Suqian native, stepped forward to protect them; the American missionaries considered him honest and simple, and helped him obtain the opportunity to sell foreign alkali and foreign kerosene.

Zhang Daosheng later became the agent of Standard Oil Company in Suqian, the richest man in the city, and his wealth also opened up the situation for American missionary work.

In 1897, Zhang Daosheng built the tallest commercial building in Suqian at that time—the Daosheng Alkali Store.

The store adopts a Chinese-Western combined style, with a three-story main body using a flat roof; the middle section rises to four stories, using a four-corner domed roof.

The walls mainly use grey bricks, while at key parts such as arches and floral decorations, more precious imported red bricks are used.

The entrance is on the south side, adopting an arched exterior corridor style, while the other three sides have simple square long windows.

This is a Western-style building spontaneously designed and built by Chinese craftsmen, reflecting China's imitation and reference to Western architecture over 100 years ago.

The Daosheng Alkali Store was renovated into the Suqian Cultural Celebrity Hall in 2009.

建筑要点 / Key Features
1882年美国传教士到宿迁传教最初外来洋教无人信奉教士走在街头常被孩子欺负宿迁人张道生出面维护美国教士认为他诚实质朴帮他谋得销售洋碱洋油的机会张道生后来成为美孚公司在宿迁的代理富冠全城他的致富也为美国人的传教打开了局面1897年张道生建造了宿迁当时最高的商业建筑道生碱店该店采用中西合璧风格主体三层采用平屋顶中段高起为四层采用四角盈顶墙体主要使用青砖在拱券和花饰等重点部位则使用较珍贵的进口红砖入口位于南侧采用拱券外廊式其他三面则开简单的方形长窗这是由中国工匠自发设计建造的西式建筑反映了100多年前中国对于西方建筑的效仿和借鉴道生碱店于2009年修缮为宿迁文化名人馆
05 耶稣堂
Jesus Chapel
民国
级别 Level
第六批省级文物保护单位（2006年）
地址 Address
黄运路119号
类型 Type
近代建筑/教堂
中文原文

1924—1925年宿迁、邳州和睢宁的耶稣教徒、教会医院医生和教会学校师生募款，牧师彭楚云主持修建。这座教堂采用砖木结构，外墙用清水青砖砌筑，以砖倚柱分隔开间，开彩色玻璃窗，上部是红瓦屋顶。平面呈十字形，东西、南北各长约20米，四个立面基本相同又略有变化。

教堂内部东侧是木地板布道台，中部是通高的厅堂，可容400人，南、北、西三侧在二层设观众席，可容200人。在宿城区黄河南路38号宿迁中学内还有一座文庙大成殿，2006年列为省保单位，不对外开放。

宿迁文庙始建于元代，原在今项王故里东南其外，为避黄河水患三易其址，明崇祯八年（1635年）迁至今址，自南向北依次为棂星门、泮池、戟门、大成殿和明伦堂，左右有配房。

今仅存泮池和崇祯年间所建的大成殿。

· · · · ·
English

In 1924-1925, Jesus believers in Suqian, Pizhou, and Suining, doctors from church hospitals, and teachers and students from church schools raised funds, with Pastor Peng Chuyun presiding over the construction.

This church adopts a brick-wood structure, with exterior walls built with plain grey bricks, brick engaged columns separating bays, colored glass windows, and a red tile roof on top.

The plan is cross-shaped, about 20 meters long east-west and north-south, with the four facades basically the same yet slightly varied.

Inside the church, the east side is a wooden-floor preaching platform, the center is a full-height hall that can accommodate 400 people, and the south, north, and west sides have audience seats on the second floor that can accommodate 200 people.

Inside Suqian Middle School at No.38 South Huanghe Road, Sucheng District, there is also a Dacheng Hall of a Confucian Temple, listed as a provincial protected unit in 2006, not open to the public.

The Suqian Confucian Temple was first built in the Yuan Dynasty, originally located southeast of today's Homeland of King Xiang Yu; to avoid Yellow River floods it changed its site three times, and in the 8th year of Chongzhen of the Ming (1635) it moved to the current site.

From south to north are依次 the Lingxing Gate, Pan Pond, Halberd Gate, Dacheng Hall, and Minglun Hall, with side rooms on the left and right.

Today only the Pan Pond and the Dacheng Hall built during the Chongzhen reign survive.

建筑要点 / Key Features
19241925年宿迁邳州和睢宁的耶稣教徒教会医院医生和教会学校师生募款牧师彭楚云主持修建这座教堂采用砖木结构外墙用清水青砖砌筑以砖倚柱分隔开间开彩色玻璃窗上部是红瓦屋顶平面呈十字形东西南北各长约20米四个立面基本相同又略有变化教堂内部东侧是木地板布道台中部是通高的厅堂可容400人南北西三侧在二层设观众席可容200人在宿城区黄河南路38号宿迁中学内还有一座文庙大成殿2006年列为省保单位不对外开放宿迁文庙始建于元代原在今项王故里东南其外为避黄河水患三易其址明崇祯八年1635年迁至今址自南向北依次为棂星门泮池戟门大成殿和明伦堂左右有配房今仅存泮池和崇祯年间所建的大成殿

盐城

Yancheng
4
处建筑

地区概述 / Regional Overview

盐城位于江苏省东部沿海，因盐得名，历史上是重要的海盐产区。盐城古建筑以寺庙、名人故居和古塔为特色，泰山庙是新四军重建军部旧址，海春轩塔是唐代密檐式砖塔的重要实例。

Yancheng is located on the eastern coast of Jiangsu Province, named after salt, and historically an important sea salt production area.

Yancheng's ancient architecture features temples, celebrity former residences, and ancient pagodas; Taishan Temple is the former site of the rebuilt headquarters of the New Fourth Army, and Haichunxuan Pagoda is an important example of Tang Dynasty multi-eave brick pagodas.

01 泰山庙（新四军重建军部旧址）
Taishan Temple (Former Rebuilt Headquarters of New Fourth Army)
1941—1945
级别 Level
第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
地址 Address
亭湖区建军西路126号泰山庙
类型 Type
古建筑/寺庙/革命旧址
中文原文

1941年1月，叶挺、项英奉命率领新四军移至长江以北，在安徽泾县遭到国民党伏击，军长叶挺被俘，副军长项英、参谋长周子昆遇难，7000余人牺牲，是为震惊中外的皖南事变。周恩来为《新华日报》写下了千古奇冤，江南一叶；同室操戈，相煎何急的题词。事变后国民党遭到各界人士的一致谴责，政治上空前孤立。同年1月新四军在盐城重建军部，军部驻地即在原泰山庙内。

泰山庙由前殿、正殿和后殿组成，正殿曾作为新四军司令部作战室。如今庙内陈列着刘少奇、陈毅和大将黄克诚的生平图片以及新四军纪念馆馆藏书画。

除了泰山庙，在建军路和解放路交叉口立有大铜马雕像（新四军重建军部纪念碑），在建军东路159号建有新四军纪念馆，三者被当地人合称为新马泰，构成全国规模最大、资料最全、特色最鲜明的新四军纪念设施。

· · · · ·
English

In January 1941, Ye Ting and Xiang Ying were ordered to lead the New Fourth Army to move north of the Yangtze River, and were ambushed by the Kuomintang in Jingxian, Anhui; Army Commander Ye Ting was captured, Deputy Army Commander Xiang Ying and Chief of Staff Zhou Zikun died, and over 7,000 people sacrificed—this was the world-shocking Southern Anhui Incident.

Zhou Enlai wrote the inscription for the 'Xinhua Daily': 'A strange injustice through the ages, a leaf south of the Yangtze; brothers fighting each other, why so urgent to fry each other.

' After the incident, the Kuomintang was unanimously condemned by people from all walks of life and became politically isolated as never before.

In January of the same year, the New Fourth Army rebuilt its military headquarters in Yancheng, with the headquarters stationed in the former Taishan Temple.

Taishan Temple consists of a front hall, main hall, and rear hall; the main hall once served as the operations room of the New Fourth Army headquarters.

Today, the temple displays life photos of Liu Shaoqi, Chen Yi, and General Huang Kecheng, as well as calligraphy and paintings collected by the New Fourth Army Memorial Hall.

In addition to Taishan Temple, a large bronze horse statue (Monument to the Rebuilt Headquarters of the New Fourth Army) stands at the intersection of Jianjun Road and Jiefang Road, and the New Fourth Army Memorial Hall is built at No.

159 East Jianjun Road; the three are collectively called 'Xin-Ma-Tai' (New Fourth Army, Bronze Horse, Taishan Temple) by locals, forming the largest, most comprehensive, and most distinctive New Fourth Army memorial facility in the country.

建筑要点 / Key Features
1941年1月叶挺项英奉命率领新四军移至长江以北在安徽泾县遭到国民党伏击军长叶挺被俘副军长项英参谋长周子昆遇难7000余人牺牲是为震惊中外的皖南事变周恩来为新华日报写下了千古奇冤江南一叶同室操戈相煎何急的题词事变后国民党遭到各界人士的一致谴责政治上空前孤立同年1月新四军在盐城重建军部军部驻地即在原泰山庙内泰山庙由前殿正殿和后殿组成正殿曾作为新四军司令部作战室如今庙内陈列着刘少奇陈毅和大将黄克诚的生平图片以及新四军纪念馆馆藏书画除了泰山庙在建军路和解放路交叉口立有大铜马雕像新四军重建军部纪念碑在建军东路159号建有新四军纪念馆三者被当地人合称为新马泰构成全国规模最大资料最全特色最鲜明的新四军纪念设施
02 宋丞相陆公祠
Lu's Shrine
明—清
级别 Level
第四批省级文物保护单位（1995年）
地址 Address
亭湖区儒学街陆公祠巷4号
类型 Type
古建筑/祠堂
门票 Ticket
免费开放
开放时间 Hours
8:30 — 11:30, 14:30 — 17:30（周一闭馆）
中文原文

陆秀夫（1236—1279）祖籍楚州盐城（今建湖县建阳镇），官至南宋左丞相，为抗元名臣，与文天祥、张世杰并称宋末三杰。1279年在崖山兵败后，他背着卫王赴海而死。

明代蒋一葵《尧山堂外纪》引用民谚，将他与文天祥并称：擎天者，文天祥；捧日者，陆秀夫。明嘉靖十年（1531年）盐城知县程节为陆秀夫建祠纪念，明清两代多次重修。今祠堂包括东西两路，皆为三进。

入口位于西路，自南向北有序厅、景忠堂和正祠堂；东路有仰止堂和浩然堂等。

· · · · ·
English

Lu Xiufu (1236-1279), whose ancestral home was Yancheng, Chuzhou (today's Jianyang Town, Jianhu County), rose to the position of Left Prime Minister of the Southern Song Dynasty, was a famous official resisting the Yuan, and was called one of the 'Three Heroes of the Late Song' together with Wen Tianxiang and Zhang Shijie.

After the defeat at Yashan in 1279, he carried King Wei on his back and died in the sea.

In the Ming Dynasty, Jiang Yikui's 'Outer Records of Yaoshan Hall' quoted a folk proverb, calling him and Wen Tianxiang together: 'The one who props up the sky is Wen Tianxiang; the one who holds up the sun is Lu Xiufu.

' In the 10th year of Jiajing of the Ming (1531), Cheng Jie, County Magistrate of Yancheng, built a shrine to commemorate Lu Xiufu, and it was repeatedly repaired in the Ming and Qing dynasties.

Today the shrine includes east and west two routes, both with three courtyards.

The entrance is on the west route; from south to north are the Preface Hall, Jingzhong (Loyalty Scenery) Hall, and the Main Shrine Hall; the east route has Yangzhi (Looking Up) Hall and Haoran (Noble Spirit) Hall etc.

建筑要点 / Key Features
陆秀夫12361279祖籍楚州盐城今建湖县建阳镇官至南宋左丞相为抗元名臣与文天祥张世杰并称宋末三杰1279年在崖山兵败后他背着卫王赴海而死明代蒋一葵尧山堂外纪引用民谚将他与文天祥并称擎天者文天祥捧日者陆秀夫明嘉靖十年1531年盐城知县程节为陆秀夫建祠纪念明清两代多次重修今祠堂包括东西两路皆为三进入口位于西路自南向北有序厅景忠堂和正祠堂东路有仰止堂和浩然堂等

Residence of Song Cao

中文原文

宋曹宅为明末清初书画家宋曹（1620—？）故居，今为盐城书画院。共有东西两进，东院包括院门、蔬枰草堂、桐引楼和中厅；西院包括听琴茶社、琴亭和碑廊。两进院落皆凿池叠石，景致幽雅可观。

· · · · ·
English

The Residence of Song Cao is the former residence of Song Cao (1620-?

), a calligrapher and painter of the late Ming and early Qing dynasties, today the Yancheng Calligraphy and Painting Academy.

It has a total of east and west two courtyards; the east courtyard includes the gate, Shuping Thatched Hall, Tongyin (Paulownia Leading) Tower, and central hall; the west courtyard includes the Tingqin (Listening to Qin) Tea House, Qin Pavilion, and Stele Corridor.

Both courtyards have ponds dug and rocks piled, with elegant and enjoyable scenery.

04 海春轩塔
Haichunxuan Pagoda
唐
级别 Level
第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
地址 Address
东台市西溪镇
类型 Type
古塔/密檐式塔
门票 Ticket
免费开放
开放时间 Hours
免费开放
中文原文

东台县设于清乾隆三十三年（1768年），从西汉到清代，一直是重点海盐产区。明代哲学家王艮、清代布衣诗人吴嘉纪和水利学家冯道立等都是东台人。东台最重要的古迹是位于城外西南的海春轩塔。

市区较重要的文物建筑有位于寺前东街的戈公振故居（8:30—12:00，15:00—17:30免费开放）、红兰南路84号的东明电气股份有限公司旧址（张謇纪念馆，未开放）和东亭南路西侧的沈氏大楼（周巍峙王昆纪念馆，未开放）等。

海春轩塔属于广福寺，据宋《晏溪遗志》记载海春轩塔，在镇南广福寺侧，传为唐太宗时大将尉迟敬德监造，塔顶有题名，可知此塔建于唐贞观年间。

学者方长源认为西溪原有海春轩塔和广福寺塔，海春轩塔废坏后，广福寺塔被讹传为今海春轩塔，他认为今塔建于北宋早期，并保留了许多唐塔的特点。据说尉迟敬德是遵母之命建塔，因此也称孝母塔、尉迟塔；因位于黄河岸边，兼有镇海和导航之用，又称镇海塔。

唐大历二年（767年）淮南西道黜陟使李承修将其定名为海春轩塔，并题诗曰：东设点将台，西有溪通淮。海春轩潮旺，皆由此塔来。这是一座七层八角砖结构密檐塔。

内部为双层空腔式结构，砖砌塔壁叠涩内挑，形成八角形弧线锥体；外为密檐式塔身，轮廓优美，底层较高，朝西北开门，二层以上8面各设一座圭形佛龛，共有48座；塔顶宝刹由铁覆盆、相轮和铜葫芦构成，反映了唐代密檐式砖塔的艺术特点。

海春轩塔所在的西溪镇有多处文保单位。塔南为北宋开挖的古运盐河，又名北官河。东北为始建于北宋的市保单位泰山护国禅寺（门票10元），寺南为通圣桥，沿河向西有颇具特色的八字桥。

周围近年新建了宋城景区和董永、七仙女文化公园，皆免费开放。

· · · · ·
English

Dongtai County was established in the 33rd year of Qianlong of the Qing (1768); from the Western Han to the Qing Dynasty, it was always a key sea salt production area.

Ming Dynasty philosopher Wang Gen, Qing Dynasty commoner poet Wu Jiaji, and water conservancy expert Feng Daoli etc.were all from Dongtai.

The most important historic site in Dongtai is Haichunxuan Pagoda, located southwest outside the city.

More important cultural relic buildings in the urban area include the Former Residence of Ge Gongzhen on East Siqian Street (8:30-12:00, 15:00-17:30, free), the former site of Dongming Electric Co.

, Ltd.at No.84 South Honglan Road (Zhang Jian Memorial Hall, not open), and the Shen Building west of South Dongting Road (Zhou Weizhi and Wang Kun Memorial Hall, not open) etc.

Haichunxuan Pagoda belongs to Guangfu Temple; according to the Song Dynasty 'Yanxi Remaining Records,' Haichunxuan Pagoda is on the side of Guangfu Temple south of the town, said to have been supervised by General Yuchi Jingde during the reign of Emperor Taizong of the Tang, with an inscription on the pagoda top, indicating this pagoda was built during the Zhenguan reign of the Tang.

Scholar Fang Changyuan believes that Xixi originally had Haichunxuan Pagoda and Guangfu Temple Pagoda; after Haichunxuan Pagoda was ruined, Guangfu Temple Pagoda was misrepresented as today's Haichunxuan Pagoda; he believes today's pagoda was built in the early Northern Song and retains many characteristics of Tang pagodas.

It is said that Yuchi Jingde built the pagoda by order of his mother, hence also called the Filial Mother Pagoda and Yuchi Pagoda; because it is located on the bank of the Yellow River, it also served to calm the sea and for navigation, hence also called the Zhenhai (Sea-Calming) Pagoda.

In the 2nd year of Dali of the Tang (767), Li Chengxiu, Surveillance Commissioner of the Huainan West Circuit, named it Haichunxuan Pagoda and inscribed a poem: 'East sets the general's platform, west has a stream connecting to the Huai.

The tides surge at Haichunxuan, all coming from this pagoda.' This is a seven-story octagonal brick multi-eave pagoda.

The interior has a double-layer cavity structure, with brick pagoda walls corbeled inward to form an octagonal curved cone; the exterior is a multi-eave pagoda body with an elegant silhouette, with a higher bottom story opening to the northwest; above the second story, each of the 8 sides has a gui-shaped Buddhist niche, totaling 48; the pagoda top finial consists of an iron basin,相轮 (ring tiers), and a copper gourd, reflecting the artistic characteristics of Tang Dynasty multi-eave brick pagodas.

Xixi Town, where Haichunxuan Pagoda is located, has multiple protected units.

South of the pagoda is the ancient salt transport canal excavated in the Northern Song, also called the North Official River.

Northeast is the city-protected Taishan Huguo (Protecting the Country) Chan Temple, first built in the Northern Song (ticket 10 yuan); south of the temple is the Tongsheng Bridge, and west along the river is the distinctive Bazi (Eight-Character) Bridge.

In recent years, the Song City Scenic Area and the Dong Yong and Seventh Fairy Cultural Park have been built around it, both free to enter.

建筑要点 / Key Features
东台县设于清乾隆三十三年1768年从西汉到清代一直是重点海盐产区明代哲学家王艮清代布衣诗人吴嘉纪和水利学家冯道立等都是东台人东台最重要的古迹是位于城外西南的海春轩塔市区较重要的文物建筑有位于寺前东街的戈公振故居830120015001730免费开放红兰南路84号的东明电气股份有限公司旧址张謇纪念馆未开放和东亭南路西侧的沈氏大楼周巍峙王昆纪念馆未开放等海春轩塔属于广福寺据宋晏溪遗志记载海春轩塔在镇南广福寺侧传为唐太宗时大将尉迟敬德监造塔顶有题名可知此塔建于唐贞观年间学者方长源认为西溪原有海春轩塔和广福寺塔海春轩塔废坏后广福寺塔被讹传为今海春轩塔他认为今塔建于北宋早期并保留了许多唐塔的特点据说尉迟敬德是遵母之命建塔因此也称孝母塔尉迟塔因位于黄河岸边兼有镇海和导航之用又称镇海塔唐大历二年767年淮南西道黜陟使李承修将其定名为海春轩塔并题诗曰东设点将台西有溪通淮海春轩潮旺皆由此塔来这是一座七层八角砖结构密檐塔内部为双层空腔式结构砖砌塔壁叠涩内挑形成八角形弧线锥体外为密檐式塔身轮廓优美底层较高朝西北开门二层以上8面各设一座圭形佛龛共有48座塔顶宝刹由铁覆盆相轮和铜葫芦构成反映了唐代密檐式砖塔的艺

上海

Shanghai
42
处建筑

地区概述 / Regional Overview

上海是中国近代化的缩影，既有豫园、城隍庙等明清古典园林和寺庙，也有外滩万国建筑博览群、国际饭店、大光明剧院等近代优秀建筑，还有徐家汇天主教堂、龙华塔等宗教建筑。上海古建筑以中西合璧、多元并存为特色，是研究中国近代建筑史的重要宝库。

Shanghai is a microcosm of China's modernization, with both Ming-Qing classical gardens and temples such as Yu Garden and City God Temple, and outstanding modern buildings such as the Bund's international architecture exhibition group, the Park Hotel, and the Grand Cinema, as well as religious buildings such as Xujiahui Catholic Church and Longhua Pagoda.

Shanghai's ancient architecture is characterized by the combination of Chinese and Western styles and pluralistic coexistence, making it an important treasure house for studying the history of modern Chinese architecture.

01 豫园
Yuyuan Garden
明—清
级别 Level
第二批全国重点文物保护单位（1982年）
地址 Address
黄浦区安仁街137号
类型 Type
古建筑/园林
门票 Ticket
旺季（4.1—6.30，9.1—11.30）40元，淡季30元
开放时间 Hours
7:30 — 18:00
中文原文

明嘉靖三十八年（1559年），潘允端（1526—1601）考试落第，回乡在宅西聚石凿池，构亭艺竹，三年后他考中进士，外出任官，园林建设随之中止。明万历五年（1577年）他从四川右布政使卸任归来，官事已了，才开始专心营筑园林，聘请造园名家张南阳主持。

潘允端的父亲潘恩（1496—1582）官至刑部尚书，当时已年过八旬，潘允端时奉老亲觞咏其间，并将园名题为豫园，取愉悦老亲之意（潘允端《豫园记》）。

园林建成后，占地70多亩，搜罗奇峰异石，点缀名花珍木，陆具涧岭洞壑之胜，水极岛滩梁渡之趣，陈所蕴《张山人传》将豫园与王世贞的弇山园并列，称赞两园百里相望，为东南名园冠。这两座园林以及陈所蕴的日涉园都是张南阳的杰作。

入清后园内建筑逐渐被同业公所（同行业的商人或工匠团体）占据，划界割裂；清乾隆二十五年（1760年）士绅们集资从潘氏后人手中购得豫园余地，陆续整治扩建，到清乾隆四十九年（1784年）大致形成今日豫园格局。

当时豫园附属城隍庙，又称西园。

晚清民国之际，豫园屡遭摧残：清道光二十二年（1842年）被英军侵占破坏；清咸丰三年（1853年）小刀会指挥部设在园内点春堂，失败后遭清军劫掠；太平天国时期，法军驻扎园内，掘石填池，建造兵营；清末将今湖心亭一带的大池划出园外，使园址缩小；抗日战争时期又遭到日机轰炸，新中国成立后逐渐修复，可分为西园、东园、中园和南部内园四区。

今豫园外的水池原为园中山池主景，清乾隆四十九年（1784年）布业商人集资在池中建湖心亭，清咸丰五年（1855年）开设宛在轩茶楼。

湖心亭造型复杂，北侧为两层卷棚歇山顶主楼，南接二层攒尖顶方楼，两侧又附六角攒尖顶翼亭，东南、西北有九曲桥与岸相连。从池北园门入园为主厅三穗堂，原为明代乐寿堂，南向正对广池，今被园墙隔开，地位尴尬。

其北一层为仰山堂，二层为卷雨楼，是欣赏池北假山的最佳位置。这座假山为明代张南阳原构，是江南现存规模最大、最完整的黄石山，在前池被划出后，成为园中主景。假山以武康石叠成，气势雄浑，北部陡峻，南部舒展。

北端高耸为主峰，上立六角望江亭，是重九登高赏景、临眺黄浦江之处；向南被一道纵深的涧谷分为东、西两支，渐趋平缓与池岸衔接，涧谷上南北各架一桥，既连起东西两山，又掩住水脉，悠远不尽。山脚设六角挹秀亭，左池右山，视野开阔；山北藏萃修堂，面对危崖峭壁，较为幽静。由仰山堂东侧沿游廊向北，左侧可赏黄石假山，向右通向一座庭园。

园北为主厅万花楼，其南有平台、曲池和假山，主厅两侧接游廊，串起亦舫、方亭、鱼乐榭和两宜轩，掩映在古树秀石间，共同构成一处空间繁复、荫翳幽深的庭院，与西部雄伟开阔的假山水池形成对比。院东是一道起伏的龙墙，龙身逶迤，龙首高昂，极有气势，过墙为东园。

此区是当年小刀会聚义之地，以中部点春堂为中心，主要建筑沿轴线布置，北有曲池、藏宝楼，南对打唱台戏台、水池与和煦堂，东侧贴墙叠筑假山，南北连贯，山顶自南向北依次点缀静怡轩、二层高阁和学圃轩，极尽曲折之能事。由点春堂向西为中园，池水环绕、桥岛勾连，其间布置九狮轩、会景楼、玉华堂和得月楼庭院，疏朗大气。

玉华堂向南隔池正对奇峰玉玲珑，潘允端《豫园记》称其为北宋花石纲遗物，王世贞赞其压尽千峰耸碧空，佳名谁并玉玲珑，许为诸峰之首，是园内极为精雅的一景。由玉玲珑向南为内园，北侧是主厅晴雪堂，堂前凿池叠山，院东绕以花墙亭廊，南部建还云楼和戏台，自成一体。

此外，豫园的雕塑极为精美，散布在云墙、屋顶、脊端和山花等处，让人时有惊喜发现。豫园历史悠久，命运曲折，由私家园林变为庙观园林、公共园林，屡遭割裂分解，形成今日多园并存的格局；但其虽不成完整系统，却记载了一段段连续而鲜活的历史，展示了一代名园的沧桑遭遇和茁壮生命。

· · · · ·
English

In the 38th year of Jiajing of the Ming (1559), Pan Yunduan (1526-1601) failed the imperial examination and returned home, gathering rocks and digging ponds, building pavilions and planting bamboo west of his residence; three years later he passed the jinshi examination and went out to serve as an official, and the garden construction was suspended.

In the 5th year of Wanli of the Ming (1577), he returned after resigning from the post of Right Administrative Commissioner of Sichuan, with official affairs finished, and then began to focus on building the garden, hiring the famous garden designer Zhang Nanyang to preside over it.

Pan Yunduan's father Pan En (1496-1582) rose to the post of Minister of Justice, and was over eighty at that time; Pan Yunduan often entertained his elderly relatives with wine and poetry there, and named the garden Yuyuan (Yu Garden), taking the meaning of 'pleasing the elderly relatives' (Pan Yunduan's 'Record of Yu Garden').

After the garden was completed, it covered over 70 mu, collecting strange peaks and rare rocks, adorned with famous flowers and precious trees, with land featuring the beauty of ravines, ridges, caves, and valleys, and water featuring the charm of islands, beaches, bridges, and fords; Chen Suoyun's 'Biography of Mountain Man Zhang' ranked Yu Garden alongside Wang Shizhen's Yanshan Garden, praising the two gardens as 'facing each other across a hundred li, the crown of famous gardens in the southeast.

' These two gardens and Chen Suoyun's Rishe Garden were all masterpieces of Zhang Nanyang.

After entering the Qing Dynasty, the buildings in the garden were gradually occupied by trade guilds (merchant or craftsman groups of the same trade), with boundaries divided and separated; in the 25th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1760), local gentry raised funds to purchase the remaining land of Yu Garden from Pan's descendants, and successively renovated and expanded it, and by the 49th year of Qianlong (1784) it roughly formed today's Yu Garden layout.

At that time Yu Garden was attached to the City God Temple, also called the West Garden.

In the late Qing and Republican periods, Yu Garden was repeatedly devastated: in the 22nd year of Daoguang of the Qing (1842) it was occupied and damaged by British troops; in the 3rd year of Xianfeng (1853) the Small Swords Society's command post was set up in Dianspring Hall in the garden, and after their defeat it was looted by Qing troops; during the Taiping Rebellion period, French troops were stationed in the garden, digging rocks and filling ponds to build barracks; at the end of the Qing, the large pond around today's Mid-Lake Pavilion was划出 outside the garden, reducing the garden area; during the War of Resistance against Japan it was bombed by Japanese planes, and after the founding of New China it was gradually restored, divided into four areas: West Garden, East Garden, Central Garden, and the southern Inner Garden.

The pond outside today's Yu Garden was originally the main mountain-pond scenery in the garden; in the 49th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1784), cloth merchants raised funds to build the Mid-Lake Pavilion in the pond, and in the 5th year of Xianfeng (1855) the Wanzaixuan Tea House was opened.

The Mid-Lake Pavilion has a complex shape: the north side is a two-story rolled-roof hip-and-gable main building, connected to a two-story pyramidal square building on the south, with hexagonal pyramidal wing pavilions attached on both sides, and the Nine-Zigzag Bridge connects to the bank in the southeast and northwest.

Entering the garden from the north garden gate by the pond, the main hall is Sansui (Three Ears of Grain) Hall, originally the Ming Dynasty Leshou Hall, facing south directly toward the broad pond, now separated by the garden wall with an awkward position.

Its north first floor is Yangshan (Admiring the Mountain) Hall, and the second floor is Juanyu (Curling Rain) Tower, the best position to appreciate the rockery north of the pond.

This rockery is the original structure of Zhang Nanyang of the Ming, the largest and most complete yellow-stone rockery existing in Jiangnan; after the front pond was划出, it became the main scenery in the garden.

The rockery is stacked with Wukang stones, with a powerful and vigorous momentum, steep in the north and舒展 in the south.

The north end rises high as the main peak, with a hexagonal Wangjiang (River-Viewing) Pavilion on top, a place for climbing high to enjoy scenery and overlook the Huangpu River on the Double Ninth Festival; to the south it is divided into east and west branches by a deep ravine, gradually flattening and connecting with the pond bank; a bridge is built north and south over the ravine, both connecting the east and west mountains and concealing the water vein, making it seem far and endless.

At the foot of the mountain is a hexagonal Yixiu (Embracing Beauty) Pavilion, with pond on the left and mountain on the right, with a broad view; north of the mountain hides Cuixiu Hall, facing steep cliffs, relatively quiet.

From the east side of Yangshan Hall going north along the corridor, on the left one can admire the yellow-stone rockery, and to the right leads to a courtyard.

North of the garden is the main hall Wanhua (Ten Thousand Flowers) Tower, with a platform, winding pond, and rockery to its south; the main hall connects to corridors on both sides,串起 Yifang (Also Boat), Square Pavilion, Yule (Fish Joy) Pavilion, and Liangyi (Two Appropriates) Pavilion, shaded among ancient trees and elegant rocks, together forming a courtyard with complex space and deep shade, contrasting with the grand and open rockery-pond in the west.

East of the courtyard is an undulating dragon wall, with the dragon body winding and the dragon head high, extremely imposing; crossing the wall is the East Garden.

This area was the place where the Small Swords Society gathered in those years, centered on Dianspring Hall in the middle, with main buildings arranged along the axis: to the north are winding pond and Cangbao (Treasure-Hiding) Tower, to the south facing the Dachangtai (Singing Stage) opera stage, pond, and Hexu (Harmonious Sunshine) Hall; on the east side, rockeries are stacked against the wall, continuous from north to south, with Jingyi Hall, a two-story high pavilion, and Xuepu (Learning Garden) Pavilion dotted on the mountain top from south to north in sequence,极尽 the art of winding and twisting.

From Dianspring Hall going west is the Central Garden, with pond water surrounding and bridges and islands interlinked, with Jiushi (Nine Lions) Pavilion, Huijing (Scenery-Gathering) Tower, Yuhua (Jade Flower) Hall, and Deyue (Moon-Gaining) Tower courtyards arranged among them, spacious and grand.

South of Yuhua Hall across the pond faces the strange peak Yulinglong (Jade Exquisite), which Pan Yunduan's 'Record of Yu Garden' calls a relic of the Northern Song Huashigang (Flower and Stone Convoy), and Wang Shizhen praised it as 'pressing down a thousand peaks soaring into the blue sky, what fine name can compare with Jade Exquisite,' ranking it first among all peaks, an extremely elegant scene in the garden.

From Yulinglong going south is the Inner Garden, with the main hall Qingxue (Clear Snow) Hall on the north, with ponds dug and rocks stacked in front of the hall; the east side of the courtyard is surrounded by flower walls and pavilions and corridors, and in the south are built Huanyun (Returning Cloud) Tower and an opera stage, forming a self-contained unit.

In addition, the sculptures in Yu Garden are extremely exquisite, scattered on cloud walls, roofs, ridge ends, and gables etc., bringing surprises from time to time.

Yu Garden has a long history and a tortuous fate, changing from a private garden to a temple garden and public garden, repeatedly divided and separated, forming today's pattern of multiple gardens coexisting; but although it is not a complete system, it records continuous and vivid periods of history, showing the vicissitudes and vigorous life of a generation of famous gardens.

建筑要点 / Key Features
明嘉靖三十八年1559年潘允端15261601考试落第回乡在宅西聚石凿池构亭艺竹三年后他考中进士外出任官园林建设随之中止明万历五年1577年他从四川右布政使卸任归来官事已了才开始专心营筑园林聘请造园名家张南阳主持潘允端的父亲潘恩14961582官至刑部尚书当时已年过八旬潘允端时奉老亲觞咏其间并将园名题为豫园取愉悦老亲之意潘允端豫园记园林建成后占地70多亩搜罗奇峰异石点缀名花珍木陆具涧岭洞壑之胜水极岛滩梁渡之趣陈所蕴张山人传将豫园与王世贞的弇山园并列称赞两园百里相望为东南名园冠这两座园林以及陈所蕴的日涉园都是张南阳的杰作入清后园内建筑逐渐被同业公所同行业的商人或工匠团体占据划界割裂清乾隆二十五年1760年士绅们集资从潘氏后人手中购得豫园余地陆续整治扩建到清乾隆四十九年1784年大致形成今日豫园格局当时豫园附属城隍庙又称西园晚清民国之际豫园屡遭摧残清道光二十二年1842年被英军侵占破坏清咸丰三年1853年小刀会指挥部设在园内点春堂失败后遭清军劫掠太平天国时期法军驻扎园内掘石填池建造兵营清末将今湖心亭一带的大池划出园外使园址缩小抗日战争时期又遭到日机轰炸新中国成立后逐渐修复可分为西园东园中园
02 城隍庙
Temple of City God
元—清
级别 Level
上海市文物保护单位（2002年）
地址 Address
黄浦区方浜中路249号
类型 Type
古建筑/寺庙
门票 Ticket
10元

8:30 — 16:30
中文原文

元代上海县内未置城隍庙，在市郊的淡井庙祭祀城隍。明永乐年间，上海知县张守约将城内原祭祀霍光的金山神庙改为城隍庙，供奉上海城隍秦裕伯。

此后历代多次修葺扩建，至清末达一万多平方米，内有大殿、城隍殿、玉清宫和星宿殿等，还有东、西两座园林，豫园曾一度成为庙产，即西园。

清末城隍庙屡遭兵燹，清道光二十二年（1842年）五月，英军占据城隍庙为兵营；清咸丰三年（1853年）小刀会起义驻扎豫园，清兵攻破上海后在寺内烧掠；清咸丰十年（1860年）外兵入城防御太平军，又以城隍庙作为英法军队营房。

1924年7月15日，城隍庙大殿起火，波及中厅、厢房和戏楼。1926年黄金荣、杜月笙集资重建，1927年完工，改为钢筋混凝土结构，由久记营造厂承建，耗资五万银币。城隍庙大门三间，前有石柱牌楼，上书海隅保障四字，南有照壁、旗杆。

门内正对大殿设戏台，两侧厢房为慈航殿、财神殿等。主殿为工字形，前殿三间供奉霍光，屋顶泥塑三国人物，精美生动；中部走廊为太岁殿，其后内天井两侧有文昌殿、关圣殿两配殿。最后一进是城隍殿，殿内仿照明代县衙公堂陈设，上悬匾额威灵显赫，中央供奉上海县城神红脸木雕像。

城隍殿两侧设父母殿、娘娘殿两配殿。

· · · · ·
English

In the Yuan Dynasty, there was no City God Temple in Shanghai County, and the City God was worshipped at Danjing Temple in the suburbs.

During the Yongle reign of the Ming, Zhang Shouyue, County Magistrate of Shanghai, converted the Jinshan God Temple in the city, which originally worshipped Huo Guang, into the City God Temple, enshrining Qin Yubo, the City God of Shanghai.

Thereafter it was repeatedly renovated and expanded through the dynasties, reaching over 10,000 square meters by the end of the Qing, with the Grand Hall, City God Hall, Yuqing (Jade Purity) Palace, and Star Constellation Hall etc.

inside, as well as east and west two gardens; Yu Garden once became temple property, namely the West Garden.

At the end of the Qing, the City God Temple repeatedly suffered from war disasters: in May of the 22nd year of Daoguang of the Qing (1842), British troops occupied the City God Temple as a military camp; in the 3rd year of Xianfeng (1853), the Small Swords Society uprising was stationed in Yu Garden, and after Qing troops captured Shanghai they burned and looted in the temple; in the 10th year of Xianfeng (1860), foreign troops entered the city to defend against the Taiping Army, and again used the City God Temple as a military camp for British and French troops.

On July 15, 1924, the Grand Hall of the City God Temple caught fire, affecting the central hall, wing rooms, and opera tower.

In 1926, Huang Jinrong and Du Yuesheng raised funds for reconstruction, completed in 1927, changed to a reinforced concrete structure, constructed by Jiuji Construction Factory, costing 50,000 silver dollars.

The City God Temple has three bays of main gate, with a stone-column paifang in front inscribed with the four characters 'Haiyu Baozhang' (Protecting the Sea Corner), and a screen wall and flagpole to the south.

Inside the gate, facing the Grand Hall, is an opera stage, with the wing rooms on both sides being the Cihang (Mercy Boat) Hall, God of Wealth Hall etc.

The main hall is I-shaped; the front hall has three bays enshrining Huo Guang, with clay sculptures of Three Kingdoms figures on the roof, exquisite and vivid; the central corridor is the Taisui (Year God) Hall, behind which on both sides of the inner courtyard are the Wenchang (Literary Prosperity) Hall and Guansheng (Lord Guan Holy) Hall as two side halls.

The last courtyard is the City God Hall, with furnishings imitating a Ming Dynasty county yamen court, with a plaque hanging above reading 'Weiling Xianhe' (Mighty and Illustrious), and in the center enshrining the red-faced wooden statue of the City God of Shanghai County.

On both sides of the City God Hall are the Parents Hall and Empress Hall as two side halls.

建筑要点 / Key Features
元代上海县内未置城隍庙在市郊的淡井庙祭祀城隍明永乐年间上海知县张守约将城内原祭祀霍光的金山神庙改为城隍庙供奉上海城隍秦裕伯此后历代多次修葺扩建至清末达一万多平方米内有大殿城隍殿玉清宫和星宿殿等还有东西两座园林豫园曾一度成为庙产即西园清末城隍庙屡遭兵燹清道光二十二年1842年五月英军占据城隍庙为兵营清咸丰三年1853年小刀会起义驻扎豫园清兵攻破上海后在寺内烧掠清咸丰十年1860年外兵入城防御太平军又以城隍庙作为英法军队营房1924年7月15日城隍庙大殿起火波及中厅厢房和戏楼1926年黄金荣杜月笙集资重建1927年完工改为钢筋混凝土结构由久记营造厂承建耗资五万银币城隍庙大门三间前有石柱牌楼上书海隅保障四字南有照壁旗杆门内正对大殿设戏台两侧厢房为慈航殿财神殿等主殿为工字形前殿三间供奉霍光屋顶泥塑三国人物精美生动中部走廊为太岁殿其后内天井两侧有文昌殿关圣殿两配殿最后一进是城隍殿殿内仿照明代县衙公堂陈设上悬匾额威灵显赫中央供奉上海县城神红脸木雕像城隍殿两侧设父母殿娘娘殿两配殿
03 沉香阁
Chenxiang Pavilion
明—清
级别 Level
第四批全国重点文物保护单位（1996年）
地址 Address
黄浦区沉香阁路29号
类型 Type
古建筑/寺庙
门票 Ticket
10元
开放时间 Hours
5:00 — 17:00
中文原文

沉香阁始建于明万历二十八年（1600年），据传豫园主人潘允端督运漕粮于江淮间，看见沉香观音像漂浮在淮河上，遂打捞奉归上海，建沉香大士阁供奉，作为母亲念佛的家庙，后改名慈云禅寺。

清康熙二十三年（1684年）修葺，清嘉庆六年（1801年）重建，嘉庆十年（1805年）重建寺前禅堂。嘉庆十九年（1814年）建大殿、天王殿。

清道光年间修建两厢楼，清同治年间又建鹤轩。沉香阁原为禅宗门庭，1943年近代高僧应慈移锡于此，弘扬华严宗，兼为华严宗道场。

新中国成立后寺庙被工厂占用，1989年复建为比丘尼丛林，在入口利用原有石柱重建四柱五楼牌坊，坊北重建天王殿，殿前左右设钟、鼓楼。大雄宝殿与寺后沉香阁在修复时进行了整体抬升。

大雄宝殿为歇山顶，面阔三间，殿后为沉香观音阁，为两层歇山顶，与其后的两层楼阁连为一体，下层为架空石柱，上层供奉1990年重刻的沉香观音像。

· · · · ·
English

Chenxiang (Agarwood) Pavilion was first built in the 28th year of Wanli of the Ming (1600); it is said that Pan Yunduan, the owner of Yu Garden, while supervising the transport of tribute grain between the Yangtze and Huai rivers, saw an agarwood Guanyin statue floating on the Huai River, so he salvaged it and brought it back to Shanghai, building the Agarwood Great Being Pavilion to enshrine it as a family temple for his mother to chant the Buddha, later renamed Ciyun (Compassionate Cloud) Chan Temple.

It was renovated in the 23rd year of Kangxi of the Qing (1684), rebuilt in the 6th year of Jiaqing (1801), and the meditation hall in front of the temple was rebuilt in the 10th year of Jiaqing (1805).

In the 19th year of Jiaqing (1814), the Grand Hall and Heavenly Kings Hall were built.

During the Daoguang reign of the Qing, the two wing buildings were built, and during the Tongzhi reign the Crane Pavilion was also built.

Chenxiang Pavilion was originally a Chan (Zen) Buddhist temple; in 1943, the modern eminent monk Yingci moved his staff here, propagating the Huayan (Avatamsaka) school, also serving as a Huayan school道场.

After the founding of New China, the temple was occupied by a factory; in 1989 it was restored as a bhikkhuni (nun) monastery, and at the entrance the original stone columns were used to rebuild a four-column five-story paifang; north of the paifang the Heavenly Kings Hall was rebuilt, with bell and drum towers on the left and right in front of the hall.

The Mahavira Hall and the Chenxiang Pavilion behind the temple were整体 lifted during restoration.

The Mahavira Hall has a hip-and-gable roof, three bays wide; behind the hall is the Agarwood Guanyin Pavilion, a two-story hip-and-gable roof connected as one with the two-story pavilion behind it, with the lower floor as elevated stone columns and the upper floor enshrining the agarwood Guanyin statue recarved in 1990.

建筑要点 / Key Features
沉香阁始建于明万历二十八年1600年据传豫园主人潘允端督运漕粮于江淮间看见沉香观音像漂浮在淮河上遂打捞奉归上海建沉香大士阁供奉作为母亲念佛的家庙后改名慈云禅寺清康熙二十三年1684年修葺清嘉庆六年1801年重建嘉庆十年1805年重建寺前禅堂嘉庆十九年1814年建大殿天王殿清道光年间修建两厢楼清同治年间又建鹤轩沉香阁原为禅宗门庭1943年近代高僧应慈移锡于此弘扬华严宗兼为华严宗道场新中国成立后寺庙被工厂占用1989年复建为比丘尼丛林在入口利用原有石柱重建四柱五楼牌坊坊北重建天王殿殿前左右设钟鼓楼大雄宝殿与寺后沉香阁在修复时进行了整体抬升大雄宝殿为歇山顶面阔三间殿后为沉香观音阁为两层歇山顶与其后的两层楼阁连为一体下层为架空石柱上层供奉1990年重刻的沉香观音像
04 书隐楼
Shuyin Building
明
级别 Level
上海市文物保护单位（1987年）
地址 Address
黄浦区南市区天灯弄77号
类型 Type
古建筑/私家宅院
中文原文

书隐楼是上海市内仅存的大型私家宅院，其地原为明代陈所蕴的日涉园，陈氏败落后，将日涉园售给陆明允。陆明允的曾孙陆锡熊曾任《四库全书》编撰，其父陆秉笏住在日涉园，自号淞南老人，新筑传经书屋。后来陆锡熊得到御赐《淞南小隐》画卷，于是改传经书屋为淞南小隐。

陆锡熊请担任《四库全书》副总裁的好友沈初重写匾额，称书隐楼。清末陆氏衰落，日涉园被分割出售，园林大部分改为住宅。20世纪30年代，郭福田购得书隐楼，至今仍为郭家私产，前任主人郭俊纶为建筑师，喜爱园林，著有《清代园林图录》，郭氏去世后为其遗孀所居。

书隐楼入口在西南，门厅朝东，门内有宽三间的轿厅。主院落为南北向，包括中央的正落和左右边的花园。第一进院落中央为三间大厅毓瑞堂，左右为书房。厅后有封火墙，将前后两座藏书楼四面围砌，安全隐秘。墙内又有前后两进，第一进正楼宽五间，高两层，上悬书隐楼匾额，后楼也是五间两层，供居住使用。两座楼前皆有两层厢房和走廊，连接成走马楼式。

正轴东侧边落为花园，最南端原有戏台已毁，戏台后为花厅话雨轩，轩北出抱厦。北侧园林依西墙设游廊，廊西为水池，中部以船舫划分水面。池北有大小两处厨房，小厨园内有水井，大厨以北原有小院，如今仅存黄石数块。正轴西侧有三间佣人房，前方小院内有宋代水井，井栏为宋代原物。

书隐楼建筑群还有精美的砖雕与木雕，题材丰富，雕工细腻，富有艺术价值。

· · · · ·
English

Shuyin (Book-Hiding) Building is the only remaining large private residence in Shanghai city; its land was originally the Rishe Garden of Chen Suoyun of the Ming Dynasty; after the Chen family declined, they sold Rishe Garden to Lu Mingyun.

Lu Mingyun's great-grandson Lu Xixiong once served as a compiler of the 'Complete Library in the Four Branches of Literature'; his father Lu Binghu lived in Rishe Garden, calling himself the Old Man of Songnan, and newly built the Chuanjing (Scripture-Transmitting) Study.

Later Lu Xixiong received an imperially bestowed painting scroll 'Small Retreat of Songnan,' so he changed the Chuanjing Study to Small Retreat of Songnan.

Lu Xixiong asked his good friend Shen Chu, who served as vice president of the 'Complete Library in the Four Branches of Literature,' to rewrite the plaque, calling it Shuyin Building.

At the end of the Qing, the Lu family declined, and Rishe Garden was divided and sold, with most of the garden converted to residences.

In the 1930s, Guo Futian purchased Shuyin Building, which remains the private property of the Guo family to this day; the former owner Guo Junlun was an architect who loved gardens and authored 'Illustrated Record of Qing Dynasty Gardens'; after Guo's death it was lived in by his widow.

The entrance of Shuyin Building is in the southwest, with the gate hall facing east, and inside the gate is a sedan-chair hall three bays wide.

The main courtyard is north-south oriented, including the central main compound and the gardens on the left and right sides.

In the center of the first courtyard is the three-bay main hall Yurui (Auspicious Jade) Hall, with studies on the left and right.

Behind the hall is a fire-sealing wall, enclosing the front and rear two book-storage buildings on all four sides, safe and secret.

Inside the wall there are again front and rear two courtyards; the first main building is five bays wide and two stories high, with the 'Shuyin Building' plaque hanging above; the rear building is also five bays and two stories, for residential use.

In front of both buildings are two-story wing rooms and corridors, connected in a 'galloping horse building' style.

The side compound east of the central axis is a garden; at the southernmost end there was originally an opera stage, now destroyed; behind the opera stage is the flower hall Huayu (Talking Rain) Pavilion, with a projecting bay to the north of the pavilion.

The north garden has a corridor along the west wall, with a pond west of the corridor, and the water surface is divided by a boat-shaped hall in the middle.

North of the pond are two kitchens, large and small; there is a water well in the small kitchen garden, and north of the large kitchen there was originally a small courtyard, now only a few yellow stones remain.

West of the central axis are three bays of servant rooms, and in the small courtyard in front there is a Song Dynasty water well, with the well railing being a Song Dynasty original.

The Shuyin Building complex also has exquisite brick carvings and wood carvings, with rich themes and delicate carving, full of artistic value.

建筑要点 / Key Features
书隐楼是上海市内仅存的大型私家宅院其地原为明代陈所蕴的日涉园陈氏败落后将日涉园售给陆明允陆明允的曾孙陆锡熊曾任四库全书编撰其父陆秉笏住在日涉园自号淞南老人新筑传经书屋后来陆锡熊得到御赐淞南小隐画卷于是改传经书屋为淞南小隐陆锡熊请担任四库全书副总裁的好友沈初重写匾额称书隐楼清末陆氏衰落日涉园被分割出售园林大部分改为住宅20世纪30年代郭福田购得书隐楼至今仍为郭家私产前任主人郭俊纶为建筑师喜爱园林著有清代园林图录郭氏去世后为其遗孀所居书隐楼入口在西南门厅朝东门内有宽三间的轿厅主院落为南北向包括中央的正落和左右边的花园第一进院落中央为三间大厅毓瑞堂左右为书房厅后有封火墙将前后两座藏书楼四面围砌安全隐秘墙内又有前后两进第一进正楼宽五间高两层上悬书隐楼匾额后楼也是五间两层供居住使用两座楼前皆有两层厢房和走廊连接成走马楼式正轴东侧边落为花园最南端原有戏台已毁戏台后为花厅话雨轩轩北出抱厦北侧园林依西墙设游廊廊西为水池中部以船舫划分水面池北有大小两处厨房小厨园内有水井大厨以北原有小院如今仅存黄石数块正轴西侧有三间佣人房前方小院内有宋代水井井栏为宋代原物书隐楼建筑群还有精美的砖雕与木雕题材丰富雕工细腻富
05 上海文庙
Temple of Confucius in Shanghai
清
级别 Level
上海市文物保护单位（2002年）
地址 Address
黄浦区文庙路215号
类型 Type
古建筑/文庙
中文原文

上海文庙是祭祀孔子、庙学合一的建筑群，先后五次易址。南宋上海建镇时，当地士绅曾建梓潼祠，供孔子像，又建古修堂作为镇学。上海设县后，元至元三十一年（1294年）改镇学为县学，在县署东首建文庙，有正殿、讲堂和斋舍等。

元大德六年（1302年）扩建为规格完整的文庙。元至大三年（1310年）在肇家浜（今复兴东路）北岸县衙（今学院路）兴建了新的文庙，四年后又迁回原址，明清两朝屡有增修。

清咸丰三年（1853年）小刀会在文庙举事，在祭孔典礼上刺杀了上海知县，并将本部设在文庙内，兵败后文庙毁于战火。当年士绅便集资在原址重建，但大梁未上便遭遇火灾，清咸丰五年（1855年）再次动工时又遭火灾。人们认为原址风水不利，迁至今址重建。

太平天国时期文庙曾作为英法军队屯兵营地，庙中建筑损毁过半。民国时期文庙先后被改为公园和图书馆，曾在此举行救亡歌咏大会。新中国成立后曾改为武庙，作为体委训练场。文革结束后重修了大成殿、明伦堂、魁星阁、崇圣祠和东西庑殿，1997年全面整修，恢复清代盛时风貌。

文庙包括文庙和学宫两路，东侧还有花园。文庙沿轴线依次为棂星门、大成门、大成殿和崇圣祠。

入口棂星门为单开间石牌坊，内有三间大成门，门后是清咸丰五年（1855年）重建的大成殿，宽三间，重檐歇山顶，屋脊有林则徐书写的海滨邹鲁四字砖雕，殿内供香樟木孔子贴金像。

大成殿左右有东西庑殿，宽六间，硬山顶，以前祭祀孔子七十二弟子，现在壁间镶嵌明清碑刻。殿北崇圣祠为供奉孔子祖先的祠堂，今为办公处。

学宫沿轴线依次为学门、仪门、明伦堂和尊经阁，其中主要建筑为明伦堂，清咸丰五年（1855年）重建。堂后的尊经阁高两层，曾作为上海首个市立图书馆，2006年重建。

东侧花园以天光云影池为中心，池北为儒学署，署右为听雨轩水榭，水池东南角建三层魁星阁。

· · · · ·
English

The Shanghai Confucian Temple is a building complex combining the worship of Confucius with temple and school, having changed its location five times.

When Shanghai was established as a town in the Southern Song, local gentry once built the Zitong Shrine to enshrine a Confucius statue, and also built the Guxiu Hall as the town school.

After Shanghai was established as a county, in the 31st year of Zhiyuan of the Yuan (1294) the town school was changed to a county school, and a Confucian Temple was built east of the county yamen, with a main hall, lecture hall, and dormitories etc.

In the 6th year of Dade of the Yuan (1302) it was expanded into a full-standard Confucian Temple.

In the 3rd year of Zhida of the Yuan (1310), a new Confucian Temple was built on the north bank of Zhaojiabang (today's East Fuxing Road) at the county yamen (today's Xueyuan Road), and four years later it moved back to the original site, with repeated additions and repairs in the Ming and Qing dynasties.

In the 3rd year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1853), the Small Swords Society launched an uprising at the Confucian Temple, assassinating the Shanghai County Magistrate at the Confucius worship ceremony and setting up their headquarters in the Confucian Temple; after their defeat the Confucian Temple was destroyed by war.

That year the gentry raised funds to rebuild on the original site, but before the main beam was installed it encountered a fire, and when construction started again in the 5th year of Xianfeng (1855) it encountered another fire.

People believed the original site had unfavorable feng shui, so they moved to the current site for reconstruction.

During the Taiping Rebellion period, the Confucian Temple was used as a military camp for British and French troops, with over half of the buildings in the temple damaged.

During the Republican period, the Confucian Temple was successively converted into a park and library, and a national salvation singing conference was once held here.

After the founding of New China, it was once converted into a Martial Temple as a training ground for the Sports Commission.

After the end of the Cultural Revolution, the Dacheng Hall, Minglun Hall, Kuixing Pavilion, Chongsheng Shrine, and east and west wing halls were renovated, and in 1997 a comprehensive renovation restored the prosperous Qing Dynasty style.

The Confucian Temple includes two routes: the Confucian Temple and the School Palace, with a garden on the east side.

Along the axis of the Confucian Temple are依次 the Lingxing Gate, Dacheng Gate, Dacheng Hall, and Chongsheng Shrine.

The entrance Lingxing Gate is a single-bay stone paifang, with a three-bay Dacheng Gate inside; behind the gate is the Dacheng Hall rebuilt in the 5th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1855), three bays wide, with a double-eave hip-and-gable roof, with brick carvings of the four characters 'Haibin Zoulu' (Zou and Lu by the Sea) written by Lin Zexu on the ridge, and inside the hall enshrines a camphor-wood gilded Confucius statue.

On the left and right of the Dacheng Hall are east and west wing halls, six bays wide, with flush-gable roofs, formerly used to worship the seventy-two disciples of Confucius, and now Ming-Qing stele carvings are inlaid between the walls.

North of the hall, the Chongsheng Shrine is a shrine for worshipping Confucius's ancestors, now an office.

Along the axis of the School Palace are依次 the School Gate, Ceremonial Gate, Minglun Hall, and Zunjing Pavilion; the main building is the Minglun Hall, rebuilt in the 5th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1855).

The Zunjing Pavilion behind the hall is two stories high, once serving as Shanghai's first municipal library, rebuilt in 2006.

The east garden is centered on the Tianguang Yunying (Sky Light and Cloud Shadow) Pond, with the Ruxue (Confucian Learning) Office north of the pond, the Tingyu (Listening to Rain) Pavilion waterside pavilion to the right of the office, and a three-story Kuixing (Star of Literature) Pavilion built at the southeast corner of the pond.

建筑要点 / Key Features
上海文庙是祭祀孔子庙学合一的建筑群先后五次易址南宋上海建镇时当地士绅曾建梓潼祠供孔子像又建古修堂作为镇学上海设县后元至元三十一年1294年改镇学为县学在县署东首建文庙有正殿讲堂和斋舍等元大德六年1302年扩建为规格完整的文庙元至大三年1310年在肇家浜今复兴东路北岸县衙今学院路兴建了新的文庙四年后又迁回原址明清两朝屡有增修清咸丰三年1853年小刀会在文庙举事在祭孔典礼上刺杀了上海知县并将本部设在文庙内兵败后文庙毁于战火当年士绅便集资在原址重建但大梁未上便遭遇火灾清咸丰五年1855年再次动工时又遭火灾人们认为原址风水不利迁至今址重建太平天国时期文庙曾作为英法军队屯兵营地庙中建筑损毁过半民国时期文庙先后被改为公园和图书馆曾在此举行救亡歌咏大会新中国成立后曾改为武庙作为体委训练场文革结束后重修了大成殿明伦堂魁星阁崇圣祠和东西庑殿1997年全面整修恢复清代盛时风貌文庙包括文庙和学宫两路东侧还有花园文庙沿轴线依次为棂星门大成门大成殿和崇圣祠入口棂星门为单开间石牌坊内有三间大成门门后是清咸丰五年1855年重建的大成殿宽三间重檐歇山顶屋脊有林则徐书写的海滨邹鲁四字砖雕殿内供香樟木孔子贴金像大成殿左右
06 上海古城墙和大境道观
Ancient City Wall of Shanghai and Dajing Taoist Temple
明—清
级别 Level
上海市文物保护单位（1984年）
地址 Address
黄浦区小北门大境路269号
类型 Type
古建筑/城墙/道观

5元
